chapters.title: Chapter 751
paragraphs: Unlike the lunatic imperialist serving as Defense Minister, Japan’s prime minister proved surprisingly easy to reason with.
“I cannot remove the Defense Minister immediately, but I will grant you and the other Koreans independent operational authority, Jinsang.”
“Please also guarantee us supplies and military support through the Defense Ministry,” Team Leader Choi said, polite but firm. “We came at your country’s request to cooperate, not to be sacrificed.”
The prime minister nodded. “Agreed. I shall do everything within my power.”
If it were up to me, I’d dunk the idiots at the Defense Ministry in a radioactive hot spring. Even that wouldn’t be enough.
But what could we do? The damage was done. We had to make the best of what we had.
“How, though, do you intend to deal with a monster that has already escaped?” the prime minister asked.
“I have a way.”
The answer came out of nowhere. The Skeleton King was staring at the prime minister with his usual arrogant glare. I made a throat-cutting gesture at him, and he flinched.
“I have a way, yo,” he corrected himself.
That was a form of polite speech found in no family tree, but the prime minister—already famous for his collection of memorable quotes—didn’t seem to mind. If anything, he looked pleased.
“Ah, Stomu-King. I have heard much about you.”
“Me? I mean... me, sir?”
“Of course. I knew of you even before this incident, when you helped suppress several mutation Gates in Korea.”

The Skeleton King had been known here and there among the public even before the vigilante incident came to light. The appearance of a previously unknown top-tier Hunter had briefly drawn attention, but the story was soon buried.
Magic Johnson had done a thorough job of laundering his identity. Besides, the truth was so ridiculous that no one had suspected he might be a monster.
*...Actually, I just took so much shit that nobody paid attention to him.*
“It is a pleasure to meet you at last, Stomu-King.”
The Skeleton King had been looking rather proud that a country’s prime minister knew who he was. Now his brow furrowed.
“The pleasure is mine. But I am—no, my name is Stone King.”
“Yes, that is what I am calling you. Stomu-King.”
“I said Stone King. Here, repeat after me slowly. S. Tone. King.”
“S. Tone. King.”
“Now a little longer. Stone. King.”
“Stone. King.”
“Excellent! Now put it together.”
“Stomu-King.”
“Good heavens. I’m going to lose my mind. I can’t believe this! What is wrong with your tongue?”
The cursed archipelago’s pronunciation system had met Demon Realm mangled-speech in a collaboration for the ages.
Team Leader Choi squeezed his eyes shut. Unable to watch any more, I stepped in.
“Enough. Stone King, Stomu-King, stalking—what difference does it make?”
“It makes a tremendous difference, you Jinsang bastard!”
“More difference than the crack I’m about to put in your skull?”
“Hmm. On second thought, perhaps not.”
“See?”
“Of course. Call me whatever you like. That can be my name.”
“Good attitude, Fucking. Now tell us how to track Leviathan.”
The Skeleton King muttered a curse at his new name, then spoke.
“First, your premise is wrong. We shouldn’t track Leviathan. We need to lure it as close to land as we can.”
“Lure it?”
“Yes. The sea is entirely its territory. Try to follow it with some half-baked scheme, and we may lose it for good.”
“You mean...”
“It was too badly wounded to flee far. Leviathan can’t have gone far yet.”

Team Leader Choi raised a question. “Although Leviathan suffered a heavy blow thanks to Mr. Jin Taekyung, I understand that it obtained an unrefined S-rank Magic Gem. Wouldn’t that be enough for it to recover from its wounds and then some?”
“Heal?”
The Skeleton King gave a quiet snort.
“Leviathan could absorb all the magical power in that gem, however much it holds. But even once it makes that power its own, completely healing its injuries is another matter.”
“Hmm.”
“It would need more magical power to heal wounds like those. By now, it must have realized that too.”
The assessment from an actual monster was persuasive.
On top of that, One Annihilation was a killing blow powerful enough to wreck even its caster’s body.
True to its name, Leviathan had twisted its body at the last moment, but those were not wounds that could heal in a short time.
*Lure it. Lure it, huh.*
I turned the word over in my mind. “It sized up the situation, took exactly what it wanted, and ran. Would something that cunning fall for a trap?”
The answer was simple.
“It will, if the conditions are right.”
“So we set a trap it has no choice but to enter, even knowing it’s a trap?”
“Think of Leviathan as a hungry, wounded beast. Hunger brought it here in the first place.”
Team Leader Choi spoke almost with a groan. “We’ll need one hell of a lure.”
“Yes. We need bait so delicious that Leviathan will risk its life to charge at it.”
And at this point, there was only one thing that could lure Leviathan in.
“Excuse me, Prime Minister?”
Koizumi had been following the conversation with glazed eyes. He looked up at my gentle tone.
“Ah, yes. Go ahead.”
“Does Japan happen to have a few of those?”
“A few of what?”
“Don’t play dumb. S-rank Magic Gems.”
“Let us borrow them for a bit.”
“...Ehhh?”
“Why so surprised? We’ll catch Leviathan and give them back. Promise.”
I held out my pinkie to the wide-eyed prime minister.
*We’ll win one and pay it back. Win it.*
In the modern world, S-rank Magic Gems were treasures of tremendous value.

Before even considering that they were the finest energy source capable of powering an entire metropolis, there were only around a hundred of them in the entire world. Their rarity alone was astonishing.

Perhaps that was why the Japanese prime minister, despite promising his full cooperation, had initially been horrified. Of course, in the end, he had no choice but to hand them over, even if it was against his will.
“Here they are.”
*Click.*
The security Magic disengaged, and a soft velvet box opened. Inside lay two Magic Gems, shedding brilliant light.
“Hmm. Only two?”
The prime minister saw my expression and answered in a rush. “These are all the S-rank Magic Gems the Japanese government owns.”
“Really?”
“Not a word of a lie! Do you know how hard I had to work to persuade the cabinet and His Majesty the Emperor?”
“If I search the place and find more, that’s one S-rank Magic Gem for every—”
“...Mr. Jin Taekyung?” Team Leader Choi said.
“Oh. Sorry. Force of habit.”
*Habits are scary.*

At Team Leader Choi’s intervention, I scratched the back of my head. The Japanese prime minister, who had been edging backward for a while now, hurriedly slipped out of the room, repeatedly begging us to return the Magic Gems safely.
But once he was gone, the mood in the room was rather lukewarm.
“Hmm. Two...”
“Not quite enough.”
“I agree,” the Skeleton King said. “They still hold a considerable amount of magical power, but not enough to lure Leviathan.”
The number of S-rank Magic Gems didn’t matter. What mattered was the amount and quality of the magical power left in them.
*Normally, they should obviously have been refined... but this time, we have a different use for them.*
We had two S-rank Magic Gems in front of us. What we needed was bait—something Leviathan would rush for even if it knew there was a trap.
A massive mass of pure magical power, like the one it had taken.
*Even if we use both of these together as bait, they still won’t come close to an unrefined Magic Gem.*
I wasn’t alone in thinking it. As we exchanged looks, the Skeleton King spoke up.
“No matter how I think about it, these will not be enough. What about bringing more?”
“Bring more from where...? Oh.”
I remembered Area A, hidden inside Ares Guild headquarters. The place had held staggering amounts of cash, artwork, and Magic Gems—including five S-rank Magic Gems.
“But those were refined too.”
“That... is true.”
The Skeleton King smacked his lips. “Still, better than nothing. Is there no way to get them?”

They were better than nothing, but adding five more wouldn’t change much. The more thoroughly a Magic Gem was refined, the more valuable it became, and the S-rank gems Lee Jungryong and Go Jun had stashed in Area A were top of the line.
There was another problem: the owner had the final say.
“They were probably acquired through illegal channels to begin with,” Team Leader Choi said. “If word gets out, the media will have a field day.”
*Especially now. It’d turn into a fucking shitshow.* Camera-toting hyenas were everywhere, ready to pounce at the first opening.
The Skeleton King thought for a moment. “Then what about gathering unrefined Magic Gems? If we collect everything coming out of the nearby Gates and bring it here—”
I beamed and patted his shoulder.
“Congratulations. You’ve been sentenced to life in prison for violating international law.”
“Goddamn it!”
“Welcome to the bright and cheerful twenty-first century. It’s surprisingly fucking hard to live here.”
*Crack.*
The Skeleton King ground his teeth. “Then we have no choice. We use those gems as bait, or we assemble a raid team from our strongest fighters, track Leviathan down, and kill it ourselves.”
“Wow, what a time to be alive. A monster suggesting a raid against another monster.”
“What else can we do?”
*What else, huh?*
I exchanged a covert glance with Team Leader Choi. Then, watching the Skeleton King’s temper, I spoke carefully.
“I didn’t say there was no other way.”
“What?”
“There is one.”
His face lit up. “What is it?”
“Before I tell you, you need to know something. If we form a raid team... you’re sitting this one out.”
“Leaving me out? What are you talking about?”
It must have been more unexpected than he could have imagined. I continued as he stared at me with perfectly round eyes.
“I can’t help it. Too many people are watching us right now.”
He wasn’t stupid. His face hardened as he caught my meaning.
“You’re leaving me out of the fight with Leviathan because my power might give me away?”
“You got it.”
“Have you lost your mind? How can you say that now?”
*Bang! Crunch!*
His fist came down, shattering the table. Suddenly he was right in front of me, his eyes full of anger and disappointment.
“You treacherous human. I was wrong about you. How could you say such a thing at a time like this?”
“What does it matter? You’re a monster.”
“...What?”
“Even if we catch Leviathan, once your identity is revealed, you’re finished. I’m only trying to avoid that.”
*Wood crackle.*
Bones shifted in his clenched fist. He stared at me in disbelief, then cried out as if the words were blood he had to spit up.
“I don’t care! If I can save them, I’ll do anything! Leviathan caused this disaster, and—”
“Anything?”
“Huh?”
*Got you. Hooked.*
I looked at the Skeleton King with a satisfied smile.
“You said you’d do anything. Right?”

chapters.title: Chapter 752
paragraphs: Leviathan.
The nightmare of the sea had slowly faded from memory. News of its return drew more attention worldwide than any of the other Monster Waves that day.
[Breaking News: Leviathan Appears—Disaster Descends on Japan]
[The Star of Asia, Jin Taekyung, Saves Japan Despite the Suspicions Surrounding Him; Wounded Leviathan Disappears]
[Anonymous Senior Japanese Official: “We Had a Real Chance to Kill Leviathan—If the Defense Minister Hadn’t Suddenly Shit Himself.” Complacency at Japan’s Defense Ministry?]
[Casualties Confirmed So Far Reach 100,000. The Archipelago in Crisis.]
[Japanese Defense Minister Fujiwara: “I Will Risk My Life to Protect the Imperial Subjects—No, the Citizens.” The True Feelings of an Imperialist Who Can’t Keep Up with the Times?]
[Japanese Defense Minister Fujiwara Leaves the Press Conference as Though Fleeing (Photo)]

[Japanese Prime Minister Vows: “We Will Kill That Monster Within Three Days and Show the Archipelago’s Strength.” Asked How by a Foreign Reporter, He Smiles Faintly: “We Will Succeed. That Is My Promise.”]
[Japanese Netizens Speak as One: “Please, Someone Shut the Prime Minister’s Mouth.”]
[The Young Hero from the Peninsula Who Saved the Archipelago. But Light and Shadow Surround Him.]
[Chinese Chairman Xiao Yang: “Mr. Jin Is a True Hero. Only Cowardly, Narrow-Minded Petty Men Would Insult Him.”]
[Operator of China’s Biggest Anti-Jin Taekyung Website Arrested by Public Security. The Charge? Being a Petty Man.]
[Leviathan Disappears Once Again. Terrorist Attacks and Monster Waves Continue.]
[Michael Silbert and Odin Guild Suppress a Third Monster Wave in a Single Day. Praise Pours in from Around the World, Along with Questions About Sky: “Why Hasn’t He Appeared?”]
*Tap.*
Huginn set down his tablet.
*Just as I thought. This isn’t good.*

Public opinion was slowly shifting. Japan’s Defense Ministry was taking the blame for letting Leviathan escape, and even the outlets that had rushed to attack Jin Taekyung were quietly changing their tune.
*What if Jin Taekyung actually kills Leviathan now?*
The damage their media campaign had done to his image could vanish in an instant. That would disrupt the plan they had prepared down to the last detail.
Huginn turned toward his superior. Michael Silbert, his back to him as he made coffee, spoke without looking around.
“The back of my head suddenly feels prickly. Is that just my imagination?”
“...Probably not.”
“If you have something to say, say it. Unless it’s about Jin Taekyung. Keep that to yourself.”
Normally, Huginn would have obeyed. But the battle that had ended only thirty minutes ago still had his blood up, and he couldn’t ignore how badly things seemed to be turning in Japan.
“Have you not heard the news?”
Michael gave a quiet laugh at the frustration in Huginn’s voice and lifted his coffee cup.
“Huginn, my friend. Do you think you know something I don’t?”
“Then why—”
“The coffee smells especially good today. Shall I make you a cup?”
“...Guild Master, if Jin Taekyung kills Leviathan, we’ll have trouble afterward.”
*Click.*
Michael set down his cup and leaned back against the leather sofa.

The inside of the tent, enchanted with spatial expansion, was as luxurious as a suite in a seven-star hotel. Michael seemed so relaxed that it was hard to believe he had defeated an S-rank monster only moments earlier.
“Huginn, I’ll say this once. Listen carefully.”
“Yes.”
“There’s nothing to worry about. All the conditions are in place, and Leviathan won’t be so easily killed.”
“I want Jin Taekyung and Leviathan to give it everything they have. To struggle with all their might to kill each other and stay alive. That’s all I want.”
“Of course, if Jin Taekyung dies in the process, so much the better.”
Michael winked at the bewildered Huginn and reached for the cup he had set down.
*Click. Splash.*
Coffee spilled across the table, steam rising from it.
Huginn, lost in thought, looked up in surprise.
“Are you all right?”
“Guild Master?”
“Ah.”
Michael’s face had gone rigid as stone. Now it relaxed, and his usual calm expression returned.
“I’m fine. I suppose several hard battles have left me a little tired.”
But Huginn had served at his side for too many years to take that at face value. He glanced at Michael’s trembling fingers.
“You’ve been training too hard these past few months.”
“Have I?”
“Yes. Especially since you learned about Jin Taekyung, you’ve been...”
Huginn trailed off. Michael was watching him. He lowered his head.
“I spoke out of turn.”
A heavy silence fell between them. Michael broke it.
“Is the press conference ready?”
“Yes. They’ve been waiting for an hour.”
“We’ll begin in thirty minutes. We leave as soon as it’s over, so have everything ready by then.”
“Understood, Guild Master.”
Huginn answered without hesitation. He didn’t ask why they were leaving already, or where they were going. He would find out once the preparations were complete.
Another terrorist attack. Another Monster Wave. And somewhere, more glory and fame would be waiting for them.
In this cruelly well-crafted script, Odin Guild was always a step ahead, building a reputation that would never die.
“I’ll return to escort you shortly.”
Huginn bowed and left. Alone, Michael Silbert murmured, “You’re right, Huginn. Perhaps that’s exactly what it is.”
Jin Taekyung.
From the moment Michael had first learned of him, a feeling he couldn’t explain had filled his chest. Hazy as fog, it was impatience.
And anxiety.
An old memory surfaced: himself with nothing but ambition to his name, forced to lie low and stay out of Cheon Taemin’s sight. The humiliation of those days.
But...
“In the end, I’ll be the only one who wins.”
The words slipped from his lips in a low murmur.
Feeling the mighty energy coursing through his body, Michael Silbert was certain the day of his victory was near.
*Whoooooosh.*
The wind blowing from far away was thick with the smell of salt.
Near the Philippine Sea, close to the Japanese archipelago, a whale surfaced through the rolling water and blinked its enormous eyes.
The sea was strangely quiet today, even to a creature as vast as this one. It had roamed for hours without seeing a whaling ship—or even an ordinary fishing boat.
*Pfooout.*
The whale sent a spout of water into the air and dove deep again. Hundreds of schooling fish followed it.
*Splash.*
The creatures that had fallen in together swam on without rest.
Not farther away, but deeper, following a call from somewhere in the dark depths.
*Gooooong.*
Hundreds became thousands, drawn from more and more species. Yet none of the sea creatures following that call sensed anything wrong.
Not even when a vast darkness unlike anything they had seen closed around them like a net.
*GRAAAAAH. CRUNCH!*
That was the end.
Teeth harder than steel tore the whale and sharks apart. Thousands of fish were sucked in. The monster opened its enormous jaws, chewed and swallowed everything, then savored the taste for a moment.
No. It absorbed every trace of energy and every memory they held.
*Whoooooosh.*
A dim light rose in the place known as the deep sea. But even after taking in that new energy, the monster’s eyes were full of hunger.
*That’s all?*

It hadn’t been like this when it roamed the five oceans at its master’s command. From the moment the Demon King Asmodeus descended, the whole world—land and sea alike—had been full of delectable magical power. Even the smallest fish had carried a little of it.
Now everything was different.
Its once-great master was gone. The monster that had ruled every sea in the world had been forced to hide from human eyes in the deep sea once more, gravely wounded.
*Hisssss.*
Green blood seeped from its unhealed wounds and mingled with the seawater. Leviathan’s enormous body shuddered with rage.
*How dare... How dare a mere human...*

Fear.

*Splash!*
Its enormous body surged upward, cutting through the currents of the deep sea.

The nightmare of the sea had slowly faded from memory.
News of its return drew more attention worldwide than any of the other Monster Waves that day.
[Breaking News: Leviathan Appears—Disaster Descends on Japan]
[The Star of Asia, Jin Taekyung, Saves Japan Despite the Suspicions Surrounding Him; Wounded Leviathan Disappears]
[Anonymous Senior Japanese Official: “We Had a Real Chance to Kill Leviathan—If the Defense Minister Hadn’t Suddenly Shit Himself.” Complacency at Japan’s Defense Ministry?]
[Casualties Confirmed So Far Reach 100,000.
The Archipelago in Crisis.]
[Japanese Defense Minister Fujiwara: “I Will Risk My Life to Protect the Imperial Subjects—No, the Citizens.” The True Feelings of an Imperialist Who Can’t Keep Up with the Times?]
[Japanese Defense Minister Fujiwara Leaves the Press Conference as Though Fleeing (Photo)]
[Japanese Prime Minister Vows: “We Will Kill That Monster Within Three Days and Show the Archipelago’s Strength.” Asked How by a Foreign Reporter, He Smiles Faintly: “We Will Succeed.
That Is My Promise.”]
[Japanese Netizens Speak as One: “Please, Someone Shut the Prime Minister’s Mouth.”]
[The Young Hero from the Peninsula Who Saved the Archipelago.
But Light and Shadow Surround Him.]
[Chinese Chairman Xiao Yang: “Mr.
Jin Is a True Hero.
Only Cowardly, Narrow-Minded Petty Men Would Insult Him.”]
[Operator of China’s Biggest Anti-Jin Taekyung Website Arrested by Public Security.
The Charge?
Being a Petty Man.]
[Leviathan Disappears Once Again.
Terrorist Attacks and Monster Waves Continue.]
[Michael Silbert and Odin Guild Suppress a Third Monster Wave in a Single Day.
Praise Pours in from Around the World, Along with Questions About Sky: “Why Hasn’t He Appeared?”]
*Tap.*
Huginn set down his tablet.
*Just as I thought.
This isn’t good.*
Public opinion was slowly shifting.
Japan’s Defense Ministry was taking the blame for letting Leviathan escape, and even the outlets that had rushed to attack Jin Taekyung were quietly changing their tune.
*What if Jin Taekyung actually kills Leviathan now?*
The damage their media campaign had done to his image could vanish in an instant.
That would disrupt the plan they had prepared down to the last detail.
Huginn turned toward his superior.
Michael Silbert, his back to him as he made coffee, spoke without looking around.
“The back of my head suddenly feels prickly.
Is that just my imagination?”
“...Probably not.”
“If you have something to say, say it.
Unless it’s about Jin Taekyung.
Keep that to yourself.”
Normally, Huginn would have obeyed.
But the battle that had ended only thirty minutes ago still had his blood up, and he couldn’t ignore how badly things seemed to be turning in Japan.
“Have you not heard the news?”
Michael gave a quiet laugh at the frustration in Huginn’s voice and lifted his coffee cup.
“Huginn, my friend.
Do you think you know something I don’t?”
“Then why—”
“The coffee smells especially good today.
Shall I make you a cup?”
“...Guild Master, if Jin Taekyung kills Leviathan, we’ll have trouble afterward.”
*Click.*
Michael set down his cup and leaned back against the leather sofa.
The inside of the tent, enchanted with spatial expansion, was as luxurious as a suite in a seven-star hotel.
Michael seemed so relaxed that it was hard to believe he had defeated an S-rank monster only moments earlier.
“Huginn, I’ll say this once.
Listen carefully.”
“Yes.”
“There’s nothing to worry about.
All the conditions are in place, and Leviathan won’t be so easily killed.”
“I want Jin Taekyung and Leviathan to give it everything they have.
To struggle with all their might to kill each other and stay alive.
That’s all I want.”
“Of course, if Jin Taekyung dies in the process, so much the better.”
Michael winked at the bewildered Huginn and reached for the cup he had set down.
*Click.
Splash.*
Coffee spilled across the table, steam rising from it.
Huginn, lost in thought, looked up in surprise.
“Are you all right?”
“Guild Master?”
“Ah.”
Michael’s face had gone rigid as stone.
Now it relaxed, and his usual calm expression returned.
“I’m fine.
I suppose several hard battles have left me a little tired.”
But Huginn had served at his side for too many years to take that at face value.
He glanced at Michael’s trembling fingers.
“You’ve been training too hard these past few months.”
“Have I?”
“Yes.
Especially since you learned about Jin Taekyung, you’ve been...”
Huginn trailed off.
Michael was watching him.
He lowered his head.
“I spoke out of turn.”
A heavy silence fell between them.
Michael broke it.
“Is the press conference ready?”
“Yes.
They’ve been waiting for an hour.”
“We’ll begin in thirty minutes.
We leave as soon as it’s over, so have everything ready by then.”
“Understood, Guild Master.”
Huginn answered without hesitation.
He didn’t ask why they were leaving already, or where they were going.
He would find out once the preparations were complete.
Another terrorist attack.
Another Monster Wave.
And somewhere, more glory and fame would be waiting for them.
In this cruelly well-crafted script, Odin Guild was always a step ahead, building a reputation that would never die.
“I’ll return to escort you shortly.”
Huginn bowed and left.
Alone, Michael Silbert murmured, “You’re right, Huginn.
Perhaps that’s exactly what it is.”
Jin Taekyung.
From the moment Michael had first learned of him, a feeling he couldn’t explain had filled his chest.
Hazy as fog, it was impatience.
And anxiety.
An old memory surfaced: himself with nothing but ambition to his name, forced to lie low and stay out of Cheon Taemin’s sight.
The humiliation of those days.
But...
“In the end, I’ll be the only one who wins.”
The words slipped from his lips in a low murmur.
Feeling the mighty energy coursing through his body, Michael Silbert was certain the day of his victory was near.
*Whoooooosh.*
The wind blowing from far away was thick with the smell of salt.
Near the Philippine Sea, close to the Japanese archipelago, a whale surfaced through the rolling water and blinked its enormous eyes.
The sea was strangely quiet today, even to a creature as vast as this one.
It had roamed for hours without seeing a whaling ship—or even an ordinary fishing boat.

The whale sent a spout of water into the air and dove deep again.
Hundreds of schooling fish followed it.
*Splash.*
The creatures that had fallen in together swam on without rest.

chapters.title: Chapter 753
paragraphs: The man looked around.
What wonderful weather. Only a little over twenty hours ago, the sea had been bucking like mad. Now it was calm, and gulls flew in flocks across the clear sky.
*Beautiful. Is this nature?*

The place where the man had lived was nothing like this. That distant, distant place was always dim and dark as night, with a terrible stench hanging in the air. Of course, for personal reasons, he had never smelled a stench in his life, but there was no doubt the place had reeked.
In any case, the man liked this world.
He could see beautiful scenery he had never seen before. Better yet, he was with some pretty decent people.
On second thought, he should probably exclude one of them.
No, two.
The man—the Skeleton King—remembered a conversation from a few hours earlier.
“Anything?”
“Huh?”
“You said you’d do anything, right?”
“Huh?”
“My goodness. Such a noble spirit of sacrifice. As battalion commander, I am genuinely moved.”
“Spirit of sacrifice? What are you talking about?”
“Shh. Enough. I know. I know how you feel, so stop pretending.”
*Holy shit...?*
Something felt off.
Things were taking a strange turn.
He looked desperately to the other human for help, but the one he had thought was at least somewhat sane turned out to be in on it too.
“Hey, handsome and intelligent human...”
“Please don’t speak to me. I’m too overcome to answer right now.”
“You son of a bitch...”
“I see you in a new light, Mr. King. Sacrificing yourself for the greater good...”
“I never said I’d sacrifice myself, so why do you keep saying that...?”
“We will never forget your sacrifice. You are a true hero.”
“Stop! Why are you coming closer?”
By the time he realized this was more than strange—that he was in danger—it was too late.
Jin Taekyung had blocked the door and was creeping toward him with a bundle of rope.
“I’ll talk to you carefully. I’ll try to find my courage.”
“Don’t sing some weird song! Put down the rope!”
“Starting today, I want to make you my bait.”
“What song has lyrics like that? Don’t rewrite it!”
“Team Leader Choi, why aren’t you grabbing him? Am I the only bad guy here?”
“Ah, my apologies. I was wiping away my tears.”
“Get the hell away from me!”
*Splash! Rattle!*
A wave rolled in from far away and struck the stern of the little motorboat.
The seawater splashed refreshingly across his face, jolting the Skeleton King out of his thoughts. He muttered,
“...Damn it.”
Naturally, resisting had been pointless.
The humans he had trusted had boxed him in from the front and rear, while Jin Taekyung—the root of all evil—made a solemn declaration like a judge delivering a verdict.
“Don’t make a fuss. Become bait quietly, and there won’t be a boneshed.”
“Isn’t it supposed to be bloodshed?”
“He doesn’t have any blood.”
“Oh.”
“So, what’ll it be?”
What else could he do?
The die had already been cast, and the hustlers had loaded it.
Realizing that he had fallen into the trap before Leviathan, the Skeleton King chose to avoid a boneshed and obediently boarded the little boat.
Along with the two S-rank Magic Gems the Japanese government had provided.
“Get rid of these cumbersome things. The monster will drool over me even without them.”
“No, no. Do you eat samgyeopsal without ssamjang and scallion salad?”
“...Is it already decided that Leviathan’s going to eat me?”
“Don’t worry. We’ll save you when it’s time to dip you in the ssamjang.”
“What if it swallows me in one bite?”
“Wow. That would be delicious.”
“...You are going to save me, right?”
“I suddenly feel like having some soju. Don’t you, Team Leader Choi?”
“I prefer wine, but soju definitely goes with samgyeopsal.”
“You’re definitely going to save me... right?”
That was the last thing he heard.

The little boat, carrying one S-rank monster and two S-rank Magic Gems, set off before he received an answer. Following GPS coordinates entered beforehand, it began circling near an uninhabited island several hundred kilometers away.
It had been circling for an hour now, waiting for the big one hiding somewhere in the deep sea to take the bait.
“You damn humans.”
The Skeleton King gazed up at the blue sky and felt his nonexistent heart pounding.
*What if the monster really shows up?*
He knew exactly how great the difference in strength was between him and Leviathan.
Unlike his former self, who had not even possessed reason, Leviathan had been born a predator, endowed with immense magical power from the start. They were fundamentally different.
Among the S-rank monsters known in the Demon Realm as the “Seventy-Two Legion Commanders,” Leviathan had ranked in the top ten.
Though its strength had waned since those days, the fear lodged in the Skeleton King’s heart would not go away so easily.
*Don’t come. Don’t come. Please don’t come...*
The Skeleton King liked this world.
Unlike him, already dead, nature was full of life. Cities were filled with dazzling, wondrous things, and there were human women of breathtaking beauty.
The way certain humans behaved occasionally disgusted him, but most were decent enough. He was even growing used to the word *friend*, which had seemed so strange at first.
But he had no desire to become nourishment for Leviathan.
He nearly cried at the thought of himself turned into a hearty samgyeopsal set meal.
*You damn humans, please let me live too!*
The fact that he could not even shout for fear of attracting Leviathan made him more miserable still. But it was far too late to turn back.
The Skeleton King touched the ssamjang and scallion salad hanging around his neck.
No—the two S-rank Magic Gems.
He glared at the sea.
*Right. You only die once, not twice.*
Repeating that phrase humans liked to use, he felt courage well up from somewhere inside him.
Besides, unlike humans, he really had died before. He had nothing left but bones, so perhaps he could survive being chewed a few times. Getting stuck between Leviathan’s teeth would be even better.
“Come on, you monster! I’ll take you on!”
And at the very moment the Skeleton King let out that brave shout—
*Zzzzt. Splat.*
Something fell from the sky onto his head and shoulder.
The Skeleton King rubbed the sticky, stark-white stuff with a bewildered look, then scowled.
Shit.
Warm bird shit.
“I ought to pluck every last feather off those bastards.”
Growling under his breath, the Skeleton King looked up.
As expected, a flock of gulls had been circling above him for some time. They had apparently decided that humans were free cafeterias and had been following the little boat.
More precisely, they were scattering shit and piss as they flew away toward some distant point.
“They’ve got a damn good sense for—”
The Skeleton King broke off. His pupils trembled.
His eyes widened at the sight of birds flying in from the opposite direction, blackening the sky.
*Birds? All of those?*

While he stared with his mouth hanging open, thousands—perhaps tens of thousands—of birds, so many species mixed together that even an ornithologist would have struggled to tell them apart, flew over his head, following the gulls into the distance.
No.
That wasn’t it.
They were...
*Fleeing.*
As the word flashed through his mind, the calm sea began to heave.
*Rrrrrumble!*
A vibration rose from deep beneath the sea.
And then—
*Whoooosh!*
A triangular wave surged upward as if to swallow the world, a massive shadow undulating within it.
“GRAAAAAAAH!”
A savage roar shook the Philippine Sea.
The moment the mythical monster, more than three hundred meters long, opened its jaws toward the feast laid out on the tiny boat—
“It’s been twenty-three hours, you motherfucker.”
Along with the unexpected voice of one man, a fierce flame shot forward, evaporating the moisture in its path.
*Crunch!*
There is a martial art in Murim called the Turtle Breath Technique.
Strictly speaking, it is more of a method than a martial art. It suppresses breathing and heartbeat as much as possible, and even lowers body temperature.
In other words, it is a strange way of hiding all signs of life for a while. It also requires considerable internal energy and martial prowess, so few people in Murim learn it.
If you knew anything about the strange creatures called martial artists, that was hardly surprising.
Murim was full of show-offs who shouted the names of their forms even while fighting for their lives. You expected them to play dead?

Roll on the ground in that world, and people would humiliate you by claiming you had achieved Great Completion in Narye tagon. Naturally, the people willing to learn the Turtle Breath Technique were few.
Members of the unorthodox faction.
Wandering martial artists.
And...
*Assassins.*
Unlike those first two groups, assassins were so rare you could go your whole life without seeing one.
An assassin could brush right past you without your realizing what they were. And if you *did* realize the person in front of you was an assassin, you were already pretty damn screwed.
Still, meeting one could sometimes be useful.
Especially when that assassin was known as the Slaughter Saint.
“I’m not sure what to teach you. But I can’t exactly teach the Fire King’s successor something like the Turtle Breath Technique...”
“Wow, the Turtle Breath Technique!”
“Teach me! I want to live!”
“...Aren’t you from the orthodox faction?”
“Do orthodox martial artists not die even when they get stabbed?”
“No, but you should be developing your martial arts—”
“Turtle Breath Technique! Turtle Breath Technique! Survival! Taekyung Grylls!”
“All right, just calm down. And stop spouting that strange nonsense.”
In short, I was lucky.

The living legend of the assassin world had teaching skills that could put even Daechi-dong’s top cram-school instructor to shame, and I was good at anything that involved using my body, so I absorbed his teachings like a sponge.
I had never dreamed I would use the Turtle Breath Technique in the modern world before using it in Murim. But it certainly worked.
*Crunch!*
A spear wreathed in blue-white flames was sucked into the dark monster’s maw.
No—it shattered the teeth that had already grown back and buried itself in the roof of its mouth.
“GRAAAAAAAH!”
*Crack-crack-crack!*
The monster thrashed with a roar, crushing the little motorboat like a dried stalk.
I grabbed the wide-eyed Skeleton King by the back of his neck, kicked off the boat as it began to sink, and shot upward.
*Boom!*
Fragments burst behind me and grazed my shoulder. A fierce wind whipped over me.
I stepped onto an invisible staircase and stopped in midair.
*Grrrrr.*
Ragged breathing. The pupils of Leviathan’s huge, crocodile-like eyes narrowed into long vertical slits.
“You. How could you...”
“Ah, that? It’s a long story.”
I grinned.
“And I’m not telling you.”
*Inventory open. Summon.*
Along with the thought that accompanied the words, I hurled the spear in my hand.
*Whoooooom!*

And at the very moment the Skeleton King let out that brave shout—
*Zzzzt.
Splat.*
Something fell from the sky onto his head and shoulder.
The Skeleton King rubbed the sticky, stark-white stuff with a bewildered look, then scowled.
Shit.
Warm bird shit.
“I ought to pluck every last feather off those bastards.”
Growling under his breath, the Skeleton King looked up.
As expected, a flock of gulls had been circling above him for some time.
They had apparently decided that humans were free cafeterias and had been following the little boat.
More precisely, they were scattering shit and piss as they flew away toward some distant point.
“They’ve got a damn good sense for—”
The Skeleton King broke off.
His pupils trembled.
His eyes widened at the sight of birds flying in from the opposite direction, blackening the sky.
*Birds?
All of those?*

While he stared with his mouth hanging open, thousands—perhaps tens of thousands—of birds, so many species mixed together that even an ornithologist would have struggled to tell them apart, flew over his head, following the gulls into the distance.
No.
That wasn’t it.
They were...
*Fleeing.*
As the word flashed through his mind, the calm sea began to heave.
*Rrrrrumble!*
A vibration rose from deep beneath the sea.
And then—
*Whoooosh!*
A triangular wave surged upward as if to swallow the world, a massive shadow undulating within it.
“GRAAAAAAAH!”
A savage roar shook the Philippine Sea.
The moment the mythical monster, more than three hundred meters long, opened its jaws toward the feast laid out on the tiny boat—
“It’s been twenty-three hours, you motherfucker.”
Along with the unexpected voice of one man, a fierce flame shot forward, evaporating the moisture in its path.
*Crunch!*
There is a martial art in Murim called the Turtle Breath Technique.
Strictly speaking, it is more of a method than a martial art.
It suppresses breathing and heartbeat as much as possible, and even lowers body temperature.
In other words, it is a strange way of hiding all signs of life for a while.
It also requires considerable internal energy and martial prowess, so few people in Murim learn it.
If you knew anything about the strange creatures called martial artists, that was hardly surprising.
Murim was full of show-offs who shouted the names of their forms even while fighting for their lives.
You expected them to play dead?
Roll on the ground in that world, and people would humiliate you by claiming you had achieved Great Completion in Narye tagon.
Naturally, the people willing to learn the Turtle Breath Technique were few.
Members of the unorthodox faction.
Wandering martial artists.
And...
*Assassins.*
Unlike those first two groups, assassins were so rare you could go your whole life without seeing one.
An assassin could brush right past you without your realizing what they were.
And if you *did* realize the person in front of you was an assassin, you were already pretty damn screwed.
Still, meeting one could sometimes be useful.
Especially when that assassin was known as the Slaughter Saint.
“I’m not sure what to teach you.
But I can’t exactly teach the Fire King’s successor something like the Turtle Breath Technique...”
“Wow, the Turtle Breath Technique!”
“Teach me!
I want to live!”
“...Aren’t you from the orthodox faction?”
“Do orthodox martial artists not die even when they get stabbed?”
“No, but you should be developing your martial arts—”
“Turtle Breath Technique!
Turtle Breath Technique!
Survival!
Taekyung Grylls!”
“All right, just calm down.
And stop spouting that strange nonsense.”
In short, I was lucky.

The living legend of the assassin world had teaching skills that could put even Daechi-dong’s top cram-school instructor to shame, and I was good at anything that involved using my body, so I absorbed his teachings like a sponge.
I had never dreamed I would use the Turtle Breath Technique in the modern world before using it in Murim.
But it certainly worked.
*Crunch!*
A spear wreathed in blue-white flames was sucked into the dark monster’s maw.
No—it shattered the teeth that had already grown back and buried itself in the roof of its mouth.
“GRAAAAAAAH!”
*Crack-crack-crack!*
The monster thrashed with a roar, crushing the little motorboat like a dried stalk.
I grabbed the wide-eyed Skeleton King by the back of his neck, kicked off the boat as it began to sink, and shot upward.
*Boom!*
Fragments burst behind me and grazed my shoulder.
A fierce wind whipped over me.
I stepped onto an invisible staircase and stopped in midair.
*Grrrrr.*
Ragged breathing.
The pupils of Leviathan’s huge, crocodile-like eyes narrowed into long vertical slits.
“You.
How could you...”
“Ah, that?
It’s a long story.”
I grinned.
“And I’m not telling you.”
*Inventory open.
Summon.*
Along with the thought that accompanied the words, I hurled the spear in my hand.
*Whoooooom!*

chapters.title: Chapter 754
paragraphs: *Whoooooosh!*
Intense heat scorched the air and evaporated the moisture in its path.
A single streak of flame fell like a meteor. Leviathan’s eyes widened as it twisted its body, forgetting even the pain that had come before.
*Shhk!*
Hot.
The spearhead sliced through scales that could shrug off missiles. A mere graze carved dozens of kilograms of flesh from its body.
No—it burned the flesh away.
*Hissssss!*
Leviathan screamed without a sound as searing pain swept through it.
From the day it first opened its eyes, the mythical monster had reigned as a calamity of the sea. Pain from fire was still foreign to it.
So was the human coming at it as fast as a beam of light.
*Shh-shh-shh-shhk!*
Leviathan had no idea when or how the spears had been launched.
It only heard the sharp whistle of something tearing through the air and saw five streaks of flame flying toward it. A red warning light flashed in its mind.
*Danger!*
Its massive body, rigid with pain, twisted desperately. Leviathan narrowly avoided the flame-wreathed spears and summoned its magical power.
*Ruuumble!*
A tremendous force pressed down from every direction.
Its wounds had not healed, but the quality and quantity of its magical power were far beyond what they had been a day ago.
A wave surged upward, brimming with magical power. At Leviathan’s will, it advanced without a breath of wind to drive it.
Toward the human who had dared challenge the ruler of the sea.
And toward the traitor who wore the skin of a worthless human and attacked its own kind.
*Whooooooosh!*
A vast shadow covered a radius of several hundred meters. Magical power churned inside the pitch-black wave, where not even the faintest light could penetrate.
“Damn it, I told you I don’t taste good...”
The Skeleton King muttered blankly.
At that very moment—
“Get lost.”
The low words came through clenched teeth. At the same moment, the human—Jin Taekyung—thrust out a fist wreathed in flame.
*Boom!*
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
Blue-white flames burst through the air and tore open the center of the wave.
A small human figure shot through the collapsing spray. Leviathan roared in fury.
“You bastard!”
*Whoooooosh!*
Streams of water surged up from every direction and shot toward Jin Taekyung’s entire body.
Each carried enough force to pierce an aircraft carrier. An ordinary human wouldn’t stand a chance.
If his opponent were an ordinary human.
*Shhk.*
The air vanished. The wind split apart.
Flames bloomed at the tip of a silver spearhead, unmistakably different from the ones Jin had hurled at Leviathan earlier.
*Fwoosh. Shhk!*
A blue line swept across the black sea.
The blue-white flame flowed like a dragon’s tail, burning away the jets of water that came at him like awls.
Jin Taekyung stepped on empty air again and accelerated. In the slowed world around him, he steadied his breathing.
*My body...*
It wasn’t like usual.
His hands and feet felt heavy. He wasn’t as fast as he used to be, and he was burning through internal energy much faster than he had expected.
*That damn debuff.*
**Broken Body** was taking an enormous toll in combat.

It might have been different if he had never possessed those capabilities in the first place. But with every attribute except Intelligence drastically reduced, the resulting void left his body unable to properly carry out the commands from his mind.
Just like now.
*Thud!*
The dull impact sent his body swaying. Jin swallowed his groan and evaded the attack that came immediately after.
*Boom! Boom! Boom!*
Hundreds of spheres of water rushed at him, filling his vision.
They looked like the attack spell mages called Water Ball. Jin knew better than anyone that they were far more powerful.
He also knew that if he backed off now, he might lose the monster in front of him again.
*Whoooom.*
The nearly translucent white shaft of his spear trembled. Flames that had seemed about to die surged up fiercely.
Jin Taekyung drew the divine weapon far back and slashed down at an angle.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear, second form.
Heavenly Strike.
*Fwoooooosh!*
A dazzling flash lit the darkness that had swallowed the surrounding sea.
Hellfire fell, evaporating the spheres of water on every side. Its glow stained the monster’s enormous eye red.
“How dare you! How dare a mere human...!”
With a cry that was almost a scream, Leviathan drew up all its magical power.
*Ruuuuumble.*
The sea heaved, and the dark clouds overhead groaned.
The moment the spearhead met the barrier of magical power shielding Leviathan’s body, a brilliant flash split the blackened sky.
It struck toward the human who had dared defy a myth.
*Fwoosh!*
In the slowed world, dozens of lightning bolts plunged from high above.
They emerged as dozens, but by the time they reached their destination, they had merged into one. That destructive force of nature was sucked toward a single point as though drawn there by something.
*Crackle, crackle, crackle!*
“Gyaaaaaaaah!”
Countless flashes lit the sea, accompanied by a scream of terrible pain.
Leviathan, holding the spearhead at bay with all its magical power, felt a surge of joy.
*I knew it!*
The voltage was in the billions of volts. No matter how strong the human was, he couldn’t take a direct hit from that column of lightning and remain unharmed—
*What?*
Leviathan blinked its enormous eye.
Beyond the slowly fading flash, the human who should have been standing there with his flesh burned and his bones shattered by the lightning was staring back at Leviathan completely unharmed.
He even spoke, looking a little embarrassed.
“Uh, he’s always been a scaredy-cat.”
“Hey, cut it out. That won’t kill you.”
What?
Leviathan tilted its head without realizing it. Beyond Jin Taekyung’s shoulder, someone was letting out a terrible scream. Leviathan could see him clearly.
“Gyaaaaaaaah...”
The scream gradually faded.
The Skeleton King glanced down at his smoking body, then awkwardly lowered the sword in his hand.
“Ah, right. I’m a skeleton.”
“Great timing. Good lightning-rod strategy.”
“I only drew this to help you... No, as expected, you saw through my strategy perfectly. Not bad.”
What the hell were these bastards?
For a moment, Leviathan couldn’t make sense of any of it.
That instant of distraction was enough to disrupt the flow of magical power that had been as solid as a wall with no gaps.
*Crack!*
The fissure was tiny compared to the whole barrier.
But it was exactly the opening Jin Taekyung had been desperately waiting for, and the flame dwelling in the spearhead smashed through the wavering magical power and plunged toward its target.
*Thrust!*
Scales shattered beneath the spearhead. Leviathan thrashed on instinct as its flesh and bone caught fire.
“GRAAAAAAAH!”
*Rumble! Whoooooosh!*
Its enormous body bucked wildly.
Jin Taekyung wasn’t satisfied. He grabbed the small horns jutting from the monster’s skin and drove more strength into the spear gripped in his hand.
*Shhhhuuuk!*
The spear’s two-meter shaft plunged into the center of Leviathan’s brow.
Its enormous head saved it from death, but the pain was beyond anything the mythical monster had ever suffered or imagined. It let out a terrible roar.
“You bastard!”
*Whoooooosh!*
Terrifyingly powerful Fear spread outward from Leviathan.

Marine creatures crouching in the deep sea rolled their eyes back and floated upward, while countless birds fleeing far away after sensing the danger that was about to arrive suddenly fell from the sky.
At this moment, Leviathan was angrier than it had ever been.
*I’ll kill them. I must!*
It would tear them apart until no one could recognize them. The human who had inflicted this pain and the traitor who had turned on its own kind would die the most gruesome deaths it could give them.
But amid the pain and fury that consumed Leviathan, fear raised its head.
*How?*
The enemies had not only inflicted such a massive wound upon it the day before—they had deceived its senses and lured it into a trap.
Especially the human. That tiny creature had driven a weapon into its head and wielded a power Leviathan couldn’t begin to understand.
*He’s strong. Stronger than any human I’ve ever seen.*
During the Great Cataclysm, such a thing would have been unimaginable.
Leviathan had roamed the five oceans and sent countless lives to watery graves. Even the humans considered the strongest had failed each time they tried to hunt it.
Leviathan had always been the one doing the hunting.
It had been born a ruler and lived as a predator. In the vast sea, humans had always been prey—not even enough for a mouthful.
Looking back over its long life, Leviathan could think of only one being who had ever forced it to submit.
The master to whom it had sworn loyalty.
The Demon King Asmodeus.
In that instant, Leviathan’s eyes, stained with pain and anger, opened wide.
*Could this bastard be...?*
It had heard of a human who had stood against its mighty master.
Leviathan had never met that human, but he had proved his strength by defeating countless monsters. The last had been the Demon King Asmodeus.
*Then could this human really be...?*
It had to be. There couldn’t be two humans this strong.
Leviathan’s mistaken conclusion swelled into terror. Its anger vanished, leaving only one thought.
*I have to run. As far away as possible. I have to get away from him!*
Anger? Fighting spirit?
None of that mattered. If this human had defeated the Demon King Asmodeus, whom Leviathan had served as its master, then its own fate was practically decided.
“GROOOOOOAR!”
Leviathan roared and shook its body.
It thrashed harder than ever, no longer from pain but in a struggle to survive. Yet it did nothing to dislodge the man already settled on its enormous body.
“Shut up. Shut up. Will you shut up?”
*Bam! Bam! Bam!*
Blood sprayed and flesh crumpled. Jin’s tremendous grip tore out scales as tough as they came, pulling them free like cabbages. Flames around his fists crushed flesh and bone.
*Thud. Crack!*
“Kuhk. Khk.”
The relentless pain nearly made Leviathan black out.
No human should have possessed such strength. In the end, only one way out remained.
The deep sea.
The place where Leviathan had first opened its eyes. An unknown domain deep beneath the ocean that no enemy had ever been able to invade.
If it reached that place, even this tenacious and terrifying human would be shaken off.
*Whoosh!*
Spray burst upward. Leviathan left the shallows for the open sea and dove deep.
Then it saw the human smiling and realized it had been wrong.
“Now we can finally fight together.”
What?
The question flashed through Leviathan’s mind.
And then—
*Whoooooosh!*
Deep in the dark water below, countless things gathered into one and blocked its path.
Bones.
They were bones.

chapters.title: Chapter 755
paragraphs: The Skeleton King was like a demonic sword.
A blade sharp enough to cut through anything, with killing power to match—yet one that had to remain sheathed.
A demonic sword that had to be drawn and wielded only when absolutely necessary, and only where no one was watching.
In that sense, the deep sea, swallowed by darkness on every side, was the perfect place.
*Shwoooooosh!*
A wave of bones surged and churned through the water.
The remains of sea creatures that had accumulated over hundreds, perhaps thousands, of years awoke at a single being’s call.
The moment they opened their eyes, countless bones raced toward one another, obeying commands that bound their souls like chains.
*Crack. Clatter-clatter!*
They joined, gathered, and at last took shape: a massive gateway of bones blocking the entrance to the deep sea. A sturdy shield of wraiths that would let nothing living pass.
At the center of it all stood the king who had roused the wraiths sleeping deep beneath the seabed.
—Stop.
*Fwoooooosh.*
A tremendous force swelled.
Brilliant blond hair swayed with the current. Above his bare forehead, a faint silver light appeared and took shape.
A crown.
It was the mark of one who had claimed a throne for himself, and the power shining from it was far too brilliant to be called mere magical power.
—This is a royal command.
His voice held authority; his gaze, arrogance.
As those shining golden eyes fixed on Leviathan, it realized the true identity of the traitor who had dared turn against his own kind.
*The Skeleton King...!*
The king of wraiths.
One of the lords of the seventy-two legions sworn to the Demon King Asmodeus. He had led an immortal legion that rose again and again to fight humanity, until he himself met Erasure.
But the crowned traitor blocking Leviathan’s path was not the Skeleton King it remembered.
*How?*
Where there was Erasure, there could also be birth. Someone else taking a vacant throne was only natural.
But this new king of wraiths was different. Far too different.
—How can you possess so much magical power and still side with mere humans?!
Leviathan’s cry rang with bewilderment and rage. Its enormous body, hundreds of meters across, shot forward like a beam of light.
*Kwaaaaaa!*
Violent whirlpools spun in every direction.
Leviathan rushed toward the wall of white bones without a moment’s hesitation.
No—it had no other choice.
It had to break through. If it could pass that wall and reach deeper water, it would survive.
Leviathan had first opened its eyes in the deep sea. In those pitch-black depths, where no one could intrude, it was certain it could win.
At least, that was what it believed until a quiet voice came with a fresh stab of agony.
“Where are you off to in such a hurry? We haven’t even settled the bill yet.”
*Crunch!*
—GRAAAAAAAH!
Leviathan’s massive body, which had been shooting forward like a ray of light, writhed violently.
Jin Taekyung gripped the spear shaft buried deep in the monster’s brow with one hand. With the other, he drove a sword—drawn from who knew where—into its enormous eye.
He spoke almost in a whisper.
“At one hit per person, we’d be here for three days and four nights. Let’s round it off at a thousand.”
Less than a day had passed, and the confirmed casualties already exceeded a hundred thousand.
They were strangers whose faces and names Jin did not know, but as he stared into the writhing Leviathan’s eyes, his own gaze burned with cold fury.
“We have to collect the blood debt, don’t we?”
Monsters and humans. Humans and monsters.
Their fate had been set the moment the Demon King Asmodeus first stepped onto this land more than thirty years ago.
Jin, once a boy whose father had gone away one day and never returned, remembered him clearly. He knew the pain of those this disaster had left in the same position.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
Spears, swords, axes.
It didn’t matter.
Countless weapons he had shoved deep into his Inventory whenever he had the chance flashed into his hands one after another, then plunged toward their targets in the blink of an eye.
*Thrust-thrust-thrust! Crunch!*
Scales shattered. Bone and flesh crumpled.
The precise circulation of internal energy he usually employed was nowhere to be seen, but even that was enough.
The mythical monster that had reigned as a calamity of the sea all its life writhed in agony unlike anything it had ever known.
—GRAAAAAAAH!
*Ruuuuumble!*
Magical power erupted from Leviathan, shaking the sea.
Marine creatures swept in by the waves succumbed to its overwhelming Fear. Their eyes rolled back—and then a quiet voice breathed new souls into their dead bodies.
—Rise.
The fin of a blue whale that had been slowly sinking twitched. Dozens of sturgeon, torn apart for the monster’s meal only hours earlier, bared their sawlike teeth.
—Grrrrrrr.
—Grk. Grk.
Dead, yet not dead.
The countless marine creatures that had finally become a single legion moved as one body. And at their head stood the king of wraiths who had awakened them.
—My legion!
*Craaaaaack!*
At the Skeleton King’s cry, the wall of bones collapsed.
No. It became a single enormous monster of bones and charged at Leviathan.
*Kwaaaaaa!*
Through a haze of green blood, Leviathan saw the Skeleton Legion rushing at it as one and roared.
—How dare you, you worthless things!
*Gooooong. Boom!*
Compressed seawater fired through the depths like cannonballs. Hundreds of blasts smashed countless bones apart.
But even Leviathan, calamity of the sea, could not control everything.
This vast ocean belonged entirely to it, but the countless deaths and wraiths flowing within the waves followed only the owner of the crown.
—Open your eyes.
Magical power surged around the Skeleton King. Amid the churning currents, wraiths on the verge of Erasure raised their heads.
—Raise Skeleton.
*Clatter-clatter-clatter!*
Leviathan opened wide the eye Jin Taekyung had half-crushed.
Bones scattered by the blasts gathered again. Broken pieces reassembled into new shapes and clung to Leviathan’s enormous body.
They seeped through the cracks in its strength and clung to the monster’s magical power, which still had not run dry, draining it like leeches.
*Shhhhhhh!*
*What the hell...?*
Leviathan was stunned. Even the Skeleton King of the past could not have rebuilt his legion so quickly and easily.
Where had this wealth of magical power come from? How could he command his legion to attack Leviathan, a monster plainly above them?
And there was something else.
*My magical power has no effect on him.*
Among monsters, power governed everything.

Yet this Skeleton King—the traitor newly seated on the throne of wraiths—was different. He might fear Leviathan, but its magical power did not control him. If anything, the deeper they went, the more freely he fought.
*How?*
Had Leviathan fully regained its former strength, or simply kept its composure, it might have understood.

The Skeleton King’s power was different in nature from ordinary magical power. And after defeating the Arch Lich and Behemoth, both named S-rank monsters, and absorbing so much magical power, his standing was not far below Leviathan’s.
But Leviathan had awoken from its long sleep only days ago. Now it was gravely wounded and exhausted. Everything happening around it seemed impossibly confusing.
Confusing enough to make it forget reality for one brief moment.
Then a terrible burning pain jolted it back to its senses.
*Fwoosh. Sizzle-sizzle!*
Leviathan clenched what remained of its teeth. Half were already gone.

It had fought countless humans called Hunters during the Great Cataclysm, but it had never felt pain like this. Blades wreathed in aura had barely stung, and even its worst injuries had soon healed after it absorbed another monster’s magical power and rested.
But the flames tearing through its enormous head even now, turning flesh and bone to ash, were different.
That tiny human was different.
“Fifty. Fifty-one. Fifty-two. Fifty-three...”
*Thrust-thrust-thrust!*
He was nothing like the humans Leviathan had fought before. He was on another level.

He kept muttering without pause as he drove weapons of unknown origin into various parts of Leviathan’s body and twisted them around. There was even a madness in his muttering that not even monsters could approach.
“We’re halfway there already. Come on, let’s keep it up a little longer.”
“Sir, just one more set.”
“Hold still. You’ll break a bone.”
“Of course, it’ll break even if you don’t. Go ahead and fuck around if you want to die in even more pain.”
—GRAAAAAAAAAH!
Leviathan let out a horrible cry.
It was no roar. It was a scream.
The Fear that had once made the shores beyond the five oceans tremble had become fear in the plainest sense, binding Leviathan itself.
All because of one human, impossibly small beside it.
*Die? I’m going to die? Me?*
An instinct for survival, forgotten over a lifetime as a predator, awoke.
One eye was so badly mangled that Leviathan could no longer make out its surroundings. Its body drew closer to death by the moment.
As its pain slowly dulled, Leviathan assessed its situation.
*One chance. I need one opening to shake them off and flee as far as I can.*
There was still hope.
Its tenacious vitality. The half of its magical power it had yet to spend. And its enemies were no longer as they had been when it first met them.
Especially that human who had dealt it such devastating damage with a single attack the day before.
*If he could use that power again, I’d already be dead. Something must have happened to him.*
Leviathan was a highly intelligent monster. Its assessment was shrewd, and it made its life-or-death decision at once.
—Kwoooooo!

Its massive body, hundreds of meters in diameter, writhed with all its strength and released its magical power. A tremendous force surged outward like something inflating, pushing away everything around it.
*Kwaaaaaa!*
Dozens of whirlpools formed under the tremendous water pressure.
Leviathan shook off the Skeletons draining its magical power like leeches and charged in one direction.
*Whoooooosh!*
The water flowing over its enormous body became violent whirlpools and churned wildly.
The Skeleton King missed it by a hair and shouted, his voice close to a scream.
—Human! Get out of the way!
*Too late.*
Leviathan kept that thought to itself and drove forward with all its strength—toward a cliff rooted deep in the seabed for thousands of years.
It would scrape that wretched human off.
And then—
*Ruuuuumble!*
The collision sent a tremendous shock through the sea.
I tried to get out of the way. I could have made it.
I’d just forgotten one important thing in the heat of battle.
Some of my powers had an expiration date.
*Beep.*

**System The duration of the **Water Rescue Worker** Title has ended! - The effects of the **Water Rescue Worker** Title have disappeared! - The **Water Rescue Worker’s Webbing** has disappeared! - The **Water Rescue Worker’s Gills** have disappeared! - Reactivation will be possible in **6 days 23 hours 59 seconds**!
Damn it.
Before I could even spit out that single curse, a massive boulder covered in green moss and seaweed had come up right behind me.
*Crack!*
“Guh!”
A powerful impact. Then pain squeezed my entire body.
Through the momentarily whitened field of vision, I saw Leviathan’s back as it staggered toward the surface, fleeing despite being unable to fully absorb the force of the collision.
I also saw the Skeleton King chasing after it while riding a half-dismembered shark.
*Clatter-clatter-clatter!*
Bone Binding.
A net of bones shot across the current and blocked the enormous body, but it could not restrain the monster thrashing with a desperate will to survive.
*Crunch!*
The bones shattered and scattered in every direction.
But it wasn’t over.
I fought the water pressure bearing down on me and tightened my grip on the spear shaft.
*Craaaaack.*
Cold, dark seawater crept toward my mouth and nose. That was fine.

My sharpened senses were still fixed on the target. So was the blue-white hellfire gathered along the transparent spearhead. So were my muscles, every fiber drawn taut toward the enormous monster fleeing in the distance.
*Shhhhhhh.*
Every nerve in my body came alive.
It was the same situation as yesterday. But this time would be different. I knew it with my whole body.
*There won’t be a second time.*
Trusting myself, intent on killing it, I hurled the spear with all my strength.
*Shhwaaaak!*
A single streak of flame crossed the sea. At its end came the scream I had been waiting for.
—GRAAAAAAAAAH!
The hunt was over.

chapters.title: Chapter 756
paragraphs: The desire to live isn’t granted to humans alone.
Any creature that can breathe and think will struggle until its final breath. All the more so a born predator that has never once imagined its own death.
*Shwoosh! Splurch!*
“GRAAAAAAAAAH!”
A spear shot in from behind and burrowed into Leviathan’s lava-like bulk.
Its vision flashed white. Screaming in pain, Leviathan clenched its broken teeth.
*I won’t die. This body won’t die. Never!*
It swam with all its might.

But for all the ferocity of its will to survive, its fins and tail—once swift enough to cut through the vast ocean like rays of light—barely moved. Its whole body, once brimming with strength, was growing heavier.
*Why the hell...?*
Leviathan gasped for breath. It couldn’t stop now.
It had finally managed to shake them off. The way to survival was open. All it had to do was flee as far as it could and hide.

Whether it took decades or centuries, it could have its revenge someday—so long as it survived today. Unlike humans, fated to die after barely a hundred years, Leviathan could live for something close to eternity as long as it had water and magical power.
*In the end, I'm the one who will survive. Not you bastards. This Leviathan!*
It forced up the body that kept trying to sink. Riding the waves left by the battle, carried by the current, it headed for the refuge waiting somewhere far away.
Or so it believed, until something cold and hard blocked its path.
*Boom.*
A dull impact sent a jolt back through its body.
*A reef?*
Leviathan raised its head. In its half-crushed eye, it saw a steel ship gleaming in the sunlight—and a human standing above it, looking down.
“Operation complete. We’ll capture the target now.”
The quiet voice reached Leviathan’s ears. It couldn’t tell whom the human was addressing, and it couldn’t understand the words. Their meaning was easy enough to guess.
“...Not yet. Not yet.”
Leviathan gathered every last scrap of strength. It raised the tail that had once smashed dozens of aircraft carriers apart in a single blow and lashed out at him.
Then—
*Splash.*
Water scattered feebly where its tail, once dozens of meters long, should have been.
Only then did the monster of myth understand. Its magnificent tail was gone. The streak of flame fired from behind had melted away half its body.
“Ah.”
Leviathan groaned.
Choi Minwoo, the human who had crushed its last hope, watched two figures approaching in the distance and smiled faintly.
“Thank you for your hard work.”
“Waaaaaaaaah!”
“Uhyooooo! Leviathan getto da ze!”
At Team Leader Choi’s words, the sailors of the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force aboard the aircraft carrier let out a tremendous cheer.
I had vomited up enough seawater to fill a kettle before barely managing to open my mouth.
“Tell them to keep it down. My head’s ringing.”
The Skeleton King, so drenched he looked pickled in seawater, chimed in.
“Tell them to stop making a fuss now that it’s over and just steer the ship. If they keep this up, I’ll summon the vengeful spirits of Pearl Harbor. You know what happens then, don’t you?”
Team Leader Choi nodded.
“Yes. We'd run another raid right here.”
“...Are you serious?”
“I’m joking.”
I left the wounded-looking Skeleton King behind and headed to the rear of the aircraft carrier.
The enormous monster lay bound tight in a magic-infused net, struggling to breathe.
Even with its crushed eye, it somehow recognized me and muttered like a groan. I brushed back my wet hair and waved.
“Yeah, it’s me, you son of a bitch.”
“K-kill me. I have not the slightest intention of suffering humiliation at the hands of a mere human.”
I blinked silently. Then I asked Team Leader Choi,
“Did anyone say we were keeping this thing alive?”
“Certainly not me.”
“Not me either. You?”
The Skeleton King had followed me over. He answered flatly.
“Are you insane?”
“Right? I was wondering what the hell that bullshit was about.”
I shrugged and drove White Flame, which I’d recovered on the way here, into Leviathan’s body.
*Splurch!*
A faint groan escaped it. It seemed as if death, which had drawn close once again, flickered in Leviathan's eyes.
Half its body was already gone. Tenacious as it was, there was no coming back from a wound like that.
But first, I needed an answer.
“You should’ve stayed asleep. What made you crawl all the way out here?”
“...Kill me.”
“Oh, you don’t need to worry about that.”
*Splurch! Crack.*
I slowly twisted the spearhead embedded in its torso. Leviathan convulsed as the blade ground against its bones, then answered in a rush.
“F-food! I smelled food!”
“An S-rank Magic Gem.”
I’d expected as much. Still twisting the spearhead, I asked my next question.
“Who woke you up?”
“Woke me up?”
“We wouldn’t know. You would.”
I tightened my grip on the spear shaft. Its answer came through a groan, but it didn’t change.
“Ghk. Ghk. I-I don’t know. I’d been starving for so long, and then I sensed magical power coming from the sea. That’s all.”
Was it telling the truth?
I didn’t have to think long. Everyone got honest when death was staring them in the face, and I couldn’t see the slightest trace of a lie in Leviathan. It had already lost the will to live.
*Damn it.*
I swallowed my disappointment.
It was obvious who had lured it here with an unrefined S-rank Magic Gem.
*Michael Silbert.*
The problem was proving it. Without evidence that he’d caused this disaster, no one would believe me.

That was how much standing Odin Guild—and Michael Silbert—had in the world. He was more than a hero of the Great Cataclysm. He was in a position to reach for the place only one person in human history had ever occupied.
*Normally, it would be impossible even if I died and came back to life... But things are different now.*
Cheon Taemin.

If Prometheus had given humanity fire, Cheon Taemin had defeated the Demon King Asmodeus and given humanity peace. He’d done it not in some myth embroidered with fiction, but in the real world, only a few decades ago. No one had done anything like it before or since.
Yet he, too, had become part of the past.
To people living in the present, Cheon Taemin was great but impossibly distant. They were still grateful to him, yet they resented him more than anyone.
The world now cheered for a hero who acted before everyone’s eyes, not one who had withdrawn from it.
For Michael Silbert—one of the countless people who had lived in Cheon Taemin’s shadow.
*...Damn it.*
The strength drained out of me. I pulled the spear shaft from deep inside Leviathan's body and aimed it at its neck.
The hunt was over. It was time to put this damn monster down.
“Goodbye. Try not to find peace in the next life.”
I raised the spear. Blue-white flames already burned along its transparent blade.
One Strike.
That was all it would take. With its strength completely spent, Leviathan’s body would split like tofu beneath the Force.
I didn’t hesitate.
*Whoom.*
The flames burned through the wind as the spear fell.
Leviathan stared blankly up at it. Then it spoke.
*The time has come.*
*What?*
I twisted the spearhead as the question flashed through my mind. But fatigue lay on me as heavy as the salt in the seawater, and my body reacted half a beat too late.
*Shhk! Shwaaaaaak!*
The thick neck, several meters across, was sliced in half.
Beyond the green blood surging up like a wave, my eyes met the monster's eyes, already overshadowed by irreversible death.
Its final thought sounded in my mind, not my ears.
*Magical power stirred my hunger. But it was you humans—and this world—that woke me from my deep sleep.*
*The time has come, human. Please survive. Survive to the very end. Survive until the end of this world, and see with your own eyes the day I never got to see...*
*Splash.*
The thought faded, then ended like an echo. At the same time, the enormous maw that had been trembling violently slammed into the surface of the water.
And as I stared at the light fading from its eyes, confused, a clear ringing filled my ears.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*
