sentences.text: The desire to live isn’t granted to humans alone.
Any creature that can breathe and think will struggle until its final breath.
All the more so a born predator that has never once imagined its own death.
*Shwoosh!
Splurch!*
“GRAAAAAAAAAH!”
A spear shot in from behind and burrowed into Leviathan’s lava-like bulk.
Its vision flashed white.
Screaming in pain, Leviathan clenched its broken teeth.
*I won’t die.
This body won’t die.
Never!*
It swam with all its might.
But for all the ferocity of its will to survive, its fins and tail—once swift enough to cut through the vast ocean like rays of light—barely moved.
Its whole body, once brimming with strength, was growing heavier.
*Why the hell...?*
Leviathan gasped for breath.
It couldn’t stop now.
It had finally managed to shake them off.
The way to survival was open.
All it had to do was flee as far as it could and hide.
Whether it took decades or centuries, it could have its revenge someday—so long as it survived today.
Unlike humans, fated to die after barely a hundred years, Leviathan could live for something close to eternity as long as it had water and magical power.
*In the end, I'm the one who will survive.
Not you bastards.
This Leviathan!*
It forced up the body that kept trying to sink.
Riding the waves left by the battle, carried by the current, it headed for the refuge waiting somewhere far away.
Or so it believed, until something cold and hard blocked its path.
*Boom.*
A dull impact sent a jolt back through its body.
*A reef?*
Leviathan raised its head.
In its half-crushed eye, it saw a steel ship gleaming in the sunlight—and a human standing above it, looking down.
“Operation complete.
We’ll capture the target now.”
The quiet voice reached Leviathan’s ears.
It couldn’t tell whom the human was addressing, and it couldn’t understand the words.
Their meaning was easy enough to guess.
“...Not yet.
Not yet.”
Leviathan gathered every last scrap of strength.
It raised the tail that had once smashed dozens of aircraft carriers apart in a single blow and lashed out at him.
Then—
*Splash.*
Water scattered feebly where its tail, once dozens of meters long, should have been.
Only then did the monster of myth understand.
Its magnificent tail was gone.
The streak of flame fired from behind had melted away half its body.
“Ah.”
Leviathan groaned.
Choi Minwoo, the human who had crushed its last hope, watched two figures approaching in the distance and smiled faintly.
“Thank you for your hard work.”
“Waaaaaaaaah!”
“Uhyooooo!
Leviathan getto da ze!”
At Team Leader Choi’s words, the sailors of the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force aboard the aircraft carrier let out a tremendous cheer.
I had vomited up enough seawater to fill a kettle before barely managing to open my mouth.
“Tell them to keep it down.
My head’s ringing.”
The Skeleton King, so drenched he looked pickled in seawater, chimed in.
“Tell them to stop making a fuss now that it’s over and just steer the ship.
If they keep this up, I’ll summon the vengeful spirits of Pearl Harbor.
You know what happens then, don’t you?”
Team Leader Choi nodded.
“Yes.
We'd run another raid right here.”
“...Are you serious?”
“I’m joking.”
I left the wounded-looking Skeleton King behind and headed to the rear of the aircraft carrier.
The enormous monster lay bound tight in a magic-infused net, struggling to breathe.
Even with its crushed eye, it somehow recognized me and muttered like a groan.
I brushed back my wet hair and waved.
“Yeah, it’s me, you son of a bitch.”
“K-kill me.
I have not the slightest intention of suffering humiliation at the hands of a mere human.”
I blinked silently.
Then I asked Team Leader Choi,
“Did anyone say we were keeping this thing alive?”
“Certainly not me.”
“Not me either.
You?”
The Skeleton King had followed me over.
He answered flatly.
“Are you insane?”
“Right?
I was wondering what the hell that bullshit was about.”
I shrugged and drove White Flame, which I’d recovered on the way here, into Leviathan’s body.
*Splurch!*
A faint groan escaped it.
It seemed as if death, which had drawn close once again, flickered in Leviathan's eyes.
Half its body was already gone.
Tenacious as it was, there was no coming back from a wound like that.
But first, I needed an answer.
“You should’ve stayed asleep.
What made you crawl all the way out here?”
“...Kill me.”
“Oh, you don’t need to worry about that.”
*Splurch!
Crack.*
I slowly twisted the spearhead embedded in its torso.
Leviathan convulsed as the blade ground against its bones, then answered in a rush.
“F-food!
I smelled food!”
“An S-rank Magic Gem.”
I’d expected as much.
Still twisting the spearhead, I asked my next question.
“Who woke you up?”
“Woke me up?”
“We wouldn’t know.
You would.”
I tightened my grip on the spear shaft.
Its answer came through a groan, but it didn’t change.
“Ghk.
Ghk.
I-I don’t know.
I’d been starving for so long, and then I sensed magical power coming from the sea.
That’s all.”
Was it telling the truth?
I didn’t have to think long.
Everyone got honest when death was staring them in the face, and I couldn’t see the slightest trace of a lie in Leviathan.
It had already lost the will to live.
*Damn it.*
I swallowed my disappointment.
It was obvious who had lured it here with an unrefined S-rank Magic Gem.
*Michael Silbert.*
The problem was proving it.
Without evidence that he’d caused this disaster, no one would believe me.
That was how much standing Odin Guild—and Michael Silbert—had in the world.
He was more than a hero of the Great Cataclysm.
He was in a position to reach for the place only one person in human history had ever occupied.
*Normally, it would be impossible even if I died and came back to life...
But things are different now.*
Cheon Taemin.
If Prometheus had given humanity fire, Cheon Taemin had defeated the Demon King Asmodeus and given humanity peace.
He’d done it not in some myth embroidered with fiction, but in the real world, only a few decades ago.
No one had done anything like it before or since.
Yet he, too, had become part of the past.
To people living in the present, Cheon Taemin was great but impossibly distant.
They were still grateful to him, yet they resented him more than anyone.
The world now cheered for a hero who acted before everyone’s eyes, not one who had withdrawn from it.
For Michael Silbert—one of the countless people who had lived in Cheon Taemin’s shadow.
*...Damn it.*
The strength drained out of me.
I pulled the spear shaft from deep inside Leviathan's body and aimed it at its neck.
The hunt was over.
It was time to put this damn monster down.
“Goodbye.
Try not to find peace in the next life.”
I raised the spear.
Blue-white flames already burned along its transparent blade.
One Strike.
That was all it would take.
With its strength completely spent, Leviathan’s body would split like tofu beneath the Force.
I didn’t hesitate.
*Whoom.*
The flames burned through the wind as the spear fell.
Leviathan stared blankly up at it.
Then it spoke.
*The time has come.*
*What?*
I twisted the spearhead as the question flashed through my mind.
But fatigue lay on me as heavy as the salt in the seawater, and my body reacted half a beat too late.
*Shhk!
Shwaaaaaak!*
The thick neck, several meters across, was sliced in half.
Beyond the green blood surging up like a wave, my eyes met the monster's eyes, already overshadowed by irreversible death.
Its final thought sounded in my mind, not my ears.
*Magical power stirred my hunger.
But it was you humans—and this world—that woke me from my deep sleep.*
*The time has come, human.
Please survive.
Survive to the very end.
Survive until the end of this world, and see with your own eyes the day I never got to see...*
*Splash.*
The thought faded, then ended like an echo.
At the same time, the enormous maw that had been trembling violently slammed into the surface of the water.
And as I stared at the light fading from its eyes, confused, a clear ringing filled my ears.
*Ding.
Ding.
Ding.*

chapters.title: Chapter 757
paragraphs: Twenty-eight hours.
That was all the time we spent in Japan.
If we’d answered every request for an interview or press conference, twenty-eight days wouldn’t have been enough.
At first, I hadn’t planned to stand in front of the cameras at all. Then Team Leader Choi said something that changed my mind.
“The survivors need courage and hope.”
Prime Minister Koizumi welcomed my decision with open arms. He’d been such an attention seeker since his youth that people had treated him like a madman.
When I entered the press conference hall, I was greeted by cheers and a barrage of camera flashes.
“Waaaaaaaah!”
*Pop-pop-pop-pop!*

It was strange. Less than a month had passed since all this began, yet it felt like ages since I’d last stood before reporters of my own free will. Ages since the media had looked on me favorably, too.
That didn’t mean I wanted to waste time. I still had a problem I couldn’t tell anyone about, and somewhere in the world, another fire was probably breaking out even now.
“Let’s make this quick.”
But the Japanese press made up more than half the room, and they weren’t easy to handle. In more ways than one.
“Jin-sama! Please become Japan’s shogun! You’re the only one who can save these islands!”
I answered the first reporter’s question—or rather, his shout.
“Get him out.”
The Self-Defense Forces personnel guarding the hall took him by both arms. As they dragged him away, the microphone dropped from his hand. Another Japanese reporter snatched it up.
“Leviathan was so feared by the people of Japan that we called it Susanoo. Yet Jin Taekyung-sama defeated it without much difficulty.”
*What the hell is he talking about? It was fucking hard.*
But I didn’t let it show and answered calmly.
“It wasn’t an easy fight, but I did my best while thinking of those who lost their lives to Leviathan.”
“I’d also like to offer my heartfelt condolences to their families.”
I bowed my head. Tears glimmered in many of the reporters’ eyes. The Japanese reporter wiped his eyes with his sleeve before continuing.
“Thank you for saying that.”
“I only did what had to be done.”
“I’m sorry, but may I ask one more question?”
Normally, no. The rule was one question per reporter, and I had no intention of letting this drag on. But he’d asked a good question, so I nodded.
“Go ahead.”
“Do you know Amaterasu, the sun goddess?”
“What? Which terrace?”
“I’m asking seriously. Jin Taekyung-sama, who defeated Susanoo—are you perhaps the reincarnation of Amaterasu, the sun goddess?”
“No, for fuck’s sake...”
The Self-Defense Forces waiting nearby rushed in, covered the reporter’s mouth, and snatched away his microphone.
Not that the remaining Japanese reporters asked normal questions.
“If you could name just three Japanese anime you like... Mmph!”
Patriotism was one thing, but these people were fucking nuts.
Once I realized how much time it took to restrain each reporter and drag them out, I decided to break through head-on.
“What have you generally thought of Japan?”
“An island. Next.”
“Japan has long been a nation that values peace and courtesy—”
“Wakō pirates, the Imjin War, the second Japanese invasion of Korea, the Japanese colonial period, World War II. Next.”
“Our S-rank Hunter Yamamoto Genji has expressed some personal regret. He claims the raid on Leviathan would have been far easier if you’d conducted a joint operation with him. What do you think?”
“Then he should’ve shown up on time. Next.”
“No, please wait a moment! Yamamoto-san had circumstances that prevented him from coming!”
“A reporter... talking back?”
I swept through the press conference like Zhao Zilong through an army of a hundred thousand.
Plenty of idiots asked questions that barely qualified as questions. But there were plenty of sharp ones, too—about the Skeleton King, for instance, rather than me.

They wanted to know how the raid had succeeded, what had happened to Leviathan’s corpse after it vanished in the explosion, and where the two S-rank Magic Gems supplied by the Japanese government had gone.
I might have stumbled if Team Leader Choi hadn’t seen those questions coming.
“Skel—no, Stone-King is an excellent Hunter who played a decisive role in this raid. Please understand that exhaustion prevented him from joining us today.”
“The details of the raid are classified. I can’t disclose them.”
“Unfortunately, the corpse disappeared. The S-rank Magic Gem used as bait to lure Leviathan was also lost in the process. We offer our deepest apologies for this.”
“What a loss...”
A high-level monster’s corpse was a treasure in its own right. Losing Leviathan’s was bad enough; losing the Japanese government’s S-rank Magic Gems drew sighs from the reporters.
Of course, if they found out it was all a lie, those sighs would turn to fury.
*Team Leader Choi could take up acting.*
I muttered as I watched him finish speaking without even twitching an eyebrow.
Leviathan’s corpse? The Magic Gems?
Of course we’d taken them all. They were in the safest, most discreet place I knew: my Inventory.

The sudden explosion of magical power while Leviathan’s corpse was being transferred to the aircraft carrier had been the Skeleton King’s work. I’d used the opening to stuff everything into my Inventory. The Maritime Self-Defense Force sailors had watched it all vanish before their eyes and stood there in a daze.
*I do feel a little bad...*
But what else was I supposed to do? Leviathan’s corpse was mine to begin with, and I’d just have to consider the Japanese government’s S-rank Magic Gems a long-term loan.
Even the finest sword in the world becomes nothing more than a kitchen knife in a cook’s hands. This was a time when I had to move like this, even if it meant selling my conscience.
*...Cataclysm.*
If I was going to solve that Quest—one question mark after another, weighing on my mind—I had to.
Even during the Great Cataclysm, Leviathan had been a monster of tremendous significance. Decades after the war’s end, it still was.
Disasters large and small were unfolding across the world, yet its death drew every eye to Japan. It also etched the name of a young hero whose star had begun to fade into everyone’s minds once more.
[**Grand Mage Magic Johnson: “I’m a mage, but Jin is magic itself.”**]
[**Prince Felix: “His nobility lies not in the blood flowing through his veins, but in his very being.”**]
[**S-rank Hunter Faye Chen, speaking to reporters after suppressing a Monster Wave in downtown Hong Kong: “Free Hong Kong, Great Jin.”**]
[**He has returned.**]
[**The star of Asia who never lost his light despite countless condemnations. No—the star of the world.**]
[**A life-or-death struggle at sea. Hope triumphs over calamity.**]
[**The world’s worst terrorist twisted a hero’s goodwill into evil. A public gripped by fear lost its judgment.**]

[**Head of North America’s largest media association finally speaks amid mounting criticism: “We have always reported only the facts. The claim that we targeted Jin Taekyung is nothing more than a malicious rumor.”**]
The world’s major news outlets were the first to change their stance.

Journalists who had remained neutral from the start, or had supported Jin Taekyung, paid Leviathan’s death all the respect they could. Those who had already joined forces with Odin Guild couldn’t change course so easily.
The fickle public had reversed its opinion overnight, and that was cause for caution. Michael Silbert, however, was more than a cause for caution. He was someone to fear.
But while those journalists fretted, the public was slowly waking from the media’s incitement and its fear of terrorism.
“Simon. Why are you still in the office? Weren’t you supposed to cover the anti-Jin Taekyung protest in the square today?”
“Uh, it was canceled.”
“What?”
“Most of the participants dropped out. They were expecting thirty thousand, but once the number fell below five hundred, everyone dispersed.”
“How does a protest that big fall apart so easily... Damn it. Fine. What about the organizer? The guy who acted like he was about to drop a bomb on Korea. Daniel, was it?”
“Oh, Daisuke?”
“Yeah, him. Tell him we’ll give him extensive coverage, so he needs to gather some people right away—”
The news director stopped badgering Simon and frowned.
“Wait. Who’s Daisuke? We’re talking about Daniel.”
“Yes. Daniel Daisuke. That’s the organizer’s full name.”
“...Don’t tell me.”
“I regret being the one to say it, Boss, but it’s exactly what you think.”
The reporter let out a put-upon sigh and explained everything to his superior point by point.
First, as the name Daisuke suggested, the protest organizer was of Japanese descent.
Second, Japanese and Koreans disliking one another was as natural as universal gravitation. That was why Daniel Daisuke had taken the lead in organizing the protest.
Third. Jin Taekyung had saved Japan, and Daniel Daisuke was a devoted son, and his mother was a Japanese woman from Tokyo.
“He’s the hero who saved his mother’s hometown. That’s basically what happened.”
It was a clean, no-frills explanation made entirely of facts. The news director, who had listened in silence, answered with one word.
“Fuck.”
His head throbbed. The protest’s cancellation wasn’t their fault, but would the “anonymous sponsor” who had promised a massive investment in return for a little biased coverage see it that way?
*Damn it. Management’s going to raise hell.*
As he sighed with a complicated expression, his eyes fell on the television screen playing silently in the background.
[**Breaking News: Magical-power readings surge in Berlin. Monster Wave likely.**]
[**German government issues a Class 2 disaster warning.**]
[**German Prime Minister Markus makes an emergency announcement. A formal request for assistance has been sent to Korea.**]
Another Monster Wave.
The news director shook his head, then turned to Simon, who was still watching him for a reaction.
“What are you waiting for? Why aren’t you rushing to Berlin right now?”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung. The German government has requested assistance.”
I answered Team Leader Choi without hesitation.
“I’ll go.”
The battle had left me exhausted, and the Broken Body debuff was still active. But this was what I had to do.
“I’ll get ready right away.”
And just as I rose from my seat, Team Leader Choi’s voice pierced my ears.
“At the same time... we also requested assistance from Michael Silbert.”
I slowly turned around.

Hope triumphs over calamity.**]
[**The world’s worst terrorist twisted a hero’s goodwill into evil.
A public gripped by fear lost its judgment.**]
[**Head of North America’s largest media association finally speaks amid mounting criticism: “We have always reported only the facts.
The claim that we targeted Jin Taekyung is nothing more than a malicious rumor.”**]
The world’s major news outlets were the first to change their stance.
Journalists who had remained neutral from the start, or had supported Jin Taekyung, paid Leviathan’s death all the respect they could.
Those who had already joined forces with Odin Guild couldn’t change course so easily.
The fickle public had reversed its opinion overnight, and that was cause for caution.
Michael Silbert, however, was more than a cause for caution.
He was someone to fear.
But while those journalists fretted, the public was slowly waking from the media’s incitement and its fear of terrorism.
“Simon.
Why are you still in the office?
Weren’t you supposed to cover the anti-Jin Taekyung protest in the square today?”
“Uh, it was canceled.”
“What?”
“Most of the participants dropped out.
They were expecting thirty thousand, but once the number fell below five hundred, everyone dispersed.”
“How does a protest that big fall apart so easily...
Damn it.
Fine.
What about the organizer?
The guy who acted like he was about to drop a bomb on Korea.
Daniel, was it?”
“Oh, Daisuke?”
“Yeah, him.
Tell him we’ll give him extensive coverage, so he needs to gather some people right away—”
The news director stopped badgering Simon and frowned.
“Wait.
Who’s Daisuke?
We’re talking about Daniel.”
“Yes.
Daniel Daisuke.
That’s the organizer’s full name.”
“...Don’t tell me.”
“I regret being the one to say it, Boss, but it’s exactly what you think.”
The reporter let out a put-upon sigh and explained everything to his superior point by point.
First, as the name Daisuke suggested, the protest organizer was of Japanese descent.
Second, Japanese and Koreans disliking one another was as natural as universal gravitation.
That was why Daniel Daisuke had taken the lead in organizing the protest.
Third.
Jin Taekyung had saved Japan, and Daniel Daisuke was a devoted son, and his mother was a Japanese woman from Tokyo.
“He’s the hero who saved his mother’s hometown.
That’s basically what happened.”
It was a clean, no-frills explanation made entirely of facts.
The news director, who had listened in silence, answered with one word.
“Fuck.”
His head throbbed.
The protest’s cancellation wasn’t their fault, but would the “anonymous sponsor” who had promised a massive investment in return for a little biased coverage see it that way?
*Damn it.
Management’s going to raise hell.*
As he sighed with a complicated expression, his eyes fell on the television screen playing silently in the background.
[**Breaking News: Magical-power readings surge in Berlin.
Monster Wave likely.**]
[**German government issues a Class 2 disaster warning.**]
[**German Prime Minister Markus makes an emergency announcement.
A formal request for assistance has been sent to Korea.**]
Another Monster Wave.
The news director shook his head, then turned to Simon, who was still watching him for a reaction.
“What are you waiting for?
Why aren’t you rushing to Berlin right now?”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.
The German government has requested assistance.”
I answered Team Leader Choi without hesitation.
“I’ll go.”
The battle had left me exhausted, and the Broken Body debuff was still active.
But this was what I had to do.
“I’ll get ready right away.”
And just as I rose from my seat, Team Leader Choi’s voice pierced my ears.
“At the same time... we also requested assistance from Michael Silbert.”
I slowly turned around.

chapters.title: Chapter 758
paragraphs: “At the same time... we also requested assistance from Michael Silbert.”
The name that Team Leader Choi suddenly blurted out.
Michael Silbert.
I paused, but I wasn’t particularly surprised. A drowning person would reach for any hand they could find.
The German government had sensed the disaster closing in and called for the two people most likely to save them.
Me and Michael Silbert.
“That gloomy, unpleasant human bastard?”
The Skeleton King looked uneasy.
“I’d rather not run into him.”
“No one here wants to.”
He clicked his tongue. “True, but something about him felt wrong from the moment I first saw him... Never mind. We need to get there before his lot.”
This wasn’t a sport where we competed to save the most lives, but I agreed with him on that.
*If this keeps up, no one will be able to stop him.*

The greatest beneficiary of these meticulously engineered disasters was Michael Silbert. Since the first terrorist attack, Odin Guild had suppressed more than ten Monster Waves around the world. Michael had killed S-rank monsters in most of those battles, earning acclaim for his extraordinary feats.
For a while, he had even made people forget Cheon Taemin’s name.
*I have to stop him now, while there’s still time. Somehow.*

I didn’t know what Michael Silbert ultimately wanted. But if a monster like him gained unchecked fame and power—if he became as untouchable as Cheon Taemin—I was certain a disaster worse than anything we’d seen would follow.
“Team Leader Choi.”
He understood what I meant and nodded. “The pilots are already waiting.”
Team Leader Choi, the Skeleton King, and I hurried toward the aircraft that had already been prepared, exchanging words as we went.
“What’s happening in Germany?”
“A Class 2 disaster warning has been issued, centered around Munich. According to the information provided by the German government, a Monster Wave will occur within five hours at the latest.”
“If five hours is the government’s upper limit...”
Team Leader Choi nodded. “It could happen at any moment.”
Running on wishful thinking in the face of disaster was a universal human trait. Or at least governments responsible for evacuating people had no choice but to do so.
The moment the German government officially admitted, “We’re fucked,” a major city like Munich would descend into chaos in an instant.
“Damn it.”

“Fortunately, their response so far has been excellent. Every country in the world has been on high alert since the terrorist attack on the Paris branch, and more than three thousand Hunters have gathered in Munich since the Class 2 disaster warning was issued. Our Ares Guild is one of them.”
“That’s something, at least. What about Odin? No—that man?” the Skeleton King asked.
“Of course, Hunters from the Odin Guild branch in Munich are standing by as well, but... the core forces led by Michael Silbert are currently in Africa.”
“Africa?”
“Yes. From what we’ve learned, they’re suppressing a Monster Wave in South Africa. They’ll head straight to Munich once they’re finished.”
“How nice for him. Starts trouble all over the place, then cleans it up one at a time?”
The Skeleton King sneered, but I shook my head.
“That’s not it.”
“Hm?”
“If it had been part of his calculations from the beginning, he would have left for Munich by now. So at least the incident in Munich wasn’t a terrorist attack he had a hand in.”
“Exactly,” Team Leader Choi said. “That makes it even more dangerous.”
“Why? If he didn’t intend for it to happen, wouldn’t that mean—”
The Skeleton King fell silent. His puzzled expression hardened.
“Ah.”
He’d realized it too. What this meant, and how much danger lay behind it.
*Monster Waves can happen on their own now. No terrorist attack required.*

They had still occurred after peace returned, of course. The problem was their frequency. A disaster that had once happened *very rarely* was becoming something that happened *sometimes*, perhaps even *often*.
Often enough to remind humanity of the days when corpses piled up like mountains and rivers ran with blood.
The Great Cataclysm.
Humanity had given that horrific past a name. But what would people call the new age of disaster that was about to begin—or perhaps already had?
And what was the System, which had brought me both happiness and pain, trying to tell me?
*Open Quest Window.*
*Ding.*

**System Quest Cataclysm** A new era has drawn close, and the final word of this long, fierce story has yet to be written. Hope. Or despair. At this moment, you alone hold the pen. May fortune favor you in battle. **Grade:** Main Quest **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung **Mission:** ??? **Reward:** ??? **Failure:** ???
The quest description offered no clear answer, and its mission was nothing but question marks.
More than anything, though, one short line under **Grade** weighed on my chest. Those five characters burned into my eyes.
*Main Quest.*

I’d received more quests than I could count, from easy Third Rate quests to Supreme Peak ones that put my life on the line. Their grades varied with the difficulty, and there were different types, too, like sudden quests.
But a Main Quest was a first.
More precisely, this was the first since I’d opened my eyes in the unfamiliar world of Murim. Since the day it had all begun.
*What the hell does this mean?*
I didn’t know what the mission was or what this approaching era would bring.
No. Deep down, I had an idea. I was trying hard to convince myself I was wrong.
Because I was afraid.
Just as the System had said, I was the only one holding the pen now.
The days when I could laugh over web novels full of satisfying victories were long gone. Now I had to write the story myself.
With a pen. With a spear.
With blood and death that might belong to anyone.
“...man. Human?”
A voice that had seemed far away pulled me out of my thoughts.
I blinked and looked around. Unfamiliar faces. Noise. A propeller spinning with a roar, and beyond the fighter jet’s windows, the tense faces of the pilots.
Two people were watching me with concern.
No. One person and one monster.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, are you all right?”
“Wicked human. Look closely. How many fingers am I holding up?”
The Skeleton King was slowly waving a hand in front of my face.
“I don’t see any.”
“Wrong. One. Your condition is worse than I thought—”
“I deliberately didn’t count the finger you’re waving because I’m going to pull it out soon.”
“You’re still waving it. Fold that finger while I’m asking nicely.”
As the Skeleton King quietly folded the middle finger he had been enthusiastically waving, Team Leader Choi spoke in a subdued voice.
“If something’s wrong, we can wait until you’ve rested. We don’t know what kind of S-rank monster will appear, but there are forces on-site capable of responding to it, so...”
“No. I’m fine.”
I cut him off. Mental exhaustion and the Broken Body debuff had left me far from my best, but every moment we delayed would mean more damage. That much was obvious.
My mission now is to stop the disaster. The disaster in Munich—and, beyond that, the disaster that would swallow this world.
“Let’s go. Before we lose any more time.”
I climbed aboard the fighter jet, thinking of the man at the center of it all. The enemy I would soon face again.
*Michael Silbert.*
*Come to Munich.*
The words lingered on my tongue, then faded without ever reaching him.
South Africa.

Commonly known in Korea by the abbreviation Nam-agong, this country was Africa’s most highly developed industrial nation. Because it had few Gates, it was also one of the countries that had suffered the least damage from monsters, from the Great Cataclysm until now.
At least until half a day ago.
*Rumble!*
Smoke and flames blotted out the clear sky.
Cape Town, the capital of South Africa, welcomed wealthy visitors and countless tourists from around the world. Now it was filled with screams, death, and the roars of monsters.
*Crunch! Crash!*
“Graaaah!”
“Ghk!”

A pack of Trolls took over the road, swinging their clubs at anything in reach. Their steel clubs struck with the immense strength of large monsters, cutting down people fleeing in every direction. Each fell with a final cry.
*Crack!*
“Kwoooaar!”
The leader stomped a fallen corpse’s head apart and let out a savage roar. Its followers, tasting human blood for the first time in ages, gave in to instinct.
*Craaaack!*

They seized a moving car and slammed it into the ground. Dozens rushed at buildings large and small, smashing them until they collapsed. Explosions erupted everywhere, but the Trolls’ tough skin and tremendous Regeneration kept them standing.
*Boom!*
Flames surged from another explosion. The leader smiled in satisfaction as its damaged hide healed in an instant, as though it would tolerate no wound at all.
At its broad, heavy feet lay the bodies of Hunters, their limbs twisted or their torsos split in two.
“Grrrk.”
Easy. Far too easy.
If this had happened not long ago, it would not have been able to deal with the humans who crossed through the Gate and invaded its territory so effortlessly.
“Ha. Ha. Ha!”
The world was changing. The monsters’ bodies held purer, stronger magical power than ever before, and humans could not stop them.
Everything was returning to its rightful place.
Over the past several decades, humans had gone from prey to hunters.
Now they were prey again.
“I. WILL. KILL. EVERY. LAST. ONE!!”
Years of oppression. Years of humans invading their territory and hunting them. The leader’s fury erupted in a roar.
*Whoosh! Boom!*
Its vision went black.
No—its head was gone.
The leader wasn’t alarmed. A Troll could survive losing its head. Unless its body was pulverized, its tremendous Regeneration would keep it alive—
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh! Boom-boom-boom!*
Along with the sound of air splitting, the leader’s consciousness snapped off.
For all its Regeneration and steel-hard flesh, the leader was helpless. Its body dropped to its knees before it could even wonder what had happened.
Silence followed its death.
“Kwo?”
The other Trolls looked around in confusion. A calm voice reached them.
“Let’s finish this quickly.”
*Step.*
With the footstep moving forward, a colossal force bore down on everything around them.
“My friend is waiting for me.”

chapters.title: Chapter 759
paragraphs: The command center felt hot and muggy, like a steam sauna.
It wasn’t. The oppressive heat was an illusion born of the anxiety weighing on everyone inside.
The temperature was kept perfect around the clock by Magic, yet cold sweat streamed down German Prime Minister Markus’s forehead.
“Magical power levels are surging!”
“Class 1 disaster level expected within thirty minutes!”
“The area of increased magical power is expanding!”
“Intelligence has revised the enemy estimate! At least ten thousand!”
“A report from Commander Scholz! He’s requesting authorization to use ‘Uran’ as a precaution!”
Markus bit his lip at the final report.
Uran.
The closely guarded code word meant uranium. In other words, nuclear weapons.
As a nation defeated in the Second World War, Germany was not supposed to possess nuclear weapons. But some truths could never be made public.
*He wants to use Uran?*

Commander Scholz, who was overseeing the blockade of Munich, was no fool who spoke without thinking. He was one of the few commanders with military successes to his name from the Great Cataclysm, and a man known for his cool judgment.
“Your Excellency.”
At his aide’s call, Markus squeezed his eyes shut. Then he forced out the words.
“Prepare Uran.”
“B-but...”
“It’s a precaution against the worst-case scenario. I’m giving you this order as the head of this country’s government.”
The generals and aides stared at him, wide-eyed. Then they nodded.
They knew as well as he did: against high-level monsters that might as well be demons, nuclear weapons were almost the only modern arms capable of dealing meaningful damage.
And...
*If the worst does happen, even nuclear weapons might be useless.*
A nuclear weapon was a double-edged sword.
If the enemy included a monster comparable to a high-ranking mage, it could use spatial teleportation to drop their nuclear missile over a major city.
If the attack succeeded, Munich—Germany’s third-largest city—would be wiped out. If it failed... Markus didn’t want to imagine what would follow.
“What about the citizens?”
“The evacuation is still underway. About ten percent of Munich’s population remains in the danger zone.”
“Move faster. Once this begins, there’s no turning back.”
“Yes, sir.”

The capital, Berlin, had already taken a direct hit in the earlier terrorist attack. Markus couldn’t stand by and let Munich suffer the same fate. The human and material losses from Monster Waves so far were astronomical.
*We have to stop this one.*
Even if it meant blowing the entire city away with nuclear weapons, the people had to survive.
A nation could exist because there were people living within its borders.
And to do that, they needed reinforcements. Hunters who were one-person armies, each capable of doing the work of a thousand—or ten thousand.
“What happened to them?”
No names were needed. Everyone in the command center knew whom he meant, and reports came from all sides.
“Michael Silbert is engaged in combat in Cape Town!”
“The battle is heavily in his favor! Estimated to end within thirty minutes!”
“Damn it. Why did it have to be Africa?”
Someone’s frustrated mutter had barely faded when another aide spoke up.
“Jin Taekyung is on his way to Munich. Estimated time until he reaches the site is about one hour.”
“What? A whole hour?”
“Didn’t you say we only had thirty minutes until Class 1?”
“I-I’m sorry. He’s traveling as fast as he can by fighter jet, but it’s more than eight thousand kilometers...”
“Goddamn it!”
While those around him lost all semblance of composure, Markus wiped his forehead with a handkerchief already soaked through.
“Everyone, stay calm. The estimated number of monsters has increased, but we’re not outmatched. Evacuate every remaining civilian while there’s still time, and deploy every force we have.”
Five thousand Hunters made up the main force surrounding the danger zone. With all the reserves waiting in the rear, they would have an army of ten thousand.
And at its head stood Germany’s own S-rank Hunter, Schumacher.
*Thud.*
Prime Minister Markus sprang to his feet and spoke in a resolute voice.
“We have every chance of winning. Thirty minutes. If we can hold out for just thirty minutes, we can minimize the damage and bring this to an end—”
“Emergency report from Commander Scholz!”
Along with the scream-like cry that swallowed the rest of the prime minister’s words, a massive shock swept through the command center.
“M-magical power! It’s passed the critical threshold!”
The critical threshold.
That could mean only one thing.
A Monster Wave.
At last, the solid dam—the barrier that had kept humans and monsters apart—had collapsed.
*Rumble!*
A tremendous tremor swept through Munich.
The concrete-covered ground split open. High-rises designed to withstand earthquakes toppled like dominoes.
*Crash! Boom!*
And beyond the thunderous noise, people could finally hear it. See it.
*Shhhh!*
The air split as though sliced by a sword, and the cries of countless monsters came from the opening.
—Grrrk.
*Hissss.*
Mist darker than gray, almost black, spilled out and seeped through the area.
Monsters with human arms and legs and the heads of bulls.
The Minotaurs emerged without end, breathing hard as they looked around.

This strange world was filled with noises they had never heard. Yet the magical power permeating it was sweeter than anything, and the countless humans in the distance stirred the ferocity they had been born with.
—Krrk, kaaaaa!
*Kill them. Kill the humans and conquer this world.*
Roaring as one, the Minotaurs charged toward the humans who had raised a wall of steel with their enormous shields.
Toward more blood and magical power.
*Rumble!*
As countless hooves pounded the ground, streaks shot across the sky with a heavy rush of air and plunged down upon the monsters.
*Boom! Boom! Boom!*
Missiles poured in from the German Armed Forces waiting in the rear.

Massive explosions accompanied by flames swallowed everything around them. Everything left behind in the area, where most of the citizens had already been evacuated, was reduced to ash and melted beneath the horrific firepower.
At least, that was what the humans hoped—even knowing that weapons born of science could not stop these monsters.
Kaaaaa...
The bombardment, which had seemed endless, finally ceased.
Silence settled over the city. One of the Hunters staring into the mist that still lingered muttered, “They’re coming.”
Everyone had been thinking it. A moment later, it came true.
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
A fierce tremor shook the earth. Beyond the dark mist, more horns than anyone could count flashed into view.
Then came the roar of a monster whose presence dwarfed every other Minotaur’s.
—Kraaaaaa!
The Fear of the S-rank Minotaur Lord spread in every direction.
At the head of its army, the leader swept away everything blocking the broad road and kicked off the ground with all its might.
*Boom! Whoosh!*
The ground sank beneath it like a sinkhole.
As the monster’s massive body charged forward with a tremendous roar, a figure shot toward it at the speed of a beam of light.
“How dare you!”
The fury in his voice was unmistakable.
Once a gold medalist who had represented Germany in fencing, he had become a symbol of the country itself: S-rank Hunter Joel Schumacher.
His hand moved, and his sabre followed.
*Swish!*
A silver line cut through the air. The Minotaur Lord swung its enormous halberd to meet it.
*Boom!*
A muffled blast and a shock wave shook everything around them.
It was the signal for the battle to begin. The two species, bound to a fate neither could escape, charged at each other.
“Formation!”
“Don’t fall back! Kill them all!”
—Kaaaaa!
*Rumble!*
*Swish-swish-swish! Crunch!*
Roars and screams rose from every side, with death close behind.
It was the beginning of a horrific bloodbath that could end only after they had killed and been killed by one another.
Joel Schumacher fought as if possessed.
He lost track of time. He had no idea who was dying around him, or how many.
He couldn’t afford to look. If he took his eyes off the Minotaur Lord for even a moment, its enormous halberd would smash his body to pieces.
*Whoosh! Crunch!*
The halberd’s blade passed right in front of him with a heavy roar of air, making the fine hairs on his body stand on end.
Yet his body, trained through countless repetitions and battles, moved with effortless fluidity.
*Swish! Bang!*
He stepped and thrust his sabre. Compressed air burst from its tip.
The Minotaur Lord retreated a step with agility that belied its massive size, its face twisting.
—Krrk?
Confusion and pain mingled in its cry. A hole the size of a child’s fist had opened in its shoulder.
*That worked.*
A thrill ran down Schumacher’s spine.
His movement had been so fast and natural that he hadn’t even been aware of it, as though invisible strings had guided his body.
*What was that? Have I lost too much blood?*
The fight had not been easy. Honestly, it had been grueling.
The rusty spearhead of the halberd tore away chunks of flesh with even a glancing hit. Every clash of their weapons sent enough force through him to drain his Stamina.
Strength: overwhelmingly inferior.
Speed: slightly superior.
That was the balance so far, and exhaustion and blood loss were beginning to blur his vision.
But for some reason, he felt as though he could do anything now.
As if he could bring down that terrifying monster and become the superhuman who saved this land.
*Yes. The Übermensch.*
Friedrich Nietzsche, the father of German philosophy, had spoken of the Übermensch: a superhuman who rose even in tragedy, a great overcomer who strove to realize his fullest potential.
And at this moment, Joel Schumacher was rising to a new level through martial force, not merely as an idea.
He drew on everything he had built through training and experience, from his years as the world’s greatest fencer until now. And on his will to survive.
*Swish! Swish-swish-swish!*
Streaks of light crossed the air.
Every time the sabre danced, swung with the least movement and the greatest speed, the Minotaur staggered backward, spraying blood.
*Thrust! Slash!*
He stabbed and cut.
To Schumacher’s hazy eyes, the monster’s body was riddled with openings. Every one of his heightened senses was fixed on a single target.
The Minotaur Lord.
*Now!*
*Slash! Fwoosh!*
A fountain of blood shot into the air. Schumacher blinked.
*Huh?*
Something was wrong.
The monster’s blood should have been green or blue. The blood falling over his head was red as a rose.
Like human blood.
“...Cough.”
Blood spilled between his dry lips.
The dreamlike haze vanished, and reality rushed in.
*I’ve been cut.*
He hadn’t cut the monster. He had been cut.
Fiery pain spread from his back, and Schumacher staggered.
At the last moment, while all his senses had been focused on the leader, another Minotaur had slashed his back with a rusty sword. His comrades cut off its head and caught him.
“Schumacher!”
“Damn it! Get him out of—”
*Whoosh! Crunch!*
The hands supporting him vanished. So did his comrade’s breathing.
Schumacher lost his balance and fell. Gasping, he lifted his head.
The Minotaur Lord stood over him, leader of the monsters that had come to Munich, an enormous double-bladed axe raised high.
*...Goddamn it.*
This was the end.
For Munich. For the Hunters here.
And for the Übermensch his homeland, Germany, had wanted so desperately.
Schumacher gave a hollow laugh and closed his eyes.
No—he was about to close them when a stranger’s voice reached him.
“You’re going to die like this?”
His fading mind stirred. Schumacher blinked slowly through his blurred vision and saw someone standing between him and the Minotaur Lord.
The man’s back seemed broader than the monster’s. His presence was calm, yet overwhelming.
A spear rested in his hand.
And Schumacher understood.
“Jin... Taekyung.”
Asia’s Übermensch had arrived on the battlefield.

sentences.text: The command center felt hot and muggy, like a steam sauna.
It wasn’t.
The oppressive heat was an illusion born of the anxiety weighing on everyone inside.
The temperature was kept perfect around the clock by Magic, yet cold sweat streamed down German Prime Minister Markus’s forehead.
“Magical power levels are surging!”
“Class 1 disaster level expected within thirty minutes!”
“The area of increased magical power is expanding!”
“Intelligence has revised the enemy estimate!
At least ten thousand!”
“A report from Commander Scholz!
He’s requesting authorization to use ‘Uran’ as a precaution!”
Markus bit his lip at the final report.
Uran.
The closely guarded code word meant uranium.
In other words, nuclear weapons.
As a nation defeated in the Second World War, Germany was not supposed to possess nuclear weapons.
But some truths could never be made public.
*He wants to use Uran?*
Commander Scholz, who was overseeing the blockade of Munich, was no fool who spoke without thinking.
He was one of the few commanders with military successes to his name from the Great Cataclysm, and a man known for his cool judgment.
“Your Excellency.”
At his aide’s call, Markus squeezed his eyes shut.
Then he forced out the words.
“Prepare Uran.”
“B-but...”
“It’s a precaution against the worst-case scenario.
I’m giving you this order as the head of this country’s government.”
The generals and aides stared at him, wide-eyed.
Then they nodded.
They knew as well as he did: against high-level monsters that might as well be demons, nuclear weapons were almost the only modern arms capable of dealing meaningful damage.
And...
*If the worst does happen, even nuclear weapons might be useless.*
A nuclear weapon was a double-edged sword.
If the enemy included a monster comparable to a high-ranking mage, it could use spatial teleportation to drop their nuclear missile over a major city.
If the attack succeeded, Munich—Germany’s third-largest city—would be wiped out.
If it failed...
Markus didn’t want to imagine what would follow.
“What about the citizens?”
“The evacuation is still underway.
About ten percent of Munich’s population remains in the danger zone.”
“Move faster.
Once this begins, there’s no turning back.”
“Yes, sir.”
The capital, Berlin, had already taken a direct hit in the earlier terrorist attack.
Markus couldn’t stand by and let Munich suffer the same fate.
The human and material losses from Monster Waves so far were astronomical.
*We have to stop this one.*
Even if it meant blowing the entire city away with nuclear weapons, the people had to survive.
A nation could exist because there were people living within its borders.
And to do that, they needed reinforcements.
Hunters who were one-person armies, each capable of doing the work of a thousand—or ten thousand.
“What happened to them?”
No names were needed.
Everyone in the command center knew whom he meant, and reports came from all sides.
“Michael Silbert is engaged in combat in Cape Town!”
“The battle is heavily in his favor!
Estimated to end within thirty minutes!”
“Damn it.
Why did it have to be Africa?”
Someone’s frustrated mutter had barely faded when another aide spoke up.
“Jin Taekyung is on his way to Munich.
Estimated time until he reaches the site is about one hour.”
“What?
A whole hour?”
“Didn’t you say we only had thirty minutes until Class 1?”
“I-I’m sorry.
He’s traveling as fast as he can by fighter jet, but it’s more than eight thousand kilometers...”
“Goddamn it!”
While those around him lost all semblance of composure, Markus wiped his forehead with a handkerchief already soaked through.
“Everyone, stay calm.
The estimated number of monsters has increased, but we’re not outmatched.
Evacuate every remaining civilian while there’s still time, and deploy every force we have.”
Five thousand Hunters made up the main force surrounding the danger zone.
With all the reserves waiting in the rear, they would have an army of ten thousand.
And at its head stood Germany’s own S-rank Hunter, Schumacher.
*Thud.*
Prime Minister Markus sprang to his feet and spoke in a resolute voice.
“We have every chance of winning.
Thirty minutes.
If we can hold out for just thirty minutes, we can minimize the damage and bring this to an end—”
“Emergency report from Commander Scholz!”
Along with the scream-like cry that swallowed the rest of the prime minister’s words, a massive shock swept through the command center.
“M-magical power!
It’s passed the critical threshold!”
The critical threshold.
That could mean only one thing.
A Monster Wave.
At last, the solid dam—the barrier that had kept humans and monsters apart—had collapsed.
*Rumble!*
A tremendous tremor swept through Munich.
The concrete-covered ground split open.
High-rises designed to withstand earthquakes toppled like dominoes.
*Crash!
Boom!*
And beyond the thunderous noise, people could finally hear it.
See it.
*Shhhh!*
The air split as though sliced by a sword, and the cries of countless monsters came from the opening.
—Grrrk.
*Hissss.*
Mist darker than gray, almost black, spilled out and seeped through the area.
Monsters with human arms and legs and the heads of bulls.
The Minotaurs emerged without end, breathing hard as they looked around.
This strange world was filled with noises they had never heard.
Yet the magical power permeating it was sweeter than anything, and the countless humans in the distance stirred the ferocity they had been born with.
—Krrk, kaaaaa!
*Kill them.
Kill the humans and conquer this world.*
Roaring as one, the Minotaurs charged toward the humans who had raised a wall of steel with their enormous shields.
Toward more blood and magical power.
*Rumble!*
As countless hooves pounded the ground, streaks shot across the sky with a heavy rush of air and plunged down upon the monsters.
*Boom!
Boom!
Boom!*
Missiles poured in from the German Armed Forces waiting in the rear.
Massive explosions accompanied by flames swallowed everything around them.
Everything left behind in the area, where most of the citizens had already been evacuated, was reduced to ash and melted beneath the horrific firepower.
At least, that was what the humans hoped—even knowing that weapons born of science could not stop these monsters.
Kaaaaa...

chapters.title: Chapter 760
paragraphs: “Über, what?”
He had definitely called my name before muttering something, but when I glanced back, Joel Schumacher was already collapsed against a pile of concrete with his head resting on it.
*He really gave it everything he had.*
I could see why. From what I’d seen, he’d been fighting in a Trance.
That dreamlike moment when enlightenment carried you into a greater realm.
Unfortunately, Schumacher had been ambushed before he could see it through. But when he opened his eyes again, he would probably be stronger.
“Should I wake him?”
“He couldn’t get up even if you did. Leave him be, and make sure he doesn’t die.”
“You heard him, right? Handsome hu—no, Team Leader Choi?”
“...Understood.”
That bastard had gotten so good at dumping work on other people, he was practically human now.
Still, the Skeleton King would be far more useful in the fight. Instead of giving him a hard time, I quietly sent him a Sound Transmission.
*You know what to do, right?*
*You treat this body like a child.*
*Say it back to me.*
His reply came back curt.
*There are human eyes watching, so suppress your magical power as much as possible. And when using your power is unavoidable, make absolutely certain that no one notices.*
*Good.*
*Satisfied now?*
*This is enough to make you about middle-school age, not a child.*
*...How dare you. You’re not even thirty. This body is an elder who has lived for over a hundred years.*
*Technically, haven’t you been dead for over a hundred years?*
“What!”
The Skeleton King’s indignant shout came out loud enough for everyone to hear. I laughed quietly and let my spearhead hang at an angle.
“I’ve said what I needed to. Go on.”
My voice sounded strange to me, as if it belonged to someone else. Dry as sand.
The hint of a smile that had touched my lips was already gone.
I crooked a finger at the enormous monster watching me warily.
“You. Come here.”
—Grrr...
The Minotaur Lord.
A low growl and a foul stench spilled from its maw. Its blood-red eyes were already full of caution.
—Who. Are. You.
“Me?”
At the center of a battlefield that had fallen into a lull when I appeared, I took a slow step forward.
“The Majang-dong Spearman.”
—...Strong. Hu. Man.

Most Minotaurs were cow-headed idiots who couldn’t even count, but a monster’s intelligence grew with its grade, whatever its species. S-rank monsters in particular had been granted exceptional power.
That was why the Minotaur Lord had stood rooted to the spot from the moment I appeared.
Instinct had already told it the truth.
It couldn’t beat me on its own.
“You caught on fast. You haven’t tried charging me.”
Step. Boom.
Our footsteps sounded together. The Minotaur Lord retreated exactly as far as I advanced, then suddenly roared like a wild beast.
—Kaaaaaa!
Fwoosh!
Magical power swelled around its massive body and spread to every corner of the battlefield.
At the same time, the thousands of Minotaurs that had sensed something wrong and begun to stop their attacks charged, their eyes gleaming with bloodlust.
Not at the Hunters they’d been fighting.
At us.
—Kwooooo!
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
Their cries shook the earth. Watching the countless bulls surge toward us from every direction, the Skeleton King muttered, “But we haven’t left yet...”
“That’s why you should’ve gone sooner.”
“Can I use a little of my power, then? I think we need an army.”
“If you want to announce that you’re a monster, why not start an internet broadcast? You could rake in virtual gifts with a ‘Skeleton Army Creation’ stream.”
“Damn it. Too late to ask them to let us through, I suppose?”
Team Leader Choi answered the Skeleton King’s nonsense.
“Spend less time worrying about that and more time drawing your weapon.”
Shing.
A silver blade slid free as he spoke. The **Hero’s Sword** pointed toward the monsters, its aura dazzling.
Then Team Leader Choi’s calm voice reached every ear.
“Formation. Now.”
Clack-clack-clack!
The three of us weren’t the only ones who had come to save Munich.

Around two hundred Hunters from the Ares Guild and Peace Guild had come with us. They hadn’t had much chance to contribute against Leviathan, but they were the elite of the elite. Without a hint of hesitation, they readied themselves to meet the enemy.
“Please give us our orders.”
Team Leader Choi. The Skeleton King. Even the Hunters who had barely survived the crisis in the middle of their grueling fight.
Everyone was looking at my mouth.
Waiting for my command alone.
And right now, there was only one thing I could tell them.
“Kill every last one.”
Whoooooosh.
The fire dragon coiled in my lower dantian woke and spread through every part of my body.
Taking the crowd’s thunderous roar as my signal, I kicked off the ground with all my strength.
Boom!
Wind whipped past me. Dozens of meters vanished in an instant, bringing the charging Minotaur army right up to my face.
No. They hadn’t come to me.
I’d come to them.
Whoosh.
I exhaled, held my breath, and raised the spear I’d been holding at an angle. Powerful Scorching Yang Qi turned to flame along its transparent blade.
And then... I let it loose.
*Now.*
Fire Dragon Divine Spear, first form.
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
Whoom—fwoooosh!
A line of flame swept through the air with a blast of superheated wind.
Curving smoothly like a dragon’s tail, the qi scythed across everything ahead of me. It melted horns that could pierce alloy with ease and burned through the monsters’ bones and hides.
Kaaaaaaboom!
One strike.
The wave of flame swallowed dozens of Minotaurs. Not one screamed.
They burned black without so much as a final cry. Even the ones charging behind them stopped and faltered at the sight.
—Kwooooo!
Their leader roared at their backs, urging them on. But instinctive terror drowned out its command, and they paid dearly for that brief hesitation.
Slash!
Heads and limbs rose into the air.
I plunged into their midst and went wild.
One Minotaur finally came to its senses and swung a mace. I cleaved through it and the monster holding it, then struck another across its thickly hide-covered chest with the back of my hand.
Crack!
Bone shattered. Its massive body flew backward and smashed through the formation.
The Minotaurs shoved their dead comrade aside and scrambled to their feet. Countless spells and arrows came flying over their heads.
Whish, thud-thud-thud!
Boom! Bzzzzzt!
Those struck through the head or eye by aura-coated arrows had the easier deaths. Fire made from mana burned through hides, while lightning split into dozens of streams and lit up the battlefield.
—Krrk, krrrk!
Boom! Thud.
Monsters convulsed and fell one after another. A familiar face was the first to burst through the acrid smoke left by fire and lightning.
“Aaaah! You goddamn monsters!”
Whoooosh—crack!
Leaving aside how naturally he’d taken to slaughtering his fellow monsters, where the hell had he found that?
The Skeleton King gripped an enormous halberd. With one swing, he split three or four Minotaurs in half.
He was about to swing at the next ones charging him when blue aura shot through the smoke.
Slash!
A clean movement. Not a bit of force wasted.
Team Leader Choi cut neatly through a neck and spoke.
“Charge.”
His voice was low but firm. Mana carried that one word across the battlefield, turning it into a rallying cry.
“Waaaaaah!”
“You fucking bastards!”
“Kill them all! Defend our home!”
Thud-thud-thud-thud!
Countless Hunters surged forward with a roar, their ranks rolling in like a wave.
They weren’t as tall or vast as the waves Leviathan had raised. But something stronger burned in their eyes.
The will not to surrender this land.
Grief for the comrades who had died here today, and vengeance reserved for the monsters before them.
And I was at their head.
Whoom—boom!
Compressed air burst from the end of a punch I drove forward like a beam of light.
A monster dropped like a rotten log, its head gone without a trace. I rained spear strikes on the enemies revealed behind it.
Whish-whish-whish!
Cut. Stab. Twist and crush.
Nothing could stop Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron wreathed in Force.

My spearhead sliced through sturdy weapons like tofu and split the monsters behind them. Even under the effects of a special debuff, my body had long since surpassed its limits—and those of the monsters.
As it did now.
—Kwooooo!
Whoooom!
A heavy rush of air bore down on my side along with the monster’s cry. With three Minotaurs skewered on my spear, I reached out with my free hand the instant I sensed it.
Thud.
A fist the size of a manhole cover stopped against my much smaller palm.
Ridiculously easily.
—Kwo?
The Minotaur blinked with the innocent look of the yellow ox at Scholar Kim’s house.
I gave a quiet laugh at the sight and gently guided the force of its trembling fist upward.
Whoom!
The fist struck empty air a handspan above me.
The monster had lost its target. My foot hadn’t. It shot forward like lightning and struck its chest with precisely the force and timing I wanted.
Crack!
Something broke with a sickening sound, and its body hurtled away. Far away, sweeping up every comrade in its path.
Straight toward the leader that had watched it all from behind.
And then...
Slash! Fwoooosh!
The lifeless body split in two. Through the fountain of blood, the Minotaur Lord glared at me.
Blood-red eyes. A double-bladed axe stained with its subordinate’s blood.
But I knew what lay deep in those eyes.
Wariness had turned to fear, and that fear kept driving it backward.
“Want to run?”
“Sure. I can see why you would. But...”
Whoooom! Crack!

Dozens of Minotaurs that had rushed in from every direction to protect their leader were flung away. At last, after the monsters had been reduced to gruesome heaps of blood and flesh, the path ahead lay wide open.
I shook the blood from my spearhead and slowly continued.
“You came here however the fuck you pleased. You don’t get to leave that way.”
Boom!
The belated cry was swallowed by the thunderous sound exploding from my toes.
I shot toward it like a beam of light, the distance vanishing between us. The Minotaur Lord gritted its teeth and hurled its double-bladed axe.
Whoooooosh!
Darkness rushed at me with a roar of displaced air.
No. Magical power.
Still flying low from that single push off the ground, I twisted my body.
Whoom.
A fierce wind thick with the smell of blood brushed the tip of my nose. I thrust my spear.
“Die.”
Crack!
This time, too, there was no final cry.
