*Technically, haven’t you been dead for over a hundred years?*
“What!”
The Skeleton King’s indignant shout came out loud enough for everyone to hear.
I laughed quietly and let my spearhead hang at an angle.
“I’ve said what I needed to.
Go on.”
My voice sounded strange to me, as if it belonged to someone else.
Dry as sand.
The hint of a smile that had touched my lips was already gone.
I crooked a finger at the enormous monster watching me warily.
“You.
Come here.”
—Grrr...
The Minotaur Lord.
A low growl and a foul stench spilled from its maw.
Its blood-red eyes were already full of caution.
—Who.
Are.
You.
“Me?”
At the center of a battlefield that had fallen into a lull when I appeared, I took a slow step forward.
“The Majang-dong Spearman.”
—...Strong.
Hu.
Man.
Most Minotaurs were cow-headed idiots who couldn’t even count, but a monster’s intelligence grew with its grade, whatever its species.
S-rank monsters in particular had been granted exceptional power.
That was why the Minotaur Lord had stood rooted to the spot from the moment I appeared.
Instinct had already told it the truth.
It couldn’t beat me on its own.
“You caught on fast.
You haven’t tried charging me.”
Step.
Boom.
Our footsteps sounded together.
The Minotaur Lord retreated exactly as far as I advanced, then suddenly roared like a wild beast.
—Kaaaaaa!
Fwoosh!
Magical power swelled around its massive body and spread to every corner of the battlefield.
At the same time, the thousands of Minotaurs that had sensed something wrong and begun to stop their attacks charged, their eyes gleaming with bloodlust.
Not at the Hunters they’d been fighting.
At us.
—Kwooooo!
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
Their cries shook the earth.
Watching the countless bulls surge toward us from every direction, the Skeleton King muttered, “But we haven’t left yet...”
“That’s why you should’ve gone sooner.”
“Can I use a little of my power, then?
I think we need an army.”
“If you want to announce that you’re a monster, why not start an internet broadcast?
You could rake in virtual gifts with a ‘Skeleton Army Creation’ stream.”
“Damn it.
Too late to ask them to let us through, I suppose?”
Team Leader Choi answered the Skeleton King’s nonsense.
“Spend less time worrying about that and more time drawing your weapon.”
Shing.
A silver blade slid free as he spoke.
The **Hero’s Sword** pointed toward the monsters, its aura dazzling.
Then Team Leader Choi’s calm voice reached every ear.
“Formation.
Now.”
Clack-clack-clack!
The three of us weren’t the only ones who had come to save Munich.
Around two hundred Hunters from the Ares Guild and Peace Guild had come with us.
They hadn’t had much chance to contribute against Leviathan, but they were the elite of the elite.
Without a hint of hesitation, they readied themselves to meet the enemy.
“Please give us our orders.”
Team Leader Choi.
The Skeleton King.
Even the Hunters who had barely survived the crisis in the middle of their grueling fight.
Everyone was looking at my mouth.
Waiting for my command alone.
And right now, there was only one thing I could tell them.
“Kill every last one.”
Whoooooosh.
The fire dragon coiled in my lower dantian woke and spread through every part of my body.
Taking the crowd’s thunderous roar as my signal, I kicked off the ground with all my strength.
Boom!
Wind whipped past me.
Dozens of meters vanished in an instant, bringing the charging Minotaur army right up to my face.
No.
They hadn’t come to me.
I’d come to them.
Whoosh.
I exhaled, held my breath, and raised the spear I’d been holding at an angle.
Powerful Scorching Yang Qi turned to flame along its transparent blade.
And then...
I let it loose.
*Now.*
Fire Dragon Divine Spear, first form.
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
Whoom—fwoooosh!
A line of flame swept through the air with a blast of superheated wind.
Curving smoothly like a dragon’s tail, the qi scythed across everything ahead of me.
It melted horns that could pierce alloy with ease and burned through the monsters’ bones and hides.
Kaaaaaaboom!
One strike.
The wave of flame swallowed dozens of Minotaurs.
Not one screamed.
They burned black without so much as a final cry.
Even the ones charging behind them stopped and faltered at the sight.
—Kwooooo!
Their leader roared at their backs, urging them on.
But instinctive terror drowned out its command, and they paid dearly for that brief hesitation.
Slash!
Heads and limbs rose into the air.
I plunged into their midst and went wild.
One Minotaur finally came to its senses and swung a mace.
I cleaved through it and the monster holding it, then struck another across its thickly hide-covered chest with the back of my hand.
Crack!
Bone shattered.
Its massive body flew backward and smashed through the formation.
The Minotaurs shoved their dead comrade aside and scrambled to their feet.
Countless spells and arrows came flying over their heads.
Whish, thud-thud-thud!
Boom!
Bzzzzzt!
Those struck through the head or eye by aura-coated arrows had the easier deaths.
Fire made from mana burned through hides, while lightning split into dozens of streams and lit up the battlefield.
—Krrk, krrrk!
Boom!
Thud.
Monsters convulsed and fell one after another.
A familiar face was the first to burst through the acrid smoke left by fire and lightning.
“Aaaah!
You goddamn monsters!”
Whoooosh—crack!
Leaving aside how naturally he’d taken to slaughtering his fellow monsters, where the hell had he found that?
The Skeleton King gripped an enormous halberd.
With one swing, he split three or four Minotaurs in half.
He was about to swing at the next ones charging him when blue aura shot through the smoke.
Slash!
A clean movement.
Not a bit of force wasted.
Team Leader Choi cut neatly through a neck and spoke.
“Charge.”
His voice was low but firm.
Mana carried that one word across the battlefield, turning it into a rallying cry.
“Waaaaaah!”
“You fucking bastards!”
“Kill them all!
Defend our home!”
Thud-thud-thud-thud!
Countless Hunters surged forward with a roar, their ranks rolling in like a wave.
They weren’t as tall or vast as the waves Leviathan had raised.
But something stronger burned in their eyes.
The will not to surrender this land.
Grief for the comrades who had died here today, and vengeance reserved for the monsters before them.
And I was at their head.
Whoom—boom!
Compressed air burst from the end of a punch I drove forward like a beam of light.
A monster dropped like a rotten log, its head gone without a trace.
I rained spear strikes on the enemies revealed behind it.
Whish-whish-whish!
Cut.
Stab.
Twist and crush.
Nothing could stop Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron wreathed in Force.
My spearhead sliced through sturdy weapons like tofu and split the monsters behind them.
Even under the effects of a special debuff, my body had long since surpassed its limits—and those of the monsters.
As it did now.
—Kwooooo!
Whoooom!
A heavy rush of air bore down on my side along with the monster’s cry.
With three Minotaurs skewered on my spear, I reached out with my free hand the instant I sensed it.
Thud.
A fist the size of a manhole cover stopped against my much smaller palm.
Ridiculously easily.
—Kwo?
The Minotaur blinked with the innocent look of the yellow ox at Scholar Kim’s house.
I gave a quiet laugh at the sight and gently guided the force of its trembling fist upward.
Whoom!
The fist struck empty air a handspan above me.
The monster had lost its target.
My foot hadn’t.
It shot forward like lightning and struck its chest with precisely the force and timing I wanted.
Crack!
Something broke with a sickening sound, and its body hurtled away.
Far away, sweeping up every comrade in its path.
Straight toward the leader that had watched it all from behind.
And then...
Slash!
Fwoooosh!
The lifeless body split in two.
Through the fountain of blood, the Minotaur Lord glared at me.
Blood-red eyes.
A double-bladed axe stained with its subordinate’s blood.
But I knew what lay deep in those eyes.
Wariness had turned to fear, and that fear kept driving it backward.
“Want to run?”
“Sure.
I can see why you would.
But...”
Whoooom!
Crack!
Dozens of Minotaurs that had rushed in from every direction to protect their leader were flung away.
At last, after the monsters had been reduced to gruesome heaps of blood and flesh, the path ahead lay wide open.
I shook the blood from my spearhead and slowly continued.
“You came here however the fuck you pleased.
You don’t get to leave that way.”
Boom!
The belated cry was swallowed by the thunderous sound exploding from my toes.
I shot toward it like a beam of light, the distance vanishing between us.
The Minotaur Lord gritted its teeth and hurled its double-bladed axe.
Whoooooosh!
Darkness rushed at me with a roar of displaced air.
No.
Magical power.
Still flying low from that single push off the ground, I twisted my body.
Whoom.
A fierce wind thick with the smell of blood brushed the tip of my nose.
I thrust my spear.
“Die.”
Crack!
This time, too, there was no final cry.

chapters.title: Chapter 761
paragraphs: No matter how powerful a monster was, unless it possessed regenerative abilities equal to or greater than a Troll’s, it was bound to die if its neck or heart was pierced.
Just like now.
*Whoosh!*
The Minotaur Lord jerked its neck back. Too late to avoid the spearhead driving toward it.
No—my strike was too fast and precise to let it escape.
*Crunch!*
The spearhead pierced its throat, cut through flesh and bone, and burst out the other side.
Its eyes went wide with pain. Blood and phlegm rattled in its slightly open mouth.
*Grrk. Grrrk...*
What tenacious vitality.
But it was time to put a period to it.
“Goodbye.”
*Boom!*
The flame carried by my spearhead exploded. Its tree-thick neck snapped in an instant, sending its head flying.
**System Defeated **Lv. 140 Minotaur Lord**! - Gained a large amount of **EXP** and **Fame**! Level Up!**
As the System notification rang in my ears, I slowly turned around.
The battlefield had fallen silent. Humans and monsters who had been fighting fiercely moments ago were all staring at me.
At me, standing before the monster’s crumpled corpse.
At me, who looked like hope to some and nothing short of disaster to others.
They had stopped as if by agreement. I kicked the Minotaur Lord’s head where it lay on the ground.
*Whoooosh—clang!*
The severed head soared high into the sky and landed at the center of the battlefield.
Kickoff for the second half. No, for the final period of overtime.
But the stunned players needed a word from the referee to get moving.
“What are you waiting for? Wipe them all out.”
Human and monster eyes widened at the same time, though for different reasons.
Joy for the humans.
Fear for the monsters.
And at the moment countless gazes filled with those different emotions left me and met one another—
“Waaaaaaaah!”
A roar loud enough to leave my ears ringing rose as a wave of humans certain of victory swept over the monsters.
*Shreeeek! Crunch!*
“All of you, come at me! You fucking monsters!”
Why was that bastard always out in front?
*The monster world’s Yi Wan-yong, or something.*
I shook my head at the sight of the Skeleton King hacking through monsters left and right with his halberd, then charged into their already half-broken ranks.
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh! Slash!*
Right.
The battle wasn’t over. All that remained was the slaughter.
The slaughter began around sunset and ended deep into the night.

With their leader dead, the fear-stricken Minotaur army fell apart in an instant and scattered in every direction. Somewhere along the way, I had become the field commander. I settled their fate with one simple order.
“Chase them. Turn the whole city upside down if you have to.”
After that, it was a hunt.
True to their name, the Hunters ground the already shattered Minotaur army into dust.
“You bastards!”
“This is revenge for Jonas! Kill every last one of them!”
*Whoooosh! Crunch!*
—Kaaaaaah!
A Hunter could die from a single stroke of bad luck. But how many people could accept a comrade’s death as just part of the job?
All the grief they had felt today turned to rage. Victory became another word for revenge.
“Minotaurs spotted! They’re headed toward the international airport!”
“What should we do?”
“Excuse me?”
“Your orders, please!”
That caught me off guard.
Never mind the military commander handling the rear guard—these Hunters had their own team leaders. Why ask an outsider like me? Still, the answer was simple enough.
“What are you waiting for? Instead of wasting time asking me this, go kill them.”
“Thank you! Team Three, follow me!”
“Waaaaaah!”
“Übermensch has ordered us to slaughter every last monster!”
“Follow Übermensch! Crush their flesh and bones, and drink their blood!”
“Übermensch! Übermensch!”
“Flesh and bone! Bone and flesh!”
What the fuck. That was scary.
Judging by the shouts echoing from every direction, this wasn’t Germany anymore. It was the Aztec Empire at minimum.
Granted, they were hunting invading monsters rather than people. That was a pretty big difference.
“Still, it would probably be better not to drink the blood...”
“What was that?”
“Nothing.”
Team Leader Choi gave me a strange look, wiped the blood from his face, and spoke.
“It seems most of them have been dealt with. The German Armed Forces deployed the rear guard they had held back, and I hear they’re right on the verge of annihilating the rest.”
“Quite a few escaped.”
“They’re tracking them all with drones. They won’t get away.”
I nodded and asked what mattered most.
“What about casualties?”
“About fifteen hundred reported so far. Nearly a thousand dead. The rest are seriously injured, but their lives aren’t in danger.”
Science and magic had come together in this world.

Most injuries could be treated with surgery, and with healing magic and potions added to the mix, even someone who had lost a limb could recover enough to move around without difficulty within a month.
But the number of dead weighed on me.
“A thousand...”
Far too many people had died.
I had arrived as fast as I could and fought with everything I had. I still hadn’t been able to save them.
“Mr. Jin.”
At Team Leader Choi’s quiet call, I shook my head.
“I’m fine. I know what you’re going to say.”
Objectively, today’s battle had been a decisive victory. We had crushed an army of nearly ten thousand Minotaurs, killed the S-rank monster leading them, and kept our losses to a minimum.
But a wound didn’t stop hurting just because it was smaller than it could have been.
The exhausted Hunters still chasing monsters for revenge were proof of that. We had won a great victory, and we were in pain.
*We had been for a long time. We still were.*
That was war.
A wheel of suffering with no real winners or losers, where the outcome depended on who inflicted the greater wounds.
Knowing that didn’t change my duty to fight. Or to stop the person reaching out from unseen darkness, setting that wheel spinning faster after its brief pause.
—What about him? Michael Silbert?
Team Leader Choi heard my Sound Transmission. Without so much as twitching an eyebrow, he moved his lips.
—He’s on his way to Munich now that he’s wrapped things up in South Africa, or so I heard.
—He was a step too late this time.
—This was never part of the plan.
Odin Guild was enormous. With branches all over the world, it could respond quickly—but even then, it couldn’t have accomplished what we had today.
Michael had used the Prophet as a tool to bring about this disaster.

To everyone else, it might look like the indiscriminate terror attack of a mad fanatic. But Michael Silbert, who had manipulated everything from behind the scenes, knew exactly when and where the terror would occur.
*The Monster Wave in South Africa was probably one of them.*
But there were exceptions.
I had intervened in the Munich Monster Wave, something Michael Silbert had failed to predict, and stopped the disaster before he could.
No.
And in doing so, I had gained the power to stand in his way: the public’s renewed support and trust.
“What is it?”
“Nothing.”
I looked around. A ruined city. Bodies and pools of blood in every street.
I felt sick. As though I had used the deaths of more than a thousand people to further my own ends. As though I, too, had become a monster no different from Michael Silbert or the Prophet.
But...
I had done everything I could. Call it self-justification. Call it telling myself I’d won. I didn’t care.
I had tried to save as many lives as possible and fought through gritted teeth to prevent a greater disaster.
And as a result, I had become the only—and greatest—obstacle in this world capable of standing against Michael Silbert.
*Open Quest window.*
*Ding.*
A familiar chime sounded, and a holographic window unfolded before me. The same Main Quest, unchanged since I had first seen it.
*Cataclysm.*
I repeated the word reflected in my eyes.
I had killed the Minotaur Lord, the greatest cause of this Monster Wave, and wiped out nearly ten thousand monsters. Still, the System had said nothing.
As if there was still a long way to go.
As if it would only finish the mission assigned to me after I had shattered all of Michael Silbert’s plans and brought him to complete ruin—or ended his life.
I was staring silently at the window when—
*Whooooom.*
I turned my head. Far off in the dark sky, beyond what an ordinary person could see, a faint light was approaching.
*What is that?*
A question. A guess. Then certainty.
My tangled thoughts worked through all three before reaching an answer.
Team Leader Choi noticed something was wrong a moment after I did and spoke in a subdued voice.
“He’s arrived.”
“Yes.”
*Crrk.*
My grip tightened on the spear shaft until my knuckles went white. I watched the light draw closer and muttered,
“He’s here.”
Simon, a reporter nearing his tenth year on the job, was bursting with excitement and nerves.
*This is a scoop. A scoop.*
His smartphone was full of notes and draft headlines he had been typing for hours.
An army of monsters led by the S-rank monster Minotaur Lord.
Estimated number: ten thousand. A massive force.
Central Munich. Urban battle breaks out.
The battle turns against humanity. And then Jin Taekyung finally appears.
S-rank Hunter Joel Schumacher in crisis, saved by a true transcendent being. Is Jin Taekyung Übermensch?
A great victory! A scoop! Are you seeing this, News Director? You bastard, you’re worse than a pig’s asshole. Why the fu— am I getting blamed because Daniel Daisuke got the rally canceled?
*Tap. Tap-tap.*
Simon stopped typing and deleted the last note.

The news director had shouted at him half a day ago over the cancellation of the rally against Jin Taekyung. But the man had also sent him here, and remembering that took some of the edge off his irritation.
*Yeah, all right. Upper management’s been riding him hard lately.*
Covering for your superior was also part of a subordinate’s duty. Simon nodded and entered a new note.
The meeting of two heroes.
Jin Taekyung and Michael Silbert meet again in Munich!
And just as Simon typed the final exclamation point, a powerful wind blew toward him and the countless other reporters.
*Whoooosh.*
“They’re here!”
“Is that Odin Guild?”
“Definitely! That’s the Guild Master’s private aircraft!”
Shouts broke out all around him. Simon watched in awe as the massive aircraft slowly descended toward a nearby open lot, then hurried after the reporters surging forward like a wave.
He had no idea what was about to happen there.

But the man had also sent him here, and remembering that took some of the edge off his irritation.
*Yeah, all right.
Upper management’s been riding him hard lately.*
Covering for your superior was also part of a subordinate’s duty.
Simon nodded and entered a new note.
The meeting of two heroes.
Jin Taekyung and Michael Silbert meet again in Munich!
And just as Simon typed the final exclamation point, a powerful wind blew toward him and the countless other reporters.
*Whoooosh.*
“They’re here!”
“Is that Odin Guild?”
“Definitely!
That’s the Guild Master’s private aircraft!”
Shouts broke out all around him.
Simon watched in awe as the massive aircraft slowly descended toward a nearby open lot, then hurried after the reporters surging forward like a wave.
He had no idea what was about to happen there.

chapters.title: Chapter 762
paragraphs: *Damn.*
Huginn clicked his tongue softly.
Through the windows, specially treated to keep anyone from seeing inside, he could see the ground drawing closer and an astonishing number of reporters waiting below.
*They’ve come out in force.*

Not that reporters gathering for Michael Silbert was unusual. His name attracted them even in ordinary times. Since the terrorist attacks began, the mere sight of the Guild Master’s private aircraft was enough to send them rushing over.
But Huginn couldn’t remember seeing a crowd this large in years.
*The problem is, those cameras aren’t pointed at us.*
The media wielded tremendous power. The easily swayed public treated cameras as its eyes and speakers as its ears.
And if every spotlight here fell on Jin Taekyung?
*Troublesome. Very troublesome.*
Huginn took his smartphone from his pocket.
“Leave them be.”
A voice suddenly slipped into his ear, and Huginn’s heart lurched.
*How?*
He knew the voice. He had served its owner for years. What startled him was that he hadn’t sensed Michael Silbert’s presence at all—not even the faintest trace of it.
And Huginn was an exceptionally skilled S-rank Hunter himself.
“...You’ve arrived, sir.”
Michael caught the agitation Huginn couldn’t quite suppress.
“Was I that unexpected?”
Huginn considered his answer. “No.”
“You looked surprised.”
“For a moment, I was. Not anymore.”
“Why is that?”
“Because you’re the Guild Master.”
“You really are a born flatterer.”
“I mean it. I’d stake my life on it.”
“Don’t go staking such a precious life so easily.”
“It’s all right. I gave it to you long ago.”
Michael let out a quiet laugh at the ready answer and looked out the window.
“It’s rather noisy outside.”
“I was just about to have them sent away.”
“I thought you might. Knowing you.”
Then he added, “Leave them be.”
Huginn ran his fingers over the smartphone in his hand. A single phone call would be enough to send all the reporters gathered outside away.
Even if they used force, not a line about it would appear in the papers. That was Odin Guild. That was the world they lived in.
But his superior’s wishes mattered more to Huginn than anything else. Even so, he couldn’t understand this order.
“May I ask why?”
“Why?”
“Why you came all the way to Munich when there’s nothing to gain here. Why you intend to meet Jin Taekyung in front of all those reporters.”

The question had been with Huginn since they left South Africa. They hadn’t foreseen the Munich Monster Wave, and by the time their aircraft took off, Jin Taekyung was already several steps ahead of them, bringing the whole crisis to an end.
In short, today’s stage belonged to Jin Taekyung.

“Public opinion toward him has taken a sharp turn. The demonstrations against him that broke out around the world after the Leviathan incident have been disbanding one after another. Even the media outlets working with us are being cautious now.”
“So?”
“Today, at least, he’s drawing more attention than you are, Guild Master. Must you meet him here and draw even more eyes?”
“You make it sound as though I’d be nothing but part of his supporting cast. A spotlight to make him shine brighter.”
“...I’m sorry, but yes.”
Huginn lowered his head. He had spoken out of loyalty, but he couldn’t bring himself to face the anger he expected.
*But this is reality.*
The tide had already turned.

Michael’s Odin Guild had built an impressive record during the terrorist crisis by suppressing more than ten Monster Waves. Yet Jin Taekyung had restored his steadily declining reputation in only two battles.

Leviathan’s infamy from the Great Cataclysm, when it had all but ruled the seas, had played a part. So had Jin’s overwhelming victory over the Munich Monster Wave, whose scale had surpassed all expectations. But Huginn believed there was a deeper reason public opinion had changed so quickly.
*Jin Taekyung.*
People who already had plenty tended to inspire envy and resentment before admiration. Jin Taekyung, though, was familiar to them. A hero who gave everything he had.

He had grown up in a family that struggled to make ends meet. From the moment he Awakened, he had supported them, going from Gate to Gate without a day off. As recently as a year ago, he’d lived on ramen in a shabby goshiwon room of barely five pyeong.

Young, poor, and among the lowest-ranked Hunters, he had been someone people could find anywhere in the world. Even after he gained tremendous wealth and Fame, the Jin Taekyung from those days remained etched in their hearts.

When he stormed a massive Guild alone in pursuit of revenge. When he stained a desert red with blood to achieve his goal. Even when he broke countless laws and procedures along the way, he faced no more than condemnation.
Huginn was certain that was why.
*The world... the public loves Jin Taekyung.*
The media offensive hadn’t shaken his core supporters. Those who had condemned him out of fear of terrorism crumbled like sandcastles after just one or two displays of what he could do.
*Of course. It’s Jin Taekyung, after all.*
They accepted him again—and blamed themselves for ever wavering.
*It’s a kind of pardon. An invisible pardon the public has given him.*
No one but Cheon Taemin had ever possessed it. Michael had worked so hard to obtain it. Jin Taekyung already had it.
*Which is exactly why we can’t make him stand out any more than he does.*
A slight vibration ran through the aircraft, and the pilot’s voice came over the speakers.
“Landing successful. The door will open shortly. Please let me know when you’re ready.”
“Not yet. Keep the door closed and wait—”
“Open it.”
Huginn jerked his head up. Michael saw his bewilderment and gave a hearty laugh.
“Huginn, my cautious friend.”
“Guild Master!”
“Don’t worry. I have no intention of becoming anyone’s spotlight.”
“What do you—”
“I’m opening the door. Please stand clear of the entrance.”
*Psssh.*
Huginn’s unfinished voice was swallowed by the noise that erupted the instant the door opened, like a dam collapsing.
*Click, click-click-click!*
“Michael! Michael! Please look this way!”
“TBC Broadcasting! Could we have a word?”
“I understand this is your second meeting. What kind of relationship do you normally have with Mr. Jin?”
“Nearly every crisis has been resolved. Why come to Munich now?”
“What do you think of Mr. Jin’s performance?”
“According to the German government, the Munich Monster Wave was nearly ten times the size of the one in Cape Town! Don’t you think it took far too long to suppress?”
Flashes fired without pause. Reporters shouted questions over one another, and Huginn’s face hardened.
Most of the questions being thrown at them revolved around Jin Taekyung. One audacious reporter had even gone so far as to compare them.
“...Whatever you have in mind, Guild Master, it would be best to postpone the interview.”
Michael calmly shook his head and strode toward the exit.
With a single remark that seemed to have nothing to do with the current situation.
“I watched the video you obtained in Japan. Very interesting.”
“Pardon?”
“Come along. We can’t keep him waiting any longer.”
*Step.*
Michael descended the aircraft stairs without hesitation and stood before the cameras and flashing lights.
Beyond the reporters clamoring for a scoop, and the German Armed Forces soldiers holding them back, he spotted someone approaching. He broke into a broad smile.
“At last, the young hero has arrived.”
*Flash!*
The night was illuminated by the most dazzling burst of flashes yet.
Reporters gasped and hurriedly parted. The two heroes walked slowly through the opening until they stood face-to-face.
“We meet again, Jin.”
*Slide.*
Michael greeted him warmly and held out a hand. Jin Taekyung stared in silence at his smiling enemy, then took it.
His voice was low and hoarse, almost as though it were boiling.
“...Michael Silbert.”
*Crack.*
Their tightly clasped hands went white.
Everyone lives behind a mask.
To get along with others. To earn a living. Or to avoid a fight they don’t want.
But Michael Silbert’s mask was harder and thicker than any I’d ever encountered. I couldn’t begin to guess what lay behind it.
*Crack.*
The bones in our clasped hands shifted with a grinding sound. Feeling the force transmitted through his grip, I widened my eyes.
*What the hell...?*
The force was unbelievable. With everyone watching, I wasn’t using my full strength either. But his grip was far stronger than I’d expected, and I couldn’t hide my surprise.
*How?*
The physical abilities I’d developed through the System were, quite literally, superhuman.
That was why neither a Supreme Peak master nor an S-rank Hunter could approach me in pure physical ability.
That was what I’d thought until I took his hand.
—That seems like enough of a greeting, don’t you think?
—We’re in front of the cameras. We should both be a little more careful.
I came to my senses and looked around. We’d been holding hands for nearly half a minute, and a few reporters were watching us with suspicion.
“Ah.”
“My friend here must be glad to see me. I feel the same way.”
*Pat, pat.*
Michael smiled and gave my shoulder a friendly tap. A few reporters smiled too.
But he and I were having a conversation their cameras and microphones couldn’t capture.
—What the fuck are you playing at?
—Who can say? I do not understand what you mean. Is coming to congratulate a young junior on his victory some kind of trick?
—A passing dog would laugh at that, you son of a bitch.
—You really won’t believe me.
—Sorry, but I’m not that much of an idiot. You’re already a step too late.
Michael let out a quiet laugh and moved his lips.
—Actually, you’re right. I came to make a very important announcement.
—An important announcement?
—One that will turn the whole world upside down.
—...What?
What the hell was he talking about?
I stared at him, stunned. Then Michael’s smile vanished. He looked straight into the cameras.
And he dropped a bombshell no one there had seen coming.

chapters.title: Chapter 763
paragraphs: A thought is only a thought until it becomes reality. But the moment it forms a complete sentence and flows out as a voice, it gains influence.
Just like now.
“I have witnessed countless deaths.”
A sorrowful voice rang out. Standing tall before countless cameras and microphones, Michael Silbert slowly continued.

“In the slums of Paris, teeming with flies and gangs. On the countless battlefields of the Great Cataclysm. And ever since the day of victory when the Demon King Asmodeus fell. I have continued to witness them.”
*Bzzzz.*
The faint hum of the cameras sounded unusually loud.
No one so much as swallowed. The reporters watched Michael with an anticipation they couldn’t quite explain.
*This is...*
*Something’s coming!*

At first, they’d wondered why he had suddenly started spouting nonsense. All they’d wanted was a friendly shot of the two heroes—one old enough to be the other’s father—with their arms around each other’s shoulders, and perhaps a few warm words.
Jin Taekyung was supposed to be the star today. Michael was merely the spotlight that would make him shine all the brighter.
Until he opened his mouth.
“Yet through all those deaths, I held on to one hope. One dream. With the Demon King Asmodeus and his monster army gone, I believed that someday every conflict would end and true peace would come.”
His tone rose and fell distinctly, and his expression was filled with appeal.
Michael Silbert’s appearance, compelling everyone who saw and heard him to focus, was reflected in the camera lenses.
Around the world, people watching live leaned closer to their living-room televisions, their computer monitors, the smartphones in their hands.
“Mom. Dad. I need to watch my cartoon...”
“Shh, Peter. Be quiet for a moment.”
└ What the fuck is No Jaehun doing? I called for a gank, and the bastard went AFK. └ What’s up with Jaehun? Fight with his girlfriend? Are we surrendering this match?
“It’s not that. I was watching an iTube live stream. Never mind—I’ll put the link in the group chat. Take a look.”
└ What girlfriend? That bastard doesn’t have one. It’s just not his promotion match, so he doesn’t give a shi—Munich live? What’s this?
Dozens of television channels and streaming sites carrying the broadcast lit up with activity. Their audiences multiplied, and the viewers watched with bated breath.
On-screen, Jin Taekyung stood grim-faced while Michael spoke one step ahead of him. Michael’s voice carried to them all.
“I have waited a long time. I have hesitated. But I stand here today to tell you one thing—for our faith in peace, and for a better future.”
Michael drew a breath. So did everyone watching him.
Then his voice emerged, dry as sand.
“A second war is nearly upon us.”
Invisible agitation and shock waves swept through every direction.

An office worker flipping through channels after work. A couple passing beneath a huge billboard. A teenager who had paused his game and opened the stream to kill time. The reporters standing right in front of Michael.
At that moment, they doubted their own eyes and ears before falling into extreme confusion.
A second war.
Everyone knew what those few words meant. Someone gave voice to it in something like a groan.
“The Great Cataclysm...?”

How could they not know? It was humanity’s clearest nightmare, a memory seared into them by fear: the worst Great War in history, which had covered the Five Oceans and Six Continents in blood and corpses.
And now Michael Silbert was saying that very Great Cataclysm would begin again. He was declaring that a second war had arrived.
Before them. No, before the entire world.
*That’s... impossible.*
*It can’t happen. It can’t.*
Yet no one could bring themselves to say it. Denial had come with another, paralyzing thought.
*What if he’s telling the truth?*
A second Great Cataclysm could not happen. It must not happen.
But people had sensed something wrong. Deep down, they had been feeling their way around the shape of that fear.
The signs were already there.

Magical power levels rose by the day. Strange phenomena grew more frequent. Only a few months ago, an Arch Lich had appeared in Sichuan Province, China, and Monster Waves triggered with Magic Gems had followed one another across the world.
Scholars had studied that method of terrorism long ago. The leading experts in magical power had agreed it was impossible—unless the world’s magical power reached a certain limit.
Today, Michael Silbert was telling them it had.
“Perhaps calling it a *second* war is wrong. But one thing is certain: what you and I believed was the end of the war was only a ceasefire.”
“I tell you now: the magical power throughout our world has already passed its critical threshold. A disaster like the one we faced before will engulf the entire world.”
People could barely breathe.

This wasn’t some drunk rambling in a neighborhood bar. It was a declaration from Michael Silbert—a hero of the Great Cataclysm who had remained at the forefront ever since, a giant who led the world’s greatest Guild.
One of the stunned reporters managed to ask, his voice shaking, “D-Does that mean the Demon King... Does it mean Asmodeus is coming back?”

“On the Day of Victory, during the final battle that decided humanity’s fate, the Demon King was undoubtedly erased without leaving so much as a trace. I saw it clearly with my own eyes, so that is an indisputable fact. However...”
Michael Silbert hesitated for a moment before adding, “Now, no one can be certain. No one can be certain what will happen in the future, or even whether the Demon King Asmodeus was truly erased.”
“Ah... Ahh.”
“How can this be...?”
Cameras shook. The reporters’ dismayed voices came through the microphones and went out to the world.

No one watching from elsewhere complained about the disruption. They were no calmer than the people on-site. The terror they had refused to face had finally taken shape, and they trembled at the truth they had tried to ignore.
An unpredictable future. No—a disaster.
And the possibility that the Demon King Asmodeus might return.

Fear spread through their minds like dark clouds. Whether they watched Michael Silbert on a screen or stood before him, their eyes shook. They wanted him to take it all back. They even entertained the absurd hope that he might laugh and say it had been a joke.
His next words crushed it.
“Peace—or what we thought was peace—is over.”
Michael looked into the camera. His sorrow and anger seemed almost tangible.
At least, they did to the people watching him.
“The war has already begun. We must fight, without hesitation and without taking a single step back.”
His voice trembled between his lips like a wave. Michael Silbert poured out his words as though sobbing, as though pleading, then clenched his teeth.
“Together! More united than ever before!”
His reddened eyes burned, and his cry thundered through the microphones.
The cameras no longer showed Jin Taekyung. Every light, every spotlight, was fixed on one man.
Michael Silbert.
In the eyes of the people, he looked like a fighter filled with determination.
In his own mind, he was already a hero and a king. A hero offering a path to people in crisis. A sovereign who would reign over the world.
Amid the trembling air and countless watching eyes, Michael took his final step. He spoke the words he had waited for this day to say.
*The World Hunter Federation.*
Everyone caught their breath. The air seemed to go still beneath the overwhelming aura radiating from him.
“A federation encompassing every nation, bound by no restrictions. The very World Hunter Federation that saved us—all humanity—from the Great Cataclysm. Its return...”
He let the words trail off. His eyes shone as he gazed toward the hundreds of millions, perhaps billions, watching him around the world. Then he released the breath he had been holding.
“I dare to propose it here today.”
The return of an international organization that stood above every law and restriction.
An unseen shock swept through the crowd, then traveled through cameras, microphones, and broadcasts to every corner of the world.
And just as everyone watching was seized by shock and an emotion they could not name, a voice shattered it all.
“Go fuck yourself.”
Hundreds of reporters. The German soldiers and police holding them back. Even the other Hunters who had arrived late.
Countless eyes turned toward me.
Beyond the gleaming camera lenses, I could almost feel the unseen gazes and voices pouring in like a wave.
I didn’t care. Or rather, I couldn’t spare them a thought.
*So that was it.*
I felt as though I’d been hit in the back of the head. My vision swam.
Inside my mind, which looked as though a kindergartner’s playroom had been turned upside down, the words I had just heard rang out with perfect clarity.
*The World Hunter Federation.*
Thirty-odd years later, all that remained of those old heroes’ organization bore the name International Hunter Federation.
Age, gender, nationality, race—even the law had meant nothing to the Hunters who followed humanity’s savior, Cheon Taemin. That was the World Hunter Federation.
They had fought solely for humanity’s survival and won at the cost of countless lives. Then, as soon as the Demon King Asmodeus fell, they had gone their separate ways.
*And he wants to bring that World Hunter Federation back?*
Of course I respected the people who had fought in it, just as everyone else did. They had fought for all of us. And when the war ended, they had surrendered that immense power without regret.
But this was different.
The World Hunter Federation Michael Silbert dreamed of was nothing more than a kingdom for one man.
So I said it again, in front of everyone.
“Go fuck yourself.”
People stared, unable to believe what they’d heard. Then a quiet voice reached my ears and threw my thoughts into turmoil all over again.
—Think it over one more time before you speak.
Michael Silbert.
The man who had driven the world into crisis so he could climb that crisis like a staircase to a throne.
The schemer in a hero’s mask smiled at me. His snake-like eyes glinted as he looked past my shoulder at someone behind me.
—If only for the sake of your monster friend.

“I have witnessed countless deaths.”
A sorrowful voice rang out.
Standing tall before countless cameras and microphones, Michael Silbert slowly continued.
“In the slums of Paris, teeming with flies and gangs.
On the countless battlefields of the Great Cataclysm.
And ever since the day of victory when the Demon King Asmodeus fell.
I have continued to witness them.”
*Bzzzz.*
The faint hum of the cameras sounded unusually loud.
No one so much as swallowed.
The reporters watched Michael with an anticipation they couldn’t quite explain.
*This is...*
*Something’s coming!*
At first, they’d wondered why he had suddenly started spouting nonsense.
All they’d wanted was a friendly shot of the two heroes—one old enough to be the other’s father—with their arms around each other’s shoulders, and perhaps a few warm words.
Jin Taekyung was supposed to be the star today.
Michael was merely the spotlight that would make him shine all the brighter.
Until he opened his mouth.
“Yet through all those deaths, I held on to one hope.
One dream.
With the Demon King Asmodeus and his monster army gone, I believed that someday every conflict would end and true peace would come.”
His tone rose and fell distinctly, and his expression was filled with appeal.
Michael Silbert’s appearance, compelling everyone who saw and heard him to focus, was reflected in the camera lenses.
Around the world, people watching live leaned closer to their living-room televisions, their computer monitors, the smartphones in their hands.
“Mom.
Dad.
I need to watch my cartoon...”
“Shh, Peter.
Be quiet for a moment.”
└ What the fuck is No Jaehun doing?
I called for a gank, and the bastard went AFK. └ What’s up with Jaehun?
Fight with his girlfriend?
Are we surrendering this match?
“It’s not that.
I was watching an iTube live stream.
Never mind—I’ll put the link in the group chat.
Take a look.”
└ What girlfriend?
That bastard doesn’t have one.
It’s just not his promotion match, so he doesn’t give a shi—Munich live?
What’s this?
Dozens of television channels and streaming sites carrying the broadcast lit up with activity.
Their audiences multiplied, and the viewers watched with bated breath.
On-screen, Jin Taekyung stood grim-faced while Michael spoke one step ahead of him.
Michael’s voice carried to them all.
“I have waited a long time.
I have hesitated.
But I stand here today to tell you one thing—for our faith in peace, and for a better future.”
Michael drew a breath.
So did everyone watching him.
Then his voice emerged, dry as sand.
“A second war is nearly upon us.”
Invisible agitation and shock waves swept through every direction.
An office worker flipping through channels after work.
A couple passing beneath a huge billboard.
A teenager who had paused his game and opened the stream to kill time.
The reporters standing right in front of Michael.
At that moment, they doubted their own eyes and ears before falling into extreme confusion.
A second war.
Everyone knew what those few words meant.
Someone gave voice to it in something like a groan.
“The Great Cataclysm...?”
How could they not know?
It was humanity’s clearest nightmare, a memory seared into them by fear: the worst Great War in history, which had covered the Five Oceans and Six Continents in blood and corpses.
And now Michael Silbert was saying that very Great Cataclysm would begin again.
He was declaring that a second war had arrived.
Before them.
No, before the entire world.
*That’s... impossible.*
*It can’t happen.
It can’t.*
Yet no one could bring themselves to say it.
Denial had come with another, paralyzing thought.
*What if he’s telling the truth?*
A second Great Cataclysm could not happen.
It must not happen.
But people had sensed something wrong.
Deep down, they had been feeling their way around the shape of that fear.
The signs were already there.
Magical power levels rose by the day.
Strange phenomena grew more frequent.
Only a few months ago, an Arch Lich had appeared in Sichuan Province, China, and Monster Waves triggered with Magic Gems had followed one another across the world.
Scholars had studied that method of terrorism long ago.
The leading experts in magical power had agreed it was impossible—unless the world’s magical power reached a certain limit.
Today, Michael Silbert was telling them it had.
“Perhaps calling it a *second* war is wrong.
But one thing is certain: what you and I believed was the end of the war was only a ceasefire.”
“I tell you now: the magical power throughout our world has already passed its critical threshold.
A disaster like the one we faced before will engulf the entire world.”
People could barely breathe.
This wasn’t some drunk rambling in a neighborhood bar.
It was a declaration from Michael Silbert—a hero of the Great Cataclysm who had remained at the forefront ever since, a giant who led the world’s greatest Guild.
One of the stunned reporters managed to ask, his voice shaking, “D-Does that mean the Demon King...
Does it mean Asmodeus is coming back?”
“On the Day of Victory, during the final battle that decided humanity’s fate, the Demon King was undoubtedly erased without leaving so much as a trace.
I saw it clearly with my own eyes, so that is an indisputable fact.
However...”
Michael Silbert hesitated for a moment before adding, “Now, no one can be certain.
No one can be certain what will happen in the future, or even whether the Demon King Asmodeus was truly erased.”
Ahh.”
“How can this be...?”
Cameras shook.
The reporters’ dismayed voices came through the microphones and went out to the world.
No one watching from elsewhere complained about the disruption.
They were no calmer than the people on-site.
The terror they had refused to face had finally taken shape, and they trembled at the truth they had tried to ignore.
An unpredictable future.
No—a disaster.
And the possibility that the Demon King Asmodeus might return.
Fear spread through their minds like dark clouds.
Whether they watched Michael Silbert on a screen or stood before him, their eyes shook.
They wanted him to take it all back.
They even entertained the absurd hope that he might laugh and say it had been a joke.
His next words crushed it.
“Peace—or what we thought was peace—is over.”
Michael looked into the camera.
His sorrow and anger seemed almost tangible.
At least, they did to the people watching him.
“The war has already begun.
We must fight, without hesitation and without taking a single step back.”
His voice trembled between his lips like a wave.
Michael Silbert poured out his words as though sobbing, as though pleading, then clenched his teeth.
“Together!
More united than ever before!”
His reddened eyes burned, and his cry thundered through the microphones.
The cameras no longer showed Jin Taekyung.
Every light, every spotlight, was fixed on one man.
Michael Silbert.
In the eyes of the people, he looked like a fighter filled with determination.
In his own mind, he was already a hero and a king.
A hero offering a path to people in crisis.
A sovereign who would reign over the world.
Amid the trembling air and countless watching eyes, Michael took his final step.
He spoke the words he had waited for this day to say.
*The World Hunter Federation.*
Everyone caught their breath.
The air seemed to go still beneath the overwhelming aura radiating from him.
“A federation encompassing every nation, bound by no restrictions.
The very World Hunter Federation that saved us—all humanity—from the Great Cataclysm.
Its return...”
He let the words trail off.
His eyes shone as he gazed toward the hundreds of millions, perhaps billions, watching him around the world.
Then he released the breath he had been holding.
“I dare to propose it here today.”
The return of an international organization that stood above every law and restriction.
An unseen shock swept through the crowd, then traveled through cameras, microphones, and broadcasts to every corner of the world.
And just as everyone watching was seized by shock and an emotion they could not name, a voice shattered it all.
“Go fuck yourself.”
Hundreds of reporters.
The German soldiers and police holding them back.
Even the other Hunters who had arrived late.
Countless eyes turned toward me.
Beyond the gleaming camera lenses, I could almost feel the unseen gazes and voices pouring in like a wave.
I didn’t care.
Or rather, I couldn’t spare them a thought.
*So that was it.*
I felt as though I’d been hit in the back of the head.
My vision swam.
Inside my mind, which looked as though a kindergartner’s playroom had been turned upside down, the words I had just heard rang out with perfect clarity.
*The World Hunter Federation.*
Thirty-odd years later, all that remained of those old heroes’ organization bore the name International Hunter Federation.
Age, gender, nationality, race—even the law had meant nothing to the Hunters who followed humanity’s savior, Cheon Taemin.
That was the World Hunter Federation.
They had fought solely for humanity’s survival and won at the cost of countless lives.
Then, as soon as the Demon King Asmodeus fell, they had gone their separate ways.
*And he wants to bring that World Hunter Federation back?*
Of course I respected the people who had fought in it, just as everyone else did.
They had fought for all of us.
And when the war ended, they had surrendered that immense power without regret.
But this was different.
The World Hunter Federation Michael Silbert dreamed of was nothing more than a kingdom for one man.
So I said it again, in front of everyone.
“Go fuck yourself.”
People stared, unable to believe what they’d heard.
Then a quiet voice reached my ears and threw my thoughts into turmoil all over again.
—Think it over one more time before you speak.
Michael Silbert.
The man who had driven the world into crisis so he could climb that crisis like a staircase to a throne.
The schemer in a hero’s mask smiled at me.
His snake-like eyes glinted as he looked past my shoulder at someone behind me.
—If only for the sake of your monster friend.

chapters.title: Chapter 764
paragraphs: For a moment, the world seemed to stop.
The hundreds of people staring at me with their mouths open. The cameras and microphones jutting up between them. The dazzling lights illuminating the broad lot in place of moonlight.
Everything around me slowed and blurred.
Everything except the one man who had brought my world to a halt.
Michael Silbert.
The most cunning, unscrupulous man I had ever met stared back at me.
His eyes, usually so calm, held unmistakable amusement and triumph. His voice came through just as clearly when it reached my ears again.
“You seem surprised.”
I came to my senses and belatedly steadied my breathing.
*A painful mistake.*
Whatever he said, I couldn’t let him see me shaken.
Show an enemy an opening, and he’d find your weakness. I needed to be especially careful when that enemy was Michael Silbert.
*It’s not too late. As far as I know, the Skeleton King’s identity is secure, and he hasn’t shown me any proof.*
I had to stay calm from here on out. Whatever he said next, all I had to do was answer without letting it rattle me...
*Damn it.*
*Crack.*
Bones shifted audibly in my clenched fist.
I could tell myself whatever I wanted. It was already too late. From the moment I’d met his gray eyes, my instincts had been screaming that his remark wasn’t a mere probe.
Michael Silbert had come here certain, not guessing.
His next words settled it.
“You have two choices. Of course, you don’t have much choice at all, but you might as well hear them for the fun of it.”
His voice was relaxed. With his back to the cameras, Michael moved his lips, looking more pleased than I had ever seen him.
“First, your friend’s identity is exposed before the entire world. Second, you leave this noisy place, and the two of us have a private talk.”
“So? What will it be?”
*Damn it.*
The curse slipped out in a whisper. Michael gave me a faint smile and stepped closer.
*Brush. Pat.*
His hand reached out slowly and brushed the dried blood and dust from my shoulder. At last, the reporters came to their senses and let loose the shouts they had been holding back.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung! Does what you just said mean you oppose the World Hunter Federation?”
“W-Wait! Please tell us exactly what you meant by that profanity!”
“Mr. Jin!”
*Click. Flash-flash-flash!*
The cameras kept rolling as flashes burst from every direction.
The dam of silence broke, releasing a wave of noise. Michael quietly raised a hand to settle the crowd, then spoke.
“My friend here is already a hero the whole world is watching. He is also a spirited young man. The battles and events of recent days must have exhausted him, so I ask for your understanding.”
“Are you saying Mr. Jin has post-traumatic stress disorder?”
“I’m sorry, but let’s leave that discussion for another time. There is only one thing I came to tell you today.”
Michael looked into the cameras.
“The war has begun again. For humanity to survive the coming flood of blood, we need an ark: the World Hunter Federation.”
“That is all. Have a good night, everyone.”
That was his final word to the crowd.

Leaving the reporters shouting behind the German Armed Forces and police officers who blocked their way, Michael Silbert turned and walked toward his private aircraft, which had landed in the center of the open lot.
He left me with one last remark that only I could hear.
“I’ll make you some coffee. I hope you won’t keep me waiting.”
*Grind.*
My teeth clenched.
I knew why he’d said it.
“Mr. Jin!”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung! Please, just one statement!”
I turned away from the cameras as though fleeing and saw two figures hurrying toward me.
Confusion and shock were written across their faces. They spoke too quietly for anyone else to hear.
“We’ve been played. This was what it was all for.”
“Damn it, what the hell is this mess? What’s this World Hunter Federation thing, anyway?”
Their questions came in a rush, but I said nothing.
*What could I say?*
*Where should I even begin, and how should I explain it?*
As I wrestled with that, someone’s face came to mind.
“Magic Johnson.”
“What?”
The Skeleton King frowned at the name.
“Why bring him up all of a sudden? First, tell me what’s going on... Wait. Is there something on my face?”
I’d been staring at him without realizing it. I shook my head.
“...No. Nothing.”
I still didn’t know whether to tell him what had just happened. Or what choice I—what choice *we*—should make.
But some feelings couldn’t be hidden just because you wanted to hide them.
Team Leader Choi finally realized I was keeping something from them. His face hardened, and his lips moved.
“What is it? What happened that made you ask for Mr. Johnson?”
“Tell me. Right now.”
My thoughts were tangled, but they didn’t have long to wait.
After several dozen seconds that felt like an hour, I sent my voice toward Team Leader Choi through Sound Transmission.
“The Skeleton King’s identity has been discovered.”

“Contact Magic Johnson. I need everything his investigation has turned up from the materials we took from the late Siegfried Bassmann’s hideout, and everything he knows about Michael Silbert. All of it. Not a single thing left out.”
Team Leader Choi’s eyes trembled. He remained silent as though he had lost his voice, then slowly nodded. I took a deep breath and began walking.
The lot was now empty of people.
I headed toward the enormous private aircraft standing at its center like an impregnable fortress.
Toward the man waiting inside.
*Michael Silbert.*
Yes. The bastard was right.
The war had already begun.
Michael Silbert kept at least one promise.
“Come in.”
The first thing I saw when I entered his private aircraft, as spacious as a suite, was a cup of coffee on the table.
It smelled freshly brewed. Beyond the steam rising from it, gray eyes—somewhere between darkness and light—watched me.
“I’m glad you came so quickly. I was worried it might get cold.”
I sat down and quietly looked at the full cup. As the silence stretched on, Huginn, who had been standing at attention behind me, spoke.
“If it isn’t to your taste, shall I prepare another coffee?”
His words were polite. The mockery in them wasn’t subtle.
I gave him no answer. I looked away from the cup and jerked my chin toward Michael.
“I don’t care if you keep a pet, but that crow won’t stop cawing. It’s getting on my nerves.”
*Whoosh.*
The air grew heavier. A faint sound reached my ears as Huginn came one step closer behind me.
“If you don’t want to walk on your arms from now on, get back where you were. And shut your mouth before I rip it open.”
“What? You think I can’t do it?”
I was speaking to Huginn, but I kept my eyes on his master. Michael stared at me for a moment, then blinked.
“You’re serious.”
“I am.”
“You would cripple Huginn right in front of me?”
“I might kill both of you.”

An ordinary person might not have taken that provocation lying down. Someone who knew my fatal weakness might have used it to threaten me. Someone powerful enough that I couldn’t afford to lower my guard might have threatened me with force.
Michael was both of those things, yet neither reaction suited him.
“Huh.”
I couldn’t read anything into the sound he made. He studied me with interest.
“Whether you could succeed aside, isn’t that a little reckless?”
“If I’d been cautious, I wouldn’t have made it this far.”
He let out a short laugh.
“True. From what I’ve seen, the last few years of your life have been one reckless act after another. Perhaps that’s how you won the public’s love and trust.”
“Maybe. But is that all? There must be things even you haven’t seen.”
“I once heard of an Eastern saying: empty bluster. Let’s not waste time on meaningless words. I already know everything about you.”
He was wrong.
Michael Silbert knew nothing.
He did not know what kind of life I had truly lived, or how much recklessness it had taken to overcome every crisis and survive until today.
No one in this world could even guess at that secret. One day, it would be a dagger I drove into an enemy’s heart.
Michael couldn’t know that. When I laughed, the smile left his face.
“Why are you laughing?”
“Because I’m enjoying this.”
“Does *this* include the fact that the Stone-King is a monster?”
He was trying to rattle me. But I’d already made that mistake once, and once was enough.
Someone else was less composed. I felt a startled movement behind me and shrugged.
“Looks like your friend didn’t know.”
“He does now.”
“He’s been getting on my nerves for a while, so I couldn’t say anything.”
“Leave now, Huginn.”
After a moment’s hesitation, Huginn bowed his head and left the aircraft. Michael spoke again.
“As you know, I could have told the cameras everything.”
“Yeah.”
I nodded.
“And one of us would be finished by now.”
“Exactly. But I didn’t. Do you know why?”
“Scared shitless?”
*Clink.*
The teaspoon he’d been stirring through his coffee stopped. His gray eyes fixed on me.
“You really are... an unusual man.”
“And you really are... a fucking asshole.”
Honestly, I didn’t know if this was the right move.
But even a cornered rat would bite a cat. Calling Michael Silbert a tiger wouldn’t have done him justice, but right now, I was the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
*Hiss.*
Terrible heat surged through the palm I had laid on the table. Vapor rose around it, overpowering the steam from the coffee. I spoke quietly.
“Go ahead. If you’re ready to die.”

chapters.title: Chapter 765
paragraphs: *Whoosh.*
The air inside the private aircraft grew heavy, pressing down on everything within.
The auras flowing from Michael Silbert and me faced each other across an invisible line. Neither of us gave an inch. The standoff felt ready to erupt at any moment.
But if we crossed that line and clashed, there would be no turning back. One of us would die.
I had no intention of backing down. Now that he had found a fatal weakness, one step backward would be the end of me.
*Tap. Tap. Crash!*
The coffee cup cracked, then burst apart.
At the same instant, I sensed dozens of people racing toward us like streaks of light.
*Bang!*
The alloy door was ripped off in an instant, and a piercing sound rang out.
In the blink of an eye, the loyal hounds had entered the aircraft, wagging their tails at their master.
“Is something wrong?”
I knew that voice. Over my shoulder, Michael Silbert calmly addressed Huginn, who had returned only minutes after leaving.
“I told you to wait outside.”
“My apologies. I thought there was trouble.”
“Nothing of the sort. Our guest accidentally dropped his coffee cup.”
“I see.”
Huginn glanced at the glass scattered across the room.
“I’ll bring another.”
“No need. Whatever you bring, our friend won’t like it.”
“Then...”
“Go back outside. Don’t return until I call for you.”
Huginn hesitated at his superior’s quiet, firm order, then led his men away.
Once the guards had left the aircraft, Michael spoke again.
“I think we should stop here. What do you say?”
“Whatever happens if we continue, we’ll both lose a great deal. Is that really what you want?”
I stared at him, then slowly reined in my aura.
I hated it, but he was right.
As long as the world did not realize what he truly was, even if I killed him here and eliminated the threat of future consequences, I would be branded the worst kind of murderer and criminal.

I would have to spend the rest of my life running from pursuit and surveillance worse than those aimed at a public enemy of the Murim, while my family and friends lost their ordinary lives completely.
That was what frightened me most, and Michael knew it.
“That’s better.”
He brushed the glass from his clothes, then crooked a finger. A fresh cup and a coffee machine half-full of coffee floated over.
“Good thing I prepared spares. Would you like some?”
“If you’ve got more cups you want to throw away.”
“I’ll take that as a no. They were hard to come by. I hate seeing them break.”
*Trickle.*
He filled his cup carefully.
“Now that you’ve calmed down, let’s get to the point. Help me.”
*Go fuck yourself.*
The words rose to my throat, but I swallowed them.
Michael already knew the Skeleton King’s identity. He also knew that, however angry I was, I couldn’t kill him here. Those two facts were the main reason I couldn’t just get up and leave.
*Damn it.*
My fist trembled beneath the table. I kept my voice as even as I could.
“What if I help you?”
“The World Hunter Federation takes root. Without any controversy. Cleanly.”
He dropped a sugar cube into his coffee.
“And I become the head of the new federation, of course.”
“You sound awfully sure of yourself.”
“Oh, Jin.”
He gave a quiet, derisive laugh and shook his head.
“You already know who would take the top seat if the federation were founded now.”
“Only you and I are qualified. And...”
*Clink.*
He slowly stirred the sugar into his coffee. After a sip, his face settled into an expression of perfect satisfaction.
“Once this useful conversation is over, I’ll be the only one still qualified.”
“Are you sure you don’t want any? The aroma and flavor are perfect.”
*Grind.*
My teeth clenched.
I felt like the sugar cube in his cup. It would dissolve whether it wanted to or not, completing the flavor of his coffee.

And the finished coffee—the World Hunter Federation—would flow into Michael Silbert’s mouth. An armed organization powerful enough to ignore nations and restrictions alike would fall into the hands of a monster wearing a hero’s mask.
*If this goes the way he wants... it’s over.*

During the Great Cataclysm, the World Hunter Federation had earned its praise by serving as humanity’s sword and shield. Its members had chosen the public good over private gain. They had risked their lives for a greater cause instead of chasing wealth and power, then disbanded after the Erasure of Demon King Asmodeus.
Michael Silbert was their opposite.
A man who caused disasters without hesitation for the sake of his own interests and power. A monster consumed by endless desire was sitting across from me.
In place of the true hero, who had fallen into an indefinite coma, that monster sat across from me.
“...Cheon Taemin.”
The name escaped me like a groan. Michael’s face stiffened for a moment before he smiled faintly.
“Ah, yes. Sky. He was there.”
*Click.*
He set down his cup with an easy hand, and his voice was just as relaxed.
“In fact, I intend to ask him to lead the federation first.”
“What did you just say?”

“Why so surprised? He has more than enough qualifications. The living savior who rescued humanity from Demon King Asmodeus. The greatest hero in history, and the man who led the World Hunter Federation during the Great Cataclysm. Who could be better suited?”
It felt as though someone had struck me in the back of the head with an iron club.
I finally understood what Michael wanted. I bit my lip.
“You son of a bitch... Don’t tell me.”
“Isn’t it tragic? A hero of his stature should be leading humanity and saving the world once more, yet his illness prevents him from stepping forward. What a cruel whim of God.”

“But the fortunate thing for the people is that Sky recommended someone else as his replacement. The captain who will lead the newly born ark known as the World Hunter Federation. Another hero of the Great Cataclysm known throughout the world, someone else who stopped the spread of terrorism through a noble spirit of sacrifice.”
My breath caught.
None of it had happened yet, but as he spoke, I could see the whole thing unfold.
Michael Silbert would nominate Cheon Taemin as Alliance Leader of the federation. Cheon Taemin would decline on account of his illness and recommend Michael for the position instead.
And after that...
“I think I’ll refuse three times or so. Humbly, of course. Once we’ve put on that little show, you can step forward. It’ll make a fine picture.”
Michael smiled at me. I couldn’t smile back.
He wanted more than my help. He wanted me to put him on the throne.

Once all those gears, large and small, had turned together, every accusation that he’d revived the World Hunter Federation for his own power would disappear. Everyone would seem to have urged him to take the throne.
Without any disturbance or suspicion.
With the support of Cheon Taemin, humanity’s living savior, and of me, his greatest obstacle, he would have an unassailable claim. The next savior—and a king with immense power at his command.
“You crazy son of a bitch...”
The words came out like a groan. Michael smiled.
“Don’t worry. If you and your friends cooperate, I’ll fulfill my duties as Alliance Leader of the World Hunter Federation.”
“You expect me to believe that?”
“Oh dear. It seems I haven’t done enough to earn your trust.”
“What?”
“You know everything I said in front of the cameras today was true. Magical power levels around the world have crossed the critical point. Humanity needs the World Hunter Federation.”
He drained his coffee and added calmly, “And I need the World Hunter Federation.”
At those words, something hot surged up from deep in my dantian.
*Grind.*
I glared at him, fire in my eyes. My fists were clenched so tightly they’d turned white, ready to erupt like volcanoes.
For the sake of the power he wanted—*that* paltry thing—dozens of cities had been destroyed and more than a few million people had died.

And that wasn’t all. Black smoke from the collapsed forests of buildings and the burning streets had blotted out the sun. Survivors who had barely escaped the sudden disaster now huddled in bomb shelters and their homes, clutching family and friends as they trembled in fear.
And he said *what*?
“You fucking bastard...!”
*Fwoosh.*
Blue-white flames surged from the fist that had been trembling all this time. Powerful Scorching Yang Qi burned the air and melted everything nearby.
Rage seized my entire body. Killing intent rose with it, and I drove my fist forward.
*Whoom! Roooar!*
*Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.*
A single punch carrying heat fierce enough to reduce anything to ash tore through the space between us.
Toward the monster in human skin. Toward the madman who would sacrifice anything to get what he wanted.
*I’ll kill him here. No matter what.*
For that moment, I forgot everything else and gave myself over to rage.
And in a world that seemed to slow without end, I saw it: a dazzling streak of light intercepting my flame-wrapped fist.
*BOOM!*
A tremendous blast shook everything around us. I withstood the shockwave driving against my body and stared wide-eyed at Michael Silbert.
At the last instant, he had drawn his sword like lightning and caught the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist on its blade.
*Sizzle-sizzle-sizzle!*
A gray aura, the color of its master’s eyes, gleamed ominously. From beyond the blade pressed against my blue-white flames, his low voice reached me.
“I’m warning you. If you don’t stop here, there really will be no going back.”
*Shhhk!*
There was still one last line we hadn’t crossed. As his warning sank in, I sensed Huginn and the guards approaching behind me. I closed my eyes.
In the darkness, the faces of my family and friends flashed before me.
*Damn it.*
My fist relaxed and slipped away from the blade.

chapters.title: Chapter 766
paragraphs: At some point, I had begun fighting without end.
When I had no power, I fought in Gates for the happiness of my people. After gaining power, I fought to protect them.
But... what an irony.
I had never backed down in the face of death. Now a few words were enough to make me retreat.
*Slide.*
The blue-white flames that had burned so fiercely died down.
Without giving an inch, I slowly drew back the fist pressed against Michael’s sword.
“A wise choice.”
His loathsome voice made my stomach twist. I lowered my fist, still trembling with rage.
No. The moment the tension in the air eased, I threw another punch.
*BOOM!*
Another deafening blast rang out, and a wave of scorching heat swept in every direction. An enraged shout erupted behind me.
“How dare you!”
*Shh-shh-shhik!*
Killing intent surged toward me with the hiss of weapons cutting through the air—
“Enough.”
At Michael’s quiet command, Huginn and the dozens of guards with him stopped dead.
Michael Silbert gave his men a calm glance that told them all they needed to know, then spoke to me.
“I believe I warned you.”
*Grrrrrk.*
Fist and blade locked together once more. Powerful blue and dark energies shuddered against each other. I glared at him.
“Yeah. You did.”
“Do you intend to see this through to the end? Here and now?”
I clenched my teeth.
In my mind, I had already killed Michael Silbert dozens of times. I had broken his limbs, crushed his mouth, and ripped out his heart before bursting it apart.
But this wasn’t Murim.
No—whatever world we were in, no one would accept what I wanted to do unless I tore off the mask he wore first.
“If that had been my intention... I would have done it long ago.”
“You’re more reckless than I thought. And even more arrogant.”
“I’d be disappointed if you thought this was just arrogance.”
Michael’s expression shifted.
*Slice.*
A faint line of blood appeared on his smooth neck with a sound so soft I could only hear it because I was close.
His skin had finally split under the immense pressure of that instant’s clash.
“Huh.”
“That’s my warning to you. Remember it.”
I spat out each word. Michael answered calmly.
“I take back what I said about arrogance. I should add something else instead. You’re more interesting than I thought.”
“You son of a bitch...”
“And thank you for the kind warning. It’s made one thing clear, at least.”
“What?”
“Jin. You can never kill me.”
Amusement crept into his dry voice.
“Because... somewhere along the way, you acquired far too much to lose.”
A chill I couldn’t explain raised the hair all over my body.
It felt as though something sticky and repulsive had reached out and seized my limbs. The horrible sensation of being dragged into a deep swamp made me knock his blade away on reflex.
*Crack!*
Our two energies mingled for an instant.
In the last flash of light, familiar faces flickered before my eyes. I stumbled before I knew it and drew a ragged breath.
I didn’t want to admit it. I couldn’t.
And yet... I had to.
Michael Silbert was right.
The moment I ended the life of the man watching me so calmly, as though the blood on his neck meant nothing, I would cut short my own life and the lives of everyone close to me.
Like the countless enemies I had defeated, they would burn to ash and vanish without a trace.
“May I take your silence to mean I was right?”
I said nothing. Michael Silbert smiled.
“I look forward to working with you. I’ll be in touch soon.”
*Swish.*
He held out his hand, smiling like a man certain of victory.
I turned away without taking it.
No moonlight came to Munich that night.
Jin Taekyung was gone.
Huginn watched him disappear into the darkness, then spoke.
“Will he cooperate willingly?”
Michael Silbert nodded.
“Without a doubt.”
“But Jin Taekyung’s recklessness defies all expectations. Hasn’t he always been difficult to predict?”
“Everyone has a weakness. And he possesses one more fatal than anyone else’s.”
“What weakness?”
“His feelings. Jin Taekyung is more emotional than anyone.”
Michael continued in the same calm voice.
“Someone whose joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure are so clear is easier to handle than a materialistic person. Wealth and honor can be regained even after they are lost, but people cannot.”
He looked at his private aircraft, all but wrecked by the force of their clashes.
It had been custom-built with cutting-edge equipment and Magic at a cost of hundreds of billions of won. Its destruction stirred nothing in him. It was only a heap of scrap metal.
People were different. Each had only one life to live.
“Jin Taekyung... has more to lose than I thought.”
*Perhaps even more than I do.*
Michael swallowed the words before they could leave his tongue.
He didn’t want to admit it.

He already had more wealth than he could ever spend and immense power besides. Once he took control of the reborn World Hunter Federation, he would be beyond anyone’s reach. He would be king of this world.
How could Jin Taekyung have more to lose than him?
*That makes no sense.*
Michael patted Huginn on the shoulder.
“There is no need to worry. In a few days, everything will be concluded successfully.”
“I hope so, but...”
Huginn kept staring into the darkness where Jin Taekyung had vanished.
“I don’t know if letting him leave was the right choice. I can’t shake the feeling we’ve made a mistake we can’t undo.”
“There’s no need to feel that way. We had no other choice, either.”
“What do you mea—”
*Crash!*
An unfamiliar sound cut him off.
Huginn turned. His superior stood holding a sword with nothing left but the hilt.
“Guild Master!”
Michael shook his head at Huginn’s alarm. With a strange look in his eyes, he gazed at the fragments scattered around his feet.
“Well, this is something...”
Only two clashes.

That was all it had taken to shatter his cherished sword, forged from the finest materials and imbued with Magic. Without the powerful aura surrounding its blade, it probably wouldn’t have held together even this long.
*He really is more interesting than I thought.*
Michael had thought he knew the extent of Jin Taekyung’s abilities.
Odin Guild had kept its eyes and ears on him since he first came to prominence. With every new report, Michael had revised his assessment of the young Asian man.
First a potential recruit. Then a promising next-generation S-rank Hunter.
And then... his greatest obstacle.
*I thought Cheon Taemin was the only one left.*
That was how it had been. That was how it should have been.
Yet today, calculations that should have allowed no margin for error had proved completely wrong.
*Jin Taekyung.*
Michael looked into the darkness that had swallowed the young man moments ago.
He pictured him from head to toe—not yet half Michael’s age—and thought again of the enormous power coiled within him.
*What if I had used all my strength?*
A moment later, he gave a faint scoff.
It was a pointless question. He had reached his current position precisely because he had never used all his strength against any enemy.
The one who uses all his strength wins the battle, but the one who hides his strength wins the war.
Michael Silbert wanted to win the war. Not the battle—the war.
He had lived for dominion, not mere survival, and only one final step remained between him and the throne.
*Everything is within reach. No need to hurry.*
At least not tonight.
Michael Silbert swallowed the words circling the tip of his tongue and suddenly raised his head toward the sky.
To his gray eyes, Munich’s night sky shone more brightly than ever. Someone else had looked at that same sky only moments before and seen no moonlight at all.
*Yes. At least not tonight.*
*Crack. Fsssh.*
In his clenched fist, the impossibly hard sword hilt crumbled into powder and scattered on the wind.
Michael Silbert was not careless enough to leave an obstacle where it stood after it had blocked his path once.
Even after I had finished telling them everything, the spacious suite remained filled with heavy air and silence.
*It couldn’t be helped.*
I looked at Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King, both of whom had gone rigid, and muttered inwardly.
It was the reaction I had expected.
Nobody stays calm when their head’s on fire. And in this case, being a monster instead of a human wouldn’t make any difference.
“Damn it.”
The Skeleton King broke the silence first. He muttered the curse, then spoke with a troubled look on his face.
“Wicked human. What happens now?”
“Hmm.”
Under normal circumstances, I would have made a joke. But the matter was too serious this time, and I found it difficult to answer.
The Skeleton King probably had plenty on his mind. His identity had been discovered, and he had no idea what would happen to him next.
I couldn’t bring myself to say any of that. I just sat there, moving my lips without making a sound. Then he spoke in a grave voice.
“If it’s too difficult to answer, tell me just one thing.”
“Go ahead.”
“Will this body never be allowed to enter the club again?”
I blinked. For a moment, I couldn’t make sense of the question.
By the time I came to my senses, White Flame’s spearhead was driving into his chest.
*Crack. Crunch.*
“AGH! Aaaagh! It was a joke! I was joking!”
“Die. Please, just die...”
“Please spare me! My ribs! I’ve got a cracked rib!”
“You thoughtless bastard. Even Myeongnyun Jinsa Galbi has more sense than you...”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung! Mr. Jin Taekyung! You mustn’t!”
I must have lost it for a moment.
After a brief, rage-induced out-of-body experience, Team Leader Choi’s pleas finally brought me back to my senses.

Seeing the Skeleton King clutching his chest and trying to force his ribs back into place made my vision turn white again, but I endured through the superhuman mental fortitude befitting a Supreme Peak master.
*Fuck. I think I’m about to suffer qi deviation.*

Another ten minutes of watching that, and my qi and blood would have tangled so badly I’d have died or ended up crippled. Michael Silbert would have done a ridiculous little dance and recruited the Skeleton King as his new right-hand man.
Fortunately, a visitor arrived before qi deviation did.
