“That’s my warning to you.
Remember it.”
I spat out each word.
Michael answered calmly.
“I take back what I said about arrogance.
I should add something else instead.
You’re more interesting than I thought.”
“You son of a bitch...”
“And thank you for the kind warning.
It’s made one thing clear, at least.”
“What?”
“Jin.
You can never kill me.”
Amusement crept into his dry voice.
“Because... somewhere along the way, you acquired far too much to lose.”
A chill I couldn’t explain raised the hair all over my body.
It felt as though something sticky and repulsive had reached out and seized my limbs.
The horrible sensation of being dragged into a deep swamp made me knock his blade away on reflex.
*Crack!*
Our two energies mingled for an instant.
In the last flash of light, familiar faces flickered before my eyes.
I stumbled before I knew it and drew a ragged breath.
I didn’t want to admit it.
I couldn’t.
And yet...
I had to.
Michael Silbert was right.
The moment I ended the life of the man watching me so calmly, as though the blood on his neck meant nothing, I would cut short my own life and the lives of everyone close to me.
Like the countless enemies I had defeated, they would burn to ash and vanish without a trace.
“May I take your silence to mean I was right?”
I said nothing.
Michael Silbert smiled.
“I look forward to working with you.
I’ll be in touch soon.”
*Swish.*
He held out his hand, smiling like a man certain of victory.
I turned away without taking it.
No moonlight came to Munich that night.
Jin Taekyung was gone.
Huginn watched him disappear into the darkness, then spoke.
“Will he cooperate willingly?”
Michael Silbert nodded.
“Without a doubt.”
“But Jin Taekyung’s recklessness defies all expectations.
Hasn’t he always been difficult to predict?”
“Everyone has a weakness.
And he possesses one more fatal than anyone else’s.”
“What weakness?”
“His feelings.
Jin Taekyung is more emotional than anyone.”
Michael continued in the same calm voice.
“Someone whose joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure are so clear is easier to handle than a materialistic person.
Wealth and honor can be regained even after they are lost, but people cannot.”
He looked at his private aircraft, all but wrecked by the force of their clashes.
It had been custom-built with cutting-edge equipment and Magic at a cost of hundreds of billions of won.
Its destruction stirred nothing in him.
It was only a heap of scrap metal.
People were different.
Each had only one life to live.
“Jin Taekyung... has more to lose than I thought.”
*Perhaps even more than I do.*
Michael swallowed the words before they could leave his tongue.
He didn’t want to admit it.
He already had more wealth than he could ever spend and immense power besides.
Once he took control of the reborn World Hunter Federation, he would be beyond anyone’s reach.
He would be king of this world.
How could Jin Taekyung have more to lose than him?
*That makes no sense.*
Michael patted Huginn on the shoulder.
“There is no need to worry.
In a few days, everything will be concluded successfully.”
“I hope so, but...”
Huginn kept staring into the darkness where Jin Taekyung had vanished.
“I don’t know if letting him leave was the right choice.
I can’t shake the feeling we’ve made a mistake we can’t undo.”
“There’s no need to feel that way.
We had no other choice, either.”
“What do you mea—”
*Crash!*
An unfamiliar sound cut him off.
Huginn turned.
His superior stood holding a sword with nothing left but the hilt.
“Guild Master!”
Michael shook his head at Huginn’s alarm.
With a strange look in his eyes, he gazed at the fragments scattered around his feet.
“Well, this is something...”
Only two clashes.
That was all it had taken to shatter his cherished sword, forged from the finest materials and imbued with Magic.
Without the powerful aura surrounding its blade, it probably wouldn’t have held together even this long.
*He really is more interesting than I thought.*
Michael had thought he knew the extent of Jin Taekyung’s abilities.
Odin Guild had kept its eyes and ears on him since he first came to prominence.
With every new report, Michael had revised his assessment of the young Asian man.
First a potential recruit.
Then a promising next-generation S-rank Hunter.
And then... his greatest obstacle.
*I thought Cheon Taemin was the only one left.*
That was how it had been.
That was how it should have been.
Yet today, calculations that should have allowed no margin for error had proved completely wrong.
*Jin Taekyung.*
Michael looked into the darkness that had swallowed the young man moments ago.
He pictured him from head to toe—not yet half Michael’s age—and thought again of the enormous power coiled within him.
*What if I had used all my strength?*
A moment later, he gave a faint scoff.
It was a pointless question.
He had reached his current position precisely because he had never used all his strength against any enemy.
The one who uses all his strength wins the battle, but the one who hides his strength wins the war.
Michael Silbert wanted to win the war.
Not the battle—the war.
He had lived for dominion, not mere survival, and only one final step remained between him and the throne.
*Everything is within reach.
No need to hurry.*
At least not tonight.
Michael Silbert swallowed the words circling the tip of his tongue and suddenly raised his head toward the sky.
To his gray eyes, Munich’s night sky shone more brightly than ever.
Someone else had looked at that same sky only moments before and seen no moonlight at all.
*Yes.
At least not tonight.*
*Crack.
Fsssh.*
In his clenched fist, the impossibly hard sword hilt crumbled into powder and scattered on the wind.
Michael Silbert was not careless enough to leave an obstacle where it stood after it had blocked his path once.
Even after I had finished telling them everything, the spacious suite remained filled with heavy air and silence.
*It couldn’t be helped.*
I looked at Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King, both of whom had gone rigid, and muttered inwardly.
It was the reaction I had expected.
Nobody stays calm when their head’s on fire.
And in this case, being a monster instead of a human wouldn’t make any difference.
“Damn it.”
The Skeleton King broke the silence first.
He muttered the curse, then spoke with a troubled look on his face.
“Wicked human.
What happens now?”
“Hmm.”
Under normal circumstances, I would have made a joke.
But the matter was too serious this time, and I found it difficult to answer.
The Skeleton King probably had plenty on his mind.
His identity had been discovered, and he had no idea what would happen to him next.
I couldn’t bring myself to say any of that.
I just sat there, moving my lips without making a sound.
Then he spoke in a grave voice.
“If it’s too difficult to answer, tell me just one thing.”
“Go ahead.”
“Will this body never be allowed to enter the club again?”
I blinked.
For a moment, I couldn’t make sense of the question.
By the time I came to my senses, White Flame’s spearhead was driving into his chest.
*Crack.
Crunch.*
“AGH!
Aaaagh!
It was a joke!
I was joking!”
“Die.
Please, just die...”
“Please spare me!
My ribs!
I’ve got a cracked rib!”
“You thoughtless bastard.
Even Myeongnyun Jinsa Galbi has more sense than you...”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung!
Mr.
Jin Taekyung!
You mustn’t!”
I must have lost it for a moment.
After a brief, rage-induced out-of-body experience, Team Leader Choi’s pleas finally brought me back to my senses.

Seeing the Skeleton King clutching his chest and trying to force his ribs back into place made my vision turn white again, but I endured through the superhuman mental fortitude befitting a Supreme Peak master.
*Fuck.
I think I’m about to suffer qi deviation.*
Another ten minutes of watching that, and my qi and blood would have tangled so badly I’d have died or ended up crippled.
Michael Silbert would have done a ridiculous little dance and recruited the Skeleton King as his new right-hand man.
Fortunately, a visitor arrived before qi deviation did.

paragraphs: *Bzzzt.*
At the sudden vibration, Team Leader Choi pulled a smartphone from inside his coat. He checked it—one of the five phones he carried, no less—then mouthed my name.
*Mr. Jin Taekyung.*
The reason he wasn’t speaking aloud was obvious. I quickly drew up my internal energy and spread it around us.
*Fwoooosh.*
An invisible barrier of qi sealed the suite without leaving a single gap.
*Bzzzt.*
Blue light poured from the smartphone lying on the table. In the blink of an eye, it gathered into a human-shaped hologram, and a deep voice rang out.
“Sorry I’m late. I just saw your message... But what happened to that guy? Don’t tell me you’ve already had a fight.”
Magic Johnson.
The towering Grand Mage blinked at the Skeleton King, who lay clutching his chest. I answered weakly.
“It’s a long story.”
Unlike the Skeleton King and Team Leader Choi, Magic Johnson’s reaction was brief and clear.
“Fuck.”
Of course, he didn’t stop there. After muttering nonstop about a son and a beach, and about a third hole he normally kept hidden from view, he rubbed his perfectly smooth, hairless scalp.
“This... is about as bad as it gets.”
Only then did something I hadn’t considered occur to me. If the Skeleton King’s existence were exposed, I would not be the only one to suffer a serious blow. Neither would Team Leader Choi.
“I’m sorry. I should’ve been more careful.”
“No need to apologize, Jin. I chose to help you.”
Johnson waved off my belated apology, then frowned.
“But how did he find out? My illusion Magic should have been perfect.”

Magic Johnson was one of only three Grand Mages in the world. No—now there were only two. He had gone to great lengths to inscribe that illusion Magic, and its effectiveness and secrecy were second to none. No wonder his face showed so many conflicting emotions.
“With Siegfried dead, there’s only one mage left who could see through my illusion Magic... And I guarantee you, even Michael couldn’t get her to act.”
If Magic Johnson was speaking with such certainty, it had to be true.
I had heard plenty about the other Grand Mage myself, and after decades had passed, most of what I had heard had turned out to be fact rather than rumor.
But even leaving her aside, we had enough clues. And I wasn’t the only one who saw where they pointed.
“Japan.”
“Leviathan.”
Although the words were different, they meant the same thing. Team Leader Choi, who had spoken at the same time as me, continued slowly as everyone’s eyes turned toward him.
“As you all know, what happened in Japan wasn’t simply a terrorist attack or a Monster Wave.”
“Choi told me about it. I think Michael Silbert was most likely behind it, too.”
“But what we need to reconsider now is his objective.”
“His objective?”
“Why did Michael Silbert wake Leviathan from its sleep deep beneath the sea? And...”
“Why lure it to Japan, of all the countries he could have chosen?”

I picked up where Team Leader Choi had left off. The five oceans covered a staggering seventy-one percent of the Earth’s surface. There was no shortage of countries with coastlines. So why had Michael chosen Japan as the place to let Leviathan run wild?
*And there was the second terrorist attack, which struck around the world on the same day.*
The answer was already there, as Team Leader Choi’s next words made clear.
“He calculated everything meticulously from the beginning, taking Japan’s situation at the time and every other factor into account.”
Johnson grasped what he meant and spoke with a groan.
“Then all of it—including the second terrorist attack—was meant to draw you in?”
“Yes. I’m certain.”
“But why Japan? If that was his goal, wouldn’t it have been easier to lure Leviathan to Korea?”
Team Leader Choi shook his head and continued in a calm voice.

“From Michael Silbert’s perspective, it was the only possible choice. Even setting aside the fact that Korean Hunters are far stronger, our government has been on high alert ever since Go Jun artificially caused two Monster Waves. If magical power had suddenly surged, they would have noticed immediately.”
“The Magic Gem...!”
“Exactly. But Japan had recently been hit by the first terrorist attack. The area around Tokyo, in particular, would have suited him in several ways.”
It wasn’t just any Magic Gem. It was an unrefined S-rank Magic Gem. The sheer amount and concentration of magical power it gave off had been enough to wake Leviathan deep beneath the distant sea.

But near Tokyo, magical power levels were already running wild because of the Monster Wave caused by the first attack. Another surge would have been hard to spot. Most importantly, there hadn’t been a Gate near Tokyo Bay—the area Leviathan destroyed—that would have given anyone cause for alarm.
“Yes,” Johnson said. “It all fits.”

“He drew the outline based on that from the start, then colored it in with the second terrorist attack. Since Japan was fairly far from the major Hunter powers, it would not have been difficult to predict that its own forces would be unable to stop a Named Monster like Leviathan.”
The Supreme Peak masters of Murim were proof enough that people at the same level could differ enormously in strength. Modern S-rank Hunters were no different.
And Japan’s S-rank Hunter, Yamamoto Genji, was stuck on the lower floors of that pyramid of power.

*If he was really as strong as all those Japanese netizens and Japan-worshipping fanboys dickriding him claimed, why had he shown up so late that Leviathan was already dead when he’d had an entire day to get there?*
*The answer was obvious.*
The Japanese government must have known it, too. That was why they’d swallowed their pride and asked for help.
A country that had come through both worldwide terrorist attacks with little damage. An indisputable Hunter powerhouse, and a neighbor close enough to reach them faster than anyone else.
Korea.
And Korea had me.
No. *Us.*
A chill ran down my spine. I abruptly raised my head as though I had just woken up and stared at the Skeleton King.
He’d been listening in a daze, too distracted even to put his dislocated bones back in place. At my stare, he flinched and shrank back.
“I—I’ve just been sitting here.”
“I told you, I was joking because everyone looked so serious! Haven’t you heard of lightening the mood?”
“That’s not it.”
“Th—then why?”
Damn it. My teeth had clenched without me noticing. My voice came out low and strained.
“It was you. From the beginning.”
“This body? From the beginning? What are you talking about?”
The Skeleton King frowned. Team Leader Choi answered, his expression grim.
“Michael Silbert’s target was never Mr. Jin Taekyung. It was you.”
“...What?”
“Don’t you see? The second terrorist attack. Leviathan. He arranged all of it to target you.”
The Skeleton King’s pupils trembled. Johnson, who had been thinking in silence, let out a sigh.
“So he’d suspected it for some time.”
“He would have needed evidence to turn that suspicion into certainty.”
“Even at the cost of so many lives?”
“Do you still not know what kind of man he is? Hundreds could die. Tens of millions could die. Michael Silbert wouldn’t bat an eye.”
Team Leader Choi looked at me. His voice was rough as iron filings, nothing like it usually sounded.
“If it meant achieving his goal—if he could get the proof he needed—he could end all of this right now.”
He was right.

That was all the bastard had wanted: the weakness that would guarantee his victory in a war against me. So he’d set the entire stage, cutting off any chance of reinforcements from other countries and creating a situation where the Skeleton King had no choice but to step in.
*And then... he finally got his hands around that weakness.*
That wasn’t all. His willingness to launch the second terrorist attack must also have had a great deal to do with the World Hunter Federation.
*The worse the damage, the greater the chance of reestablishing it.*
How far ahead had Michael Silbert calculated?
The question stole my breath. It felt as though an invisible cord were tightening around my neck. I took a deep breath and looked around.
Team Leader Choi. Magic Johnson. Finally, the Skeleton King.
At some point, all three had fallen silent. They were looking at me.
No. They were waiting for me to speak. Waiting for me to decide where we went from here.
Thoughts and doubts raced through my mind. At last, I broke the long silence.
Three days passed.
No one said a word about the tremendous boom that had echoed across the vacant lot outside Munich, where the Odin Guild Master’s private aircraft had landed on the night disaster struck.

The reporters who had all but been driven from the scene wanted to know what had made the sound they’d faintly heard from a distance. But the German Armed Forces, which controlled the Munich area, gave them a firm answer.
First: no pointless questions, and no approaching the site.
Second: anyone who failed to comply would be deported immediately.

Even the most hot-blooded reporters, who had bristled at the first point, fell quiet at the second. With the proposed revival of the World Hunter Federation shaking the world, getting deported over something like this would be madness.

Two people central to that debate were still in Munich. One was Jin Taekyung, whose behavior in front of the cameras the previous night had baffled everyone. The other was Michael Silbert, the man who had lit the fuse on this powder keg.
“Hey, sorry, but have you heard anything about either of them?”
“No.”
“Do you mean there’s nothing to hear, or that you know something and won’t tell me?”
“Hmm. Both?”
“Come on, we’re colleagues. We ought to help each other out. Those Germans can’t take a joke, and they’re being ridiculously strict. What’s your name, anyway?”
“Franz Meyer.”
“...You’re not German, are you?”
“I believe I am. A strict, foul-tempered German who can’t take a joke. That’s me.”
“I didn’t say foul-tempered—damn it. Sorry. I didn’t mean that.”
“It wouldn’t matter even if you did. But if you’re really sorry, throw me a decent scoop.”
“A decent scoop? Then how about the emergency convening of the UN General Assembly?”
The bearded German reporter gave a short laugh.
“You’re joking. Who doesn’t know about that? The meeting’s been going on for ages.”
He was right.

At midnight three days earlier, following the Munich incident, the UN—reorganized after the Great Cataclysm—had called an emergency General Assembly. The leaders of 185 countries, led by the six permanent member states, were locked in fierce debate over videoconference.
They had gathered for one reason: the proposal to reestablish the World Hunter Federation.
Given what was at stake, the emergency session was being held under unusually tight secrecy. But word always leaked out. Major news outlets had already learned of it and were watching closely.
“And you call something everyone knows a decent scoop? Your sense of humor is worse than I thought. You’re in no position to make fun of Germans.”
“Hmm. What if I told you the vote is about to begin?”
The German reporter stopped as he was turning away. He stroked his stubbly beard.
“...Now that’s interesting.”
“Glad you think so. It isn’t a joke.”
“You’re sure?”
“Is anyone ever sure of anything? If you want a number, I’d say ninety-nine point nine percent.”
*99.9 percent.*
The German reporter repeated the near-certain figure under his breath and swallowed.
“That means...”
“Yes. That’s right. The UN will announce it soon.”
Simon, the reporter who looked a good ten years younger than the German man facing him, went on slowly.
“The result of the vote on the birth of the World Hunter Federation. An organization that would span the globe.”

“Hmm.
What if I told you the vote is about to begin?”
The German reporter stopped as he was turning away.
He stroked his stubbly beard.
“...Now that’s interesting.”
“Glad you think so.
It isn’t a joke.”
“You’re sure?”
“Is anyone ever sure of anything?
If you want a number, I’d say ninety-nine point nine percent.”
*99.9 percent.*
The German reporter repeated the near-certain figure under his breath and swallowed.
“That means...”
“Yes.
That’s right.
The UN will announce it soon.”
Simon, the reporter who looked a good ten years younger than the German man facing him, went on slowly.
“The result of the vote on the birth of the World Hunter Federation.
An organization that would span the globe.”

chapters.title: Chapter 768
paragraphs: Marie Antoinette Syndrome.
The name came from the story that Queen Marie Antoinette’s hair suddenly turned white a few days before her execution during the eighteenth-century French Revolution.
No one had established the true nature or cause of the strange phenomenon, but at that moment, Baek Hanseong, the President of Korea, was certain it was extreme stress.
His own situation felt similar enough.
*Fuck.*
The curse he had kept to himself since his closely watched debut in politics swirled around in his mouth.
The sharp-eyed secretary who had worked with him since his days in the National Assembly gestured for him to cover his mouth. Baek ignored him.
The room was full of foreigners. None of them knew Korean well enough to read his lips, and they were far too busy to watch his mouth in the first place.
Why would they, when presidents from around the world had abandoned all dignity and were pointing fingers at one another?
“You call that an argument? Of course we have to reestablish the World Hunter Federation!”
“I’m not saying we should never establish it! I’m saying we should put it on hold. Do you know what *on hold* means?”
“Did you just speak informally to me? Are you insane?”
“You’re the insane one. What are we going to do about the Federation’s enormous authority? We haven’t even properly reviewed the proposed changes. We can’t just approve this in a few days!”
“You fucking... What’s your country’s GDP?”
Shouts flew through the translators. Faces glowed red.
Baek held a perfect three-for-three record in the brawls for which Korea’s National Assembly was famous, so the sight was oddly familiar. But after days of it, he felt as though his head might burst.
*What are they, children?*

It wasn’t always like this. Sometimes sharp words were exchanged and an uncomfortable atmosphere formed in accordance with international affairs, but the UN General Assembly was supposed to be a place where nations demonstrated their dignity and their leaders showed their character.

However, as the situation spiraled toward the worst possible outcome and the presidents were crushed beneath immense stress and pressure from all sides, they had no choice but to throw off the masks they had been wearing and reveal their true faces.
“We’re all going to die! What happens if we put off establishing the Federation even now?”
“Exactly! Saudi Arabia strongly supports the establishment of the World Hunter Federation—”
“The Middle East should know when to bow out. You’ve sold more than enough oil, and now you’ve even exported terrorists to the entire world.”
“What?”
At the words of the Russian president, who was old beyond measure, a middle-aged man wearing a turban bulged his eyes.
“How dare you, you dictator!”
“A dictator? That’s rich coming from a king. At least I was elected in a fair vote. I wasn’t born into a royal family and handed this seat.”
“Ah, are you talking about that fair election where the voter turnout reached 140 percent in the last presidential election?”
“Well, these things happen. It was a long time ago.”
More than twenty years earlier, Vladimir Furin had become Russia’s president for life in an election whose astonishing turnout exceeded the country’s entire population.
He swept his gleaming eyes around the room. Long past a hundred, he kept himself healthy with cutting-edge medical technology and Magic potions, and his voice remained strong.
“What matters is that I—and Russia—oppose establishing the World Hunter Federation.”
“Let’s be frank. I don’t think the Federation is unnecessary. I’m concerned about who will take charge of it.”
Tap. Tap.
His wrinkled fingers struck the table. The force of the gesture carried through the hologram, silencing the supporters who had been about to protest.
“When we first discussed establishing the World Hunter Federation, I supported it because I trusted Sky. I met him myself. He had little interest in power.”
“And the circumstances were far worse,” said the President of the United States, Doramp Jr.
Furin nodded. “They were. That damned Asmodeus was sweeping across the world.”

“The situation is still serious, but it is not as bad as it was then. I hope everyone will consider that the World Hunter Federation possesses far too much authority for us to make such a hasty decision.”
The Cold War between Russia and the United States had ended more than a century ago. Their long-standing resentment had not vanished, but here, at least, the two presidents agreed.
For Baek, the first to call for a delay, that was welcome news. So was the support of another ally who had already promised to stand with Korea.
“Our People’s Republic of China must once again express its deep concern.”
Chairman Xiao Yang looked toward Baek.
“As President Baek of Korea has repeatedly stated, the establishment of the World Hunter Federation must be discussed with great care.”
“Er, Japan also agrees with Kankoku’s position—”
“Thank you both.”
*What the hell is that bastard about to say now?*
President Baek Hanseong hurriedly cut off Prime Minister Koizumi before he could dump shit all over the discussion. He leaned toward the microphone fitted with a translation device.
“As I’ve said several times, we must handle the question of the World Hunter Federation with care. Deciding it after only three days would be far too hasty—”
“Only three days? Hasty?”
The French president cut in with a scoff.
“Do you have any idea what has happened outside during those three days?”
“That—”
“I don’t know how things are in Korea, but France has already had five major riots. Doomsday fanatics are out in the streets screaming, and work and production have all but stopped.”
“...Please, hear me out.”
“If it’s what we’ve been hearing for three days, I must respectfully decline. Half the Louvre Museum has burned. What else is there to hear?”
President Baek Hanseong was rendered speechless. Without realizing it, he rubbed his throbbing temples.
*That damned bastard.*
He knew perfectly well that Odin Guild’s support had helped the French president reach office. But he could hardly argue when the man was telling the truth.
*Michael Silbert.*
A single statement from a hero with enormous public support had lit the fuse on a world full of fear and anxiety.
Half the world’s population had watched him warn of a second Great Cataclysm in real time. Within a day, the fire had spread beyond the metaphor.
Huge demonstrations bordering on riots. People driven into the streets by fear and anger had little patience left, and fires soon broke out across their cities.
The police? The military?
Armed officers and soldiers demanded that the crowds disperse, but their calls fell on ears already half-deaf to reason.
If France, one of the world’s ten most developed countries, was in that state, there was no need to guess how others were faring.
“What the people want now is a result. A result that will reassure them. A result that will guarantee the lives of themselves and their families.”
“If the World Hunter Federation isn’t reestablished, our country is finished. At the very least, the presidential palace will burn, and I won’t escape unscathed.”
“We have no choice but to support it wholeheartedly. The movements of our military factions are already deeply suspicious.”
“You’re opposing it now? Have you lost your mind? Do you think you can watch from the far bank while the rest of us burn?”
The spotlight was bright. Everything around it was dark.
A handful of developed nations enjoyed a civilization more advanced than ever. But how many of the UN’s 185 member states shared in all of it?

Demon King Asmodeus had fallen, yet hunger and civil war remained. More than a few countries were still struggling to keep their governments intact while nursing the deep wounds left by the Great Cataclysm.
For them, this was more than a powder keg exploding.
It was a nuclear blast—one that would soon swallow their entire country.
At this rate, it would not be monsters burning down presidential palaces. It would be furious citizens and coup forces.
“We can’t delay any longer!”
“Let’s vote!”
“We do not trust the Security Council or the permanent members! We demand a full vote!”
The calls came from all sides. Baek knew the long meeting was nearing its end.
*This... can’t be stopped anymore.*

The UN Security Council still held enormous power. The United States, the United Kingdom, France, Russia, and China had been permanent members since their victory in the Second World War. Korea had joined them after the Great Cataclysm.
Of those six, the United Kingdom had remained neutral on this question and France supported the proposal. The other four stood on the side effectively calling for a delay.
But even the permanent members’ veto power had clear limits under the reorganized UN.
*So this is how it ends.*
The secretary-general’s announcement that voting had begun sounded distant. All Baek could hear clearly was his conversation with Choi Minwoo three days earlier.
“We need to delay the UN’s decision as long as possible.”
“Delay it? Not stop it?”
“If we could stop it, I’d ask for nothing more. But even with the United States and China helping us, that would be nearly impossible.”
“...You want to buy time.”
“Even a few weeks. No, even a few days would be enough. Please do everything you can until we reach the limit of what is possible.”
“Hah. What exactly is happening right now?”
After a long silence, Choi’s answer had been brief.
“War.”
“...Mr. President. Mr. President.”
Baek snapped out of his thoughts. His chief secretary was watching him, concern and impatience mingling on his face.
“You need to vote. We’re the last.”
“Ah.”
After letting out a short groan that sounded almost like a sigh, President Baek Hanseong looked at the presidents filling the office.
No—the holograms.
Then, thinking of Choi Minwoo and Jin Taekyung, who were probably preparing for war somewhere by now, he cast the final vote of this miserable meeting.
Sometimes you did not need to see someone’s face, or hear more than a few words, to understand them.
A voice’s tone and pitch could tell you enough.
In that sense, Choi Minwoo understood everything the moment he answered the call from President Baek Hanseong.
“I did everything I could.”
A long silence followed. The few words they exchanged after that felt hollow.
When the short call ended, Choi walked toward a room crowded with documents and monitors. Inside, someone was so absorbed in what he was doing that he had not noticed Choi arrive.
Then, suddenly, Choi opened his mouth.
“The UN... has approved reestablishing the World Hunter Federation.”
The reply was short.
*Fuck.*

chapters.title: Chapter 769
paragraphs: Even the most clearheaded person could not stay composed every moment of every day.
Michael Silbert realized he was shaken only after brewing three cups of coffee in a row.
*Shaken? Me?*
The realization surprised even him. That surprise soon turned to displeasure.
A leader must never show himself wavering. Not to enemies, not to allies, and not even to himself.
To win this war, he could not show the slightest opening.
In the heat of battle, a person’s movements began to slow the moment they realized they had been wounded.
Michael believed he could have everything only if he could ignore any pain. He had lived by that belief ever since the day he returned from the brink of death, long ago.
But today, two things had shaken him.
One was the thrill of being so close to his grand dream.
The other...
*It’s probably that bastard.*
A face flickered through the steam rising from the coffee cups.
A young man far younger than himself, who had won the public’s love in an absurdly short time and become his most troublesome obstacle.
*Jin Taekyung.*
The name lingered in his mouth, accompanied by a faint pain at his throat.
Swish.
Michael carefully pulled down the turtleneck that covered his neck. A dark-red mark stood out against his skin, warped by a brief surge of heat.
It was the first wound he had suffered in more than a decade. He was tracing the mark Jin Taekyung had left several days ago when—
Bzzzt.
A phone vibrated somewhere. His fingertips trembled against the wound, which had yet to heal.
Instinctively, Michael pulled his collar back up and looked at the name on his smartphone screen.
[Emmanuel]
There were many people in the world named Emmanuel. But only one could contact him directly without going through Huginn.
Click.
“Congratulations, Guild Master.”
The President of France’s voice came through the moment the call connected. Michael laughed aloud and tipped all three cups of coffee onto the floor.
Out went his anxiety and agitation, along with the face that had appeared in the hazy steam.
Once he had poured it all away, nothing remained in the empty cups but joy and triumph.
*I... won.*
The throne was ready. All that remained was a magnificent coronation.
Michael found himself wondering what expression Jin Taekyung wore now that he had heard the news.
The scene came so vividly to mind that his lips twitched.
It was strange.
Something that should never have happened had come to pass, yet I felt oddly calm.
Probably because I’d seen it coming.
“Fuck.”
Still, I had to do what needed to be done. It wasn’t like I could shout, *Yay!*
Having cursed out of habit, I looked at Team Leader Choi, who had just come through the door.
“So... we couldn’t stop it?”
Team Leader Choi nodded gravely.
“There was only so much we could do.”
“Even with Russia helping us? Russia, of all countries?”
“Even if the United Kingdom had joined us instead of remaining neutral at this General Assembly, I doubt the result would have changed much. We’re already effectively at war.”

Even someone as clueless about politics as I was knew how much power the permanent members of the Security Council held. I also knew that the “international situation” the experts went on about on TV was, in the end, a power game between nations.
This world was another Murim.

Martial artists flaunted their families and martial arts. Great powers showed off their militaries, economies, production capacity, and other resources, then used that power to crush weaker countries.
At this UN General Assembly, five permanent members—among the most powerful countries in the world—had joined forces to oppose the reestablishment of the World Hunter Federation.
Ordinarily, plenty of countries under their influence would have fallen in line like appendages, whether they liked it or not.
Ordinarily.

“More than twenty countries, including Congo, Syria, Ethiopia, and Myanmar, are on the verge of civil war,” Team Leader Choi said. “Coup factions are rising in the name of public sentiment. Those countries must have wanted a decision as soon as possible. The others aren’t in much better shape.”
“Damn it.”
“Fear is breaking down the rule of law. This is what Michael Silbert wanted.”
Politics had nothing to do with it anymore. This was about survival.
If several big, powerful men blocked the fire hydrant while your house was about to burn to ashes and told you to wait just a little longer, who would obediently turn around and leave?
I understood where those countries were coming from.
But...
*Finding out the fire extinguisher is actually a flamethrower is another matter.*
I had to admit it.
The World Hunter Federation was absolutely necessary.

During the last Great Cataclysm, when terrible flames had spread in every direction, they had played the role of excellent firefighters. They had done their best as heroes more devoted than anyone else.
But Michael Silbert was no firefighter.
What could be a greater black comedy than the person who had secretly started the fire being appointed as the new firefighter?
That was why, three days ago, I had told everyone we had to stop him. Within the time we had been given, we had to use every ounce of our strength to hold Michael Silbert back.
Now the sand in the hourglass we had turned over was almost gone.
After just three days.
“This... isn’t this too soon?”
Team Leader Choi and I weren’t alone in the room.

The Skeleton King’s words came out like a groan. He clenched the papers in his hand, crumpling them badly. Between his fingers, I could see a familiar face printed on one of the sheets: a man looking into the camera, younger than he was now, his expression more human.
Michael Silbert.
Michael Silbert several decades ago, to be precise.
For the past three days, we had been digging through everything brought back from Siegfried Bassmann’s hideout and investigating Michael’s past, searching for anything that might help us stop him.
But Michael Silbert was one of the most famous people in the world. Decades of information had piled up since the Great Cataclysm. There was too much of it, and time wasn’t waiting for us.
“Can’t we stop him?”
I had no answer for the Skeleton King.
Magic Johnson, who had been put in charge of the material from the hideout, might have discovered something by now, but the possibility was slim.
Even when he had come to us by hologram three days earlier, he had already gone over all the material more than ten times—and then gone over it again.
All I had left was a guess bordering on despair.
“Yeah. Probably not.”
“So far, all we’ve done is confirm what everyone already knows.”
A heavy silence settled over the room.
The Skeleton King stared at the mountains of paperwork, his eyes trembling. Then he spoke.
“No. There is still a way.”
“There’s... a way?”
“A very simple one. No need to take the long way around.”
What he said next was the last thing I expected.
“Wicked human, you need only erase this body.”
“What?”
At first, I thought I’d misheard him.
But as I stared at him, the Skeleton King continued calmly.
“Not right away, of course. Reveal my identity in front of everyone, with important people watching, and then erase me. That will make the effect certain.”

“It is a simple solution, is it not? If you have been caught by a weakness so serious that you have no choice but to comply with his demands, then eliminate the weakness. Along with a suitable explanation.”
A chill ran down my spine. Every hair on my body stood on end.
He stood before me as he always did, yet he had never felt more like a stranger.
His deeply sunken gaze. His faint smile. Even his calm voice.
Every part of him.
“This body is a monster. To you humans, I am practically evil itself, and I am also cunning enough to deceive the eyes of insignificant humans and approach them whenever I wish.”
The Skeleton King grinned.

“You, human—I confess that you are not nearly as wicked as I have called you. You are merely absurdly strong and even more stupid. The other humans know that too. If you show them with your actions, they should have little trouble believing you.”
Thump. Thump. Thump.
My heart hammered.
Thoughts tore through my head. My mouth had fallen open, but I couldn’t force a sound out.
*This is fucking insane...*
I had never once considered it. That made it all the more shocking.
Then, as I froze for an instant, a voice pierced my ears like a needle.
“It is a possibility.”
“Team Leader Choi!”
My shout burst out instinctively, but Team Leader Choi did not flinch in the slightest.
His face rigid, he continued.
“A weakness is only a weakness when it’s exposed and an enemy can use it. If you remove it yourself, there’s no problem.”
“What the hell are you talking about right now...”

“The public still loves you, Mr. Jin Taekyung. Although the extermination of the terrorist group brought about the appearance of The Prophet, it was done for the sake of a greater good, and you gave everything you had to save people despite the countless accusations thrown at you. In particular, the self-sacrifice you showed against Leviathan and during the Monster Wave in Munich...”
“Enough!”
My second shout finally stopped him.
But not for long.
“Then what are you going to do?”
“Is there another way? A way to stop Michael Silbert from taking the World Hunter Federation—the entire world—into his hands?”
I couldn’t breathe.
With me at a loss for words, Team Leader Choi let everything he’d been holding back pour out.
“We could hide the Skeleton King somewhere far away, somewhere no one knows, or somewhere no one could ever find him. But if Michael Silbert revealed the truth, would people believe it?”
“But he...”
“Yes, I know. He’s saved many people. He fought beside us in Sichuan, Busan, Japan, and Munich. Perhaps hundreds of thousands of people owe him their lives. But—”
Thud.
Team Leader Choi stepped forward hard, bringing his face close to mine. His eyes held a tangle of emotions, and his voice was firm.
“People don’t believe it.”
His last words dwindled like a dying campfire.
“Because the Skeleton King... is a monster.”

In the heat of battle, a person’s movements began to slow the moment they realized they had been wounded.
Michael believed he could have everything only if he could ignore any pain.
He had lived by that belief ever since the day he returned from the brink of death, long ago.
But today, two things had shaken him.
One was the thrill of being so close to his grand dream.
The other...
*It’s probably that bastard.*
A face flickered through the steam rising from the coffee cups.
A young man far younger than himself, who had won the public’s love in an absurdly short time and become his most troublesome obstacle.
*Jin Taekyung.*
The name lingered in his mouth, accompanied by a faint pain at his throat.
Swish.
Michael carefully pulled down the turtleneck that covered his neck.
A dark-red mark stood out against his skin, warped by a brief surge of heat.
It was the first wound he had suffered in more than a decade.
He was tracing the mark Jin Taekyung had left several days ago when—
Bzzzt.
A phone vibrated somewhere.
His fingertips trembled against the wound, which had yet to heal.
Instinctively, Michael pulled his collar back up and looked at the name on his smartphone screen.
[Emmanuel]
There were many people in the world named Emmanuel.
But only one could contact him directly without going through Huginn.
Click.
“Congratulations, Guild Master.”
The President of France’s voice came through the moment the call connected.
Michael laughed aloud and tipped all three cups of coffee onto the floor.
Out went his anxiety and agitation, along with the face that had appeared in the hazy steam.
Once he had poured it all away, nothing remained in the empty cups but joy and triumph.
*I... won.*
The throne was ready.
All that remained was a magnificent coronation.
Michael found himself wondering what expression Jin Taekyung wore now that he had heard the news.
The scene came so vividly to mind that his lips twitched.
It was strange.
Something that should never have happened had come to pass, yet I felt oddly calm.
Probably because I’d seen it coming.
“Fuck.”
Still, I had to do what needed to be done.
It wasn’t like I could shout, *Yay!*
Having cursed out of habit, I looked at Team Leader Choi, who had just come through the door.
“So... we couldn’t stop it?”
Team Leader Choi nodded gravely.
“There was only so much we could do.”
“Even with Russia helping us?
Russia, of all countries?”
“Even if the United Kingdom had joined us instead of remaining neutral at this General Assembly, I doubt the result would have changed much.
We’re already effectively at war.”
Even someone as clueless about politics as I was knew how much power the permanent members of the Security Council held.
I also knew that the “international situation” the experts went on about on TV was, in the end, a power game between nations.
This world was another Murim.
Martial artists flaunted their families and martial arts.
Great powers showed off their militaries, economies, production capacity, and other resources, then used that power to crush weaker countries.
At this UN General Assembly, five permanent members—among the most powerful countries in the world—had joined forces to oppose the reestablishment of the World Hunter Federation.
Ordinarily, plenty of countries under their influence would have fallen in line like appendages, whether they liked it or not.
Ordinarily.
“More than twenty countries, including Congo, Syria, Ethiopia, and Myanmar, are on the verge of civil war,” Team Leader Choi said.
“Coup factions are rising in the name of public sentiment.
Those countries must have wanted a decision as soon as possible.
The others aren’t in much better shape.”
“Damn it.”
“Fear is breaking down the rule of law.
This is what Michael Silbert wanted.”
Politics had nothing to do with it anymore.
This was about survival.
If several big, powerful men blocked the fire hydrant while your house was about to burn to ashes and told you to wait just a little longer, who would obediently turn around and leave?
I understood where those countries were coming from.
But...
*Finding out the fire extinguisher is actually a flamethrower is another matter.*
I had to admit it.
The World Hunter Federation was absolutely necessary.
During the last Great Cataclysm, when terrible flames had spread in every direction, they had played the role of excellent firefighters.
They had done their best as heroes more devoted than anyone else.
But Michael Silbert was no firefighter.
What could be a greater black comedy than the person who had secretly started the fire being appointed as the new firefighter?
That was why, three days ago, I had told everyone we had to stop him.
Within the time we had been given, we had to use every ounce of our strength to hold Michael Silbert back.
Now the sand in the hourglass we had turned over was almost gone.
After just three days.
“This... isn’t this too soon?”
Team Leader Choi and I weren’t alone in the room.
The Skeleton King’s words came out like a groan.
He clenched the papers in his hand, crumpling them badly.
Between his fingers, I could see a familiar face printed on one of the sheets: a man looking into the camera, younger than he was now, his expression more human.
Michael Silbert.
Michael Silbert several decades ago, to be precise.
For the past three days, we had been digging through everything brought back from Siegfried Bassmann’s hideout and investigating Michael’s past, searching for anything that might help us stop him.
But Michael Silbert was one of the most famous people in the world.
Decades of information had piled up since the Great Cataclysm.
There was too much of it, and time wasn’t waiting for us.
“Can’t we stop him?”
I had no answer for the Skeleton King.
Magic Johnson, who had been put in charge of the material from the hideout, might have discovered something by now, but the possibility was slim.
Even when he had come to us by hologram three days earlier, he had already gone over all the material more than ten times—and then gone over it again.
All I had left was a guess bordering on despair.
“Yeah.
Probably not.”
“So far, all we’ve done is confirm what everyone already knows.”
A heavy silence settled over the room.
The Skeleton King stared at the mountains of paperwork, his eyes trembling.
Then he spoke.
“No.
There is still a way.”
“There’s... a way?”
“A very simple one.
No need to take the long way around.”
What he said next was the last thing I expected.
“Wicked human, you need only erase this body.”
“What?”
At first, I thought I’d misheard him.
But as I stared at him, the Skeleton King continued calmly.
“Not right away, of course.
Reveal my identity in front of everyone, with important people watching, and then erase me.
That will make the effect certain.”
“It is a simple solution, is it not?
If you have been caught by a weakness so serious that you have no choice but to comply with his demands, then eliminate the weakness.
Along with a suitable explanation.”
A chill ran down my spine.
Every hair on my body stood on end.
He stood before me as he always did, yet he had never felt more like a stranger.
His deeply sunken gaze.
His faint smile.
Even his calm voice.
Every part of him.
“This body is a monster.
To you humans, I am practically evil itself, and I am also cunning enough to deceive the eyes of insignificant humans and approach them whenever I wish.”
The Skeleton King grinned.
“You, human—I confess that you are not nearly as wicked as I have called you.
You are merely absurdly strong and even more stupid.
The other humans know that too.
If you show them with your actions, they should have little trouble believing you.”
Thump.
Thump.
Thump.
My heart hammered.
Thoughts tore through my head.
My mouth had fallen open, but I couldn’t force a sound out.
*This is fucking insane...*
I had never once considered it.
That made it all the more shocking.
Then, as I froze for an instant, a voice pierced my ears like a needle.
“It is a possibility.”
“Team Leader Choi!”
My shout burst out instinctively, but Team Leader Choi did not flinch in the slightest.
His face rigid, he continued.
“A weakness is only a weakness when it’s exposed and an enemy can use it.
If you remove it yourself, there’s no problem.”
“What the hell are you talking about right now...”
“The public still loves you, Mr.
Jin Taekyung.

Although the extermination of the terrorist group brought about the appearance of The Prophet, it was done for the sake of a greater good, and you gave everything you had to save people despite the countless accusations thrown at you.
In particular, the self-sacrifice you showed against Leviathan and during the Monster Wave in Munich...”
“Enough!”
My second shout finally stopped him.
But not for long.
“Then what are you going to do?”
“Is there another way?
A way to stop Michael Silbert from taking the World Hunter Federation—the entire world—into his hands?”
I couldn’t breathe.
With me at a loss for words, Team Leader Choi let everything he’d been holding back pour out.
“We could hide the Skeleton King somewhere far away, somewhere no one knows, or somewhere no one could ever find him.
But if Michael Silbert revealed the truth, would people believe it?”
“But he...”
“Yes, I know.
He’s saved many people.
He fought beside us in Sichuan, Busan, Japan, and Munich.
Perhaps hundreds of thousands of people owe him their lives.
But—”
Thud.
Team Leader Choi stepped forward hard, bringing his face close to mine.
His eyes held a tangle of emotions, and his voice was firm.
“People don’t believe it.”
His last words dwindled like a dying campfire.
“Because the Skeleton King... is a monster.”

chapters.title: Chapter 770
paragraphs: “Because the Skeleton King... is a monster.”
Silence followed as Team Leader Choi’s voice faded. But his last words kept echoing in someone’s ears.
*A monster... A monster, huh.*
The Skeleton King turned the bitter truth over in his mind.
It was true. He was a monster.
Monsters were humanity’s greatest and worst enemy in all of history. And among them, he wielded the cursed power of death.
He might look human now, but once the Magic shrouding his body fell away, all that would remain was the skeleton of a dead man who had defied his mortal fate.
That was the only truth.
*Yes. That’s all there is.*
The Skeleton King looked down at his hands, indistinguishable from a human’s, then raised his head.
Before him stood a young human with a familiar face, though his expression was so twisted he almost looked like a stranger.
The strongest being the Skeleton King had ever seen. Foolish, too, and therefore unable to accept the truth before his eyes.
But if they were to take the only way out, they had to accept that truth and use it.
“That human is right. It is all true.”
So many emotions filled Jin Taekyung’s strained voice. A few months ago, the Skeleton King would not have known what to call them. Now he did.
He shook his head at Jin, who could say no more.
“No matter what you say, this is the only way.”
“This body is a monster. Whatever the reason, we cannot be allowed to remain together.”
Of course, some might understand even after the truth came out. They might trust Jin Taekyung and accept that the Skeleton King was different from the monsters they knew.
But...
“How many of them do you think would truly accept this truth?”
The Skeleton King pointed toward the closed window.
Most of the humans out there were ordinary people. They could hardly help hating monsters to the bone. Monsters had taken their families, their friends, or the people they loved.
Monsters killed humans, and humans killed monsters.
The chain forged with the descent of the Demon King Asmodeus was too thick and strong for anyone to break.
Not even a young hero loved by everyone was exempt. No—if everything came to light, he could no longer be the hero he had been.
“Many will condemn you, and Michael Silbert will get everything. So...”
His voice trailed off. Turning away from Jin Taekyung, the Skeleton King put a hand on the doorknob and added one last thing.
“Erase this body in front of everyone.”
Click.
The door closed behind him.
The Skeleton King crossed the hallway in silence without looking back. The lights overhead were bright, but the path before him was dark.
Like that place filled with thick fog and the energy of death.
Like the Gate he had been unable to leave from the moment he first opened his eyes—until one unexpected day, a human had taken him away.
*What am I? What’s my name? My past? My homeland?*
He thought he finally knew the answer to the questions that had come to haunt him.
He was a monster.
A cruel, savage monster without a trace of reason.
A being born of pure evil, incapable of living alongside humans.
That was the truth. No—it had to be the truth.
Faced with a reality he had no choice but to accept, the Skeleton King gave a hollow laugh.
*Damn it. I’ll never be able to go to a club again.*
And yet, for some reason, part of him felt relieved.
He was a monster without a heart, incapable of even ordinary emotions.
He was supposed to be.
You didn’t need anyone to tell you. Living day to day taught you soon enough: life was a series of choices.
They weren’t all grand ones. Small decisions started the moment you opened your eyes in the morning.
*Get up or stay in bed? If I get up, take a shower? Or just wash my face and hair before heading out?*
It depended on the situation. If you woke earlier than expected, you could sleep a little longer. If you were worried about being late, you could skip the shower.
What mattered was considering the result before you chose.
Because you were the one who had to live with it.
And right now, I stood at a crossroads where I could barely bear either choice.
“You... fucking lunatic.”
I barely managed to force the words out.
I might have been cursing the one who had left, or the other person still in the room.
Or maybe myself, unable to go one way or the other.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
My tangled thoughts made my head throb. At the quiet voice in my ear, I closed my eyes without a word.
“You must choose.”
It felt like an invisible awl had gone straight through my skull. Every word made the headache worse.
“He has already chosen his path. A sacrifice that only he could decide to make...”
I grabbed him. Thud!
I didn’t know when I’d opened my eyes, much less how I’d ended up gripping Team Leader Choi by the collar.
Riiip.
The collar of his crumpled designer shirt tore under the force of my grip. Above my whitening knuckles, a pair of eyes silently gazed at me.
“Do as you wish. Beat me to a pulp. Break my limbs, or even kill me. But...”
His breath trembled. So did his voice.
“Afterward, you must choose. You must.”
“You know time won’t wait for us.”
His words, his gaze—the strength went out of me all at once.
The energy boiling through my entire body as if it were about to explode, the hand clenched with all its strength—everything felt strangely unfamiliar.
I stumbled back as if I’d come to my senses after being possessed.
“...I’m sorry.”
I knew Team Leader Choi had done nothing wrong. Everything he had said was true. It was simply the only solution capable of breaking through this situation.
If the Skeleton King hadn’t offered it himself, Team Leader Choi would never have said a word.
That was who he was.
His cool judgment had shown him the only solution, but he had the decency not to force that sacrifice on someone else.
Some might call him a hypocrite. I wouldn’t. I knew the Skeleton King wasn’t just another monster to be killed and disposed of to him, any more than he was to me.
*Even if he were the one who had to sacrifice himself, he would have offered it as the solution before anyone else.*
Unlike me, Team Leader Choi was a born leader.
If the choice had been his instead of mine, he wouldn’t have run from it. He might have suffered alone, but he wouldn’t have turned away from the truth like a coward.
*Damn it.*
Time wouldn’t wait for us.
At the thought of his words, another world waiting for me beyond this one flashed before my eyes.
Murim.
If the Main Quest hadn’t blocked the Login function, if I could spend far longer thinking about this there, what would I choose?
No. Given enough time, would I even be able to choose?
*And could I live with the result?*
I’d fought countless battles. I’d struggled to survive and fought to protect my people.
But both paths before me ended in pain.
If I refused to sacrifice the Skeleton King, this world would fall into Michael Silbert’s hands. If I did sacrifice him... I didn’t think I could bear it.
Somewhere along the way, the Skeleton King had become my friend.
A comrade I’d fought beside. A friend.
Not someone I could sacrifice for the sake of the greater good.
*I’d have to erase him. Do it myself, in front of everyone.*
A cheap trick like using the Inventory to fake his Erasure wouldn’t work. Michael Silbert wasn’t that careless.
Proving I had complete control over the Skeleton King wouldn’t change anything, either.
To humanity, monsters were a raw nerve no one could touch. Hadn’t decades of experiments already shown that monsters could never be tamed?
The Skeleton King was unprecedented. But some truths were rejected the moment they became known.
*In the end... there’s only one answer.*
I closed my eyes. Countless thoughts flashed through my mind, and then I spoke.
“Team Leader Choi.”
He had been waiting in silence for my decision.
“Go ahead.”
“Is there any chance the approval to reestablish the World Hunter Federation could be revoked?”
“Why do you suddenly—”
“Just answer me.”
I opened my eyes. Team Leader Choi studied me with a conflicted look before replying.
“There is no chance of that.”
“You’re sure?”
“Yes.”
“Why?”

“The World Hunter Federation is now indispensable. Given the current situation, with magical power levels rising every day, it is the only way to stop a spark that has already been lit from spreading.”
“Even if something happens to me or that bastard?”
His eyes shook violently. A moment later, he understood what I meant and shouted.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung!”
But I had already chosen.
Neither the first path nor the second. A third one, dark and choked with thorns.
I would kill Michael Silbert, the man at the center of it all.
“No!”
“Nothing’s impossible. It’s just difficult.”
I answered calmly and kept going before he could interrupt.
“If I pull this off... you’ll need to make your move, Team Leader Choi. Magic Johnson will do everything he can to help.”
“Stop! Stop talking!”

“There’s Chuck Hagel, Faye Chen, and Prince Felix too. Get the support of the S-rank Hunters you’ve built ties with and the nations friendly to us. Then take control of the reestablished World Hunter Federation.”
“I don’t want to hear it! And how could I possibly...?”
“Your maternal grandfather walked that path. If you can make people understand the weight of Cheon Taemin’s name, you have a shot. If that seems impossible, you could back Magic Johnson instead.”
I grinned.
“Well, you’re smart enough to figure it out yourself.”
“Still, one more thing, just in case. Even if Michael Silbert loses his head, the rest of his organization will remain. You should find those people and get rid of them first—”
Shing.
A cold sound cut me off.
A sword stood in my way.
Team Leader Choi had drawn the *Hero’s Sword* without my noticing. He glared at me, his face set.
“You’re not going.”
“Hmm. I don’t think you can stop me.”
“Nothing’s impossible. It’s just difficult.”
He threw my words back at me. I stepped toward him.
“Fine. I was going to rough you up anyway. This works out.”
“What do you mean?”
“Everyone knows we’re close. If I beat you half to a pulp before I leave, it might keep them from getting suspicious.”
Team Leader Choi gritted his teeth. A dazzling aura flared around him, its immense power rippling along the blade and stirring the air.
Rumble. Whoooosh!
A tremor spread through the entire building. The wind rose into a gale.
“You really do have talent. You’ve improved a lot.”
I gave him a calm smile and was about to step forward when—
Bzzzt.
A faint vibration sounded from somewhere, cutting through the tension between us.

A dazzling aura flared around him, its immense power rippling along the blade and stirring the air.
Rumble.
Whoooosh!
A tremor spread through the entire building.
The wind rose into a gale.
“You really do have talent.
You’ve improved a lot.”
I gave him a calm smile and was about to step forward when—
Bzzzt.
A faint vibration sounded from somewhere, cutting through the tension between us.

chapters.title: Chapter 771
paragraphs: Bzzzt.
It wasn’t hard to identify the vibration. I had something in my own pocket that made a similar sound.
“Team Leader Choi, looks like you’re getting a call. Aren’t you going to answer?”
“Don’t worry about it. That isn’t what matters right now.”
“What, afraid I’ll jump you while you’re on the phone?”
“That...”
Team Leader Choi trailed off.
The fact that we were facing off at all was absurd. No matter how gifted he was or how quickly he’d improved, he couldn’t stop me.
The only reason he was still on his feet was that I was letting him stay there. I was holding back for a friend I had no choice but to bring down.
And I had another reason to hold back.
“If someone’s calling your direct line, it must be important. Go ahead and answer. I need to wait for enough witnesses to gather anyway.”
“Witnesses...?”
“Yes. Witnesses.”
I watched Team Leader Choi turn the word over in his mind, then went on.
“The more people who see what happens next, the better. For all of us.”
There was no other way.

Team Leader Choi and I had been in the same boat for a long time. If I killed Michael Silbert, he’d be implicated as my accomplice. And it wouldn’t stop with him. The Peace Guild, the Ares Guild, my family and friends—everyone connected to me would be hurt.
That would be the end of everything.
*To prevent the worst, I have to draw a line between us where plenty of people can see it.*
Soon, I’d be a criminal as notorious as The Prophet, if not more so.
A traitor to humanity who, when a longtime comrade confronted him about joining forces with an undead monster, struck him down without hesitation and fled with the monster.
And... the murderer who killed Michael Silbert, the hero of the age, in broad daylight.
“A couple of broken bones won’t be the end of it. While you’re taking the call, check that you have a potion ready.”
Team Leader Choi bit his lip.
“...You’re serious.”
“I’ve thought it through. I know which road I’m taking.”
At some point, I’d gained too many things to protect. Every choice demanded that I think it through, then think it through again.
But once I’d decided, I had to cast hesitation aside. The moment I looked back, I’d hesitate. I’d leave an opening.
Little by little, I’d learned not to look back.
In Murim. In the modern world.
Among monsters that came charging at me to kill me, and loathsome people even worse than the monsters.
“This is the path I chose. Right now, it’s the best one.”
Sacrifice the Skeleton King, or hand the world to Michael Silbert.
I couldn’t choose either. So I’d made a different decision.
Rather than let Michael control me like a puppet, I would kill a hero and become a traitor who had joined forces with a monster.
Even if that was what it took, I would tear out the root of this disaster.
*He dies by my hand today.*
Whoosh.
A scorching heat spread throughout my body. Spitting out a single word as though I were chewing it to pieces, I unleashed the qi wave I had drawn up to its limit in every direction.
Rumble!
A violent tremor shook not just the building, but the surrounding area.
The force dwarfed anything Team Leader Choi had released. The hologram television, which had been playing silently, crackled and shut off. Alarms throughout the building began to wail.
Beep, beep! Weeeee!
“What the hell is—ah!”
“Aaaah!”
“Emergency! This is an emergency! Everyone, please evacuate!”
The murmurs that Team Leader Choi’s earlier tremor had stirred up turned to screams.

Amid the countless footsteps passing outside the door and the desperate shouts they were vomiting out, Team Leader Choi, who had been staring at me with a hollow expression, suddenly raised the *Hero’s Sword*.
Thunk!

The silver blade plunged into the floor, slicing through it like tofu. He squeezed his eyes shut, then opened them and pulled a smartphone and a potion from inside his clothes as though he had resigned himself to everything.
Then I saw his eyes widen. A moment later, his fingers flew across the screen.
Flash.
A huge man appeared in midair amid the glow of a hologram. Magic Johnson looked more frantic than I’d ever seen him.
“Damn it. Why are you taking so long to answer? Did you look at the materials I sent? I found something strange a little while ago—wait, what the hell is going on here?”
He looked from Team Leader Choi to me. I didn’t answer. I strode toward him.
More precisely, toward the documents in his hand.
*This is...*
Several photographs. Pages packed with tiny text.
My eyes were sharp enough to take in every detail in barely a dozen seconds. As I read, possibilities I’d never considered began to take shape.
*Why the hell would this...? Wait. If that’s true...*
One thought led to another, tangling with the rest. A pale fog filled my mind, and I groped for whatever lay hidden inside it.
“Ah.”
The sound escaped my lips. The energy roiling inside me, ready to explode, began to settle.
Fwoosh.
My qi wave dispersed, and the tremors slowly died away.
But my gaze wavered more than ever, as did my mind after glimpsing the true shape of something beyond the fog filling my head.
*If this is true...*
Yes. If it really was...
Unable to finish the thought, I stared blankly at Magic Johnson. Then I turned to Team Leader Choi—and to the *Hero’s Sword* planted in the floor before him like Excalibur.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes?”
“Why did you pull your sword out all of a sudden? You scared me.”
“What?”
“I need to think. Put it away and calm everyone down. It’s really loud out there.”
“...What?”
*What the hell? Is he insane?*
Reading the thought plainly conveyed through Team Leader Choi’s eyes, I let out a hollow laugh.
No matter how people around us looked at me, I continued to quietly chuckle to myself like a madman for quite some time before suddenly slapping both cheeks hard.
Smack!
Maybe a little too hard.
The full-force slap rattled my skull, but it brought my mind back from its brief AWOL stint before it got beyond the garrison limits.
*All right.*
Finally back in the room, I looked at the two men’s bewildered faces and spoke.
“All right, everyone. Now let’s all...”
Good breathing. Good emotion.
Deliver the last part solemnly.
“Let’s carve out a fourth path where every last fucking bastard dies and we survive.”
Team Leader Choi’s and Magic Johnson’s eyes twitched at my grand, solemn declaration.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung...”
“Hey, Jin...”
What more needed to be said?
I gave a faint smile and nodded as though I understood everything.
The new hope I’d glimpsed at the last moment had lit a heat somewhere inside me, different from Scorching Yang Qi. It kept welling up.
No. It was overflowing.
Drip. Splash!
“...What the fuck?”
Was it really going to overflow?
Heat—or rather, a torrent of red liquid—gushed from my nostrils, which had opened up with refreshing force before the fourth path even had a chance to do so. The two men’s gazes went cold.
“You have a nosebleed. A really bad one.”
“It reminds me of the fountain in the plaza of my mansion. More precisely, it looks like the baby angel built into the fountain is pissing like that.”
“You should have slapped yourself more gently.”
“He’s going to pass out from blood loss at this rate. Choi, do you have a potion?”
“I took one out just now. I didn’t expect to use it for this...”
“Good. Give it to Jin. And what did you mean by a fourth path? No, never mind. Stop the nosebleed first, then explain.”
“Here, take it. And step back a little, please. You’re spraying blood.”
As I accepted the potion from Team Leader Choi, I thought that going straight to fight Michael Silbert might have looked a lot cooler than this.
But this was me.
A man who might look anything but cool right now, who might make a damn fool of himself, but would still struggle for the best outcome he could get.
A realistic man busting his ass for the sake of this world where no one could see him, the true man of this era who was—
“What are you doing? Swallow it. All in one gulp.”
“Jin, do you have trouble taking potions? Want me to help?”
Team Leader Choi was nagging me like a mother-in-law. Magic Johnson had started licking his lips for some reason. I looked at them in alarm, then hurriedly emptied the potion into my mouth.
Ssshhh.
Ice-cold healing energy coursed through me. The tremors stopped as if they’d never happened, and the hologram television came back on.
A familiar face filled the screen.
Gray hair. Gray eyes.

The man looked as though he had been born somewhere between light and darkness. He stood before countless camera flashes and cameras, continuing to speak without sound. Stark subtitles ran beneath him.

**Live:** UN Emergency General Assembly Approves Reestablishment of World Hunter Federation by Overwhelming Vote **Michael Silbert:** I offer my wholehearted praise for the UN’s decision on behalf of humanity, and propose an inaugural ceremony for the newly reestablished World Hunter Federation.
“Turn off mute!”
Beep.
At Team Leader Choi’s urgent command, the sound trapped in the speakers rushed out like a flood.
“Does that statement mean that you intend to become the representative of the World Hunter Federation yourself?”
“Michael! Can an inaugural ceremony really be held in a situation like this?”
“When and where would you like it to be held?”
“We’re from the *Washington Post*. Please give us a statement!”
The questions came like screams.
So many reporters surrounded Michael Silbert that the cameras couldn’t fit them all in. He answered none of them, merely waving a hand with a grave expression.
Swish.
He was a hologram. In reality, he had to be several kilometers away at the very least. Yet it all felt vivid.
The air around him. The sense that the entire scene had been arranged for him alone.
The presence of that man, radiating suffocating majesty simply by being seen and heard.
Only Michael Silbert was free to speak there now.
“I swear to God, I proposed the reestablishment of the World Hunter Federation three days ago for one reason alone: for this world, for humanity.”
I could feel it. The tumult wrapping around them.
And there he stood beneath a spotlight brighter than any he’d known in his life: a born agitator and orator.
“The representative of the World Hunter Federation should go to someone other than me. A living savior, the hero of the Great Cataclysm who already saved humanity from the Demon King once before!”
His voice, infused with internal energy, carried on and on. Overcome with excitement, people looked to the sky and cried out.
Sky. Slayer. Cheon Taemin.
Many names for one man. But a considerable number of people were chanting another name, too.
Michael Silbert.
As the fervor spread like fire, he pressed on.

“The inaugural ceremony will be held without fail. Whether it is the mad terrorist who calls himself The Prophet, any monster whatsoever, or even the return of the Demon King, the Hunters of the World Hunter Federation will gather in one place, choose their representative, and swear that they have become humanity’s sword and shield!”
“Waaaaah!”
My ears rang. I could hear the roar now without the speakers.
Through the cracks around the tightly shut door, I heard the whole city shouting as one.
No. Perhaps it was happening all over the world.
Everywhere light reached and electricity flowed.
All those people cheering for the hero shining alone at the center of it, without the faintest idea that he was behind everything.
As the fervor swelled beyond anything the crowd could contain, Michael Silbert spoke with more force in his eyes and voice than ever before.
To the people caught up in it. To the cameras trained on him.
Or perhaps...
“Two days from now. Seoul, Korea.”
*Toward me—the one who could do nothing but watch him from here.*
Michael Silbert made his declaration to the world.
“In the savior’s homeland, where the World Hunter Federation first began, we will rise once more, just as we did then.”

chapters.title: Chapter 772
paragraphs: The incitement, the speech, the declaration—it was over.
But the enormous roar did not end. It continued without pause.
Reporters’ cameras caught the crowds pouring into the streets, while their microphones picked up cheers shouted in half-hoarse voices. Everywhere felt like a festival.
Only days ago, disaster had descended on this city. Now an inexplicable hope and joy filled it. Those feelings gathered and flowed toward one man.
“Michael! Michael!”
They chanted his name and applauded with all they had.
For a very long time. With all their strength.
They poured out their gratitude and respect for a true hero who had stepped forward for their sake, without the slightest desire for the immense power of the World Hunter Federation.
Their hero stood on the stage and gazed at them, his face full of emotion. Then, unable to hold back his tears, he turned and hurried away.
The retreating figure of a hero who had always seemed so strong was beautiful.
From behind.
“You’ve arrived.”
Huginn was waiting below the stage. He gave a slight bow and gestured, and the Odin Guild’s Hunters hurried to block the reporters following Michael.
“Please step back.”
“Just a moment. It’ll only take—”
“I’m sorry, but not today.”
As Michael walked on, the bright lights and the cheers gradually faded behind him. He wiped the tears from the corners of his eyes and spoke in a dry voice.
“They responded well. Better than I expected.”
“They needed hope that badly. And those tears at the end—you were magnificent.”
“Did you think I was acting?”
Huginn slowed at the unexpected question.
“You... meant them?”
“I did. Though I’m not sure I felt what they did.”
Tears were strange things. They came with joy, sadness, anger—even emotions the person shedding them could not easily name.
His tears had been closest to that last kind.
*What was it?*
Joy at finally reaching his grand objective?
Or... a few of the fragments of feeling he had left?
Michael Silbert thought about the reason for his tears, which even he did not know, but soon shook his head inwardly.
He did not always need to find the right answer.
If he had tried to find the right answer to every problem he had faced, he would not be standing here now.
No. He would have died decades ago.
On that day.
“Guild Master?”
Huginn’s voice broke into his thoughts.
“Go on.”
“I have something to report. Just before you began your speech...”
“The small disturbance on the outskirts of the city?”
“You’ve already received a report?”
“No. I sensed it, faintly.”
Huginn, who had been following behind him, stopped short. Michael Silbert smiled faintly.
“Surprised?”
“To be honest, yes.”
“I thought you might be.”
The disturbance had been considerable, but it had happened several kilometers away. Michael recalled the sensation that had swept over him.

“It surprised me too. Heat reached me from all that way off, so suddenly it felt as though every hair on my body might stand on end. For an instant, it was as if I could look down over the entire city.”
“...Guild Master, could it be—”
“I know what you’re thinking, but I wouldn’t worry. I only felt it that intensely for a moment.”
Michael muttered, almost to himself, “Perhaps I’ve been training too hard.”
“You should stop training for a while.”
“I’ve already been holding back. I did push myself too hard this past year. Perhaps I grew impatient without realizing it.”
He already knew what had made him impatient.
As well as the identity of the intense heat he had suddenly felt in the distance just before beginning his speech.
“What happened to Jin Taekyung? If it had been an emergency, you would have interrupted me in the middle of the speech. It can’t have been too serious.”
“According to the watchers, the Stone-King left the hotel first. Not long afterward, the area shook.”
“The top floor where they’re staying must have been the source.”
“Yes. Then everything went quiet, as if nothing had happened.”
“The monster left first. What else?”
“They tried various types of magic after approaching as closely as possible, but both the view inside and even the sounds were blocked, so...”
“That’s enough. I’d expect as much.”
Michael fell into thought. Then he murmured, “It seems they’ve had a disagreement.”
“A disagreement?”
“They must differ on what to do. And judging by what Jin Taekyung has shown us, he may do something even more reckless than we expect.”
“If you mean *that* reckless, surely...”
“What else? He doesn’t have many options in this situation.”
Huginn’s eyes widened. Michael continued.

“Increase security and strengthen the surveillance network until the inaugural ceremony. In particular, don’t take your eyes off that monster for even a moment. He is the most important key to this entire affair—he cannot be left out of it.”
“Understood.”
Huginn answered grimly, then asked, “Wouldn’t it be better to use this opportunity to capture the monster alive?”
“Capture him?”
“Yes. If they hide him, or reveal his identity and sacrifice him before we can...”
“Huginn.”
Michael cut him off gently and looked at his right-hand man.
“I told you before that Jin Taekyung has a more fatal weakness than anyone else. Do you remember what it is?”
“His emotions...?”
“Exactly. And that is why he has no choice but to hold on to the monster until the very end.”
“You mean...”
“Yes. Somewhere along the way, Jin Taekyung began to think of the monster as a friend.”
“Funny, isn’t it?”
Michael could not suppress a quiet laugh.

Even though he was remembered as one of the heroes of the Great Cataclysm, there had been plenty of walls in his way. Back then, he had not been overwhelmingly powerful, and the Odin Guild could hardly have been called a major guild.
So he had become stronger. He had brought down the walls and rivals before him by any means necessary.
But it was truly laughable.
And now? He had built a force and fighting strength no one could ignore, only to find that the obstacle in his path was the softest-hearted bastard he had ever faced.
*Idiot.*
