sentences.text: The incitement, the speech, the declaration—it was over.
But the enormous roar did not end.
It continued without pause.
Reporters’ cameras caught the crowds pouring into the streets, while their microphones picked up cheers shouted in half-hoarse voices.
Everywhere felt like a festival.
Only days ago, disaster had descended on this city.
Now an inexplicable hope and joy filled it.
Those feelings gathered and flowed toward one man.
“Michael!
Michael!”
They chanted his name and applauded with all they had.
For a very long time.
With all their strength.
They poured out their gratitude and respect for a true hero who had stepped forward for their sake, without the slightest desire for the immense power of the World Hunter Federation.
Their hero stood on the stage and gazed at them, his face full of emotion.
Then, unable to hold back his tears, he turned and hurried away.
The retreating figure of a hero who had always seemed so strong was beautiful.
From behind.
“You’ve arrived.”
Huginn was waiting below the stage.
He gave a slight bow and gestured, and the Odin Guild’s Hunters hurried to block the reporters following Michael.
“Please step back.”
“Just a moment.
It’ll only take—”
“I’m sorry, but not today.”
As Michael walked on, the bright lights and the cheers gradually faded behind him.
He wiped the tears from the corners of his eyes and spoke in a dry voice.
“They responded well.
Better than I expected.”
“They needed hope that badly.
And those tears at the end—you were magnificent.”
“Did you think I was acting?”
Huginn slowed at the unexpected question.
“You... meant them?”
“I did.
Though I’m not sure I felt what they did.”
Tears were strange things.
They came with joy, sadness, anger—even emotions the person shedding them could not easily name.
His tears had been closest to that last kind.
*What was it?*
Joy at finally reaching his grand objective?
Or... a few of the fragments of feeling he had left?
Michael Silbert thought about the reason for his tears, which even he did not know, but soon shook his head inwardly.
He did not always need to find the right answer.
If he had tried to find the right answer to every problem he had faced, he would not be standing here now.
No.
He would have died decades ago.
On that day.
“Guild Master?”
Huginn’s voice broke into his thoughts.
“Go on.”
“I have something to report.
Just before you began your speech...”
“The small disturbance on the outskirts of the city?”
“You’ve already received a report?”
“No.
I sensed it, faintly.”
Huginn, who had been following behind him, stopped short.
Michael Silbert smiled faintly.
“Surprised?”
“To be honest, yes.”
“I thought you might be.”
The disturbance had been considerable, but it had happened several kilometers away.
Michael recalled the sensation that had swept over him.
“It surprised me too.
Heat reached me from all that way off, so suddenly it felt as though every hair on my body might stand on end.
For an instant, it was as if I could look down over the entire city.”
“...Guild Master, could it be—”
“I know what you’re thinking, but I wouldn’t worry.
I only felt it that intensely for a moment.”
Michael muttered, almost to himself, “Perhaps I’ve been training too hard.”
“You should stop training for a while.”
“I’ve already been holding back.
I did push myself too hard this past year.
Perhaps I grew impatient without realizing it.”
He already knew what had made him impatient.
As well as the identity of the intense heat he had suddenly felt in the distance just before beginning his speech.
“What happened to Jin Taekyung?
If it had been an emergency, you would have interrupted me in the middle of the speech.
It can’t have been too serious.”
“According to the watchers, the Stone-King left the hotel first.
Not long afterward, the area shook.”
“The top floor where they’re staying must have been the source.”
“Yes.
Then everything went quiet, as if nothing had happened.”
“The monster left first.
What else?”
“They tried various types of magic after approaching as closely as possible, but both the view inside and even the sounds were blocked, so...”
“That’s enough.
I’d expect as much.”
Michael fell into thought.
Then he murmured, “It seems they’ve had a disagreement.”
“A disagreement?”
“They must differ on what to do.
And judging by what Jin Taekyung has shown us, he may do something even more reckless than we expect.”
“If you mean *that* reckless, surely...”
“What else?
He doesn’t have many options in this situation.”
Huginn’s eyes widened.
Michael continued.
“Increase security and strengthen the surveillance network until the inaugural ceremony.
In particular, don’t take your eyes off that monster for even a moment.
He is the most important key to this entire affair—he cannot be left out of it.”
“Understood.”
Huginn answered grimly, then asked, “Wouldn’t it be better to use this opportunity to capture the monster alive?”
“Capture him?”
“Yes.
If they hide him, or reveal his identity and sacrifice him before we can...”
“Huginn.”
Michael cut him off gently and looked at his right-hand man.
“I told you before that Jin Taekyung has a more fatal weakness than anyone else.
Do you remember what it is?”
“His emotions...?”
“Exactly.
And that is why he has no choice but to hold on to the monster until the very end.”
“You mean...”
“Yes.
Somewhere along the way, Jin Taekyung began to think of the monster as a friend.”
“Funny, isn’t it?”
Michael could not suppress a quiet laugh.
Even though he was remembered as one of the heroes of the Great Cataclysm, there had been plenty of walls in his way.
Back then, he had not been overwhelmingly powerful, and the Odin Guild could hardly have been called a major guild.
So he had become stronger.
He had brought down the walls and rivals before him by any means necessary.
But it was truly laughable.

chapters.title: Chapter 773
paragraphs: It was good to have somewhere to return to. Better still if there were people waiting for me there.
“Team Leader Choi! Taekyung!”
After several hours of flying, we arrived at Incheon Airport. From far away, a hairy giant came thundering toward us with both arms spread wide.
Whump!
The air caught in my throat.
Even as Im Kkeokjeong squeezed us in a hug that felt more like a chokehold, Team Leader Choi and I patted his shoulders while he sobbed.
It just felt like the thing to do.
“Why are you crying? Hit menopause already?”
“You’ve been okay—waaah! You’re not hurt anywhere—waaaah!”
“We’re fine. Please calm down.”
“I was so worried, so worried—sniff!”
Going by appearances, even the Green Forest Alliance Leader would have to step aside for him. But when it came to being sensitive, no one could match him.
The man’s outside and inside couldn’t have been more different.
And from over Im Kkeokjeong’s shoulder came a voice as clear and direct as the impression its owner gave.
“You should say *we* were worried, not *I*. What does that make me when you put it like that?”
Song Song stopped and looked Team Leader Choi and me over carefully.
“Hmm. You both look better than I expected.”
I asked in return,
“Are you sure? I’ll be suffocated in five minutes at this rate.”
“That’s five minutes from now. You look fine at the moment.”
“Can’t you see how bloodshot my eyes are? I haven’t slept properly in three days.”
“Why? You look much better than you did on TV a few days ago.”
She added, “Your eyes were completely gone then. You looked like you were about to drop dead.”
“...And now?”
“Hard to say. Like you might die in a hundred years or so?”
I couldn’t think of an answer, so I grinned.
Song Song was right. My body was exhausted, but my mind was incomparably clearer than it had been a few days ago.
Team Leader Choi’s was, too.
“How did the matter I asked you to handle go?” he asked.
“I delivered your instructions properly—to both the Peace and Ares Guilds. Once I narrowed the list down, there weren’t even ten people. But the ones I chose are all staunch loyalists.”
“Is there any chance the information leaked?”
“I picked only the most trustworthy senior members of the two Guilds. All their families are in Korea, too.”
“Well done. I’ll give the instructions myself from here on, so please make sure everything stays confidential, Miss Song.”
She nodded, then spoke cautiously. “But is Michael Silbert really...?”
“Shh.”
Looking perfectly composed, as though he hadn’t been sobbing a moment ago, Im Kkeokjeong cut her off. He whispered just loud enough for us to hear.
“He’s coming.”
He was right.
Several limousines glided across the quiet runway and stopped in front of us. President Baek Hanseong stepped out of one of them, looking as though he’d aged ten years since we last saw him.
“Welcome home, both of you.”
His voice sounded as worn out as his face.
A weekday afternoon.
The airport would normally have been packed. Instead, it was quiet inside, and outside was no different.

Police officers and soldiers appeared everywhere in the scenery passing beyond the limousine window. Here and there, people in black suits wore earpieces and, of course, Blue House badges on their chests.
“It’s nice and quiet,” I said.
“As you requested, we cleared everyone out in advance for security.”
Baek Hanseong continued as he threw away the red ginseng juice he had finished drinking.
“Of course, it was a necessary precaution with that terrorist out there.”
He meant The Prophet.
Only a few hours earlier, he told us, a huge crowd of reporters and well-wishers had surrounded the area.
“This may not be something I should say as President,” he muttered, “but lately, everyone seems to have lost their minds. Things are getting far too extreme.”
I agreed with him. I understood the crowds, too.

People who had no power to protect themselves were bound to go to extremes in a crisis. One moment they trembled as though humanity would be wiped out tomorrow; the next, the word *hope* made them blindly devoted.
*...That’s what he was counting on.*
“Pardon?”
“Nothing. Just talking to myself.”
Baek Hanseong seemed to sense something in my unthinking mutter. A complicated expression crossed his face, but I turned back to the window without another word.
He had helped us a great deal already. Depending on what happened next, he might be able to help us even more.
I couldn’t tell him everything—not because I distrusted him, but because I couldn’t trust what surrounded him.
*There are plenty of ways.*
Michael Silbert’s eyes and ears were everywhere.
There could be a mole among Baek Hanseong’s closest advisers, and there was every chance he was being watched.
The moment anyone was confronted with an unbelievable truth, they were bound to be shaken.
Being an experienced politician did not mean he could hide every emotion. If the enemy noticed something because of that, the situation would become even more disadvantageous.
*And we can’t rule out the possibility that the clue we found isn’t the truth.*
My eyes met Team Leader Choi’s, and I could tell he was thinking the same thing.

He had limited his instructions to a tiny handful of the most trustworthy senior members of the Peace and Ares Guilds. Those instructions had been delivered covertly, and even they had nothing to do with the truth we’d uncovered.
They were only a safeguard for a worst-case scenario—a way to act before the grenade’s pin was pulled, or to contain the blast if it went off.
For now, though, we couldn’t be certain of anything.
Less than twenty-four hours remained before the inaugural ceremony. How it ended would decide everyone’s fate.
Michael Silbert and me.
Beyond the simple divide between the enemy and us, it would decide where the world went from here.
Vroooom.

While my thoughts tangled themselves up, our limousine raced down the open road. Baek Hanseong filled us in on the latest news: the international situation, the decision to hold the inaugural ceremony at the National Assembly, and the list of participants confirmed so far.
He even told me how my mother and Hayeon were doing under heavy security.
“Your family has heard the news, and they’re very worried. If you’d like, we could take you to them right now...”
I understood what his trailing words meant and shook my head.
“No. I’m planning to see them after the inaugural ceremony.”
“Are you sure that will be all right?”
“Of course.”
I missed my family more than anyone in the world, but I couldn’t see them like this.
No. I mustn’t.
I was afraid I’d lose my composure if I did.
Once everything was over, I wanted to face my mother and Hayeon with a peaceful mind. I wanted to rest in their warm embrace.
*...If I can.*
The words I couldn’t bring myself to say lingered on the tip of my tongue, then faded. Just then, Baek Hanseong asked as though something had occurred to him.
“Where is the other person, by the way?”
“Ah.”
“I’m fairly certain he was on the list of people entering the country... Has something happened?”
I hesitated, then met Team Leader Choi’s eyes. I gave a bitter smile.
“He’ll be late. Something came up.”
It was a lie.
The Skeleton King was with us right now. He was simply keeping an endless silence inside a mysterious space no one else could see or sense.
Even now.
*How long are you going to stay holed up in there?*
This time, too, there was no answer.
That day, the whole world’s attention was fixed on a small peninsula in East Asia.

The usual laughing, chattering variety shows were nowhere to be found on television. News channels, current-affairs programs, and internet forums were all abuzz over the World Hunter Federation’s first inaugural ceremony, now less than a day away.

└ Who’s coming to the inaugural ceremony? └ No idea. They flat-out said they wouldn’t release the list because of the terrorist threat. Cleared out the airport, too. └ Heard they aren’t broadcasting it live, either. They’ll record it, though, so I guess we’ll find out after it’s over. └ Why keep the list secret? If they’re that worried about terrorism, why not hold a video conference like they did at the UN? └ Fact: They showed up in person even during the Great Cataclysm. └ It’s a declaration that they won’t back down, no matter what. Everyone’s been fighting separately until now. Once the Federation is established, The Prophet is fucked. └ Cheon Taemin’s the most likely representative, right? └ Yeah. Who else but Lord Taemin? └ Michael Silbert. └ Jin Taekyung. └ I like Lord Fuck, but he doesn’t measure up to Michael Silbert. Michael’s got the seniority, and what he’s done lately has been huge. └ Doesn’t matter. It’s Cheon Taemin either way. └ True. └ Maybe it’s because Cheon Taemin hasn’t shown up in so long, but I’m getting a chill. Just me? └ Then turn on the boiler.
The questions kept coming. Who would attend? Once they were all together, whom would they choose to represent them?
As the hours crept by, guests who had crossed thousands—even tens of thousands—of kilometers began arriving on the peninsula.
“We’ll need to conduct a brief identity check.”
The young man had neatly styled brown hair and faintly green eyes. He looked as though he’d stepped out of a fairy tale, and when he spoke, his voice carried an air of authority.
“I am Felix Alexander Louis, Duke of Cambridge, Earl of Strathearn, Baron Carrickfergus, Knight of the Order of the Garter, and Knight of the Order of the Chain.”
“Pardon?”
“Those titles are merely for show. Feel free to address me casually.”
“Ah, of course. Then, Mr. Felix...”
“Feel free to call me His Highness Prince Felix Alexander Louis. Casually.”
Prince Felix had just finished the brief scan when a large shadow fell over him.
“It’s been a while, Felix. Oh, should I call you His Highness?”
At the familiar face looking down at him from far above, Prince Felix seemed about to frown, but then relaxed his expression.
He would have scolded anyone else. But this was one of the few people from whom he could tolerate a little rudeness.
“Mr. Johnson.”
Magic Johnson smiled faintly.
“Just get here?”
“I did.”
“Faye Chen will be here soon, too. All of us who fought together in China will be in one place.”
“So it seems. And who is the gentleman behind you?”
“He’s with me. Though he’s no gentleman.”

Felix had never met the middle-aged man in person, but he recognized him at once. He was as huge as Magic Johnson, dressed like he’d stepped straight out of the American frontier, and had a cigar between his lips.
“...Chuck Hagel.”
Chuck Hagel, who had been puffing away at his cigar in front of a no-smoking sign, answered,
“You calling me, Prince?”
At his irritable tone, Magic Johnson eased forward. “Since we’ve run into each other, how about a drink? Faye Chen can join us.”
Felix studied them both for a moment, then shook his head.
“I have no interest.”
“Too bad.”
“See you tomorrow. Both of you.”
“Sure. Then we’ll do that.”
A perfectly ordinary exchange.
Felix gave them a brief nod and walked off with his attendants. Under tight security, he reached his assigned lodgings, unpacked, and went to bed early ahead of the next day’s ceremony.
Or so everyone thought.
But...
Click.
The locked door opened. The lights came on.
Felix had slipped out of his lodgings unseen. Now he could make out the figures who had been waiting for him in the dark—and the young man seated among them.
“It’s been a while, Your Highness.”
Felix gave a quiet laugh.
Choi Minwoo laughed with him. So did Magic Johnson, Chuck Hagel, and Faye Chen.
Their night, known to no one else, deepened.

Depending on what happened next, he might be able to help us even more.
I couldn’t tell him everything—not because I distrusted him, but because I couldn’t trust what surrounded him.
*There are plenty of ways.*
Michael Silbert’s eyes and ears were everywhere.
There could be a mole among Baek Hanseong’s closest advisers, and there was every chance he was being watched.
The moment anyone was confronted with an unbelievable truth, they were bound to be shaken.
Being an experienced politician did not mean he could hide every emotion.
If the enemy noticed something because of that, the situation would become even more disadvantageous.
*And we can’t rule out the possibility that the clue we found isn’t the truth.*
My eyes met Team Leader Choi’s, and I could tell he was thinking the same thing.
He had limited his instructions to a tiny handful of the most trustworthy senior members of the Peace and Ares Guilds.
Those instructions had been delivered covertly, and even they had nothing to do with the truth we’d uncovered.
They were only a safeguard for a worst-case scenario—a way to act before the grenade’s pin was pulled, or to contain the blast if it went off.
For now, though, we couldn’t be certain of anything.
Less than twenty-four hours remained before the inaugural ceremony.
How it ended would decide everyone’s fate.
Michael Silbert and me.
Beyond the simple divide between the enemy and us, it would decide where the world went from here.
Vroooom.
While my thoughts tangled themselves up, our limousine raced down the open road.
Baek Hanseong filled us in on the latest news: the international situation, the decision to hold the inaugural ceremony at the National Assembly, and the list of participants confirmed so far.
He even told me how my mother and Hayeon were doing under heavy security.
“Your family has heard the news, and they’re very worried.
If you’d like, we could take you to them right now...”
I understood what his trailing words meant and shook my head.
“No.
I’m planning to see them after the inaugural ceremony.”
“Are you sure that will be all right?”
“Of course.”
I missed my family more than anyone in the world, but I couldn’t see them like this.
No.
I mustn’t.
I was afraid I’d lose my composure if I did.
Once everything was over, I wanted to face my mother and Hayeon with a peaceful mind.
I wanted to rest in their warm embrace.
*...If I can.*
The words I couldn’t bring myself to say lingered on the tip of my tongue, then faded.
Just then, Baek Hanseong asked as though something had occurred to him.
“Where is the other person, by the way?”
“Ah.”
“I’m fairly certain he was on the list of people entering the country...
Has something happened?”
I hesitated, then met Team Leader Choi’s eyes.
I gave a bitter smile.
“He’ll be late.
Something came up.”
It was a lie.
The Skeleton King was with us right now.
He was simply keeping an endless silence inside a mysterious space no one else could see or sense.
Even now.
*How long are you going to stay holed up in there?*
This time, too, there was no answer.
That day, the whole world’s attention was fixed on a small peninsula in East Asia.
The usual laughing, chattering variety shows were nowhere to be found on television.
News channels, current-affairs programs, and internet forums were all abuzz over the World Hunter Federation’s first inaugural ceremony, now less than a day away.
└ Who’s coming to the inaugural ceremony? └ No idea.
They flat-out said they wouldn’t release the list because of the terrorist threat.
Cleared out the airport, too. └ Heard they aren’t broadcasting it live, either.
They’ll record it, though, so I guess we’ll find out after it’s over. └ Why keep the list secret?

If they’re that worried about terrorism, why not hold a video conference like they did at the UN? └ Fact: They showed up in person even during the Great Cataclysm. └ It’s a declaration that they won’t back down, no matter what.
Everyone’s been fighting separately until now.
Once the Federation is established, The Prophet is fucked. └ Cheon Taemin’s the most likely representative, right? └ Yeah.
Who else but Lord Taemin? └ Michael Silbert. └ Jin Taekyung. └ I like Lord Fuck, but he doesn’t measure up to Michael Silbert.
Michael’s got the seniority, and what he’s done lately has been huge. └ Doesn’t matter.
It’s Cheon Taemin either way. └ True. └ Maybe it’s because Cheon Taemin hasn’t shown up in so long, but I’m getting a chill.
Just me? └ Then turn on the boiler.
The questions kept coming.
Who would attend?
Once they were all together, whom would they choose to represent them?
As the hours crept by, guests who had crossed thousands—even tens of thousands—of kilometers began arriving on the peninsula.
“We’ll need to conduct a brief identity check.”
The young man had neatly styled brown hair and faintly green eyes.
He looked as though he’d stepped out of a fairy tale, and when he spoke, his voice carried an air of authority.
“I am Felix Alexander Louis, Duke of Cambridge, Earl of Strathearn, Baron Carrickfergus, Knight of the Order of the Garter, and Knight of the Order of the Chain.”
“Pardon?”
“Those titles are merely for show.
Feel free to address me casually.”
“Ah, of course.
Then, Mr.
Felix...”
“Feel free to call me His Highness Prince Felix Alexander Louis.
Casually.”
Prince Felix had just finished the brief scan when a large shadow fell over him.
“It’s been a while, Felix.
Oh, should I call you His Highness?”
At the familiar face looking down at him from far above, Prince Felix seemed about to frown, but then relaxed his expression.
He would have scolded anyone else.
But this was one of the few people from whom he could tolerate a little rudeness.
“Mr.
Johnson.”
Magic Johnson smiled faintly.
“Just get here?”
“I did.”
“Faye Chen will be here soon, too.
All of us who fought together in China will be in one place.”
“So it seems.
And who is the gentleman behind you?”
“He’s with me.
Though he’s no gentleman.”
Felix had never met the middle-aged man in person, but he recognized him at once.
He was as huge as Magic Johnson, dressed like he’d stepped straight out of the American frontier, and had a cigar between his lips.
“...Chuck Hagel.”
Chuck Hagel, who had been puffing away at his cigar in front of a no-smoking sign, answered,
“You calling me, Prince?”
At his irritable tone, Magic Johnson eased forward.
“Since we’ve run into each other, how about a drink?
Faye Chen can join us.”
Felix studied them both for a moment, then shook his head.
“I have no interest.”
“Too bad.”
“See you tomorrow.
Both of you.”
“Sure.
Then we’ll do that.”
A perfectly ordinary exchange.
Felix gave them a brief nod and walked off with his attendants.
Under tight security, he reached his assigned lodgings, unpacked, and went to bed early ahead of the next day’s ceremony.
Or so everyone thought.
But...
Click.
The locked door opened.
The lights came on.
Felix had slipped out of his lodgings unseen.
Now he could make out the figures who had been waiting for him in the dark—and the young man seated among them.
“It’s been a while, Your Highness.”
Felix gave a quiet laugh.
Choi Minwoo laughed with him.
So did Magic Johnson, Chuck Hagel, and Faye Chen.
Their night, known to no one else, deepened.

chapters.title: Chapter 774
paragraphs: Back when I was a rookie Hunter, I used to cry sometimes.
No—if I’m being honest, pretty often.
Looking back, I suppose it was all growing pains. But that was how it was back then.
It was only natural. I had barely reached adulthood, and the Hunter Training Center was just that: a training center.
What was my first real fight like?
No matter how hard I try to remember, it’s hazy as fog. Not because the memory has faded with age, but because I half-lost my mind the moment the battle began.
A few fragments remain clear.
The backs of the tanks as they buckled under the sheer number of monsters. The thick stench of blood and the reek of creatures that didn’t belong to this world.
The spear feeling heavier than it ever had before. Sweat pooling in my grip...
That was all. The moment we clashed, everything around me seemed to recede. When I came to, there was blood everywhere.
The Team Leader had been waiting for me to wake up, a cigarette between his lips. The first thing he said was:
“You. Rookie.”
“Y-Yes.”
“You fucking bastard.”
“Excuse me?”
“I almost died saving your ass. Did my wife put you up to it? Tell you to kill me so you two could split the insurance payout?”
“N-No.”
“You fought pretty well for someone who’d lost his mind, but pull that shit again and you’re going to die. Seriously.”
“...I’m sorry.”
“By the way, what’s your name?”
“Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung, sir.”
“What year were you born?”
“Fuck. People were still being born in 2020?”
The Team Leader glared at me, puffing hard on his cigarette. Only then did he tell me his name.
“I’m Hong Cheonsu.”
“Oh. Yes, sir.”
“From now on, when we’re off duty, call me... Uncle? No, that’s a bit much. Call me hyung. Cheonsu hyung.”
“Yes, Cheonsu hyung.”
“This kid doesn’t even pretend to refuse. And we’re still inside the Gate, you little shit.”
I didn’t know it then.
I didn’t know that I’d come to stick with that foul-tempered Team Leader like a brother through thick and thin. Or that, only a few years later, he would sacrifice himself for me.
“You did good. Here’s your payout.”
Six 50,000-won bills, after taxes and the Guild’s fee.
I took my pay for risking my life that day and went back to my goshiwon.
When I opened the door, the room—less than four pyeong—smelled of mold. A family photograph sat on a table with a chipped corner.
And I cried.
At first, I sobbed quietly. Before long, I had buried my face between my knees and was bawling like a child.
If someone hadn’t opened the locked door, I might have kept the entire goshiwon awake all night.
“Hey, new guy. Sorry for barging in without asking. I’m the manager here, but the complaints kept coming, so I had to use the master key...”
The manager took one look at my tear-streaked face and trailed off. He scratched his greasy hair, then closed the door.
He looked like some middle-aged guy, and I figured he wouldn’t be back.
A little later, he returned with soju in one hand and a bag of ramen in the other.
“Want a drink? Oh, wait. You’re not a minor... Obviously not. Look at the size of you. Whew.”
Memories from nearly ten years ago.
Time passed, and I changed. My fear of monsters and the loneliness of being away from my family gradually faded.
No. I grew numb to them.
Like a hamster on a wheel, I just kept running.
Even if I wasn’t getting anywhere, running was better than stopping. There were things I could protect only by keeping that wheel turning.
Family. Friends. Comrades.
I couldn’t stop anymore.
At some point, the little wheel in the cage that held me had become the enormous wheel of fate. And the word *duty*, which I carried in my heart, had grown clearer and heavier.
Maybe that was why.
Why I had been able to revisit that fading memory, if only in a dream.
Why my cheeks were wet when I opened my eyes to someone shaking me awake.
“...kyung. Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
I blinked. My blurred vision finally came into focus.
A familiar face looked down at me with concern. His expression had barely changed, which only made the small trace of emotion stand out more.
“Are you all right?”
I rubbed my wet eyes and answered.
“I don’t know.”
“Did you have a bad dream?”
“I’m not sure.”
I sat up, my voice hoarse. The clock showed that it was just past noon. Through a gap in the curtains, I could see how dark it was outside.
“I don’t know if it was a bad dream or a good one. I really don’t.”
Team Leader Choi watched me in silence before speaking calmly.
“Don’t dwell on it. It was only a dream.”
He was right. A dream was only a dream. Whether today brought good or bad fortune was up to us—and deciding that was my role.
No. It was everyone’s.
“I’m still half-asleep, so let me ask you something. Was last night a dream too?”
“Last night?”
“Yeah. There were a lot of familiar faces. Toward the end, I even saw a British prince dressed as a hotel bellboy.”
Only then did a faint smile touch Team Leader Choi’s lips.
“How strange. I had the same dream.”
“Oh, you did? Personally, I thought it was a pretty good one.”
“So did I.”
That part, of course, hadn’t been a dream.
Our secret conversation had gone on until the small hours of the morning. Worn out by the past few days, I’d fallen asleep as if I’d passed out.
Maybe that was why my mind felt clear and my body felt light.
Almost too light.
*There is one small problem, of course.*
I focused on the faint pain deep inside me.
**Broken Body** still hadn’t healed. Its effects weren’t just numbers displayed by the System. Like a parasite clinging to a host, it was eating away at some of my strength.
*Can I do it? Even like this?*
The question flashed through my mind. I shook my head.
Whether I could do it wasn’t the question.
I had to.
For me, for my people, and for everyone else.
“Are we ready?”
Team Leader Choi answered without hesitation.
“Everything is ready.”
There was certainty in his voice—the kind that came from having done everything he could to prepare.
But I asked again, this time addressing someone else, crouched somewhere out of sight.
“And you?”
Once again, there was no answer.

He must have seen and heard everything, but he chose silence again. As though he were trying to cut away every last shred of affection between us. As though he were a traveler packed and ready to leave.
But... I had no intention of letting him go.
Especially not for a reason as fucked up as this.
“Let’s go.”
I said it evenly and left the room. Team Leader Choi followed at once, and the Hunters of the Peace Guild and Ares Guild filled the corridor behind us, trailing like a dragon’s tail.
It was time to set the enormous wheel in motion.
The sky was gray that day.
Dark clouds had spread across the capital region before dawn, bringing a light drizzle. The air felt chilly against the skin.
But the weather meant nothing to the people.
They expected the clouds to clear and the sun to shine through soon.
No. *Certainty* might have been a better word.
The historic inaugural ceremony of the new World Hunter Federation.
That was the sunlight they had been waiting for: an alliance of superhumans who would save them from the second Great War, soon to descend on them—or perhaps already begun.

Heroes of the past, present, and future would gather in one place and become Hunters in the truest sense. They would be humanity’s sword and shield, drive away the dark clouds, and protect the world from the monsters surging in like waves.
Today.
Here.
*New history begins.*
Michael Silbert ran his fingertips across the table.
The enormous round table had three hundred seats. Marks left by sharp weapons covered its surface.
*The marks the heroes left behind.*
He remembered that day clearly.
When the World Hunter Federation—an alliance unlike any before it—was born, Michael Silbert had been there to share in its glory.

Beside those now long dead, he had shouted with his blood aflame. They had drawn their weapons and pointed them skyward, then driven their swords into the great round table and sworn to become humanity’s sword and shield.
*Yes. Right here.*
He could never forget it.
Michael Silbert gently stroked the chair he had once occupied. Age had left it rough and creaking, yet even that stirred something in him.
But that was all.
He looked down at the chair that held those memories without sitting in it or leaning against it. His gaze drifted away from it, toward the center of the round table.
The only empty space.
There was no chair or platform there. Ringed by three hundred seats, it almost looked as desolate as an uninhabited island.
But neither Michael nor anyone else had thought so back then.
One man had always filled that space.
Stronger and brighter than anyone else. A hero among heroes, whom even those who envied him could only regard with awe and fear.
*Sky.*
Michael Silbert raised his head and looked around.
The First National Assembly Hall had since become a World Heritage site. Stained glass installed just after the war, depicting humanity’s victory in the Great Cataclysm, glittered on every side.
Humans and monsters locked in fierce battle. Blood flowing in rivers. Corpses piled everywhere...
His gaze passed over the old heroes immortalized there by their dazzling feats, most of them now dead. Then it settled on the highest point in that glorious record.
Two figures set into the ceiling.
*Well. You’re still looking down at me from up there.*
Michael Silbert gave a quiet laugh.
The savior who had driven his sword into the heart of Asmodeus—the Demon King who had cast humanity into a pit of fire—looked down at him.
As though warning Michael not to forget him.
As though he might descend at any moment and mete out divine punishment.
But...
*Not anymore, Sky.*
Michael Silbert smiled softly.
In his youth, he had been neither particularly strong nor particularly weak beside the other heroes. Now he had returned, his strength beyond anyone’s denial.
*And what about you?*
Cheon Taemin—the man Michael had revered and feared, the man who had forced him to lie low for fear of attracting his notice—was gone.
All he could do now was remain as a record in this place and watch Michael, who would soon ascend the throne.
“I’ll take the place where you once stood.”
The words came out full of elation.
Grrrnnng.
The tightly shut door opened. Light spilled through the gap, along with a voice.
“What a load of bullshit. What a load of bullshit.”

chapters.title: Chapter 775
paragraphs: Every now and then, what I really think slips out before I can stop it.
Like right now.
“What a load of bullshit. What a load of bullshit.”
Michael Silbert showed no reaction to my tone. Instead, he greeted me with the last traces of elation still on his face.
“You’re earlier than I expected. I’ve been waiting.”
“Practicing your musical all by yourself?”
“Musical?”
He considered that for a moment, then gave a short laugh.
“I suppose that isn’t wrong. What happens here today is a musical of sorts. One man directing, staging, and starring in the whole thing.”
“My mother used to say that if you eat whatever’s put in front of you, sooner or later you’ll make yourself sick.”
“No need to worry. Nothing will go wrong, and the show is guaranteed to be a hit.”
“That line you delivered just now was pretty awful. You sure it’ll be a hit?”
“It was only a rehearsal before the main performance, but I’ll take your opinion into account.”
The easy manner. The faint smile on his lips.
As he came closer, my stomach twisted. Each breath felt like a huge needle stirring around inside it.
*Was this the effect of **Broken Body**? Or was it because I was standing face-to-face with the lunatic now right in front of me?*
*Maybe both.*
“Did that friend come with you?”
“Find out for yourself.”
“Not a bad idea.”
Michael gazed at the firmly shut door over my shoulder, then nodded.
“I’ve confirmed it. You brought him here safely.”
An ordinary civilian watching us might have wondered what the hell he meant. I didn’t.
There was no sound. No visible shape.
But I felt it: the wave of qi he had sent out, slipping back into his body the instant it found what he was looking for.

He did it with a natural, practiced ease more like a Supreme Peak master of Murim than a Hunter. He was unlike any ordinary Hunter I’d met. Worse, even I couldn’t gauge how strong he truly was. He still hadn’t shown his full strength.
*But I couldn’t let him see that anything was amiss.*
A brief silence fell between us. I broke it.
“He came with me.”
“Hmm?”
“I didn’t bring him. We came together.”
Michael looked puzzled for a moment, then laughed aloud.
“Very well. If the person involved insists on putting it that way, perhaps there is a difference. But what possible difference could it make?”
“A hell of a difference. Someone like you wouldn’t understand, even if you died and came back.”
“No. What matters is that you and your friend are here. And if anything matters more than that...”
The voice reaching my ears suddenly dropped into a low murmur.
“Your intention.”
“My intention?”
“Yes. Your intentions today.”
He watched me as though he’d suspected them from the start. I let the silence sit for a moment, then spoke.
“Let me ask you something.”
“I’m the one who should hear an answer first, but very well. I’ll permit the question.”
“What are *your* intentions?”
“What?”
“Why commit all these atrocities? What could you possibly want badly enough to sacrifice so many people and push the whole world into a pit of fire?”
*Step.*
I closed the few paces between us until our noses nearly touched. I could see the smallest change in his expression, the fine hairs on his skin. I could feel his breath.
*Human.*
Considering everything he had done, it was difficult to believe, but Michael Silbert was undeniably human, just like me.
Blood, flesh, and bone.
*So why?*
“Why did you do it? What the hell was it all for?”
Ever since I’d first met him, all I’d felt toward Michael was anger. Not now.
I genuinely wanted to know. I couldn’t understand him. The more clues I found about him, the more questions I had.
“Born on March 18, 1994, in Paris’s Tenth Arrondissement. His father ran away before he was born, and his alcoholic single mother, who lived with him, died in 2012.”
What I’d learned of one man’s life spilled from my mouth.
I turned away from Michael Silbert and began to walk.
*Step. Step.*
One step, then another. As I crossed the First National Assembly Hall, now a World Heritage site, I retraced his past.
A polite, diligent child despite a difficult home life. Then, after his mother’s death, a late turn toward delinquency and several criminal convictions.
Finally came the event that changed his life completely.
“In 2020, when the Great Cataclysm began, he awakened in his mid-twenties.”
I stopped.
I raised my head. In the stained glass set into the wall, a young man stood alone amid countless heaps of corpses, tears running down his face.
*December 25, 2020 — The Great Battle of Paris*
They said it had been one of the ten fiercest battles of the entire Great Cataclysm.

Instead of bells ringing through the streets to celebrate Christmas, screams and thunderous explosions echoed through Paris. A thousand Hunters stationed in the city waged an urban battle against monsters that outnumbered them dozens of times over.
For a whole week.
Without reinforcements. A desperate fight in every sense.

When seven days and nights had passed and the last sun of 2020 had set, reinforcements arrived after finishing another battle. They found countless bodies, pools of blood, and one young man standing among them.
“That was you.”
I turned slowly.
The face of the young man in the stained glass was there—the young man who had survived alone in that ruin, more than thirty years ago, while the stench of blood hung thick in the air.
“Michael Silbert.”
He had listened without a word. At my quiet call, he finally spoke.
“I’ll give you credit for the effort. You must have worked hard. The records from before my awakening were erased. They couldn’t have been easy to find.”
“You erased them. Having a criminal record wouldn’t have done your reputation any favors.”
“I won’t deny it. I thought it might stand in my way one day. Everyone was in chaos then, so it was easy enough to deal with.”
Michael Silbert answered calmly, then stared at me.
“But... if that’s all you found, I’m a little disappointed.”
“What?”

“The Tenth Arrondissement, where I was born, was a shithole. Fights broke out several times a day. Gunshots rang out every night. The alley wall I passed on my way to and from school was always dark red. Nobody cleaned the blood off. It would only be red again the next day.”
“That was my hometown. By day, gangs of every race roamed the streets. By night, neon signs lit up the entertainment district. You called my mother an alcoholic, didn’t you?”
He answered his own question without a change in tone.
“Apparently you didn’t know she was addicted to drugs, too. Whenever I came home from school, she’d be sprawled across that worn-out sofa with men I’d never seen before.”
Everyone had a painful past. Yet as Michael recalled his, a faint smile touched his lips.

“A man who planted his seed and ran. A woman who was my mother only in the eyes of the law. And their child, whose life became a string of assaults and thefts. That was me. But I’m also the hero who saved Paris twice, and the pioneer who was first to speak up for people in danger.”
“I used to be ashamed of my past. Not anymore. From slum child to hero of the world. Excellent marketing, wouldn’t you say?”
I stared at him, at a loss for words.
*What did someone have to go through to become so worn down?* The clock that had run without stopping since the day he was born looked as though it had been ticking for six hundred years, not sixty.
His heart looked much the same.
Under my gaze, Michael’s smile widened.
“You’re looking at me as if I’m a monster. Are you afraid of me now, too?”
“Too?”
“Everyone who knows me looks at me with fear and respect. You aren’t the first.”
“Some of them are dead by now, I’m guessing.”
“If they won’t bow their heads on their own, shouldn’t they be forced to yield? They were fools.”
He wasn’t talking about enemies long gone. He was talking to me.
A warning to lower my head before he crushed me by any means necessary. A meticulous attempt to make sure not even the slightest possibility of things going wrong remained.
I studied him for a moment, then broke the silence.
“You’re half wrong and half right.”
“What do you mean?”
“It’s true that I see you as a monster. But this isn’t fear. It’s pity. You could call it disgust, too.”
“I just wanted to ask. Whether this could be cleaned up before irreversible sacrifices occurred. Whether any trace of humanity remained in this lunatic. And...”
My voice sank.
“I’m a little disappointed. That you thought I could hold you back with nothing more than a few criminal convictions.”
“What?”
Before he could make sense of it, I turned and held out my hand.
*Whoosh. Bang!*
Qi flowed from my fingertips and gently pushed the shut doors open. Beyond them, I could sense people drawing closer up the stairs.
I tipped my head toward Michael. His face had gone rigid.
“Don’t keep busy people waiting. Start the inaugural ceremony you were so eager to hold, you fucking bastard.”
“You haven’t even transferred the deed, and you’re already acting like the landlord. What a fucking asshole.”
I ignored his icy stare, sat in the nearest chair, and leaned back.
The die had been cast. It was still rolling, and soon we would see whether it came up one or six.
We’d find out who died and who survived, too.
And I had not the slightest intention of dying in a place like this.
Especially not at the hands of a monster instead of a human being.
*Step. Step. Step.*
Hundreds of footsteps finally entered the now-silent conference hall.
The first page in the history of the new World Hunter Federation was turning.

chapters.title: Chapter 776
paragraphs: Some questions in this world remain unanswered.
The relationship between troubled times and heroes is one of them.
Do heroes appear first, bringing troubled times in their wake?
Or do troubled times give rise to heroes?

Even after many years had passed, no clear answer had emerged that could satisfy everyone. But when faced with the history of the Great Cataclysm, even those who had argued for the former were forced to turn toward the latter.
A Great War unlike any other in human history.
The Great Cataclysm shattered everything people had thought they knew. It gave rise to countless heroes, then cast them into the jaws of death, leaving behind only their names and deeds.
But many heroes survived, too.
Heroes like those now gazing at the National Assembly Hall, filled with traces of glory, and the enormous round table at its center.
“Ah. This place hasn’t changed. Even the air feels the same as it did that day.”
“It’s changed a little. When did they put up that painting?”
“What are you talking about, hyung? It’s been almost thirty years. Weren’t you at the commemorative event?”
“No.”
“Why not?”
“Because I never wanted to remember those days again.”
Power beyond that of ordinary humans did not preserve everyone’s youth.
An old man whose hair had turned white with the passing years murmured in a hoarse voice.
“So many empty seats.”
The survivors had carried losses as great as their glory.
Where were the comrades who had once sat around this table and cheered? The ones who had fought back-to-back against monsters surging in from every direction?
“I never thought I’d come back here...”
Yet fate had brought them back, as if playing a cruel joke.
Back to this place marked by glory and pain. Back to swear once more that they would be humanity’s sword and shield.
And new faces were filling the seats left empty by those who were gone.
“Hello, Senior.”
“Who are you?”
“My name is Liam. We met during the Defense of Frankfurt, but I suppose you don’t remember me. Haha.”
“I’m sorry. I must be getting old if I can’t recognize someone I fought beside.”
“No, of course you wouldn’t recognize me. I was fifteen then.”
“Fifteen? Were you...?”
“Yes. I was one of the citizens in the bunker. You may not remember, Senior, but you saved my life back then.”
“Well, I’ll be.”
The great trees with sturdy roots were not the only ones to survive the typhoon.
Those who had once been saplings, weeds, or mere seeds had grown, too, and earned the right to sit at the round table.
But warm reunions like theirs were rare among the heroes of past and present. Humanity faced another grave crisis, and the heroes differed in both their values and the course they wanted to take.
Whom would they choose as their representative?
That was the most important question before them today. The older and younger heroes had naturally gathered with those who shared their views.
Two men stood at the center of it all.
Michael Silbert, renowned for his achievements and the first to call for the World Hunter Federation’s reestablishment.
And...
*Jin Taekyung.*
Michael Silbert repeated the name silently. He shook hands and exchanged greetings with the followers surrounding him, but his shadowed eyes remained fixed on the young man beyond their shoulders.
*What exactly did you mean by that?*
The voices flattering him seemed far away. All he could hear was what Jin had said moments earlier.
“I’m a little disappointed. That you thought I could hold you back with nothing more than a few criminal convictions.”
The voice had faded, but the memory remained vivid. So did the shock Michael had felt at the time.
His heart, usually so calm, began to beat faster.
*Wait. Could it be?*
His gray eyes trembled as he watched Jin Taekyung.
Of all the possibilities he had considered, one had come to mind. It was the only way Jin could stop him now.
But... no. It couldn’t be. It was absurd.
*It’s all but impossible for anyone else to notice. No, it’s impossible.*
Only one person could have done so: Cheon Taemin.

Even he, who had reached a one-of-a-kind realm, had merely sensed something in passing at the time. Michael Silbert, who had immediately noticed the warning sign, had been forced to lie low like a wanted criminal for a long time.
Until Cheon Taemin disappeared from the public eye.
Until Michael was certain Cheon Taemin’s attention had shifted away from him.
*And now Jin Taekyung, of all people? Not Sky?*
As his unease grew, Michael shook his head inwardly.
No. Everything Jin had said was nothing but bravado.
Bravado meant to search for one final opening after everything was already over. The last desperate struggle of someone who had sensed his defeat.
But why?
Even as he dismissed it as a bluff, Jin’s image rose before him like a haze, clouding his eyes and ears.
“Then what is your intention?”
One question.
“Why did you do those things? What in the world were you doing it for?”
Then another.
“This isn’t fear. It’s pity. You could call it disgust, too.”
That expression. Those eyes. That calm voice.
The young man had lived barely half as long as Michael, yet the emotion Michael had sensed in him was unmistakably close to genuine.
*And if it was genuine...*
*Crack.*
Bones shifted under the pressure of Michael’s grip. A strained voice broke through his thoughts.
“G-Guild Master?”
“Hmm?”
“W-Why are you squeezing my hand...?”
“Ah.”
Michael realized what he had done and loosened his grip.
The follower whose hand he had been shaking forced a smile through the pain.
“You certainly live up to your reputation. I used to be a tank, so I can hold my own when it comes to raw strength, but you’re incredible, Guild Master.”
The S-rank Hunters and heads of the great Guilds watching nearby were quick to agree.
“Of course he is.”
“Haha. Odin Guild didn’t become the best for nothing. Michael Silbert’s name has been famous since the Great Cataclysm.”
“Really, this was Paul’s fault. I saw him squeeze first. Hahaha.”
Laughter mingled with flattery disguised as praise.
Michael watched them, then felt a smile tug at his lips.
Yes. This was power.
This was why he had to gain authority by any means necessary.
The actions of the strong were always justified by the weak who feared their power.
It did not matter if they did not respect him. It did not matter if they did not love him.
If he could make them afraid—if he could reign over them rather than lead them—he would have everything.

Michael had first learned that truth in the back alleys of Paris’s Tenth Arrondissement. He had seen gang members walk the streets with guns tucked into their waistbands, and people too frightened to report them. That was when he understood the path he had to take.
*This is how the world works.*
He gave his followers a gentle smile and turned his head.
Jin Taekyung was with the elders, many of whom had retired once already or still remembered Cheon Taemin’s presence. Several other familiar faces were there, too.
Grand Mage Magic Johnson. Chuck Hagel, who had resigned as United States Secretary of Defense after the vigilante incident. Faye Chen of Hong Kong. Even Prince Felix of the United Kingdom.
They were formidable figures, even among the people gathered here from around the world. But their side held fewer than half of the three hundred seats.
*The old generation must have come here looking only toward Sky, while the new generation followed Jin Taekyung.*
But whom would they support once Cheon Taemin’s condition became known?
His maternal grandson, whose only claim was their shared blood?
Or Jin Taekyung, absurdly young and so often reckless?
Even Magic Johnson, with all his achievements and popularity, fell short of Michael in fame and reputation.
*Whether you wanted it or not, only one person remains.*
Him.
The man who had harbored greater ambitions than anyone else and spent years preparing for this moment.
To Michael, the people across the table looked like sandcastles about to crumble.
*Still... it pays to prepare for the unexpected.*
He slipped a hand into his pocket.
The moment he pressed the pager inside, sending a signal to someone, his eyes met Jin Taekyung’s.
A pair of reddish, heated eyes.
Michael felt the heat in them as keenly as a searing pain at the back of his neck, beneath his armor.
“Oh. What’s wrong?”
“Mr. Silbert, are you feeling unwell?”
“I brought a potion just in case. Good thing I—”
“I’m fine. It’s nothing. There’s no need to fuss.”
Michael answered firmly, then stared at Jin. Had Jin seen his reaction?
He fought down the unease.
But Jin was already looking elsewhere, and the sight of the figure seated beside him steadied Michael.
No—a monster in human form.
*Stone-King.*
As long as that creature was here, Michael would stand at the center of the round table.
He had to.
—All attendees have arrived. Please take your seats.
The announcement came over the speakers. Michael clenched his fist.
The inaugural ceremony began, but the attendees did not fall silent.
If anything, their quiet whispers grew louder.
“All attendees have arrived?”
“That can’t be right. You must have misheard.”
“There must have been a minor mistake.”
The elders and the younger generation shared the same confusion. One person who surely had to attend was nowhere to be seen.
But after everyone took their seats, no correction came over the speakers.
Only then did they understand.
Cheon Taemin, humanity’s savior, would not appear.
Not today. Not tomorrow or the day after. Perhaps not before this second Great War came to an end.
“What in the world...?”
“Where is Sky? Where is that person?”
What everyone had taken for a simple mix-up set off a rising murmur, then shock and confusion.
And then—
*Step. Step.*
Someone rose from their seat and walked toward the center of the round table.

He shook hands and exchanged greetings with the followers surrounding him, but his shadowed eyes remained fixed on the young man beyond their shoulders.
*What exactly did you mean by that?*
The voices flattering him seemed far away.
All he could hear was what Jin had said moments earlier.
“I’m a little disappointed.
That you thought I could hold you back with nothing more than a few criminal convictions.”
The voice had faded, but the memory remained vivid.
So did the shock Michael had felt at the time.
His heart, usually so calm, began to beat faster.
*Wait.
Could it be?*
His gray eyes trembled as he watched Jin Taekyung.
Of all the possibilities he had considered, one had come to mind.
It was the only way Jin could stop him now.
But... no.
It couldn’t be.
It was absurd.
*It’s all but impossible for anyone else to notice.
No, it’s impossible.*
Only one person could have done so: Cheon Taemin.
Even he, who had reached a one-of-a-kind realm, had merely sensed something in passing at the time.
Michael Silbert, who had immediately noticed the warning sign, had been forced to lie low like a wanted criminal for a long time.
Until Cheon Taemin disappeared from the public eye.
Until Michael was certain Cheon Taemin’s attention had shifted away from him.
*And now Jin Taekyung, of all people?
Not Sky?*
As his unease grew, Michael shook his head inwardly.
No.
Everything Jin had said was nothing but bravado.
Bravado meant to search for one final opening after everything was already over.
The last desperate struggle of someone who had sensed his defeat.
But why?
Even as he dismissed it as a bluff, Jin’s image rose before him like a haze, clouding his eyes and ears.
“Then what is your intention?”
One question.
“Why did you do those things?
What in the world were you doing it for?”
Then another.
“This isn’t fear.
It’s pity.
You could call it disgust, too.”
That expression.
Those eyes.
That calm voice.
The young man had lived barely half as long as Michael, yet the emotion Michael had sensed in him was unmistakably close to genuine.
*And if it was genuine...*
*Crack.*
Bones shifted under the pressure of Michael’s grip.
A strained voice broke through his thoughts.
“G-Guild Master?”
“Hmm?”
“W-Why are you squeezing my hand...?”
“Ah.”
Michael realized what he had done and loosened his grip.
The follower whose hand he had been shaking forced a smile through the pain.
“You certainly live up to your reputation.
I used to be a tank, so I can hold my own when it comes to raw strength, but you’re incredible, Guild Master.”
The S-rank Hunters and heads of the great Guilds watching nearby were quick to agree.
“Of course he is.”
“Haha.
Odin Guild didn’t become the best for nothing.
Michael Silbert’s name has been famous since the Great Cataclysm.”
“Really, this was Paul’s fault.
I saw him squeeze first.
Hahaha.”
Laughter mingled with flattery disguised as praise.
Michael watched them, then felt a smile tug at his lips.
Yes.
This was power.
This was why he had to gain authority by any means necessary.
The actions of the strong were always justified by the weak who feared their power.
It did not matter if they did not respect him.
It did not matter if they did not love him.
If he could make them afraid—if he could reign over them rather than lead them—he would have everything.
Michael had first learned that truth in the back alleys of Paris’s Tenth Arrondissement.
He had seen gang members walk the streets with guns tucked into their waistbands, and people too frightened to report them.
That was when he understood the path he had to take.
*This is how the world works.*
He gave his followers a gentle smile and turned his head.
Jin Taekyung was with the elders, many of whom had retired once already or still remembered Cheon Taemin’s presence.
Several other familiar faces were there, too.
Grand Mage Magic Johnson.
Chuck Hagel, who had resigned as United States Secretary of Defense after the vigilante incident.
Faye Chen of Hong Kong.
Even Prince Felix of the United Kingdom.
They were formidable figures, even among the people gathered here from around the world.
But their side held fewer than half of the three hundred seats.
*The old generation must have come here looking only toward Sky, while the new generation followed Jin Taekyung.*
But whom would they support once Cheon Taemin’s condition became known?
His maternal grandson, whose only claim was their shared blood?
Or Jin Taekyung, absurdly young and so often reckless?
Even Magic Johnson, with all his achievements and popularity, fell short of Michael in fame and reputation.
*Whether you wanted it or not, only one person remains.*
Him.
The man who had harbored greater ambitions than anyone else and spent years preparing for this moment.
To Michael, the people across the table looked like sandcastles about to crumble.
*Still... it pays to prepare for the unexpected.*
He slipped a hand into his pocket.
The moment he pressed the pager inside, sending a signal to someone, his eyes met Jin Taekyung’s.
A pair of reddish, heated eyes.
Michael felt the heat in them as keenly as a searing pain at the back of his neck, beneath his armor.
“Oh.
What’s wrong?”
“Mr.
Silbert, are you feeling unwell?”
“I brought a potion just in case.
Good thing I—”
“I’m fine.
It’s nothing.
There’s no need to fuss.”
Michael answered firmly, then stared at Jin.
Had Jin seen his reaction?
He fought down the unease.
But Jin was already looking elsewhere, and the sight of the figure seated beside him steadied Michael.
No—a monster in human form.
*Stone-King.*
As long as that creature was here, Michael would stand at the center of the round table.
He had to.
—All attendees have arrived.
Please take your seats.
The announcement came over the speakers.
Michael clenched his fist.
The inaugural ceremony began, but the attendees did not fall silent.
If anything, their quiet whispers grew louder.
“All attendees have arrived?”
“That can’t be right.
You must have misheard.”
“There must have been a minor mistake.”
The elders and the younger generation shared the same confusion.
One person who surely had to attend was nowhere to be seen.
But after everyone took their seats, no correction came over the speakers.
Only then did they understand.
Cheon Taemin, humanity’s savior, would not appear.
Not today.
Not tomorrow or the day after.
Perhaps not before this second Great War came to an end.
“What in the world...?”
“Where is Sky?
Where is that person?”

And then—
*Step.
Step.*

chapters.title: Chapter 777
paragraphs: *So it’s finally starting.*
I muttered to myself as I watched the back of someone walking alone.
Then again, it wasn’t just me. Everyone here was doing the same.
The cameras positioned throughout the room and some three hundred pairs of eyes around the round table followed Michael Silbert’s every step.
*Step. Step.*
He walked without the slightest hesitation.
The murmuring had long since died away. As if by agreement, everyone had fallen silent, though they watched him with very different feelings.
Some couldn’t hide their confusion at his sudden move. Others looked deep in thought. A few nodded as if this were only to be expected, or wore faint smiles.
I took them all in.
I caught every emotion that slipped across their faces, every slight movement at the corners of their mouths, and committed those faces to memory.
Then—
*Swish.*
Michael stopped just short of the center of the enormous round table. For decades, that place had belonged to one man alone.
His final step never came. It was as though something invisible stood in his way. He parted his lips.
“Everyone. Today, I received some deeply shocking news.”
His voice was thick with emotion. Tears glimmered at the corners of his eyes beneath the lights.
He looked from the people unsettled by this unexpected turn to the cameras recording it, then continued.

“Just before the inaugural ceremony began, two young men came to see me and delivered the news. At first, I found it hard to believe. In the end, I had no choice but to accept it, and I needed time to compose myself.”
“Could you tell us who those two young men were, and what news they brought?”
The question came at just the right moment.
Perfect timing. As if it had been planned.
No, it clearly had been.
In this scripted musical, the leading man delivered his next line in response to the bit player’s perfectly placed question.
“There’s no difficulty in telling you who came to see me. Both young men are well known, and both are here with us now. But I’m afraid I can’t be the one to tell you what they said.”
“Why not?”
“Because I’m not qualified to do so.”
Michael answered calmly, then turned toward me—or, rather, toward Team Leader Choi, seated to my right.
“Unless you’re family by blood, of course.”
Even the most oblivious person in the hall would have understood what he meant.
Hundreds of eyes converged on us. Amid them, a voice reached my ear in secret.
*I don’t know what you came here intending to do, but remember one thing from this moment on.*
Michael Silbert was looking straight at me. The crocodile tears were gone from his eyes. Only ambition shone there now.
*Every choice has consequences to match.*
*So choose carefully. You’ll get only one chance, and you won’t be able to take it back.*
His final warning came with a stare. His eyes, and all the others fixed on us, felt so hot that I closed mine.
*Yeah. So this is how it turns out.*
*From the very beginning...*
*There was no other way.*
I opened my eyes, feeling hollowed out. Team Leader Choi met my gaze, read what was there, and rose from his seat.
*Scrape.*
The chair, which had endured for ages longer than its new master, slowly scraped backward. At that moment—
“Before we elect a representative—the purpose of today’s inaugural ceremony—I must inform you that my maternal grandfather, Hunter Cheon Taemin...”
At last, his name was spoken. In the breathless silence that followed, the savior’s only blood relative continued quietly.
“...has become seriously ill and will be unable to take part in this war.”
An enormous, unseen shock swept through the hall.
A suffocating silence settled over the First National Assembly Hall.
Frozen by shock and confusion, the people inside could do nothing but turn those words over and over in their minds.
*My maternal grandfather, Hunter Cheon Taemin, has become seriously ill and will be unable to take part in this war.*
Barely ten minutes into the inaugural ceremony, a bomb had gone off.
No. In another sense, it was a catastrophe.
*Sky is sick? What on earth does that mean?*
*How could he be? It can’t be true.*
The elders—the Hunters of the older generation—rejected the news most fiercely.
They remembered Cheon Taemin, the great hero who had saved humanity from the Demon King. The shock struck them harder than anyone.
It was only natural. In their memories, Cheon Taemin had been more than human, almost a living god.
They had seen him single-handedly destroy monster armies tens of thousands strong and tear the limbs from mighty S-rank monsters. His bearing had been as commanding as his strength.
With Cheon Taemin beside them, they had willingly marched into the jaws of death. Shoulder to shoulder, they had cut through wave after wave of monsters and kept advancing.

The elders could bear to remember those horrific battlefields because Cheon Taemin was part of those memories. Because those memories held the shining glory of having led humanity to victory alongside him.
And now he was ill?
The savior who had defeated even the Demon King Asmodeus was too ill to join the war?
Shock gave way to a hollow sense of loss. Some of the elders grew angry.
“What—what on earth is this supposed to mean?”
“Gravely ill? Even for someone like your maternal grandfather, that’s too much to believe!”
“Explain yourself. There’s no way he could be sick!”
But contrary to the elders’ desperate wishes, Cheon Taemin’s only maternal grandson merely shook his head, calm and composed.
“Everything I’ve told you is absolutely true.”
“Young man!”
“I understand how you feel, Seniors. I felt the same way a few months ago.”
“What... do you mean?”
“I always wondered where my grandfather was. What reason could he possibly have for not showing himself even to his only grandson, after all this time?”
Choi Minwoo looked around at everyone and continued.

“I didn’t learn the truth until after Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong and Go Jun died. At some point, for reasons we still don’t know, my grandfather fell into a coma. A very small number of people had been hiding it.”
Shock swept through the hall again. This time, the silence did not last.
“It’s hard to believe, but it’s true. I can vouch for it.”
A low voice had spoken up. A towering Black man, who had been watching the situation in silence, was looking at them.
“Magic Johnson!”
“Y-You knew too?”
Magic Johnson nodded before answering.
“Those young men contacted me a few months ago, and I came to this country. I didn’t expect to find Sky unconscious.”
“Th-Then it really is...”

“Yes. I drew on everything I know, every bit of Magic I could think of, and found no way to bring him back to consciousness. I couldn’t tell anyone else, either. If a secret like that got out, it would have caused even more chaos.”

People remembered what had been happening then. Magical power readings had begun to rise, and strange events had followed. In China, an Arch Lich had led a monster army through Sichuan, drenching it in blood. The public had grown more anxious by the day.
“But we can’t hide it any longer. The whole world is looking for Sky. Now that the World Hunter Federation has taken its first step, it has to give them the answer they want, just as the UN did.”
One word crossed everyone’s mind.
*Leader.*

With Cheon Taemin incapacitated, they needed a new leader somehow. A new hero who could fill the savior’s absence as much as possible. Someone who could win the support of a majority of the three hundred people gathered around this enormous round table.
*Then...*
By the time that thought formed, most had already made up their minds.
Strength. Fame. Popularity. A spirit of sacrifice and courage. Leadership...
Each had their own standards, and even among those already called heroes, only a handful met them.
One man in particular could not be overlooked.
Michael Silbert.
Countless eyes turned his way. Some people smiled triumphantly, as though the moment they had been waiting for had arrived. Others watched him, still weighing their decision.
Michael gave nothing away.
With only one step left to take, he was already thinking about what came after.
*It’s sooner than I expected, but... I need to get rid of him. As soon as possible.*
The absolute power of the World Hunter Federation already felt close enough to touch. But an obstacle that would continue to trouble him had to be removed.
Michael Silbert fixed his sunken eyes on one man.
Even as voting began, Jin Taekyung sat with his lips firmly closed. Beside him was a blond monster with a calm expression.
I looked down at the scrap of iron in my hand.
*What was it called again?*
Ostracism? A pottery-shard lottery?
I thought it had originated with a method the ancient Athenians used to banish tyrants, but I wasn’t sure.

One thing I did know: what I held wasn’t a piece of pottery, but a fragment of a Tower Shield. And the person whose name appeared on the most fragments wouldn’t be banished—they’d become the leader of the World Hunter Federation.
*Would’ve been nice if it worked the other way around, huh?*
I sent the Sound Transmission on a whim. To my surprise, an answer came back.
*What the hell are you talking about all of a sudden?*
*Just saying. You’re answering me this time, though.*
*Because this will probably be the last time.*
I turned the scrap of iron over in my fingers.
*You crazy bastard. I wondered why you’d answered me, but you’re still on about that.*
*I know what you’re thinking. But it’s too...*
*Dangerous?*
After a brief silence, the Skeleton King answered.
*Yes. Even now, this body cannot be certain.*
*The odds are close to fifty-fifty. And this is just a guess, but I think the chance of success is a little higher.*
*Do you understand what that means? There’s a fifty percent chance you could lose everything.*
*Really? To me, it sounds like there’s a fifty percent chance I could protect everything.*
*Trust me.*
I looked around. Familiar faces. People I could trust, right beside me. Every one of them a comrade and a friend.
*If you really can’t trust me, trust us.*
This silence lasted longer than the first. Then, for the first time in a long while, I met the Skeleton King’s eyes.
*Why go this far? Why take that risk when your family and friends could get hurt?*
I answered with a truth that might have been settled the day I first met him.
*Because you’re my friend, too.*
