chapters.title: Chapter 778
paragraphs: *Because you’re my friend, too.*
At those quiet words, the Skeleton King’s eyes trembled. I looked straight at him and continued.
*That’s all there is to it. You’re my friend, too. If I lost you like this, I’d feel like shit for the rest of my life. That’s why I can’t give up.*
*Remember when we fought the Arch Lich in China?*
The Skeleton King nodded silently.
Yeah. How could I forget?
That fierce battle was still etched vividly in my mind.
*I really thought I was going to die. No—if things had kept going the way they were, I’d probably have died nine times out of ten.*
It had been that hard a fight.
Countless monsters had blocked our path. And the Arch Lich we’d finally faced after killing Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing, who had chosen to betray us, had been too much for me at the time.
But...
*You saved me. Even knowing you might be erased.*
I could still see him leaping out of my Inventory without even asking permission and taking the Arch Lich’s strike in my place at that life-or-death moment.
It was a sacrifice.
A pure, noble sacrifice.
At the same time, it was a great deed that allowed an ordinary someone to finally become a new being.
And so the Skeleton Warlord who had ruled the Black Forest gained a crown.
He returned from the brink of Erasure, took up the radiant [Hero’s Sword], and drove it into the Arch Lich’s chest.
*Why did you make that choice back then?*
*...Who knows. I don’t.*
The Skeleton King turned his gaze to empty space and muttered.
*All I know is that I had a very stupid, very trivial reason.*
*A reason?*
*There was something I’d always wondered. Who am I? Where was I born, and what sin did I commit to become the monster I am now? Surely I wasn’t always like this.*
His hollow thoughts echoed in my ears.

*But no matter how hard I tried, I couldn’t remember my life before this. Even while living among humans, I was confused every moment I spent with them. I felt like something that was neither monster nor human. As though I were serving an endless sentence for a sin I’d committed in the past.*
Yeah. Back then, that was how the Skeleton King had been.
He was always lost in thought, looking troubled. Sometimes he’d go into my Inventory and not say a word for days.
Then one day, I’d said something to him in passing.
*I bet you were a pretty decent guy.*
I didn’t know for sure, but I was certain of it.
*That was why. Maybe you’d only said it to comfort me, but I wanted to believe you. And part of me wanted to prove you right. If I really had been a decent guy in the past...*
The Skeleton King slowly tilted his head. His gaze left the empty space and settled on me.
*Then perhaps I could sacrifice myself for someone else... for a friend.*
*Yes, that’s right, you damn crafty human.*
A faint smile touched the Skeleton King’s lips.
*You were the first friend this body made after coming into this world.*
For a moment, I couldn’t speak.
I had to say something. I should have, but not a single word came to mind.
So I just smiled.
I smiled silently at first, then let out a few quiet chuckles before I couldn’t hold back any longer and burst out laughing.
Loud enough for everyone across the enormous round table to hear. Loud enough to draw hundreds of pairs of eyes toward us.
Then I looked at the Skeleton King, who was blinking in surprise, and said, “You only figured out something that simple now, you dumbass?”
*C-Could you keep your voice down?*
“Just say it out loud. Stop whispering so no one else can hear.”
*What the—*
“It’s too late anyway. Can’t you see everyone’s already staring?”
The Skeleton King looked around, then muttered in a half-resigned voice.
“Madman.”
“What, madman? You finished?”
“I’m not finished. You attention-seeking bastard.”
“Listen to the way this guy talks. Team Leader Choi, aren’t you going to manage him?”
“Manage... what?”
Suddenly singled out, Team Leader Choi clenched his teeth, looking as if grim reality had just hit him.
“Yes, that’s right. I’m sorry. This is all my fault for failing to manage Jin Taekyung.”
“Come on, Team Leader. You’re going to hurt my feelings if you pile on, too.”
“I’m the one whose feelings are hurt. If things had gone according to plan, in a little while... No, why even make a plan if you’re going to do this?”
Fair enough.
But what could I do? Things had gone this way.
People’s affairs often took turns no one could predict. Just like right now.
Even so, I wasn’t the least bit uneasy about having done things out of order.
Yeah. That was good enough for me.
I burst out laughing again, then put on a deep, serious voice as I addressed Team Leader Choi.
“Team Leader Choi, haven’t you heard the saying, ‘It doesn’t matter how you get there as long as you get to Seoul’?”
“I don’t want to hear it. And we’re already in Seoul.”
“Come on, say it with me. Heave. Ho. Heave. Ho.”
“To hell with heaving and ho-ing. I think we’re royally fucked.”
“You’re acting all stubborn because you’re sulking, aren’t you? This was going to happen anyway.”
“The order is wrong! The order! Do you put the ramen in before the water boils?”
“No. Today I’m crushing it up and eating it without boiling it.”
“You motherfucking—!”
The man who could make Team Leader Choi swear like that.
That was me.
Just as Team Leader Choi’s eyes rolled back and he was about to spring to his feet, two enormous hands shot out from behind him and grabbed him.
*Grab!*
“Hey, Choi! Calm down!”
“Let go! You hear me? Get your hands off me right now!”
“Please, get a grip! I think Jin made a mistake, too, but... Wait. Have you been bulking up lately?”
This was a mess beyond all messes.
Seeing my chance, I gave Magic Johnson a thumbs-up as he felt Team Leader Choi’s lean muscles, then stood and looked around.
Open mouths. Faces asking what the hell was going on. Eyes gone unfocused.

A commotion had erupted out of nowhere at this important meeting to elect the World Hunter Federation’s representative as humanity faced a crisis. Everyone looked as if they’d just seen Demon King Asmodeus brought back with Edo Tensei.
Except for the few who already knew what was going on.
“Ah, I’m sorry. I wasn’t planning to spring this on you yet.”
It was a sincere, polite apology. But sometimes sincerity just didn’t get through.
“You damn bastard. This might be the last cigar of my life.”
Chuck Hagel pretended to answer with the bleak resignation of a terminal lung cancer patient, all while puffing on his cigar twice as fast.
“It’s okay. I trust you. But go fuck yourself, Jin.”
Faye Chen gave me a warm smile and raised her middle finger.
“I’m sorry, Your Majesty. I trusted that lunatic and made a rash choice...”
Prince Felix, third in line to the British throne, muttered with a look of regret.
But if I had to name the most bewildered person among the three hundred gathered here, it would be Michael Silbert.
*What on earth... are you up to?*
His voice crossed the space between us and reached my ear.
His face was stiffer than I’d ever seen it. I couldn’t help laughing.
*You’re laughing?*
It was only natural to answer someone who was curious.
I opened my mouth without a care.
“Yeah, I laughed. What are you going to do about it?”
The voice in my ear cut off. By now, everyone in the room was following my gaze, looking back and forth between Michael Silbert and me.
“If you have something to say, say it out loud so everyone can hear. You’re too old to be whispering in my ear.”
That sounded a little rude, so I shyly added one more thing.
“You motherfucker.”
The room went silent, as if hundreds of nuclear missiles had swept through it. The air around us froze.
But unlike the others watching this unbelievable scene, I welcomed that cold air. It felt as if something blocking my throat and chest had finally cleared.
*I can finally breathe.*
How long had it been since I’d felt this relieved?
I took a deep breath and started trudging along. I passed between the round tables, then got tired of even that after a few steps and leaped over everyone’s heads.
*Whoosh. Tap.*
I landed lightly in the empty center of the round table.
Michael Silbert clenched his teeth. He stood there unable to set foot in that space, as though an invisible wall held him back.
“What... is this insolence?”
His voice was tightly restrained.
His eyes, fixed on me, held anger he couldn’t hide. And I knew exactly why.
“What, you spent half your life wishing for that seat, and now some nobody gets there before you? That piss you off?”

“Honestly, I understand. Something similar happened to me once. I’d saved some ice cream to eat after my bath, but when I came out, my little sister had eaten it all and left me the wrapper. I was pretty pissed. But...”
I trailed off, watching Michael Silbert’s rigid face, then continued slowly.
“Then I suddenly thought, what am I getting so mad about over something this trivial? Is it really worth throwing a fit over?”
I looked around. Just as I’d expected, most people were staring at me like I was crazy.
Naturally. I’d caused a scene at the most important moment, hurled curses at a Senior, and now I was telling an ice cream story nobody had asked for.
Their expressions were so funny that I laughed again.
“Anyway, that’s all.”
At the same time, I drew up my internal energy and stamped my foot down hard.
“Don’t—!”
*Crack! Crunch!*
Michael Silbert’s belated shout vanished beneath the roar.
In the split second when nobody could stop me, I completely crushed the center of the round table, a place set aside for just one man. Then I looked at the faces staring at me in shock.
“After thinking about it, I realized that seat was just like that ice cream. If nobody was greedy, there’d be nothing to get angry about. But the greedy ones always step forward and cause trouble.”
Of course, the difference between ice cream and the World Hunter Federation was beyond comparison.
Their importance in this world. And... the scale of what that greed had caused.
People had died because of that greed.
Hundreds of thousands of people had lost their families and friends, their homes and their hopes.
After paying such a high price, all they’d gained was despair and fear.
So what made that seat any different from the ice cream?
It was ridiculous. And it left me feeling hollow.
I spoke to the hundreds of people staring at me in shock.
“Everyone, listen.”
No. I was speaking to Michael Silbert.
“The Stone-King is a monster.”
That one casually tossed-out line swallowed everyone whole and exploded.

paragraphs: For a moment, the world seemed to stop.
If not for the camera flashes blinking at regular intervals and the ticking of second hands, people might have thought time really had frozen.
But the silence didn’t last long.
“He’s crazy.”
The words came from somewhere in the room.
Countless others looked back and forth between Jin Taekyung and the Stone-King, laughing in disbelief.
They couldn’t help it. Everyone here knew who the Stone-King was.
No—ask anyone on the street, and they’d know, too.
An S-rank Hunter with United States citizenship who had appeared out of nowhere like a comet.
As skilled as he was handsome, he was always at Jin Taekyung’s side. That had drawn attention from the start, and he’d distinguished himself in several major incidents.

He’d faced criticism alongside Jin for taking part in the operation against the terrorists in the so-called “vigilante incident.” But most agreed that his contributions far outweighed anything held against him.
And now the Stone-King—a young hero of the new generation who had even earned a seat at the round table—was a monster?
Instead of confusion, disbelieving laughter spread through the room.
“Enough with the nonsense.”
Speaking up once was hard. After that, it got easier.
Those who had held their tongues out of respect for Jin Taekyung’s strength and standing began to raise their voices.
“Young man, we’ve let you go on long enough. Aren’t you taking this too far?”
“Jin, I respect you as a fellow Hunter, but... you owe us a proper explanation for what you’ve done here today.”
“They said he had post-traumatic stress disorder. Looks like it was true.”
The fuse was burning down fast.
Even the elders who had looked favorably on Jin from the start murmured uneasily. Those who had already opposed him seized their chance and criticized him outright.
“Everyone, look at what he’s done. He caused a disturbance while we were electing the leader of the Federation that will save humanity. He even damaged the round table.”
“And now he’s spouting nonsense.”
“What kind of disrespect is this?”
Criticism poured in from every direction.
But Jin Taekyung, at the center of it all, addressed the room as though he hadn’t heard a word.
Once again.
Without changing a single word.
“The Stone-King is a monster.”
“That’s all you have to say? The same nonsense again?”
“He’s crazy. Completely crazy.”
Jin Taekyung slowly looked around.
Some laughed in disbelief. Some frowned. Others watched with grave, steady eyes.
Their reactions varied, but the words that came from Jin Taekyung’s mouth did not.
“The Stone-King is a monster.”
“What is this—!”
“Strip him of his qualifications at once!”
The criticism had become shouting. Jin paid it no mind and opened his mouth again.
“The Stone-King is...”
As if those were the only words he knew. As if imprinting that one fact on their minds were his sole purpose in life.
Without pause, ignoring every gaze and every accusation pouring toward him.
Calmly, he repeated the truth that might become his greatest weakness, looking straight at Michael Silbert—the one man who had remained silent through the uproar around the enormous round table.
“A monster.”
For the third time.
The mocking smiles faded as people watched him repeat the words like a machine.
The shouts stopped. So did the pointing fingers. No one moved or spoke.
Silence settled over the room.
And in that silence, too complete for even the sound of someone swallowing, a realization came to them.
Jin Taekyung was telling the truth.
His expression. His voice. His eyes. Nothing about him suggested a lie.
And they understood what that meant.
*...No way.*
The same impossible question crossed everyone’s mind.
At the same time, hundreds of pairs of eyes turned toward one person.
No—toward something that might not be a person at all.
The Stone-King.
The handsome American was still sitting where he had been all along. But they could see it. They could feel it.
The slight trembling of his eyes and the faint fear seeping through them. The certainty that this was the answer to their question.
Then the truth they had finally accepted came with an enormous unseen shock that swept through the room like a wave.
No. Like a hammer.
Everyone stared, mouths agape.
What was reflected now in roughly three hundred pairs of wide-open eyes was neither a handsome young man nor an S-rank Hunter with outstanding skills and Fame.
There stood a cursed being who could never coexist with humanity, one who had once driven mankind to the brink of disaster.
“...A monster.”
Someone’s mutter, almost a groan, broke the silence.
*Clang, clang, clang!*
Hundreds of weapons flashed beneath the lights of the vast hall.
The radiance of Aura—the power God had given humanity—spread in every direction before turning toward a single being.
With it came killing intent so palpable it seemed one could touch it.
*Ssssss.*
A wind whipped up from somewhere. In the freezing air, countless needle-sharp gazes pierced the Stone-King.
Everyone here had been chosen by God for the sole purpose of fighting monsters, and given the name Hunter by humanity.
From the beginning, they had had only one duty.
*Kill monsters.*
*Whoooosh.*
Hundreds of surging powers and killing intent joined, pressing down on the hall and bearing toward their target—
“Stop!”
*Bang!*
The shout roared like a wild beast. Its deep resonance found a gap in that split second and scattered everything like mist.
The faces of the people who had been ready to swing their weapons went rigid.
*What the hell...*
A place awash in killing intent and mana was as good as a death trap.
But the voice’s owner had broken that flow. At the very last moment, just as an attack was about to be unleashed, he had slipped through an invisible gap.
And he’d done it with ease.
*Step. Step.*
The low thud of footsteps broke the suffocating silence.

As one young man cut through the mountain of sabers and forest of swords formed by countless weapons and stood in front of everyone, an elder Hunter with a full head of white hair spoke with a stern expression.
“What are you doing?”
Recognizing the elder, Jin Taekyung answered respectfully.
“I’m doing what I have to do, Senior.”
“And what you have to do is... protect that monster?”
“I do.”
At Jin’s unhesitating reply, the elder Hunter asked with an expression of disbelief.
“Why?”
“Because he’s my friend.”
“...Your friend?”
“He’s also a comrade-in-arms who saved my life. I have to protect him, just as he protected me.”
Friend? Comrade-in-arms?
No one had imagined hearing those words used for a monster. While they struggled to respond, a voice rose from the encirclement that had formed around Jin.
“If you’re going that far, there’s no need to hear anything more.”
A shining suit of full armor. A massive war hammer in his hand.
The middle-aged man stepped forward, radiating a weighty aura and an oppressive presence. His eyes were on Jin Taekyung, but he addressed the whole room.
“This is treason against humanity. An unforgivable betrayal. You know the punishment, don’t you?”
Jin Taekyung nodded.
“Of course.”
“Good. Then, as of this moment, your Hunter qualifications are revoked. The traitor will be executed on the spot.”
*Rumble.*
A dense glow gathered in layers around the war hammer.
He was an S-rank Hunter who had fought since the Great Cataclysm, a man who had made the Kronos Guild one of the world’s top ten Guilds.
But Jin Taekyung’s response went far beyond anything the onlookers expected.
“Fuck, don’t be so damn ridiculous.”
“What?”
“That speech was so long-winded I couldn’t even follow every stupid point. But first, I want to ask you one thing.”
Jin Taekyung fixed a cold gaze on the Guild Master of the Kronos Guild.
“If you were going to throw this kind of fit, why did you treat me like a lunatic just now?”
“That’s...”
“That’s what?”
The Guild Master of the Kronos Guild fell silent.
So did everyone else who had heard the question.
Jin had struck a nerve.
They’d dismissed his words as nonsense from the start. Through all their criticism, he had quietly told them the same thing three times.
Until the smiles vanished. Until they realized it was true.
But why hadn’t they believed him, when he’d meant every word?
The answer was simple.
Perhaps it was a truth they had known all along and could only pretend not to see.

“Let’s be honest. Now that you know the truth, you don’t want to accept it. That the guy sitting over there—a monster, of all things—has fought harder for humanity than some of the assholes here who have no business being at this table.”
“Though I get it, too. Who’d believe the Stone-King was a monster just because I said so? Right?”
No one answered. Jin Taekyung smiled.

“This is a black comedy if I’ve ever seen one. There are assholes everywhere who aren’t even human, but the guy who nearly worked himself to death trying to save one more person is standing at death’s door the moment his identity comes out.”
Cold flames flickered in the young man’s eyes, visible above his raised smile.
Countless weapons surrounded them. As he looked at that forest of blades, poised to come flying at any moment, the emotion rising inside him had a name: anger and bitterness.
“I didn’t want this. I wasn’t asking for much. I just... thought you’d give me enough time to explain.”
Jin Taekyung’s voice sounded hollow.
Of course he understood. Many of them must have lost people close to them to monsters.
He had, too.
But... even so, something churned inside him.

He felt sorry for the Skeleton King, who had fought while sacrificing himself for humanity. He felt bitter watching those people try to kill him without a moment’s hesitation, and his anger rose when he realized how many of them still showed outright hostility, even in this situation.
Because he knew their hostility wasn’t only about his calling the Skeleton King—a monster—his friend and comrade-in-arms.
He knew where that hostility was aimed, what it was meant to accomplish, and who stood behind those people, using them like puppets.
*Step.*
Jin Taekyung started forward.
The Guild Master of the Kronos Guild was the first to grasp what the movement meant. He moved to swing his war hammer like a bolt of lightning.
Or he would have, if a voice hadn’t reached his ear.
“You’d better stop there, Fabian.”
*Rumble.*
The air trembled.
The Guild Master of the Kronos Guild turned toward the towering Black man who had risen from his seat. His expression hardened.
“Johnson.”
“Been a while. Age has made you even more charming.”
Magic Johnson winked and gestured with his staff toward the war hammer rippling with Aura.
“Whoa. Don’t do anything rash. Take it from a comrade-in-arms who’s risked his life fighting beside you.”
“Do you know what your actions mean right now?”
“Of course. You don’t have to tell me. We know exactly where we’re going from here.”
Fabian repeated the word without thinking. Then he saw the answer for himself.
*Rustle. Thud.*
People rose from their seats—some quietly, some noisily, some with an air of dignity.
The Guild Master of the Kronos Guild’s gaze darkened as he took in those familiar, distinguished faces.
Magic Johnson. Chuck Hagel. Faye Chen. Prince Felix.

And then Choi Minwoo, whose symbolic significance as Cheon Taemin’s only blood relative was unmistakable. Finally, even the Stone-King, who had been watching the weapons aimed at him with a hard expression, stood up.
*This is bad. It’s already beyond the range Michael predicted.*
But the greatest surprise was the young man who had reached him.
“Move.”
“I can’t—”
“I said move.”
For the first time in a long while, a chill sank into the Guild Master of the Kronos Guild’s bones.
It came from a young man who hadn’t lived half as long as he had.
Magic Johnson’s warning flashed through his mind. *You’d better stop there. Don’t do anything rash.*
He understood, too, who that warning had been for.
*Step.*
By the time he came to his senses, it was already too late. The Guild Master of the Kronos Guild instinctively shifted to the side, and Jin Taekyung walked on as if that were only natural.

Half of the roughly three hundred people surrounding them tried to stop him, then found themselves making way without knowing why. Of those who remained, half merely watched; others closed around Jin as if to escort him.
Amid the frozen air and mounting tension, two men faced each other again at the center of the round table.
Jin Taekyung and Michael Silbert.
Michael Silbert and Jin Taekyung.
Their gazes met and flared—cold yet fiery, fiery yet cold.
A voice rang out clearly enough for everyone to hear.
“Do you know what consequences your actions today, and the truth you’ve revealed, will bring?”
“Hard to say. I guess all kinds of assholes will come after me now.”
Jin Taekyung added calmly, “And the worst of them is standing right in front of me.”
A muscle twitched in Michael Silbert’s cheek.
His composure had begun to falter the moment Jin Taekyung revealed the truth to everyone.
But it was fine. It was fine.
The throne was still there.
Once the vote began, the place where he sat would become the throne.
Jin Taekyung, on the other hand, had no seat left at this round table.
Soon, he would have no place anywhere in the world.
“I can tell you one thing for certain. Now that the Stone-King’s identity has been revealed, I’m afraid the World Hunter Federation’s first vote will be on your permanent expulsion.”
“Really? Why?”

“If he truly was unlike an ordinary monster, and you’d told us immediately, everyone—including me—would have given it careful thought. But it’s too late. You hid a secret this serious. No one can trust you now.”

Michael Silbert continued, his voice raised as if to call out to everyone.
“They’ll be executed on the spot.”

*Thump.*
His heart dropped.
*Thump. Thump-thump.*

What was it? Why was it?
Why was that bastard smiling even in a situation like this?
Why?

His pounding heart and trembling pulse filled his ears. Every one of his senses, fixed on Jin Taekyung, caught the words that followed.
“What if you hadn’t colluded with a monster, but...”

“You were already no different from one? What would happen then?”
No—it shook everyone’s world.
With a contemptuous gaze fixed on something neither human nor monster, Jin delivered one final line.
“Has the wound on your neck healed, Michael?”

sentences.text: For a moment, the world seemed to stop.
If not for the camera flashes blinking at regular intervals and the ticking of second hands, people might have thought time really had frozen.
But the silence didn’t last long.
“He’s crazy.”
The words came from somewhere in the room.
Countless others looked back and forth between Jin Taekyung and the Stone-King, laughing in disbelief.
They couldn’t help it.
Everyone here knew who the Stone-King was.
No—ask anyone on the street, and they’d know, too.
An S-rank Hunter with United States citizenship who had appeared out of nowhere like a comet.
As skilled as he was handsome, he was always at Jin Taekyung’s side.
That had drawn attention from the start, and he’d distinguished himself in several major incidents.

He’d faced criticism alongside Jin for taking part in the operation against the terrorists in the so-called “vigilante incident.” But most agreed that his contributions far outweighed anything held against him.
And now the Stone-King—a young hero of the new generation who had even earned a seat at the round table—was a monster?
Instead of confusion, disbelieving laughter spread through the room.
“Enough with the nonsense.”
Speaking up once was hard.
After that, it got easier.
Those who had held their tongues out of respect for Jin Taekyung’s strength and standing began to raise their voices.
“Young man, we’ve let you go on long enough.
Aren’t you taking this too far?”
“Jin, I respect you as a fellow Hunter, but... you owe us a proper explanation for what you’ve done here today.”
“They said he had post-traumatic stress disorder.
Looks like it was true.”
The fuse was burning down fast.
Even the elders who had looked favorably on Jin from the start murmured uneasily.
Those who had already opposed him seized their chance and criticized him outright.
“Everyone, look at what he’s done.
He caused a disturbance while we were electing the leader of the Federation that will save humanity.
He even damaged the round table.”
“And now he’s spouting nonsense.”
“What kind of disrespect is this?”
Criticism poured in from every direction.
But Jin Taekyung, at the center of it all, addressed the room as though he hadn’t heard a word.
Once again.
Without changing a single word.
“The Stone-King is a monster.”
“That’s all you have to say?
The same nonsense again?”
“He’s crazy.
Completely crazy.”
Jin Taekyung slowly looked around.
Some laughed in disbelief.
Some frowned.
Others watched with grave, steady eyes.
Their reactions varied, but the words that came from Jin Taekyung’s mouth did not.
“The Stone-King is a monster.”
“What is this—!”
“Strip him of his qualifications at once!”
The criticism had become shouting.
Jin paid it no mind and opened his mouth again.
“The Stone-King is...”
As if those were the only words he knew.
As if imprinting that one fact on their minds were his sole purpose in life.
Without pause, ignoring every gaze and every accusation pouring toward him.
Calmly, he repeated the truth that might become his greatest weakness, looking straight at Michael Silbert—the one man who had remained silent through the uproar around the enormous round table.
“A monster.”
For the third time.
The mocking smiles faded as people watched him repeat the words like a machine.
The shouts stopped.
So did the pointing fingers.
No one moved or spoke.
Silence settled over the room.
And in that silence, too complete for even the sound of someone swallowing, a realization came to them.
Jin Taekyung was telling the truth.
His expression.
His voice.
His eyes.
Nothing about him suggested a lie.
And they understood what that meant.
*...No way.*
The same impossible question crossed everyone’s mind.
At the same time, hundreds of pairs of eyes turned toward one person.
No—toward something that might not be a person at all.
The Stone-King.
The handsome American was still sitting where he had been all along.
But they could see it.
They could feel it.
The slight trembling of his eyes and the faint fear seeping through them.
The certainty that this was the answer to their question.
Then the truth they had finally accepted came with an enormous unseen shock that swept through the room like a wave.
No.
Like a hammer.
Everyone stared, mouths agape.
What was reflected now in roughly three hundred pairs of wide-open eyes was neither a handsome young man nor an S-rank Hunter with outstanding skills and Fame.
There stood a cursed being who could never coexist with humanity, one who had once driven mankind to the brink of disaster.
“...A monster.”
Someone’s mutter, almost a groan, broke the silence.
*Clang, clang, clang!*
Hundreds of weapons flashed beneath the lights of the vast hall.
The radiance of Aura—the power God had given humanity—spread in every direction before turning toward a single being.
With it came killing intent so palpable it seemed one could touch it.
*Ssssss.*
A wind whipped up from somewhere.
In the freezing air, countless needle-sharp gazes pierced the Stone-King.
Everyone here had been chosen by God for the sole purpose of fighting monsters, and given the name Hunter by humanity.
From the beginning, they had had only one duty.
*Kill monsters.*
*Whoooosh.*
Hundreds of surging powers and killing intent joined, pressing down on the hall and bearing toward their target—
“Stop!”
*Bang!*
The shout roared like a wild beast.
Its deep resonance found a gap in that split second and scattered everything like mist.
The faces of the people who had been ready to swing their weapons went rigid.
*What the hell...*
A place awash in killing intent and mana was as good as a death trap.
But the voice’s owner had broken that flow.
At the very last moment, just as an attack was about to be unleashed, he had slipped through an invisible gap.
And he’d done it with ease.
*Step.
Step.*
The low thud of footsteps broke the suffocating silence.

As one young man cut through the mountain of sabers and forest of swords formed by countless weapons and stood in front of everyone, an elder Hunter with a full head of white hair spoke with a stern expression.
“What are you doing?”
Recognizing the elder, Jin Taekyung answered respectfully.
“I’m doing what I have to do, Senior.”
“And what you have to do is... protect that monster?”
“I do.”
At Jin’s unhesitating reply, the elder Hunter asked with an expression of disbelief.
“Why?”
“Because he’s my friend.”
“...Your friend?”
“He’s also a comrade-in-arms who saved my life.
I have to protect him, just as he protected me.”
Friend?
Comrade-in-arms?
No one had imagined hearing those words used for a monster.
While they struggled to respond, a voice rose from the encirclement that had formed around Jin.
“If you’re going that far, there’s no need to hear anything more.”
A shining suit of full armor.
A massive war hammer in his hand.
The middle-aged man stepped forward, radiating a weighty aura and an oppressive presence.
His eyes were on Jin Taekyung, but he addressed the whole room.
“This is treason against humanity.
An unforgivable betrayal.
You know the punishment, don’t you?”
Jin Taekyung nodded.
“Of course.”
“Good.
Then, as of this moment, your Hunter qualifications are revoked.
The traitor will be executed on the spot.”
*Rumble.*
A dense glow gathered in layers around the war hammer.
He was an S-rank Hunter who had fought since the Great Cataclysm, a man who had made the Kronos Guild one of the world’s top ten Guilds.
But Jin Taekyung’s response went far beyond anything the onlookers expected.
“Fuck, don’t be so damn ridiculous.”
“What?”
“That speech was so long-winded I couldn’t even follow every stupid point.
But first, I want to ask you one thing.”
Jin Taekyung fixed a cold gaze on the Guild Master of the Kronos Guild.
“If you were going to throw this kind of fit, why did you treat me like a lunatic just now?”
“That’s...”
“That’s what?”
The Guild Master of the Kronos Guild fell silent.
So did everyone else who had heard the question.
Jin had struck a nerve.
They’d dismissed his words as nonsense from the start.
Through all their criticism, he had quietly told them the same thing three times.
Until the smiles vanished.
Until they realized it was true.
But why hadn’t they believed him, when he’d meant every word?
The answer was simple.
Perhaps it was a truth they had known all along and could only pretend not to see.
“Let’s be honest.
Now that you know the truth, you don’t want to accept it.
That the guy sitting over there—a monster, of all things—has fought harder for humanity than some of the assholes here who have no business being at this table.”
“Though I get it, too.
Who’d believe the Stone-King was a monster just because I said so?
Right?”
No one answered.
Jin Taekyung smiled.
“This is a black comedy if I’ve ever seen one.
There are assholes everywhere who aren’t even human, but the guy who nearly worked himself to death trying to save one more person is standing at death’s door the moment his identity comes out.”
Cold flames flickered in the young man’s eyes, visible above his raised smile.
Countless weapons surrounded them.
As he looked at that forest of blades, poised to come flying at any moment, the emotion rising inside him had a name: anger and bitterness.
“I didn’t want this.

I just... thought you’d give me enough time to explain.”
Jin Taekyung’s voice sounded hollow.
Of course he understood.
Many of them must have lost people close to them to monsters.
He had, too.

*Step.*

“You’d better stop there, Fabian.”
*Rumble.*
The air trembled.

Age has made you even more charming.”

chapters.title: Chapter 780
paragraphs: The world was full of events and the possibilities that followed them.
The problem was that none of those possibilities was certain.
No matter how far civilization advanced, no matter how deeply cutting-edge science reached into realms once beyond its grasp, there was no such thing as absolute, one-hundred-percent certainty.
Especially where people, rather than machines, were concerned.
But at this moment—
“Has the wound on your neck healed, Michael?”
Looking at his trembling gray eyes, I was certain.
The unbelievable question that had begun with the tiniest clue had finally revealed its dark shape.
At last, I’d driven Michael Silbert to the edge of a cliff.
But I wiped the smile from my lips. My disgust for the man before me outweighed any pleasure I took in turning the tables.
I despised everything about that man steeped in gray.
“You filthy piece of shit.”
My voice broke the silence.
Unlike when I’d revealed the Skeleton King’s identity, not one person in the room laughed at me this time.
No. They hadn’t fully understood what they’d just heard.
Or perhaps they couldn’t bring themselves to accept a truth so far beyond anything they’d imagined.
“What... what the hell does that mean?”
The Guild Master of Kronos. I kept my eyes on Michael Silbert as I answered.
“Ask him yourself.”
In the suffocating silence, hundreds of pairs of eyes turned toward Michael Silbert. Among those watching were his supporters—some I’d identified through my investigation, and some I hadn’t.
“You were all kissing his ass from every angle earlier. Guess nobody bothered telling you what was really going on. Well, I can see why. Can’t you?”
Michael Silbert didn’t answer. He simply stared at me.
His gray eyes were still unsettled, and I could almost read the thoughts racing through his head.
But—
“Don’t strain yourself trying to figure it out. You already know, don’t you?”
Once all the equations lined up, the answer was clear.
“Michael Silbert.”
I felt as if I’d finally found my way out of a maze I’d wandered for ages.
Beyond the walls that had hemmed me in on every side, someone waited at the exit.
A gray monster who’d lingered somewhere between light and darkness, then crossed a river from which there was no return.
The last edge of the veil hiding what he really was.
I let out the breath I’d been holding.
“You’re fucked now.”
Michael Silbert found himself wondering when things had started going wrong. How? Where?
But no matter how hard he thought, he couldn’t find an answer.
Everything that had led to this moment came down to one person. Even if Michael found an answer, the man before him would surely create another variable.
*Jin Taekyung.*
Another name for endless variables.
An Eastern young man far too young, reckless, and frivolous to stand in his way.
Yet Michael Silbert could no longer deny it.
That young man wasn’t merely an obstacle to be removed. He was another wall Michael should have broken down at all costs.
*Such heat.*
The heat in those black eyes.
At the same time, the wound on the back of Michael’s neck—still there like a brand—burned with pain.
*Tap.*
Without realizing it, Michael Silbert reached for his neck.
But when his fingertips met the cold armor that covered it all the way up to his throat, hiding the wound, a dry laugh escaped him.
Excuses? Damage control?
Meaningless now. They would only make him look pathetic.
As a single drop of water could split a rock, one palm-sized bottle of potion was enough to bring down the mountain that was Michael Silbert.
*Now that my body can no longer accept the mana in a potion, no excuse will do me any good.*
But one question remained.
How had Jin Taekyung learned the secret? And what had made him willing to use a double-edged sword fraught with danger and uncertainty against Michael?
So instead of making excuses, Michael Silbert asked.
“I’ll ask you one thing. How did you find out?”
The question was brief, but the shock it sent through the room was immense.
“What... what did you just say?”
“G-Guild Master...”
His words were as good as an admission. The people most shaken were those who had supported Michael Silbert most fervently.
He didn’t so much as glance at his allies, frozen like statues. Just as Jin Taekyung had revealed the truth amid their accusations, Michael repeated himself.
“I asked how you found out.”
The answer was shorter than the question.
“Siegfried Bassmann.”
“Siegfried?”
“Yeah. Turns out the man investigated all sorts of things before he died.”
*Whoosh!*
A sheet of paper shot through the air like an arrow. Michael Silbert caught it between two fingers and murmured the title written at the top.
“...The Compatibility of Mana and Magical Power.”
“They say he was the greatest monster scholar of his age, even before you count his being a Grand Mage. Looks like he researched just about everything.”
“There shouldn’t have been any research material left.”
“Sure. That’s what people knew.”
Michael Silbert looked down at the paper in his hand. His gray eyes darted across it; he read and understood the entire page in an instant.
“Studying whether a human body could take in a monster’s magical power and coexist with it. Sounds like the sort of insane idea only an eccentric like Siegfried Bassmann would pursue. Of course...”
Jin Taekyung’s low voice reached his ears.
“That wouldn’t have been true for you.”
Michael Silbert raised his head. The paper, now badly crumpled in his grip, caught fire.
*Fwoosh. Crumble.*
Ash drifted through the air. Beyond it, the eyes that had gone cold now held a reddish glow.
“Looks like Siegfried Bassmann wondered about it too. But even he never managed to prove it. Or maybe he stopped because he thought he’d crossed a taboo.”
Jin Taekyung watched the ash drift toward him and continued.
“Maybe he decided material like this shouldn’t be left behind. Or maybe whoever killed him wanted it gone. Either way, almost nothing remained of that research. It took me a while to find this.”
“You think that’s why I killed him?”
“At first.”
“At first?”
“Yeah. But you killed Siegfried Bassmann for another reason.”
“I won’t deny it. But I’d like to know why you think so.”
“Simple. You’re not careless enough to leave research material like this behind.”
Michael Silbert stared at Jin Taekyung for a moment, then laughed aloud.
“I appreciate that. I’d have been disappointed if even you took me for an idiot.”
“Don’t thank me. I took you for a fucking bastard instead.”
“But you still haven’t given me a clear answer. This material alone couldn’t have been enough to make you suspect me.”
“No, it was enough.”
“Why?”
“When a crime happens, it’s only natural to suspect the ex-convict who lives nearby first.”
“I was looking over what little research remained when the thought struck me.”
Jin Taekyung turned his head with a contemptuous sneer.
Now that the truth behind the Grand Mage’s death—long a mystery—had come to light, the stunned crowd stood frozen, watching the two men.
“What if Michael Silbert, that fucking bastard, was already as good as half human and half demon? What if he’d made that absurd research a reality?”
In the utter silence, Jin Taekyung recalled the moment the thought had first come to him.
Before hundreds of watching eyes and listening ears, on a stage someone else had planned meticulously from beginning to end, he spoke as though he stood alone in the spotlight.
“And then... every piece finally fell into place.”
That possibility, one no one else had considered, was the last piece of the complicated puzzle.
It explained how Michael Silbert had recognized the Skeleton King for what he was.
How a man who’d been just one hero among hundreds during the Great Cataclysm had risen from the dragon’s tail to its head.
Why the Odin Guild’s growth had begun when Cheon Taemin disappeared, and why Michael hadn’t shown his face even at Lee Jungryong’s funeral, where prominent figures from around the world had gathered.
All of it came down to one thing.
“Magical power.”
Jin Taekyung slowly turned around. Looking into the gray eyes that no longer wavered, he continued.
“I don’t know how it happened or what gave you the chance, but... you were able to grow stronger by absorbing magical power. Just like a monster.”
Yet Michael also held mana within himself. He had perfectly controlled and concealed the balance between the two energies, so no one had discovered what he was.
Not even the Skeleton King.
Whenever they spoke of Michael Silbert, the Skeleton King habitually called him an “unpleasant human.” Even he, a monster, couldn’t quite say what he meant by it.
If there was one person in the world Michael Silbert feared above all others, one person from whom he had to hide his true nature, it was—
“Cheon Taemin. He would’ve seen right through you.”
As Jin Taekyung’s low voice reached everyone in the room, a pair of dry lips parted, breaking the long silence.
“Yes. Because of him, I had to keep my head down for many years. Almost as many as you’ve been alive.”
More than thirty years had passed, but Michael Silbert still remembered it vividly.
He had only recently gained his new power. Amid a great gathering of people, that supreme being’s gaze had fixed precisely on him. Fear had gripped his entire body.
Back then, he’d possessed such a tiny amount of magical power that the man hadn’t looked his way again. But the fear of that day had never truly faded.
Even after time had passed and Cheon Taemin had vanished. Even after Michael had learned the secrets of Zone A from Siegfried Bassmann.
He hadn’t even attended Lee Jungryong’s funeral.
The information he had might have been wrong. Cheon Taemin—the only person who could see through him—might have been there.
But...
“There’s one thing you’ve got wrong.”
Speaking quietly, Michael Silbert awakened the enormous energy dormant deep within him.
That unprecedented, turbulent power in which light and darkness had mingled for years—but which, from a certain day onward, had been stained a deeper and deeper shade by the swelling darkness.
“The only person in this world I fear isn’t here right now.”
*Rumble, rumble, rumble.*
A vast wave of force rose and pressed down on everything around them.

Beyond the walls that had hemmed me in on every side, someone waited at the exit.
A gray monster who’d lingered somewhere between light and darkness, then crossed a river from which there was no return.
The last edge of the veil hiding what he really was.
I let out the breath I’d been holding.
“You’re fucked now.”
Michael Silbert found himself wondering when things had started going wrong.
How?
Where?
But no matter how hard he thought, he couldn’t find an answer.
Everything that had led to this moment came down to one person.
Even if Michael found an answer, the man before him would surely create another variable.
*Jin Taekyung.*
Another name for endless variables.
An Eastern young man far too young, reckless, and frivolous to stand in his way.
Yet Michael Silbert could no longer deny it.
That young man wasn’t merely an obstacle to be removed.
He was another wall Michael should have broken down at all costs.
*Such heat.*
The heat in those black eyes.
At the same time, the wound on the back of Michael’s neck—still there like a brand—burned with pain.
*Tap.*
Without realizing it, Michael Silbert reached for his neck.
But when his fingertips met the cold armor that covered it all the way up to his throat, hiding the wound, a dry laugh escaped him.
Excuses?
Damage control?
Meaningless now.
They would only make him look pathetic.
As a single drop of water could split a rock, one palm-sized bottle of potion was enough to bring down the mountain that was Michael Silbert.
*Now that my body can no longer accept the mana in a potion, no excuse will do me any good.*
But one question remained.
How had Jin Taekyung learned the secret?
And what had made him willing to use a double-edged sword fraught with danger and uncertainty against Michael?
So instead of making excuses, Michael Silbert asked.
“I’ll ask you one thing.
How did you find out?”
The question was brief, but the shock it sent through the room was immense.
“What... what did you just say?”
“G-Guild Master...”
His words were as good as an admission.
The people most shaken were those who had supported Michael Silbert most fervently.
He didn’t so much as glance at his allies, frozen like statues.
Just as Jin Taekyung had revealed the truth amid their accusations, Michael repeated himself.
“I asked how you found out.”
The answer was shorter than the question.
“Siegfried Bassmann.”
“Siegfried?”
“Yeah.
Turns out the man investigated all sorts of things before he died.”
*Whoosh!*
A sheet of paper shot through the air like an arrow.
Michael Silbert caught it between two fingers and murmured the title written at the top.
“...The Compatibility of Mana and Magical Power.”
“They say he was the greatest monster scholar of his age, even before you count his being a Grand Mage.
Looks like he researched just about everything.”
“There shouldn’t have been any research material left.”
“Sure.
That’s what people knew.”
Michael Silbert looked down at the paper in his hand.
His gray eyes darted across it; he read and understood the entire page in an instant.
“Studying whether a human body could take in a monster’s magical power and coexist with it.
Sounds like the sort of insane idea only an eccentric like Siegfried Bassmann would pursue.
Of course...”
Jin Taekyung’s low voice reached his ears.
“That wouldn’t have been true for you.”
Michael Silbert raised his head.
The paper, now badly crumpled in his grip, caught fire.
*Fwoosh.
Crumble.*
Ash drifted through the air.
Beyond it, the eyes that had gone cold now held a reddish glow.
“Looks like Siegfried Bassmann wondered about it too.
But even he never managed to prove it.
Or maybe he stopped because he thought he’d crossed a taboo.”
Jin Taekyung watched the ash drift toward him and continued.
“Maybe he decided material like this shouldn’t be left behind.
Or maybe whoever killed him wanted it gone.
Either way, almost nothing remained of that research.
It took me a while to find this.”
“You think that’s why I killed him?”
“At first.”
“At first?”
“Yeah.
But you killed Siegfried Bassmann for another reason.”
“I won’t deny it.
But I’d like to know why you think so.”
“Simple.
You’re not careless enough to leave research material like this behind.”
Michael Silbert stared at Jin Taekyung for a moment, then laughed aloud.
“I appreciate that.
I’d have been disappointed if even you took me for an idiot.”
“Don’t thank me.
I took you for a fucking bastard instead.”
“But you still haven’t given me a clear answer.
This material alone couldn’t have been enough to make you suspect me.”
“No, it was enough.”
“Why?”
“When a crime happens, it’s only natural to suspect the ex-convict who lives nearby first.”
“I was looking over what little research remained when the thought struck me.”
Jin Taekyung turned his head with a contemptuous sneer.
Now that the truth behind the Grand Mage’s death—long a mystery—had come to light, the stunned crowd stood frozen, watching the two men.
“What if Michael Silbert, that fucking bastard, was already as good as half human and half demon?
What if he’d made that absurd research a reality?”
In the utter silence, Jin Taekyung recalled the moment the thought had first come to him.
Before hundreds of watching eyes and listening ears, on a stage someone else had planned meticulously from beginning to end, he spoke as though he stood alone in the spotlight.
“And then... every piece finally fell into place.”
That possibility, one no one else had considered, was the last piece of the complicated puzzle.
It explained how Michael Silbert had recognized the Skeleton King for what he was.
How a man who’d been just one hero among hundreds during the Great Cataclysm had risen from the dragon’s tail to its head.
Why the Odin Guild’s growth had begun when Cheon Taemin disappeared, and why Michael hadn’t shown his face even at Lee Jungryong’s funeral, where prominent figures from around the world had gathered.
All of it came down to one thing.
“Magical power.”
Jin Taekyung slowly turned around.
Looking into the gray eyes that no longer wavered, he continued.
“I don’t know how it happened or what gave you the chance, but... you were able to grow stronger by absorbing magical power.
Just like a monster.”
Yet Michael also held mana within himself.
He had perfectly controlled and concealed the balance between the two energies, so no one had discovered what he was.
Not even the Skeleton King.
Whenever they spoke of Michael Silbert, the Skeleton King habitually called him an “unpleasant human.” Even he, a monster, couldn’t quite say what he meant by it.
If there was one person in the world Michael Silbert feared above all others, one person from whom he had to hide his true nature, it was—
“Cheon Taemin.
He would’ve seen right through you.”
As Jin Taekyung’s low voice reached everyone in the room, a pair of dry lips parted, breaking the long silence.
“Yes.
Because of him, I had to keep my head down for many years.
Almost as many as you’ve been alive.”
More than thirty years had passed, but Michael Silbert still remembered it vividly.
He had only recently gained his new power.
Amid a great gathering of people, that supreme being’s gaze had fixed precisely on him.
Fear had gripped his entire body.
Back then, he’d possessed such a tiny amount of magical power that the man hadn’t looked his way again.
But the fear of that day had never truly faded.
Even after time had passed and Cheon Taemin had vanished.
Even after Michael had learned the secrets of Zone A from Siegfried Bassmann.
He hadn’t even attended Lee Jungryong’s funeral.
The information he had might have been wrong.
Cheon Taemin—the only person who could see through him—might have been there.
But...
“There’s one thing you’ve got wrong.”
Speaking quietly, Michael Silbert awakened the enormous energy dormant deep within him.
That unprecedented, turbulent power in which light and darkness had mingled for years—but which, from a certain day onward, had been stained a deeper and deeper shade by the swelling darkness.
“The only person in this world I fear isn’t here right now.”
*Rumble, rumble, rumble.*
A vast wave of force rose and pressed down on everything around them.

chapters.title: Chapter 781
paragraphs: *Rumble, rumble, rumble!*
A roar shook everything around us.
At the same time, murky energy—light and darkness mixed together—poured out, engulfed the room, and hung over everyone’s heads.
Dark.
It was far too early for the sun to have set, yet the National Assembly building had already turned the first page of night.
A night without a bright moon or stars scattered across the sky.
And yet, in a haze fainter than moonlight, someone radiated a presence clearer than anything else.
*Step. Step.*
The air shifted with each slow step he took.
No, the air wasn’t the only thing that had changed.
His gray eyes were slowly turning black, like ink spreading through water.

The characteristically pale skin of a white man was covered in a thin membrane like leather, and his entire body—now longer and thicker—seemed to radiate strength and elasticity unlike anything he’d shown before.
As if...
*He wasn’t human.*
And yet, he wasn’t a monster, either.
The immense energy pouring from his body clearly held mana within it.
So what should I call that bastard—Michael Silbert?
His slow footsteps finally stopped.
My face, twisted with contempt, was reflected in his eyes, where darkness rippled.
“You monstrous bastard.”
I probably wasn’t the only one thinking that.
Shock spread across hundreds of faces.
The best fighters from countries all around the world had gathered here, but no one dared to speak or move.
Every one of them had reached a high realm. They could feel just how vast—and terrifyingly powerful—the aura Michael Silbert was giving off.
And with it, they understood the true meaning of what he’d said earlier.
*The only person I fear isn’t here right now.*
Even I had to admit it, at least to myself.
Michael Silbert hadn’t been arrogant after all.
No matter how vile and impure the source of his power was, its sheer scale was beyond anything I’d faced before.
*If I had to name one person who came close, it would be the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.*
But for all their similarities, there was a clear difference between them.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress was constantly supplied with magical power flowing from the rift.
Michael Silbert, on the other hand, had found a way to make magical power coexist with mana—and had made it entirely his own.
*Just how much magical power has he absorbed?*
I fixed my eyes on Michael Silbert, my gaze sinking deep.
Something that was no longer human, but wasn’t a monster, either.
A monster that had spent decades building up its power while evading the notice of an absolute being stood before me.
Now he was revealing every last bit of the strength he’d kept hidden.
With a predator’s smile, he looked at me and everyone else before opening his tightly closed lips.
“I told you. As long as he’s not here, no one can stop me now.”
The air had gone cold. Eyes wavered around the room.
But not everyone here was overwhelmed by Michael Silbert’s aura.
“You’ve gotten a lot better at joking since I last saw you, Michael.”
*Whoooosh.*
A gust of wind suddenly swept through the room.
No—it wasn’t wind. It was so much mana that it felt like wind.
Dense smoke rose behind Magic Johnson, who had slung his staff over his shoulder like a steel pipe.
*Crackle.*
The last stub of his cigar was crushed beneath a military boot. Revived by a fresh dose of nicotine, Chuck Hagel spat out a glob of phlegm.
Flames streamed from his eyes as he glared at Michael Silbert.
“Say that again. Go on, you damned neo-Nazi bastard.”
And he wasn’t the only one.
Faye Chen had already drawn her bow, and Prince Felix unsheathed an ornate longsword set with brilliant jewels, his bearing full of dignity.
Team Leader Choi, however, did something different.
*Shing.*
At last, the [Hero’s Sword] slid free of its scabbard. He handed it to someone else.
“Please take it. It suits you better than it does me.”
The recipient blinked at this unexpected gesture of goodwill, then nodded in thanks.
He silently looked at the sword in his hands before suddenly speaking.
“It’s a little late to say this, but...”
The Skeleton King.
The King of the Dead stared at Michael Silbert and continued.
“From the moment I first saw you, I’ve never liked you.”
*Kiiing.*
A golden line crossed the Skeleton King’s pure-white forehead, tracing out a crown.
At the same time, a chilling aura at odds with that brilliant light flowed through his body. But this time, no one raised a weapon against him.
Now that the truth was out, it was clear who their enemy was.
*Shhhhh.*
Weapons and dazzling radiance cut through the murky darkness, all aimed at Michael Silbert.
But the smile on his face remained.
No—it grew broader and more vivid as he spoke.
“Oh, Fabian. You too?”
The Guild Master of Kronos, unexpectedly called by name, clenched his jaw.
His eyelids trembled, and the blade in his hand wavered.
Michael Silbert laughed heartily at his obvious agitation, then turned to the others.
“Christopher, Fernando, Joanne, Marcel, Khalid...”
The names of powerful figures spilled from his lips, one after another.
The spark Michael Silbert had struck spread from the Guild Master of Kronos to people throughout the room.
Every one of them was either the head of a major Guild or an S-rank Hunter, yet they froze like statues just from hearing their names.
Race, nationality, gender, age—they differed in every way but one.
Until just a moment ago, they’d all been Michael Silbert’s supporters.
And the ties they’d built over so many years were more tangled and weighty than anyone could imagine.
“Even the shortest of our relationships goes back more than ten years. You all feel like old friends to me. Don’t I to you?”
No one answered. Michael Silbert smiled at those frozen in place.
“If this is what you’ve chosen, I won’t stop you... but think it over once more. Think about the trust and friendship we’ve shared all these years.”
I could feel unease and confusion spreading through the room.
This wasn’t simply an appeal to their affection.
Michael Silbert was pressuring the people who’d turned their backs on him.
Behind the words *trust* and *friendship* lurked the ugly secrets only those involved knew. He was using them as leverage.
The spark he’d tossed among them blazed up, feeding on the fear and anxiety hidden deep in their hearts.
Then he said something that made them forget even the little conscience they had left.
“If the whole truth came out, do you think you’d be safe?”
“But you needn’t worry. History is the spoils of the victor, after all.”
Michael Silbert slowly turned his head to look at me and added,
“And not just history. The whole world.”
That was the finishing blow.
And just as Fabian, the Guild Master of Kronos, led the Hunters who made up nearly half the people present in lowering their weapons—
A voice slipped from my lips, cold and unfamiliar, as if it belonged to someone else.
“Yeah. I should thank you, actually. For showing yourselves like this, at least.”
“What?”
The confusion that crossed Michael Silbert’s face didn’t last long.
No—almost at once, someone’s scream swallowed his voice.
“Argh!”
“Urgh!”
*Slash! Splatter!*
Fountains of blood shot up amid overlapping screams.
The ambush began on all sides the instant the weapons came down. The Guild Master of Kronos realized what was happening a moment too late and shouted,
“You fucking—!”
“I regret it too, Fabian. I’d hoped it wouldn’t come to this.”
Magic Johnson had already risen into the air. He answered coolly as he gripped his staff.
*Vmmmm.*
The air trembled.
Fire and ice filled the sky on a massive surge of mana, then plunged toward the ground like streaks of light.
Toward the traitors who had once been his comrades-in-arms.
*Whoosh! Thud-thud-thud!*
“St—urgh!”
Three or four A-rank Hunters, relatively weaker than the others, dropped to their knees with dying groans.
Meanwhile, the Guild Master of Kronos, who had been about to hurl his weapon at Magic Johnson in midair, found someone else standing in his way.
“You’ve gone completely off the rails since I last saw you. Why’d you make such a stupid choice, Fabian, you dumb son of a bitch?”
Grimy military boots. The acrid smell of cigar smoke clinging to his whole body.
The Guild Master of Kronos clenched his jaw as he faced the white man, well past middle age and nearing old age.
“Chuck Hagel.”
He was no easy opponent.
No—he was dangerous.
Fabian looked back, hoping for help from his allies, but that hope was in vain.
Just a few steps away, the S-rank Hunters who’d turned to Michael Silbert’s side with him were struggling against other enemies.
Faye Chen, Prince Felix, the Skeleton King—who was already raising the dead Hunters and sending them charging—and Choi Minwoo.
There wasn’t a hint of hesitation in their swift movements.
“You bastards... You planned this from the start?”
“Once you start, you have to pull it up by the roots.”
With a ferocious laugh, Chuck Hagel charged at the Guild Master of Kronos.
*Bang!*
The air burst with their collision.
But the next moment, more crashes and screams surged in from every direction like waves, drowning it out. Red blood sprayed into the air.
Right. The enemies’ blood was red.
Human blood, not monster blood.
The red blood I’d never wanted to see in the world where I was born and raised soaked the National Assembly building and the enormous round table.
Maybe that was why my mouth tasted so bitter and my blood was boiling, even though I’d expected this.
*Fwoosh.*
The fire dragon coiled in my dantian surged up.
I felt heat like molten lava seep through every part of my body, and suddenly I spoke.
“Fucking awful sight, isn’t it?”
Michael Silbert had ignored everything happening around him and watched me in silence. Instead of answering, he asked,
“Is everything happening here your doing?”
“What if it is?”
“Then I applaud your bold decision.”
*Bold decision.*
The words pierced something in my chest like an awl.
But I kept it off my face and answered calmly.
“Then don’t just flap your gums. Clap your hands, you dumbass.”
“Sorry, but I can’t do that.”
“Why not?”
“Because if I give you even the slightest opening, I have a feeling something will happen. Of course...”
Michael Silbert’s smile faded as he continued.
“That won’t happen.”
“Maybe. You sure about that?”
And just as silence fell for a moment—
*Whoosh.*
All the space between us vanished, and two immense forces shot toward each other.
*Kwaaaang!*

chapters.title: Chapter 782
paragraphs: *Kwaaaang!*
The deafening crash left my ears numb.
But before the ringing came, an enormous shock wave traveled through our hands, which had touched for only an instant.
*Boom!*
It felt as if a giant’s palm had struck my entire body.
The irresistible force sent me flying backward. I twisted in midair, and a blade of gray energy came rushing toward my face.
*Shhk!*
A hair’s breadth. That was all.
I snapped my head aside, and the gray energy skimmed past the tip of my nose, cleaving the ground like soft tofu. I landed lightly on the spot it had cut through.
Then I watched a man walk toward me, his entire body wrapped in gray energy.
No—something that had crossed beyond the bounds of humanity.
“Michael Silbert.”
He smiled at the sound of my voice. The shadow in his deep-set dimple seemed especially dark. That wasn’t just my imagination.
*Crack. Crack.*
The ground crumbled beneath each step he took.
The energy pouring from Michael Silbert was so overwhelming that even those fighting nearby choked on their breath and retreated as far as they could.
But not me.
I couldn’t back down. I had no intention of doing so.
Just as I’d decided before coming here, I would fight.
To stop that monster strolling toward me. To keep him from hurling billions of people into the flames all over again.
I stepped forward, putting my weight into it.
*Whoosh.*
One step.
Wind brushed past my body, and space folded. At the same time, two keywords formed in my mind and became commands.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
The spear I’d hidden where no one could see it settled into my grip.
The world had slowed. Blue-white flames surged along the spearhead, painting the gray eyes where darkness rippled as I brought it down.
Michael Silbert.
Straight for the crown of that monster’s head.
*Fwoosh!*
The concentrated heat evaporated every trace of moisture within several meters.
Through air hot enough to catch fire at a touch, I saw his eyes widen.
The corners of his mouth were still turned up, even in the face of a strike no one here could have expected.
Then—
A sword flashed upward like a streak of light and struck the spearhead of White Flame as it fell toward his crown.
*Kwaang!*
A deafening crash rang out, as if the sky itself had split open.
*Grrrrk.*
The spearhead and sword blade locked together in midair, neither giving an inch. Beyond them came a low laugh.
“So that’s it. I’d been wondering why I never saw that spear.”
“Are you done with the surprise magic trick you prepared?”
*Grit.*
The sword, wrapped in a murky aura, slowly pushed back the flame-wreathed spearhead.
Strength no human should have possessed and a boundless, unprecedented power burst forth all at once.
*Kwaaaah!*
The moment I faced that immense force head-on, I knew for certain:

Even my physical abilities, pushed far beyond their limits thanks to the System, and my three jiazi of internal energy—a level no one in Murim could afford to underestimate—weren’t enough to fully suppress his power.
*If the fallout reaches the people around us...*
I didn’t need to think hard about what would happen.
At least dozens would die. Half of them would be heroes who should never die in a place like this.
I had only one option left.
*Neutralize it.*
With that word flashing through my mind, I let go of White Flame, flung upward by the force of the clash, and thrust out both hands without hesitation.
*Flicker. Boom!*
The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist with my right hand. The Flame Divine Palm with my left.
One fist and one palm.
Two branches from the same root—the Fire Gate Clan. From their tips, two streams of flame surged into the murky aura.
*Grrrrk!*
The tremendous recoil sent throbbing pain through my body. The ground turned over beneath my sliding feet, exposing its ugly innards in long furrows.
But I focused only on the energy in front of me, pouring the flames from both hands into the murky aura.
Not swallowing it—gnawing it away.
Not stopping it—throwing it out of balance.
At last, the mass of destructive energy visibly shrank. I twisted it with all my strength and hurled it behind me.
*Whoooosh—Kwaang!*
A tearing crash and tremor shook the National Assembly building.
The Skeleton King drove his Bone Sword into the chest of a traitor who had staggered off balance, then shouted, “Watch out!”
It was good advice, but half a beat too late.
Michael Silbert was already right in front of me.
*Shwack!*
An aura filled with murky light grazed the back of my neck.
I dodged the lightning-fast thrust and slipped inside his reach, driving a fist at him without hesitation.
*Boom!*
Michael Silbert blocked my Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist with a hand wrapped in layer upon layer of aura, then brought his knee up.
No—just as he was about to, he shoved me away and retreated.
*Whoosh! Thwack!*
A silver streak plunged from the air, piercing the exact spot where he’d stood a moment ago.
He watched me silently pull White Flame free, then smiled.
“Sure. If it were too easy, it wouldn’t be any fun.”
Fun. That was what he called it.
I looked around at the screams and the blood spraying everywhere. A disbelieving laugh escaped me.
“You crazy bastard. No matter how I look at it, you’re never going to be human again.”
“Even if I’m not human, what of it?”
“What?”

“I’ve experienced imbalances like this several times before. The stronger my magical power grew, the further it fell out of balance with my mana. There were even times I couldn’t control the magical power I absorbed from Magic Gems. But do you know what I thought every time it happened?”
Michael Silbert didn’t wait for an answer.
Hundreds of Hunters were fighting a horrific civil war in the same space, but he looked utterly at ease as he watched.
“Demon King.”
“If someone kept getting in my way. If they prevented me from reaching the pinnacle as a human... I thought becoming the new Demon King after Asmodeus wouldn’t be so bad.”
I stared at Michael Silbert, at a loss for words. Then I realized I needed to correct what I’d said earlier.
“...Now that I look at you again, you’re not just a crazy bastard. You’re completely out of your fucking mind.”
“Call me whatever you like for now. By the time the sun sets, everything will be decided. Whether you and those friends of yours live or die, and the name the world will know as my true one.”
The whole world already knew the name Michael Silbert.
But that wasn’t what he meant by his “true name.”
Depending on how this fight turned out, he could become the Alliance Leader of the World Hunter Federation—or the new Demon King.
Of course, as far as I was concerned, that was all in Michael Silbert’s head.
“Idiot. What’s a leech like you going to do?”
“A leech?”
“Yeah, you leeching bastard.”
His face slowly stiffened. I let out a scornful laugh.

“An imugi from a clear pond ascends to heaven. Ever seen a grub wriggling in a sewer turn into a dragon? No matter how strong you get, your nature stays the same. At best, you’re a mosquito or a leech.”
“A mosquito drunk on power, with a straw stuck in a Magic Gem. A useless leech that does nothing but suck people’s blood. That’s what you are, you pathetic bastard.”
*Pathetic bastard.*
Those words were for me, too.
There’d been a time when I’d seriously considered giving up on everything and backing away.
If the end of his pathetic ambition was simply taking control of the World Hunter Federation, if his only goal was to stand at the top... I’d thought maybe no more disasters would happen.
It hurt.
I had the power and abilities everyone wished for, yet I couldn’t save the cities collapsing into ruins or the countless people dying inside them.
It felt as though these terrible disasters were happening because I’d stood against Michael Silbert.
That was why, for a little while, I couldn’t help but wonder.
*No. I was afraid.*
Fine. I’d admit it.
I was afraid to keep running down a path strewn with countless dead.
The closer I chased Michael Silbert, the more blood and bodies I feared I’d trample underfoot.
I thought that if I simply handed him the world, he’d stop The Prophet and every other disaster, if only to protect what had become his.
But... now I understood.
When I finally came out of that long, dark tunnel I’d walked alone in my heart, where no one else could see, there was the light I’d wanted so badly.
No. There was an answer.
All of it had come from my own weakness. My foolish hope was wrong, and Michael Silbert was a monster who wouldn’t stop running even after he crossed the finish line.
That was why I had to kill him, as a human being.
“No matter how I look at it, the answer is to stomp on leeches like you until they burst. Don’t you think?”
“From now on, shut your mouth. You’re wasting oxygen.”
I leveled my spear at Michael Silbert.
His eyes had turned so black there was no trace of their original color. At the same time, an immense, seemingly endless power wrapped around his entire body and began to whirl.
*Kwaaaah.*
Everything the rising strands of power touched broke and split apart.
His voice, once gentle and unhurried, rang out as though it belonged to something from another world.
“Your corpse will be buried here today, along with every truth that will never come to light.”
At his words, I looked up at the cameras installed all around us.
Half had been destroyed, but the rest were still doing their job.
*The truth, huh?*
I had a fair idea why Michael Silbert, who loved attention so much, wasn’t broadcasting the brightest moment of his life to the whole world.
And where was that damned pet crow that always followed him like a shadow? Why was everything outside still so quiet despite all this chaos?
But right now, there was only one thing I could say to him.
“I said shut your mouth, you fucking bastard.”
*Grrrrrrk!*

As I charged toward his energy, surging like waves across a boundless sea, I suddenly wondered why that immense power—enough to make even my three jiazi of internal energy feel hopelessly inadequate—didn’t frighten me.
Why Michael Silbert, who’d absorbed a Magic Gem and gained physical abilities comparable to mine and a seemingly inexhaustible supply of magical power, seemed so small.
And as I thrust out the spearhead, I found the answer.
*Because I’m a Hunter.*
Hunters aren’t afraid of their prey.
*Whoooosh!*
