chapters.title: Chapter 783
paragraphs: *Whoooosh!*
As I charged, the spearhead flashed forward, cleaving through space. Flames surged up, burning the air and erasing the wind as they pierced the thick darkness.
*Boom!*
One precise point pierced the invisible flow.

Some of the magical power sweeping toward me like a wave dispersed helplessly. My vision plunged through the gap in the magical power at the same speed as my thrust—and a familiar face came into view.
No. Familiar and strange at once.
Because the Michael Silbert standing there was no longer Michael Silbert.
“Not bad.”
The moment that chilling voice reached my ears—
*Shhk.*
His figure vanished as if it had been erased.
My target disappeared from sight, but instead of panicking, I twisted around on instinct.
*Whoosh!*
A sword sprang up behind me, skimmed my side, and stabbed through empty air.
If I hadn’t dodged, it would have pierced my heart. I spun and struck with my palm.
*Kwaang!*
His body was supposed to be flesh and bone. Yet when our palms met, the impact sounded like an explosion.
And the shock wave hit even harder.
*Grrrrk!*
The ground tore up beneath my sliding feet. I was driven back several meters while Michael Silbert stood rooted to the spot. One corner of his mouth curled upward.
“Do you understand now how foolish it was to stand against me?”
*Ptoo.*
I spat out the blood pooled in my mouth instead of answering. Before it hit the ground, I stepped forward with all my strength.
*Kwaang!*
The ground shattered beneath my foot.
Wind swept over me as I crossed more than ten meters in an instant. My spear and his sword flashed toward each other.
*Kaaang!*
The sharp clash burst the air around us. His sword had grown so long and massive it hardly looked like a sword anymore, swollen with magical power. It knocked my spearhead far aside.
*Crack.*
Pain shot through my wrist.
This wasn’t just a difference in physical ability. It was a difference in the sheer amount of power we held.
Absorbing the Magic Gem had made Michael Silbert’s body much stronger, and the magical power welling up without end reinforced it further. Of course he was pushing me back.
As long as I insisted on fighting him head-on.
*Grrrrk!*
I turned my spearhead in a smooth arc, and his blade slid along it.
Despite the enormous difference in force, Michael Silbert’s sword slipped out of his control. My hunch confirmed, I drove a fist toward him.
*Fwoosh, whoom!*
Flames burst forth in a flash.

The thick darkness moved like a living creature and hurried to envelop its master, but my Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, thrown with all my strength, burned through the magical power and slammed into his chest.
*Kwaaaang!*
A deafening crash rang out, and his body flew away like a cannonball.
Michael Silbert hastily flung out both arms, pouring magical power toward me to keep me back. Then he coughed up blood.
*Kh-erk.*
I cut down every bolt of magical power flying toward me and watched him stagger. A strange feeling stirred in me.
Not because I’d finally landed a solid hit. Because the blood spilling from his mouth was red.
“So even a monster like you is still human. For now, anyway.”
Michael Silbert clenched his teeth at my mutter. His eyes trembled; he hadn’t expected that blow.
“What did you do?”
I answered readily.
“Four Ounces Deflecting a Thousand Catties.”
“What?”
“You don’t need to understand. There’s a shitload of things in this world you don’t know about anyway.”

“So I don’t bother trying to understand, either. You, or those lunatics fighting over there—who knows what kind of fucked-up shit they got up to while working with you to end up in that fight? None of it makes any sense to me.”
I stared straight at Michael Silbert.
“No. The moment I understood it, I’d become the same kind of idiot.”
A new emotion spread across his face, over the traces of pain.
Anger. Or humiliation.
Watching his face twist felt better than I’d expected.
“I told you earlier. A leech is still a leech. It couldn’t become a dragon even if it died and came back to life.”
“You bastard...”
“Yeah. Putting everything else aside, I’ll give you one thing.”
My breath was as hot as a fire dragon’s. I stepped toward him.
“You’re the strongest leech I’ve ever met.”
With that, I hurled White Flame without hesitation, gripping it in reverse.
*Bang!*
The air burst in layer after layer, as if a sonic boom had gone off.
And at the end of its path stood Michael Silbert.
*Kwaang! Grrrrrung!*
Flame and magical power erupted together.

The stained glass, which had barely held its shape thanks to dozens of layers of defensive magic, couldn’t withstand the shock wave and shattered. I flashed through the rain of countless shards falling overhead and thrust out both palms.
*Boom!*
A gale of flame swept through the room.
Amid the haze left by the explosion, the shadow of someone staggering was etched clearly into my eyes.
*That’s him.*
No doubt about it.
I kicked off the ground and charged, reaching out to grab empty air.
No—two spears appeared as if drawn into existence by the command I shouted in my mind. I caught them and launched them once more.
*Shweeeek!*
Two streaks of light crossed the space between us.
When Michael Silbert twisted aside and dodged the spears, I tore through the darkness surrounding us again and closed in right in front of him.
“Jin Taekyung!”
*Whooom!*
Beyond his furious shout came the heavy whistle of a weapon cutting through the air.
Fed an absurd amount of magical power, the enormous blade came down as if to cleave me in two.
*Shwaaaak! Shhk!*
Space split open, and the sword, having missed its target, cleaved the ground.
Pain stung across my chest. I’d dodged sideways at the last moment, but the pressure behind the sword was stronger—and sharper—than I’d imagined.
His strength and speed made my hair stand on end.
But just as he had a vast store of power I could never possess, I had something he lacked.
Something more important than the amount of internal energy you held when your life was on the line.
Martial arts.
*Thump! Grrrrk!*
As he raised his sword again, I drew up my internal energy and stamped down.
Using the Thousand-Catty Drop, I pressed the blade beneath a crushing weight. Michael Silbert’s eyes widened.
A natural reaction from someone encountering martial arts for the first time. I’d been astonished every day when I first learned proper martial arts from Jeok Cheongang.
But Michael Silbert was neither my teacher nor my disciple. He was a monster I had to kill.
An enemy, plain and simple. I owed him no friendly explanation.
*Fwoosh.*
The Flame Divine Palm, now at the eighth stage, poured out a dreadful heat.
It was too late for him to free the hand gripping his sword. As he thrust out his other hand, I gave a command in my mind.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
*Thwack!*
Instead of a crash, blood burst out. Michael Silbert clenched his teeth at the sight of the dagger that had pierced his magical power and his palm.
His eyes bulged, pain mingling with some realization I couldn’t read.
“This is...!”
Meticulous as he was, Michael Silbert might already have suspected I had an Inventory.
But I was stronger than he thought—and even better at improvising.
Even if he’d guessed, it wouldn’t have changed much.
*The amount of internal energy you have is only one factor in deciding who lives and who dies.*
The powerful opponents who’d fallen at my hands could serve as witnesses, prosecutors, and judges all at once.
Some called me the greatest young prodigy and the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon. Others called me a lucky man who’d suddenly gained tremendous power through reawakening.
They were all wrong.
I’d been an F-rank Hunter, born in muddy water. I’d struggled and grown through countless brushes with death.
I would keep struggling with all my might until every bit of dirt filling this pit around me was gone. Until it finally became a clear pond.
And yet... I couldn’t hand my pond over to some leech. Not a mantis, not a toad—a leech.
Especially one that would fill it with blood instead of muddy water.
*Thrust, thrust-thrust!*
My hand flashed.
Still clutching Michael Silbert’s hand, pierced by the dagger, I summoned another weapon from my Inventory and slashed, stabbed, twisted, and drove it into him wherever I could.
“Graaah!”
Blood sprayed from his wide-open mouth. At the same time, the hand that had belatedly let go of the sword hilt drove into my side like a battering ram.
*Whoom!*
The air whistled with a weight that made my skin crawl.
He had the magical power of two or three S-rank monsters combined and enough raw strength to tear a large monster apart with his bare hands.
The System had given me a body like steel, but I wouldn’t come away unscathed if that blow landed.
At least, if I did nothing.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
*Crack!*
The impact jolted my upper body. I heard bones shift, and a little blood welled into my mouth.
But that was all.
Michael Silbert’s desperate punch had neither split my skin nor broken my bones.
It had only damaged part of the red-tinged armor that had appeared around my upper body.
*Beep.*
**System** Part of the **Fire Dragon Armor** has been destroyed! **Current damage:** 44% At 90% damage or higher, it will be recalled to the Inventory and enter automatic repair mode.
As the alert sounded in my ears, I smiled brightly at Michael Silbert, who had frozen in a daze.
“Mm-hmm. I can just repair it~”
And in that instant—
*Ptoo!*
I spat the blood pooled in my mouth into his face.
As he flailed instinctively, his face drenched in blood, I drove my fist into him.
Like hammering a nail farther into the ground.
*Kwaang! Grrrrk!*

A heavy crash and tremor swept in all directions. The ground around us sank into a vast crater. At its bottom, Michael Silbert lay sprawled, coughing up blood after my Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist struck him squarely in the chest.
“Khk, k-kergh...!”
The blood he coughed up pooled in the crater.
His armor had long since been smashed to pieces. Blood and soot had stained his once-pale skin dark red.
“...You fucking idiot.”
I smiled bitterly. When I reached out, White Flame’s shaft shot into my grasp.
Without hesitation, I raised the spearhead.
*Whoosh!*

*Boom!*
One precise point pierced the invisible flow.
Some of the magical power sweeping toward me like a wave dispersed helplessly.
My vision plunged through the gap in the magical power at the same speed as my thrust—and a familiar face came into view.
No.
Familiar and strange at once.
Because the Michael Silbert standing there was no longer Michael Silbert.
“Not bad.”
The moment that chilling voice reached my ears—
*Shhk.*
His figure vanished as if it had been erased.
My target disappeared from sight, but instead of panicking, I twisted around on instinct.
*Whoosh!*
A sword sprang up behind me, skimmed my side, and stabbed through empty air.
If I hadn’t dodged, it would have pierced my heart.
I spun and struck with my palm.
*Kwaang!*
His body was supposed to be flesh and bone.
Yet when our palms met, the impact sounded like an explosion.
And the shock wave hit even harder.
*Grrrrk!*
The ground tore up beneath my sliding feet.
I was driven back several meters while Michael Silbert stood rooted to the spot.
One corner of his mouth curled upward.
“Do you understand now how foolish it was to stand against me?”
*Ptoo.*
I spat out the blood pooled in my mouth instead of answering.
Before it hit the ground, I stepped forward with all my strength.
*Kwaang!*
The ground shattered beneath my foot.
Wind swept over me as I crossed more than ten meters in an instant.
My spear and his sword flashed toward each other.
*Kaaang!*
The sharp clash burst the air around us.
His sword had grown so long and massive it hardly looked like a sword anymore, swollen with magical power.
It knocked my spearhead far aside.
*Crack.*
Pain shot through my wrist.
This wasn’t just a difference in physical ability.
It was a difference in the sheer amount of power we held.
Absorbing the Magic Gem had made Michael Silbert’s body much stronger, and the magical power welling up without end reinforced it further.
Of course he was pushing me back.
As long as I insisted on fighting him head-on.
*Grrrrk!*
I turned my spearhead in a smooth arc, and his blade slid along it.
Despite the enormous difference in force, Michael Silbert’s sword slipped out of his control.
My hunch confirmed, I drove a fist toward him.
*Fwoosh, whoom!*
Flames burst forth in a flash.

The thick darkness moved like a living creature and hurried to envelop its master, but my Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, thrown with all my strength, burned through the magical power and slammed into his chest.
*Kwaaaang!*
A deafening crash rang out, and his body flew away like a cannonball.
Michael Silbert hastily flung out both arms, pouring magical power toward me to keep me back.
Then he coughed up blood.
*Kh-erk.*
I cut down every bolt of magical power flying toward me and watched him stagger.
A strange feeling stirred in me.
Not because I’d finally landed a solid hit.
Because the blood spilling from his mouth was red.
“So even a monster like you is still human.
For now, anyway.”
Michael Silbert clenched his teeth at my mutter.
His eyes trembled; he hadn’t expected that blow.
“What did you do?”
I answered readily.
“Four Ounces Deflecting a Thousand Catties.”
“What?”
“You don’t need to understand.
There’s a shitload of things in this world you don’t know about anyway.”
“So I don’t bother trying to understand, either.
You, or those lunatics fighting over there—who knows what kind of fucked-up shit they got up to while working with you to end up in that fight?
None of it makes any sense to me.”
I stared straight at Michael Silbert.
“No.
The moment I understood it, I’d become the same kind of idiot.”
A new emotion spread across his face, over the traces of pain.
Anger.
Or humiliation.
Watching his face twist felt better than I’d expected.
“I told you earlier.
A leech is still a leech.
It couldn’t become a dragon even if it died and came back to life.”
“You bastard...”
“Yeah.
Putting everything else aside, I’ll give you one thing.”
My breath was as hot as a fire dragon’s.
I stepped toward him.
“You’re the strongest leech I’ve ever met.”
With that, I hurled White Flame without hesitation, gripping it in reverse.
*Bang!*
The air burst in layer after layer, as if a sonic boom had gone off.
And at the end of its path stood Michael Silbert.
*Kwaang!
Grrrrrung!*
Flame and magical power erupted together.
The stained glass, which had barely held its shape thanks to dozens of layers of defensive magic, couldn’t withstand the shock wave and shattered.
I flashed through the rain of countless shards falling overhead and thrust out both palms.
*Boom!*
A gale of flame swept through the room.
Amid the haze left by the explosion, the shadow of someone staggering was etched clearly into my eyes.
*That’s him.*
No doubt about it.
I kicked off the ground and charged, reaching out to grab empty air.
No—two spears appeared as if drawn into existence by the command I shouted in my mind.
I caught them and launched them once more.
*Shweeeek!*
Two streaks of light crossed the space between us.
When Michael Silbert twisted aside and dodged the spears, I tore through the darkness surrounding us again and closed in right in front of him.
“Jin Taekyung!”
*Whooom!*
Beyond his furious shout came the heavy whistle of a weapon cutting through the air.
Fed an absurd amount of magical power, the enormous blade came down as if to cleave me in two.
*Shwaaaak!
Shhk!*
Space split open, and the sword, having missed its target, cleaved the ground.
Pain stung across my chest.
I’d dodged sideways at the last moment, but the pressure behind the sword was stronger—and sharper—than I’d imagined.
His strength and speed made my hair stand on end.
But just as he had a vast store of power I could never possess, I had something he lacked.
Something more important than the amount of internal energy you held when your life was on the line.
Martial arts.
*Thump!
Grrrrk!*
As he raised his sword again, I drew up my internal energy and stamped down.
Using the Thousand-Catty Drop, I pressed the blade beneath a crushing weight.
Michael Silbert’s eyes widened.
A natural reaction from someone encountering martial arts for the first time.
I’d been astonished every day when I first learned proper martial arts from Jeok Cheongang.
But Michael Silbert was neither my teacher nor my disciple.
He was a monster I had to kill.
An enemy, plain and simple.
I owed him no friendly explanation.
*Fwoosh.*
The Flame Divine Palm, now at the eighth stage, poured out a dreadful heat.
It was too late for him to free the hand gripping his sword.
As he thrust out his other hand, I gave a command in my mind.
*Inventory open.
Summon.*
*Thwack!*
Instead of a crash, blood burst out.
Michael Silbert clenched his teeth at the sight of the dagger that had pierced his magical power and his palm.
His eyes bulged, pain mingling with some realization I couldn’t read.
“This is...!”
Meticulous as he was, Michael Silbert might already have suspected I had an Inventory.
But I was stronger than he thought—and even better at improvising.
Even if he’d guessed, it wouldn’t have changed much.
*The amount of internal energy you have is only one factor in deciding who lives and who dies.*
The powerful opponents who’d fallen at my hands could serve as witnesses, prosecutors, and judges all at once.
Some called me the greatest young prodigy and the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
Others called me a lucky man who’d suddenly gained tremendous power through reawakening.
They were all wrong.
I’d been an F-rank Hunter, born in muddy water.
I’d struggled and grown through countless brushes with death.
I would keep struggling with all my might until every bit of dirt filling this pit around me was gone.
Until it finally became a clear pond.
And yet...
I couldn’t hand my pond over to some leech.
Not a mantis, not a toad—a leech.
Especially one that would fill it with blood instead of muddy water.
*Thrust, thrust-thrust!*
My hand flashed.
Still clutching Michael Silbert’s hand, pierced by the dagger, I summoned another weapon from my Inventory and slashed, stabbed, twisted, and drove it into him wherever I could.
“Graaah!”
Blood sprayed from his wide-open mouth.
At the same time, the hand that had belatedly let go of the sword hilt drove into my side like a battering ram.
*Whoom!*
The air whistled with a weight that made my skin crawl.
He had the magical power of two or three S-rank monsters combined and enough raw strength to tear a large monster apart with his bare hands.
The System had given me a body like steel, but I wouldn’t come away unscathed if that blow landed.
At least, if I did nothing.
*Inventory open.
Summon.*
*Crack!*
The impact jolted my upper body.
I heard bones shift, and a little blood welled into my mouth.
But that was all.
Michael Silbert’s desperate punch had neither split my skin nor broken my bones.
It had only damaged part of the red-tinged armor that had appeared around my upper body.
*Beep.*
**System** Part of the **Fire Dragon Armor** has been destroyed! **Current damage:** 44% At 90% damage or higher, it will be recalled to the Inventory and enter automatic repair mode.
As the alert sounded in my ears, I smiled brightly at Michael Silbert, who had frozen in a daze.
“Mm-hmm.
I can just repair it~”
And in that instant—
*Ptoo!*
I spat the blood pooled in my mouth into his face.
As he flailed instinctively, his face drenched in blood, I drove my fist into him.
Like hammering a nail farther into the ground.
*Kwaang!
Grrrrk!*
A heavy crash and tremor swept in all directions.
The ground around us sank into a vast crater.
At its bottom, Michael Silbert lay sprawled, coughing up blood after my Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist struck him squarely in the chest.
“Khk, k-kergh...!”
The blood he coughed up pooled in the crater.
His armor had long since been smashed to pieces.
Blood and soot had stained his once-pale skin dark red.
“...You fucking idiot.”
I smiled bitterly.
When I reached out, White Flame’s shaft shot into my grasp.
Without hesitation, I raised the spearhead.
*Whoosh!*

chapters.title: Chapter 784
paragraphs: *Shwoosh!*
It was strange.
I’d only raised my spear. So where had that whistle cutting through the air beside my ear come from?
And what the hell gave those idiots the confidence to charge at me?
In that brief instant, split into even smaller fragments, I turned and brought my spearhead down.
*Whooom. Kaang!*
The pressure bursting along the spearhead knocked away a dozen or so daggers. At the same moment, two swords came slashing in from either side, aiming for my upper and lower body at once.
*Shhk, slice!*
It burned like I’d been scalded.
An alert sounded to tell me the durability of my Fire Dragon Armor had dropped, and a considerable stream of blood gushed from my thigh.
Still, that was a decent price for fending off a surprise attack by three S-rank Hunters.
Even more so if I’d given as good as I got, instead of being the only one to take a hit.
*Pshaaa!*
Blood sprayed belatedly, soaking the ground. A middle-aged man and woman stared wide-eyed as they saw their comrade collapse, his chest split wide open.
“When did you—!”
“No, Fernando!”
It had all happened so quickly that I hadn’t had time to see who they were. But now that I was facing them, I recognized them all too well.
S-rank Hunters who represented their respective countries and stood as symbols of humanity.
Or rather, who *had*.
“Well, look who it is. I know all of you.”
At my greeting, tinged with a hollow laugh, the middle-aged pair swallowed hard.
Fernando Lucas, Brazil’s S-rank Hunter, had made the reckless choice to aim for my chest. Even as he spilled an enormous amount of blood, he was fumbling for a potion with trembling hands.
He looked so desperate that I spoke to him in the warm voice of a romantic lead.
“Drink that, and I’ll kill you.”
“But hold on until this is over and I’ll get you treated. I’ll even find you a nice prison. All right? Promise.”
Fernando Lucas stared at me as though he’d forgotten the pain.
Then he shoved the potion into his mouth with lightning speed.
Bottle and all, without even removing the cap.
*Crunch! Thud!*
Shattered glass and potion poured into his open mouth.
But even a Top-Grade Potion, capable of restoring torn organs in the blink of an eye, couldn’t bring back someone who was already dead.
“I told you not to drink it.”
I murmured to Fernando Lucas’s corpse, a hole through his forehead where my Finger Qi had struck.
The two middle-aged Hunters who’d survived him—slightly luckier and far more skilled—spoke with rigid faces.
“Did it really have to come to this?”
“It’s not too late, Jin. If you stop, we’ll withdraw. There’s no need for any more sacrifices, is there?”
Stop? No need for more sacrifices?
For a moment, I had no words. I looked around the National Assembly, where the floor was still being stained with blood, then at Michael Silbert, sprawled there and twitching like an insect.
Finally, I looked at the two people standing in front of him and thrust out my spear.
One of the few lessons I’d learned was that I didn’t have to answer every stupid thing people said.
*Shhk!*
They might not know martial arts, but they were S-rank Hunters with plenty of combat behind them.
They gasped and barely dodged the attack, landing in front of and behind me. The spearhead had come without warning, and their eyes had turned grave.
“So that’s your answer?”
“Wait. Don’t provoke him for no reason. Right now, we need to save Michael first—”
The woman had a much better grasp of the situation than the man, but she made me want to laugh just as much.
*What the hell had they been doing all this time? How much had they done for things to come to this?*
There’d been a time when I hadn’t known anything, either.

Back when I’d gone mechanically from Gates to my goshiwon and back. I’d fought monsters for money, not out of some sense of duty as a Hunter, yet I’d still felt vaguely offended whenever I heard someone say Hunters had become corrupt.
But... now I knew too much.
There was no going back.
I didn’t care what they’d accomplished or how valuable they might be in the war to come.
If we didn’t cut out the tumors rooted deep in society, humanity would collapse before it could fight the monsters.
Another Lee Jungryong. Another Go Jun. Another Michael Silbert. They were right in front of me.
The moment they’d turned their weapons against us despite the ugly truth being exposed, they’d become tumors that had to be cut out.
“I already gave you a chance. The choice... was yours.”
I charged without hesitation at the people I’d once admired and respected.
*Shweeeek!*
It was ironic. Pain tormented people, yet as death drew near, they could no longer feel it.
And... that numbness was more frightening than any terrible pain.
*Ah.*
Michael Silbert blinked blankly.

His lips were slightly parted, but he couldn’t even groan. The strength was draining from his arms and legs, from which powerful energy had surged without pause. The blood that had soaked his body and was now sloshing around him felt dull and distant.
*Damn it.*
If this was how he fell, what had he lived for?
*Grrk. Cough.*
Instead of a hollow laugh, a bloody bubble welled in his mouth. His head tipped to the side as if he were collapsing, and he saw the corpse of a man frozen with his eyes wide open.
A familiar face.
Fernando Lucas.
Fernando had been a gang member since childhood, a delinquent who’d won fervent support among South America’s poor. Over the past ten years, Michael Silbert had done him various “favors.”
The public and the courts would, of course, call those favors something else.
*It started small.*
But time dulled everything, and each repetition made it snowball.

He’d eliminated a powerful rival and disguised the killing as an accident. He’d used a politician with the right connections to bury tax-evasion charges. He’d even kidnapped a brave journalist and his family when the man was preparing an article about how the hero of Brazil’s poor secretly ran a gang and made a fortune on the side.
The others spilling blood and dying for him throughout the chamber were no different.
*No. They aren’t doing this for me.*
Michael Silbert knew why they fought.
They fought for themselves. They knew there was too much to lose if they admitted and accepted everything now.
In the end, he and they were nothing but filth seething in the same pit.
But thanks to that—thanks to how long he’d indulged their greed and ambition—Michael Silbert had bought himself a little time.
Precious time to cast off the human bonds he’d clung to until the end and become the Demon King.
*Slosh. Splash.*
The blood that had filled the crater rippled like a wave. Through his blurred vision, he saw a spearhead flash through the air and graze the neck of a middle-aged man.
*Slice!*
A body fell with a wet thud. A head rolled toward him, its eyes meeting his.
The scent of blood rising from the blackened cut, as though it had been seared, smelled as sweet as chocolate. He doubted he was imagining it.
*Heh-heh.*
Michael Silbert laughed softly. Now that he could make a sound again, his five senses gradually sharpened.
His quickening heartbeat thundered in his ears.
*Thump. Thump-thump. Thump-thump-thump!*
As his heart beat faster, the blood pooled in the crater surged toward its owner.
But it was no longer red.
Thick, gleaming green blood that no one could mistake for a human’s.
The same blood spilled by the unprecedented monster he’d encountered in Paris more than thirty years ago, when the city had overflowed with blood and corpses, filled Michael Silbert’s entire body.
Its endless magical power and Regeneration came with it.
*Shhhh!*
The blood was sucked deep into his body. Severed muscles rejoined. Broken bones and ruined organs mended.
A short scream rang out, as though to celebrate his return from the brink of death.
“Kh-erk!”
It was a victory cry announcing the resurrection of one life—and a death rattle announcing the end of another.
A middle-aged woman staggered backward with a hole through her chest.

A hero of the Great Cataclysm with an impressive record—and filth from the pit Michael Silbert had chosen—even at the brink of death, she drove a dagger into a gap in Jin Taekyung’s damaged armor. Her back arched like a bow.
*Crunch. Pshaaa!*
The spearhead came free, and blood spurted.
*Thump.*
In front of the corpse that had crumpled like a rotten log stood a young man, tall as an iron tower. Michael Silbert saw him.
—Jin Taekyung.
Michael Silbert looked at Jin Taekyung. No—Jin Taekyung looked at Michael Silbert.
At his eyes, swallowed by utter darkness, with none of their former gray or even their whites remaining.
And... at the monster spreading enormous wings made of magical power.
*Whooosh!*
The National Assembly, with a radius of hundreds of meters, fell silent. So did the fierce battle within it, just as it had been nearing its end.
Everyone was stunned into silence at the sight of Michael Silbert, who had lost all semblance of human form.
Scales covered his body. Two horns jutted from his forehead. At the sight of his vast, dark wings, the name of a monster flashed through their minds.
Someone voiced it in a near-groan.
“...Dragon.”
The origin and very embodiment of the dragonkin, born with nightmarish power.
The oldest and worst of monsters, with magical power that never ran dry, strength enough to tear heaven and earth apart, and tremendous Regeneration.
Then people remembered a fact they’d forgotten.

In the Great Battle of Paris more than thirty years ago—the battle that had made Michael Silbert who he was—the creature that had claimed a thousand lives, including four S-rank Hunters, had been a young Dragon. It hadn’t even reached full maturity.
And its Dragon Heart had never been found.
—Yes. Now do you understand?
Michael Silbert laughed aloud.
The roar shook the entire National Assembly, and several people seized by Fear turned deathly pale.
But one man did not.
*Whoooom.*
A dreadful mass of energy gathered around the two horns rising from Michael Silbert’s forehead. Jin Taekyung watched the Breath form without a trace of panic.
He merely looked on for a moment before tossing out a single word like a sigh.
“Fucking bastard. I’m already in bad shape...”
And the next moment—
*Whooosh!*
Immense darkness poured down, staining the whole world, and collided with blue-white flames swirling along the spearhead.
*Gooooong.*
At the end of it all came a blinding flash.

The origin and very embodiment of the dragonkin, born with nightmarish power.
The oldest and worst of monsters, with magical power that never ran dry, strength enough to tear heaven and earth apart, and tremendous Regeneration.
Then people remembered a fact they’d forgotten.

In the Great Battle of Paris more than thirty years ago—the battle that had made Michael Silbert who he was—the creature that had claimed a thousand lives, including four S-rank Hunters, had been a young Dragon.
It hadn’t even reached full maturity.
And its Dragon Heart had never been found.
—Yes.
Now do you understand?
Michael Silbert laughed aloud.
The roar shook the entire National Assembly, and several people seized by Fear turned deathly pale.
But one man did not.
*Whoooom.*
A dreadful mass of energy gathered around the two horns rising from Michael Silbert’s forehead.
Jin Taekyung watched the Breath form without a trace of panic.
He merely looked on for a moment before tossing out a single word like a sigh.
“Fucking bastard.
I’m already in bad shape...”
And the next moment—
*Whooosh!*
Immense darkness poured down, staining the whole world, and collided with blue-white flames swirling along the spearhead.
*Gooooong.*
At the end of it all came a blinding flash.

chapters.title: Chapter 785
paragraphs: It was a reverberation.
More than a roar—a sound that left their ears muffled.
*Gooooong.*
Darkness and flames collided, then mingled.
Everyone watched as the two immense forces drew in wind, air, and debris, slowly swelling. A red warning light flashed through their minds, along with a single word.
Annihilation.
Before power unlike anything they had ever felt, everything else seemed meaningless.
If it burst, everything within a few hundred meters would turn to ash.
No—the blast might reach beyond the National Assembly and sweep across the entire city.
*At this rate... even the civilians will get hurt.*
But not everyone was thinking of the civilians.

They might all have sensed the same danger, but they stood on opposite sides of it. Some fought to protect the world of the people outside. Others had turned their weapons on them to protect only their own.
That difference soon showed in what each side did.
“Get them!”
*Shhk-shhk-shhk!*
With their backs to the cliff’s edge, the traitors had nowhere left to retreat.
Already outnumbered, those who had chosen Michael Silbert seized on the sudden upheaval and made one last desperate attack.
Their numbers had been cut in half, but their auras flashed with more vicious intent than ever.
*Krrrraack!*
A massive Tower Shield split apart. The ground opened like a block of tofu under a knife.
Lethal strikes rushed in from every direction. A moment’s carelessness would cost someone their life, yet no one stepped back.
They were Hunters.
Even if the word meant nothing more to those traitors than a faded slogan, they had upheld what it meant to be a Hunter—and they would continue to do so.
That was their duty. The responsibility that came with their strength.
“Mr. Johnson!”
Choi Minwoo shouted as if giving a battle cry and swung his sword with all his might.
Its wielder was drenched in blood, but a dazzling crescent of aura swept through the air, grazed past the towering Black man standing there, and cleaved the dozens of arrows flying toward him.
*Shhk!*
The severed arrows scattered before Johnson’s eyes.
Even amid the battle raging on every side, Magic Johnson drew a deep breath and gathered his mana, muttering to himself.
*I keep telling him to call me Johnson.*
When this battle was over—when the blood finally stopped flowing—he would tell Choi Minwoo again that there was no need to be so formal with him.

He wanted to clap Faye Chen on the shoulder as she drew her bowstring with bloodied fingers. Prince Felix, too, fighting drenched in blood despite his noble station. And Chuck Hagel, who had just ripped off the Kronos Guild Master’s arm.
No. He wanted to get drunk, laugh, and talk with every Hunter who survived.
And Jin would surely be there.
*Yeah, Jin. You’ll be there.*
His unheard words dissolved into the reverberation.
Through the blinding light now filling the National Assembly, Johnson caught a hazy glimpse of a young man.
He saw someone else running toward him without hesitation—toward the heart of the disaster.
*Chrrrrrrk!*
Something white as snow surged forward like a wave.
It sealed every gap around Jin Taekyung and Michael Silbert, the two figures who stood opposed with neither able to give way.
As it took shape, Magic Johnson smiled faintly and roused every bit of mana in his body. He spread it throughout the National Assembly as if to wrap the whole world in it, then spoke.
“Absolute Shield.”
The spell consumed the Grand Mage’s vast reserves of mana and spread across a radius of several hundred meters.
*Whooosh.*
Then the light finally burst forth, filling everyone’s vision.
In a sliver of time divided into moments finer still—
*Boom! Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
The world shook with a roar so vast it hurt. Pitch-black darkness and flashes of light flickered before my eyes. Sensations flooded through my body.
Pain. Heat. Cold. Wetness.
And... weight.
It pressed down on my whole body, almost more than I could bear.
*Huff. Huff.*
My breathing was ragged. I struggled to clear my blurred vision, then drove the shaft of my spear into the ground to support myself.
*Thump.*
At times like this, I was glad I’d chosen a spear.
It reminded me of what the red-capped Instructor had said when I first arrived at the Hunter Training Center and he handed out our weapons.
“Just use a spear. Spears are the best.”
“Yes, sir. Sorry, but may I ask why?”
“What’s your Awakening Grade?”
“F-rank, sir.”
“Right. There’s your answer. In a fight between weaklings like you, reach is everything. I’ve used one, so I know. And another important thing...”
“What’s that, sir?”
“It looks cool.”
“Sorry, I didn’t quite catch that...?”

“I said it looks cool. Look. Say you meet an enemy. You fight like hell, one-on-one. You both use every last bit of strength until neither of you can lift a finger. Who falls over first—the guy with the sword or the guy with the spear?”
“The guy with weaker legs, I’d think.”
“Wrong. The guy with the sword. Every time.”
“Could you tell me why, sir...?”
I still remembered the Instructor’s answer, delivered with a solemn expression.
“The guy with the spear can use it as a cane.”
“Sir?”

“Jam it into the ground or a wall and you’ve got something to lean on. The guy with the sword has to fall. Why? His sword’s too short. That’s what decides it: one man down, one man standing. What do you think? Like a scene from a movie, right?”
“Ah.”
“Good. Decided what weapon you want?”
“Yes, sir.”
“What is it?”
“A bow.”
“Get down.”
It was a stupid, dusty old memory.
He’d promptly whacked me on the ass about twenty times with a spear shaft from the armory, then practically forced me to take that spear as my first weapon.
The next day, he turned up for our first training session with a sword at his side. I learned one of life’s great truths.
This line of work was crawling with some truly spectacular assholes.
But even that Instructor, who must have stayed at the training center for the pleasure of messing with recruits like me, couldn’t have imagined where his stupid joke would lead.
That because of his stupid little joke, I’d be standing here now.
That the F-rank Hunter he’d seen back then would make Michael Silbert kneel just a little over ten years later.
*Thump.*
I raised my head at the heavy sound that pierced my ears.
Through my blurred vision, I saw him trembling on one knee.
Michael Silbert’s wings of magical power were gone. So were his gleaming black scales. He stared at me, panting.
“Y-you bastard...”
*Cough.*
With a cough, a torrent of bloody fluid mixed with bits of his organs poured out.
He’d exhausted all his magical power, and his body refused to heal as it had before, no matter how badly he wanted it to.
No. It would never heal like that again.
Michael Silbert was going to...
*Die today. By my hand.*
I had no strength to say it aloud. I spoke the words in my head, gritted my teeth, and used White Flame to push myself upright.
Then I walked toward him.
*Thud.*
Pain tore through my body with every step, as though I might break apart.
Or perhaps I already had.
*Beep. Beep. Beep-beep!*
Strange.
My eardrums had burst, and my ears had been ringing for a while, but the System’s warning beeps were still loud and annoying.
*My body must be pretty thoroughly wrecked.*
A hollow laugh escaped me. It didn’t matter.
Since when had I ever worried about my condition in a fight?
I was happier that I’d finally brought Michael Silbert down—and that, despite the immense aftermath, all those familiar faces had made it through alive.
Of course, not everyone felt the same joy I did.
“Jin Taekyung!”
The middle-aged giant charging at me—the Kronos Guild Master—certainly didn’t.
As proof of how fierce the fighting had been, he’d lost an arm to some powerful fighter I couldn’t identify. Unable to accept that his life was over, he charged at me.
Then a fierce rush of air sounded behind me, and he had no choice but to accept it.
*Boom!*
An absurdly huge War Hammer swept past. The Kronos Guild Master’s face vanished.
Behind his corpse, which crumpled like a rotten log, Chuck Hagel stood posed like a shot-putter.
He stared at me for a moment, let out a short laugh, and turned to charge the remaining traitors.
He had a warm little line to thaw their frozen hearts.
“Let’s keep playing to the end, you sons of bitches.”
Cheers and screams mingled in my muffled ears. Some fell, spraying blood. Others stepped over their bodies and pressed on.
The tide had turned.
Even if the goddess of fate showed up to tip the scales back, all we had to do was take her down, too.
Just as I would take down the monster struggling to rise now that I was right in front of him.
*Thud.*
When had I gotten this close?
I stopped. Like an old man who had leaned on his cane through a long journey to see a lifelong friend, I greeted him, weary but glad to have arrived.
“Hey. I’m here.”
*Clang!*
His answer was the still-brilliant blue blade of his sword.
But even an edge forged from Dragon Bone, a material beyond compare, couldn’t cut through Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. There was nowhere near enough strength or speed behind the strike.
Even I, barely able to stand, could block it with ease.
And return his rude greeting.
*Thud. Crunch.*
Michael Silbert’s eyes flew wide. Both arms crumpled. Blood and a scream he couldn’t force out bubbled in his open mouth.
*Grrk. Grrrk.*
Blood spurted intermittently, splattering my face.
But why?
If I thought about what he’d done up until now, the scent of blood seeping into my nose should have been sweet. But all I could smell was something revolting.
Maybe that was why I stopped.
Why the face reflected in his eyes, dark with blood and tears, looked twisted into a monster’s.
“...So this is the world you wanted so badly?”
I knew he couldn’t give me the answer I wanted, no matter what I asked.
No answer could calm this heart and these emotions threatening to burst out of me.
But I still wanted to hear him speak. I had to.
For all the people who had died because of his pathetic ambition.
“Answer me.”
*Grab.*
I seized Michael Silbert’s one remaining horn and hauled him upright. Fighting the pain that surged through me, I whispered to him as he slipped closer to death.
“Say something. Anything. Come on.”
And then I understood.
I knew where his other horn had gone. Why I hadn’t seen it anywhere nearby.
*Thud.*
The horn shot up from somewhere and pierced a palm with a dull, wet sound.
But there was no blood. No groan from someone enduring the pain.
Only Michael Silbert’s trembling gaze, fixed over my shoulder, and his voice.
“How dare... How dare a monster like you...”
“Wrong. I’ll tell you once, and only once, so remember it.”
I knew that voice. I realized who stood behind me and laughed aloud.
“My name is Stone-King, you hideous monster.”

chapters.title: Chapter 786
paragraphs: “My name is Stone King, you hideous monster.”
The moment he spat out those words as if biting them off, the Skeleton King finally understood.
He had found the answer to the question that had tormented him for so long.
All those nights when everyone else slept and he could not. All those days when everyone else went about their lives and he alone remained dead.
And the question that had bound his body and mind like a chain.
*Who am I?*
No matter how hard he’d thought about it, he’d never found an answer. But the answer had been there all along, within the Skeleton King himself.
*So that’s it.*
The Skeleton King muttered to himself.
In the black eyes he saw over a man’s shoulder, the radiance cast by his golden crown was reflected.
“What, exactly, did you want to become?”
Michael Silbert’s eyes trembled at the offhand question.
The Skeleton King continued calmly.
“There was a time when I desperately wanted to know. I tried to recover a past I can no longer remember, and I didn’t know what to call the person I am now.”
That was why he had followed a human he’d met one day out of a forest filled with nothing but death and darkness, and into an unfamiliar world.
“I wanted to find the answer in the world you live in. I believed I could.”
But he hadn’t. Even there, amid enormous metal things rolling on wheels and buildings taller than trees, the answer was nowhere to be found.
To the Skeleton King, who had left the forest in search of it, the human world was simply another forest.
“I can’t breathe or sleep. I can’t feel the cool breeze other humans talk about, or the taste of food. I can’t even feel the faintest pain.”
That was when he first learned that being unable to feel pain could itself be painful. And that some kinds of pain lay in the truth itself.
*Monster.*
It was the first word the Skeleton King had searched online the day he received a smartphone. One of the words he’d heard most often in the human world. A word for beings like him.
His questions gave way to an emotion he’d never felt before.
Anguish.
Anguish at having awakened as a monster through no choice of his own.
Fear that, to the people he had begun to talk with, share his feelings with, and grow close to, he might be nothing more than a monster.
“I wanted to deny that I was one of them. So I fought alongside you, and for you, with everything I had. I believed it was the right thing to do.”
He still believed it. Otherwise, he would never have considered sacrificing himself here today.
The Skeleton King didn’t want the humans he cared about to fall before the world did.
Humans were more complicated than he’d imagined. Some harbored terrible rage and killing intent, as monsters did—or worse.
But humans also knew restraint and love. They thought and acted according to their own will.
When petty disputes left countless people dead or injured, when children still little more than infants were abandoned in the street, it was humans who took those children into their arms.
That was why the Skeleton King had wanted to become human like them. To be welcomed among them not as a monster, but as a neighbor and a friend.
And why realizing it was impossible had driven him to despair.
But...
“Not anymore.”
The Skeleton King murmured calmly and gripped the horn piercing the back of his hand.
*Crack.*
He caught Michael Silbert’s hand around the horn as well. Though it had been bent and broken earlier, it was slowly healing.
A voice seething with fury escaped through Michael’s clenched teeth.
“You think... you think doing this will make a mere monster like you human...?”
“It doesn’t matter.”
“What?”
“I know. I’m a monster, so I can’t be called human. And because I live among humans, I can’t be called a monster.”
The Skeleton King smiled faintly.
“What does that matter? This is enough.”
“You hideous, pitiful monster. Let me introduce myself once more.”
Looking into Michael Silbert’s wide eyes, the Skeleton King spoke slowly.

“I am the master of the Black Forest, the ruler of all the undead, and a hero of this world who fought for you humans. Call me the Skeleton King or the Stone King. Whatever name you give me is part of who I am. But...”
*Tap.*
The Skeleton King raised a hand and rested it on a man’s shoulder.
“I won’t tell you the first name I was given in this world.”
Because that was a name only a friend could use.
“Isn’t that right, Jin Taekyung? You conniving human.”
I didn’t know what to say.
Should I laugh at the bastard for finally coming to his senses? Get angry? Or smack him upside the head as hard as I could, like I usually did?
Like someone who’d forgotten how to speak, I sank into a brief but deep debate before suddenly opening my mouth.
“Golgoli, you stupid son of a bitch.”
Bones.
The first name I’d given the undead I’d met in the Black Forest.
Usually he’d have thrown a fit and told me not to call him that. Today, his answer was meek.
“I admit it. I was a stupid son of a bitch.”
“I won’t doubt you again.”
Damn it.
I was speechless. I had nothing to say. But somehow, I didn’t feel frustrated at all.
I just... felt relieved.
As if a stone had lifted from my chest. As if the last bit of distance between us had finally vanished.
Yeah. That was enough.
Feeling lighter, I threw a punch.
*Thwack!*
Michael Silbert’s face snapped back. I still had him by the hair, and he’d been standing there looking half out of it.
I didn’t even let him fall.
*Thwack, thwack. Crack.*
His proud nose caved in. Teeth spilled through his mangled lips.
I hit him until blood or tears ran down his cheeks from eyes veined with burst capillaries. Until his twitching limbs went limp.
*Crack. Crunch.*
I kept hitting him. Breaking him. Crushing him.
Every time I moved, every time my fists and feet slammed into him, the lingering aftermath of One Annihilation sent excruciating pain through my whole body. But I didn’t care.
If someone hadn’t grabbed my wrist, I might have beaten Michael Silbert to death right there.
*Grab.*
“Please stop, Mr. Jin. Not yet.”
A familiar voice, worn with exhaustion.
I turned without thinking and blinked. Team Leader Choi stood there, drenched from head to toe in blood.
No. Everyone was there.
“Jin, it’s over. It’s finally... finally over.”
Magic Johnson approached with Chuck Hagel supporting him. He smiled weakly, but there was no joy in it, despite their victory in a battle that had decided their fate.
After killing people who had once been his comrades, the hero’s smile was dark and bitter.
Just like the silence that had settled over us, and everyone surrounding me.
“Oh.”
A sound escaped me—part gasp, part groan.
Only then did I raise my head and look around. Everything they’d said was true.
*Whoooosh.*
A wind heavy with the smell of blood swept past.
Abandoned weapons and corpses filled every part of my view.
Pools of blood on the floor soaked our shoes. The enormous Round Table, once a symbol of the heroes who had saved the world, had been shattered, leaving only ruins behind.
Yeah. It was over.
The first battle for humanity’s fate.
The battle between duty and self-interest. Between humans and monsters.
It had ended here—and outside, where blood had been spilled beyond our sight.
*Creeeeak. Boom.*
The entrance door, already half broken, toppled with a heavy crash. Weary footsteps followed as people climbed over it.
*Clank. Clank.*
Their armor and weapons were soaked in blood.
At the sight of the blood-drenched figures filing in, quite a few of the surviving Hunters reached for their weapons. They stopped when Team Leader Choi spoke.
“How did it go?”
One of the two people at the front—a young man who still had peach fuzz on his face—answered in a soldier’s clipped tone.

“We killed or captured them all. We took more casualties than expected because of a man named Huginn, but we joined forces with the Peace and Ares Guilds and subdued him. Then we dispelled the illusion magic around the area and notified the Korean government a little while ago. Oh, and Mr. Shu here played a major part.”
“You’ve both worked hard. It would have been a difficult fight if you hadn’t trusted us and helped.”
At Team Leader Choi’s heartfelt words, the man in his thirties whom the young man had called “Mr. Shu” shook his head.
“I only trusted the Übermensch’s judgment and his choice. What I saw of him that day in Munich... He was a true superhuman.”
When he looked my way, I gave him a small nod in greeting. I nodded to the young man beside him, too. He was watching me with an expectant look.
*Joel Schumacher. Xiao Shen.*
They’d owed me, and today they’d paid me back with interest.
The others probably had no idea that Joel Schumacher, who had politely declined to attend the inaugural ceremony because of his injuries in Munich, had secretly entered Korea.
Or that Xiao Shen had brought Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department and joined the elite forces of the Peace and Ares Guilds, who were fully prepared.
I remembered a question Team Leader Choi had asked me a few days ago.
“There’s a meticulous man. When do you think he’s most vulnerable, Mr. Jin?”
The answer hadn’t been hard. I’d seen it happen several times, and I’d made the same mistake myself.
“When he thinks he’s succeeded.”
I’d been right.
Michael Silbert might have guarded against things going wrong, but part of him had been certain he would win.
If he’d been acting like himself, he would have chosen France—his stronghold—or somewhere else with a firm support base, instead of Seoul, for the inaugural ceremony.
But that small lapse, that petty desire to stamp his name on this historic place, had brought down his vast ambition.
I could hear it clearly.
“We’ve won.”
Along with Team Leader Choi’s words, echoing through the silent air, someone’s hideous ambition crumbled to pieces.
I knew what I had left to do.
*...Yeah.*
To end everything, I had to erase the starting line where it all began.
Just as we had executed the traitors here today, the people who would have stood in the way of the great war to come.
I had to pull out the root. Otherwise, new weeds—and offshoots of this thorn tree—would keep growing.
*Michael Silbert.*
*Crack.*
I stomped on the chest of the man lying at my feet. Bones shifted beneath my boot.
Michael Silbert came to, blood surging from his mouth. He looked around with bleary eyes.
“So... that’s how it ended.”
His voice was fading, but his tone was composed.
He had probably realized it instinctively the moment he looked around.
That Huginn, his right-hand man, and the private army he had spent so many years training would never make it here.
“Did you kill them all?”
I answered evenly.
“The ones who were going to die died. The ones who were going to live lived.”
“Huginn must be among the latter. You’ll have plenty to ask him.”
“You know it.”
“Then I have a favor to ask.”
A favor.
That simple word suddenly made me sick. I kicked him in the face.
*Thwack.*
His head snapped aside, spraying blood.
But maybe he couldn’t feel pain anymore. Without so much as a groan, Michael Silbert spat the blood filling his mouth and stubbornly continued.

“Tell Huginn I’m grateful for everything he’s done, and that he no longer needs to be loyal to me. Grant me that favor, and it will be easier for both of you. You can at least spare yourselves a messy, tedious round of torture and interrogation.”
“Is that a kindness for a retainer who’s been loyal his whole life, or your last words?”
“Both, I suppose. From the look in your eyes, this place will be my grave soon.”
I looked down at Michael Silbert as he smiled soundlessly.
And I knew, more certainly than ever, that I couldn’t leave him the slightest chance.
The law? A trial?
Those institutions were made for humans, not monsters.
A monster should die like a monster.
So they could never struggle again. So that even the tiniest chance of the tumors he’d planted in this land over the past several decades saving that monster would disappear.
Yet this was also a lawful judgment.
Everyone here had witnessed the truth and fought through the bloodshed. They were witnesses and jurors, prosecutors and judges.
And from this moment on, they and I would finally become *us*.
Race. Sex. Age. Borders.
Even species would cease to divide us as we stood under one banner.
In the name of the World Hunter Federation.
*Michael Silbert.*
My voice broke the silence. Though I put no internal energy behind it, it carried through the chamber, clear and steady.
Loudly and clearly. On and on.
“From this moment forward, the World Hunter Federation revokes all your qualifications and summarily executes you as a traitor. Anyone who objects, step forward.”
Team Leader Choi answered at once.
“No objections.”
Magic Johnson spoke next.
“Everything according to the rules.”
Prince Felix bowed with dignity instead of answering. Faye Chen and Chuck Hagel struck their weapons together.
*Clang!*
The deep note rang out over the ruins.
Others joined in. One weapon became dozens, then hundreds, striking together and throwing blue sparks.
Someone pounded his armor with his one remaining hand. A white-haired elder struck the ground with a bloodied cane.
*Boom. Boom. Boom-boom-boom.*
The world shook. Pooled blood splashed in every direction.
No one objected. Everyone agreed.
To the World Hunter Federation’s first resolution.
To the death of a traitor born human who had become a monster.
Amid the deep resonance that rang on and on, I stared at Michael Silbert and asked,
“Any objections?”
After a moment’s silence, he answered.
“None. At first, I fought with all my strength to survive. After that, I fought to get what I wanted.”
“Any last words?”
“It’s your turn now. Go on—struggle with everything you have. I’ll be watching from up above.”
I raised my spear as his mocking words reached me. The shaft felt heavier than it ever had before.
Then, in front of hundreds of pairs of eyes, I drove the spearhead down with all my strength.
*Thrust!*
The spearhead pierced straight through his throat.
A strangled sound failed to make it past his lips. Michael Silbert’s body went rigid.
I looked into the monster’s eyes as life quickly drained away, then delivered the last words I’d put off until now.
“Just like you said, watch closely. Not from up above—from the very bottom, beneath my feet.”
Was it anger that made his eyes widen at the end? Or the death he could no longer hold off?
Maybe both.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*
Countless chimes and radiance welled up inside me.

No matter how hard he’d thought about it, he’d never found an answer.

*So that’s it.*
The Skeleton King muttered to himself.
In the black eyes he saw over a man’s shoulder, the radiance cast by his golden crown was reflected.
“What, exactly, did you want to become?”
Michael Silbert’s eyes trembled at the offhand question.
The Skeleton King continued calmly.
“There was a time when I desperately wanted to know.
I tried to recover a past I can no longer remember, and I didn’t know what to call the person I am now.”
That was why he had followed a human he’d met one day out of a forest filled with nothing but death and darkness, and into an unfamiliar world.
“I wanted to find the answer in the world you live in.
I believed I could.”
But he hadn’t.
Even there, amid enormous metal things rolling on wheels and buildings taller than trees, the answer was nowhere to be found.
To the Skeleton King, who had left the forest in search of it, the human world was simply another forest.
“I can’t breathe or sleep.
I can’t feel the cool breeze other humans talk about, or the taste of food.
I can’t even feel the faintest pain.”
That was when he first learned that being unable to feel pain could itself be painful.
And that some kinds of pain lay in the truth itself.
*Monster.*
It was the first word the Skeleton King had searched online the day he received a smartphone.
One of the words he’d heard most often in the human world.
A word for beings like him.
His questions gave way to an emotion he’d never felt before.
Anguish.
Anguish at having awakened as a monster through no choice of his own.
Fear that, to the people he had begun to talk with, share his feelings with, and grow close to, he might be nothing more than a monster.
“I wanted to deny that I was one of them.
So I fought alongside you, and for you, with everything I had.
I believed it was the right thing to do.”
He still believed it.
Otherwise, he would never have considered sacrificing himself here today.
The Skeleton King didn’t want the humans he cared about to fall before the world did.
Humans were more complicated than he’d imagined.
Some harbored terrible rage and killing intent, as monsters did—or worse.
But humans also knew restraint and love.
They thought and acted according to their own will.
When petty disputes left countless people dead or injured, when children still little more than infants were abandoned in the street, it was humans who took those children into their arms.
That was why the Skeleton King had wanted to become human like them.
To be welcomed among them not as a monster, but as a neighbor and a friend.
And why realizing it was impossible had driven him to despair.
But...

The Skeleton King murmured calmly and gripped the horn piercing the back of his hand.
*Crack.*
He caught Michael Silbert’s hand around the horn as well.
Though it had been bent and broken earlier, it was slowly healing.
A voice seething with fury escaped through Michael’s clenched teeth.

“What?”

*Tap.*
The Skeleton King raised a hand and rested it on a man’s shoulder.

Because that was a name only a friend could use.

I didn’t know what to say.
Should I laugh at the bastard for finally coming to his senses?
Get angry?
Or smack him upside the head as hard as I could, like I usually did?
Like someone who’d forgotten how to speak, I sank into a brief but deep debate before suddenly opening my mouth.

Bones.
The first name I’d given the undead I’d met in the Black Forest.

I just... felt relieved.

Yeah.

paragraphs: “Ah.”
Jin Taekyung let out a single exclamation.
At that moment, he felt the full blessing of the supernatural power that had come to him.
Clear chimes, audible to him alone, rang without pause, while countless holographic windows rose above the ruins and filled his vision.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*

**System** You have defeated Lv. 175 Michael Silbert! You have gained a tremendous amount of EXP and Fame! You have achieved the rare feat Cut the Weeds and Pull Up the Roots! We offer our unreserved praise for your bold decision to cut down the diseased grass and pull out its roots for the sake of the forest we all share. But remember: the great fire that could consume the forest is more dangerous than any disease. You have gained a tremendous amount of EXP and Fame as a reward for your achievement! You have gained 20 points as a special bonus reward! Level Up! Level Up! Most of your injuries and Stamina have been restored by the stacked effects of leveling up! The special debuff Broken Body rejects the power of healing!
Countless notifications filled his eyes and ears.
At the same time, a warm radiance no one else could see or feel welled up from deep inside Jin Taekyung.
*Whoosh.*
Energy washed over him like a downpour—something that deserved to be called purification, not merely healing.
It enveloped the waste that had built up inside him, his damaged blood vessels and organs, his broken bones, and his torn skin.
*Shhhhh.*
The terrible pain throughout his body rapidly faded.
Beneath the sticky blood covering him from head to toe, wounds no one had noticed healed without a trace.
But none of that mattered to Jin Taekyung.
Not compared to the relief he felt.
*It’s over.*
He let out the breath he’d been holding.
Michael Silbert lay dead, his eyes wide open. Jin could no longer sense any trace of life in him.
There was no doubt.
The bastard was dead.
More cunning than any enemy Jin had ever faced, the scheming man who had shaken him to his core had been born human and left this world a monster.
No. Perhaps by now his soul had tumbled into the abyss reflected in those staring eyes.
Just like Jin’s final farewell to him, in the moment the cold spearhead pierced his throat.
“...Go to hell.”
Jin spat out the words and gripped the spear shaft. He twisted it hard, cutting through the monster’s neck.
*Slash. Splash.*
A jet of green blood erupted as Michael Silbert’s head came free of his body and rolled across a pool of blood.
At the same moment, as if on cue, a tremendous roar erupted. No—it was both a roar and a cheer.
*Boom! Boom-boom-boom!*
*Rumble!*
The hundreds of surviving Hunters roared as one.
Their mana-charged shouts burst through the compressed air. Feet and weapons pounded the ground without pause, shaking the National Assembly building.
Some were simply overjoyed. Others trembled with anger that had yet to fade. Still others stared at them blankly and began to cry.
Jin Taekyung let the spear that had ended it all hang limply at his side.
“...Fuck.”
What was the big deal? What the hell was so important about this?
He didn’t know himself.
Why had the curse suddenly come out? Why was he crying like an idiot while everyone else celebrated?
But a voice at his ear supplied the answer.
“I don’t know what stupid thought is going through your head right now, but I’ll tell you one thing.”
The Skeleton King put a hand on Jin’s shoulder.
“The people who died aren’t your fault. I became a monster against my will, too.”
“So stop bawling like an idiot. No one is blaming you or holding you responsible.”
Jin fell silent at those prickly but warm words.
Then, amid the endless cheering and rumbling, he let out a wry chuckle.
“Hey.”
“Hmm? Did you call?”
“Why are you acting all serious, you monster bastard?”
“What are you looking at? Keep your eyes nice and polite.”
The Skeleton King had been quietly hoping for a response, though he’d tried not to show it. Now, he muttered with a stunned look on his face.
“Is this truly what human nature is like...?”
“I can hear you.”
“I meant you to.”
“A monster... talking back?”
“Ah, enough already!”
Teasing the Skeleton King—no, teasing his friend—was always fun.
Jin laughed at the Skeleton King’s fit of outrage, wiping his tears with his blood-soaked sleeve.
“And don’t think I missed you wiping your tears. It’s too late to hide it.”
“...You’re spreading lies, you bastard. When did I do that? Got proof?”
“No proof, but I’ve got witnesses. Plenty of people saw you besides me—huh?”
*Grab.*
Jin suddenly staggered. The Skeleton King caught him by the arm, his eyes widening.
“Ah. The floor’s slippery with blood.”
Jin answered with a grin. But he couldn’t hide the tremble at the corners of his mouth or the crushing exhaustion in his half-closed eyes.
It was only natural.

Leveling up twice had healed most of his injuries. But everything that had happened on the way here, and the strain it had left on his mind, was more than a young man barely in his twenties could bear alone.
The sleepless nights and countless battles had begun the day he learned the truth about Michael Silbert’s hideous nature and ambitions.
For the past few weeks, Jin had fought day and night.
And Michael Silbert and his countless monster hordes weren’t the only enemies he’d faced.

There was the world’s condemnation, growing harsher by the day. There were the disasters he’d heard about on the news from every corner of the world, and his own self-loathing at being powerless to stop those deaths.
Jin had fought himself, and he had fought the world.
Now that he’d finally defeated Michael Silbert, even standing still demanded superhuman patience.
But...
*I can’t.*
He forced his drooping eyelids open.
Not yet. He had to hold on a little longer. Just a little longer.
Until he finished what he’d started.
Sirens had begun to mingle with the cheers, drawing closer. He couldn’t collapse before he told the world the whole truth about what had happened here today.
*No matter what.*
*Thud.*
Using the spear he’d driven into the ground as a cane, Jin Taekyung leaned against it and murmured in a voice that seemed about to fade away.
“Thanks so fucking much, Assistant Hwang, you son of a bitch...”
“Are you really all right...? Wait, what did you just say?”
“Hey, Golgoli.”
“Huh?”
“You should use a spear too. Not a sword.”
What? Out of nowhere?
The Skeleton King blinked, unable to make sense of it.
“Why?”
“Compared to a sword...”
“Compared to a sword.”
“A spear...”
“A spear.”
“Looks cooler.”
“Looks coo—fuck.”
The Skeleton King sighed.
Why had he listened so closely to that inhuman bastard? Half of what Jin said was nonsense, and the other half was abuse directed at him.
*I’m the idiot.*
But the Skeleton King said nothing more. He only let out a long sigh.
He didn’t want to wake his friend, who had fallen into a deep sleep as if he’d passed out, still leaning against the spear planted deep in the ground.
*You’ve worked hard. Rest.*
Perhaps everyone felt the same.
As if they’d never cheered at all, the hundreds of Hunters pressed their lips together in silence and simply looked on.
They watched the young man who had been braver and shone brighter than anyone else here today.
The superhuman who had stood against the whole world and kept to his path, even when the truth ahead was too dark to see through.
*Could I have done what he did?*
Each of them asked themselves the question and arrived at the same answer.
No one there could have.
They would have fallen, been scraped raw, battered and broken, and finally gone down, never to rise again.
But that young man, barely in his twenties—Jin Taekyung—had done it.
However many times he fell, he got back up. However badly he was battered and broken, he refused to stay down.
He alone had become a signpost and a light for those lost in the darkness.
The one who led everyone from the front.
The one who shared the pain of the wounded without ever yielding to weakness, who pressed bravely onward with an indomitable will.
And people had a word for someone like that, a word filled with all the reverence and love in the world.
*Hero.*
The moment that short word filled their minds, everyone there was overcome by a feeling they couldn’t describe.
Hero. They knew the word all too well.
At some point, the whole world had begun calling them heroes. One ordinary day, they’d gained unexpected powers, fought monsters, and become humanity’s sword and shield.
But why?
Why did that word, heard so often it had nearly worn grooves in their ears, make their hearts swell like this?
Why did looking back leave them both ashamed and choked with emotion?
One image kept coming back to them: the look in Jin’s eyes as he shouted the truth without fear, surrounded by hundreds of weapons.
And the sight of a young man weeping alone, while everyone cheered at the end of the fierce battle.
Perhaps that was why the reinforcements entering the ruined National Assembly stopped without realizing it and held their breath.
And why, in a silence so deep it seemed you could hear a needle drop, someone let out the breath they’d been holding.
“Fuck.”
People turned toward the voice and were surprised three times.
First, that anyone could deliver a curse in such a refined tone.
Second, that a curse could sound so awkward.
And finally, that the person who had managed both at once was the last man they’d expected.
Prince Felix paid their stares no mind.
No. He no longer cared.
“Fuck. Fuck. Fuck.”
What a relief.
His pronunciation was still clumsy, but with each curse, something knotted in his chest seemed to loosen.
Felix found himself chuckling.
*Damn it. What was so important about any of it?*
Bloodline. Dignity. Appearances. Etiquette.
Everything he’d taken pride in for more than thirty years suddenly felt empty and burdensome.
He wanted to cast it all off, right then and there.
So he did.
For the first time in his life, he cursed like a dockworker and threw off the armor bearing the royal crest.
He wondered for a moment what expression His Majesty the King—his father—would wear if he saw him like this. But, well...
*Did it matter?*
*Step. Step.*
With everyone watching, Felix slowly crossed the ruined chamber and stopped.
Then he spoke without preamble.
“It looks as though you could use another pair of hands. If you don’t mind, may I help?”
At Prince Felix’s most courteous offer yet, the Skeleton King nodded. He was supporting Jin Taekyung, who had collapsed into sleep against the spear shaft.
“If you wish, then do so, human prince.”
Felix’s reply astonished everyone nearby.
“Please call me Felix, Mr. King. My friend.”
He gave the people staring at him a faint smile. As he took Jin by one shoulder, another hand reached out to help.
“Watching from over there, it looked as though you still needed another pair of hands.”
Choi Minwoo answered calmly, and more hands joined them.
One trembling hand belonged to Chuck Hagel, who was already acting as though he were going through withdrawal. The small hand covered in unusually thick calluses belonged to Faye Chen.
As for Magic Johnson, he stared at the staff in his hand for a moment, then suddenly grinned.
“Sometimes everything I’ve learned feels useless. Like right now.”
He tucked the staff away and strode over to lend a hand.
At first glance, it made no sense.
A Grand Mage who had mastered hundreds of spells, and the finest Hunters, capable of slicing through several metric tons of concrete in an instant, had all gathered to lift one young man.
But this was how they chose to show him their respect.
*Rustle. Rustle.*
Only the soft brush of clothing broke the silence. Hands multiplied until there were hundreds of them, passing the sleeping young hero slowly overhead like a gentle ripple across a lake.
As carefully as if they were handling glass.
Careful not to disturb the peace that had finally found him, if only for a little while.
When they laid Jin down on the ground, everyone realized something.
The inaugural ceremony of the New World Hunter Federation, which would be recorded in the history of humanity, was not over yet.
The young man before them would be both the beginning and the end of the Great War to come.
*Shing.*
The cold scrape of steel cut through the silence.
A sword slid slowly from its sheath and pointed toward the sky.
Soon, countless weapons—dozens, then hundreds—glinted in the sunset streaming through the shattered stained glass.
In the ruins, steeped in the reddish warmth of flames, they were turned toward the young man immersed in an unbreakable peace.
No.
Toward their new Alliance Leader.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*

**System** You have achieved the unbelievable feat A Coronation for One Person Alone! The World Hunter Federation appoints you as its Alliance Leader! You have gained a tremendous amount of EXP and Fame!
The chimes, audible to just one person, rang clearer and louder than ever.
Loud enough to bring a smile to the lips of someone deep in sleep.
Loud enough to melt the guilt still lingering in a corner of his heart.
And so, at the end of a long and fierce day, a new page of history was turning.
