**System** You have defeated Lv.
175 Michael Silbert!
You have gained a tremendous amount of EXP and Fame!
You have achieved the rare feat Cut the Weeds and Pull Up the Roots!
We offer our unreserved praise for your bold decision to cut down the diseased grass and pull out its roots for the sake of the forest we all share.
But remember: the great fire that could consume the forest is more dangerous than any disease.
You have gained a tremendous amount of EXP and Fame as a reward for your achievement!
You have gained 20 points as a special bonus reward!
Level Up!
Level Up!
Most of your injuries and Stamina have been restored by the stacked effects of leveling up!
The special debuff Broken Body rejects the power of healing!
Countless notifications filled his eyes and ears.
At the same time, a warm radiance no one else could see or feel welled up from deep inside Jin Taekyung.
*Whoosh.*
Energy washed over him like a downpour—something that deserved to be called purification, not merely healing.
It enveloped the waste that had built up inside him, his damaged blood vessels and organs, his broken bones, and his torn skin.
*Shhhhh.*
The terrible pain throughout his body rapidly faded.
Beneath the sticky blood covering him from head to toe, wounds no one had noticed healed without a trace.
But none of that mattered to Jin Taekyung.
Not compared to the relief he felt.
*It’s over.*
He let out the breath he’d been holding.
Michael Silbert lay dead, his eyes wide open.
Jin could no longer sense any trace of life in him.
There was no doubt.
The bastard was dead.
More cunning than any enemy Jin had ever faced, the scheming man who had shaken him to his core had been born human and left this world a monster.
No.
Perhaps by now his soul had tumbled into the abyss reflected in those staring eyes.
Just like Jin’s final farewell to him, in the moment the cold spearhead pierced his throat.
“...Go to hell.”
Jin spat out the words and gripped the spear shaft.
He twisted it hard, cutting through the monster’s neck.
*Slash.
Splash.*
A jet of green blood erupted as Michael Silbert’s head came free of his body and rolled across a pool of blood.
At the same moment, as if on cue, a tremendous roar erupted.
No—it was both a roar and a cheer.
*Boom!
Boom-boom-boom!*
*Rumble!*
The hundreds of surviving Hunters roared as one.
Their mana-charged shouts burst through the compressed air.
Feet and weapons pounded the ground without pause, shaking the National Assembly building.
Some were simply overjoyed.
Others trembled with anger that had yet to fade.
Still others stared at them blankly and began to cry.
Jin Taekyung let the spear that had ended it all hang limply at his side.
“...Fuck.”
What was the big deal?
What the hell was so important about this?
He didn’t know himself.
Why had the curse suddenly come out?
Why was he crying like an idiot while everyone else celebrated?
But a voice at his ear supplied the answer.
“I don’t know what stupid thought is going through your head right now, but I’ll tell you one thing.”
The Skeleton King put a hand on Jin’s shoulder.
“The people who died aren’t your fault.
I became a monster against my will, too.”
“So stop bawling like an idiot.
No one is blaming you or holding you responsible.”
Jin fell silent at those prickly but warm words.
Then, amid the endless cheering and rumbling, he let out a wry chuckle.
“Hey.”
“Hmm?
Did you call?”
“Why are you acting all serious, you monster bastard?”
“What are you looking at?
Keep your eyes nice and polite.”
The Skeleton King had been quietly hoping for a response, though he’d tried not to show it.
Now, he muttered with a stunned look on his face.
“Is this truly what human nature is like...?”
“I can hear you.”
“I meant you to.”
“A monster... talking back?”
“Ah, enough already!”
Teasing the Skeleton King—no, teasing his friend—was always fun.
Jin laughed at the Skeleton King’s fit of outrage, wiping his tears with his blood-soaked sleeve.
“And don’t think I missed you wiping your tears.
It’s too late to hide it.”
“...You’re spreading lies, you bastard.
When did I do that?
Got proof?”
“No proof, but I’ve got witnesses.
Plenty of people saw you besides me—huh?”
*Grab.*
Jin suddenly staggered.
The Skeleton King caught him by the arm, his eyes widening.
“Ah.
The floor’s slippery with blood.”
Jin answered with a grin.
But he couldn’t hide the tremble at the corners of his mouth or the crushing exhaustion in his half-closed eyes.
It was only natural.
Leveling up twice had healed most of his injuries.
But everything that had happened on the way here, and the strain it had left on his mind, was more than a young man barely in his twenties could bear alone.
The sleepless nights and countless battles had begun the day he learned the truth about Michael Silbert’s hideous nature and ambitions.
For the past few weeks, Jin had fought day and night.
And Michael Silbert and his countless monster hordes weren’t the only enemies he’d faced.
There was the world’s condemnation, growing harsher by the day.
There were the disasters he’d heard about on the news from every corner of the world, and his own self-loathing at being powerless to stop those deaths.
Jin had fought himself, and he had fought the world.
Now that he’d finally defeated Michael Silbert, even standing still demanded superhuman patience.
But...
*I can’t.*
He forced his drooping eyelids open.
Not yet.
He had to hold on a little longer.
Just a little longer.
Until he finished what he’d started.
Sirens had begun to mingle with the cheers, drawing closer.
He couldn’t collapse before he told the world the whole truth about what had happened here today.
*No matter what.*
*Thud.*
Using the spear he’d driven into the ground as a cane, Jin Taekyung leaned against it and murmured in a voice that seemed about to fade away.
“Thanks so fucking much, Assistant Hwang, you son of a bitch...”
“Are you really all right...?
Wait, what did you just say?”
“Hey, Golgoli.”
“Huh?”
“You should use a spear too.
Not a sword.”
What?
Out of nowhere?
The Skeleton King blinked, unable to make sense of it.
“Why?”
“Compared to a sword...”
“Compared to a sword.”
“A spear...”
“A spear.”
“Looks cooler.”
“Looks coo—fuck.”
The Skeleton King sighed.
Why had he listened so closely to that inhuman bastard?
Half of what Jin said was nonsense, and the other half was abuse directed at him.
*I’m the idiot.*

He only let out a long sigh.

Rest.*

paragraphs: Paris, France. The Élysée Palace.
Despite the French fondness for fine food, President Emmanuel had finished a short, simple breakfast. Now he gazed at a box of cigars he had carefully stored away, overcome by memories.
*At last, the day has come to take these out.*
President Emmanuel had not smoked in twenty years.
In his youth, he’d been known as a cigar aficionado. But everything had changed after he met one man.
“I hear you like cigars.”
“Ah, I enjoy one now and then as a hobby.”
“Then that’s quite an expensive hobby. Most people can’t afford to spend over ten thousand euros a month sitting in their garden and burning grass.”

“You said you wanted to go into politics, didn’t you? Then you’d be wise to cut back on the cigars. They’re a monster that devours both your time and your health. And there’s no easier target to tear apart than an extravagant politician from a family of businesspeople. Now, off you go.”
His first meeting with the powerful man, arranged through his family’s connections and enormous lobbying efforts, had ended just like that—with the absurdly simple advice to cut back on cigars.
But Emmanuel, a promising young lawyer, hadn’t forgotten it.
As soon as he returned to his mansion, he threw every last one of his cigars—worth hundreds of thousands of euros—into the fireplace and began living a far more modest life.
A few years later, at Easter, he received a card bearing the image of two ravens.
Congratulations on your rebirth. M. S.
That was how Emmanuel was chosen by Michael Silbert. The following year, he made a dazzling debut in French politics under the glare of the spotlight.
And after that?
What more was there to say?
Emmanuel rose faster than anyone.
It took barely a decade for him to become someone no political heavyweight—not even a prime minister or president—could treat lightly. Michael Silbert’s shadow covered everything.
“Run in the next presidential election. You won’t be the youngest president, but I’ll help you make history as the longest-serving.”
*I’ll help you.*
At those words from Michael Silbert, Emmanuel—now a senator who embodied Paris and the leader of the largest party in parliament—had a sudden certainty.
The election was over before it had even begun.
He would be the next master of the Élysée Palace.
And at last, on the day that prediction came true, President Emmanuel mustered the courage to ask the benefactor who had come to see him:
“Why did you choose me, of all people?”
The answer was brief.
“You listened well.”
“Pardon?”

“I want only one thing. Give me your absolute loyalty, just as you have until now. If I tell you to bark, bark. If I tell you to bite, bite. Don’t repeat your predecessor’s mistake, and I’ll put not only enormous wealth and honor in your hands, but this entire country.”
“Will you be loyal to me?”
“No. I’ll obey you.”
Michael Silbert laughed aloud at that perfect answer and handed his new watchdog a box of cigars decorated with gold leaf.
“These are...”
“A gift. When my goal is realized, you’ll be as good as a king. Save these cigars for that moment.”
The memory of that day was still vivid.
As President Emmanuel gazed at the box and sank into thought, he felt his heart pound.
*A king. A king.*
A king in the twenty-first century—in this country obsessed with revolution, no less.
It was madness.
But when Michael Silbert said it, that was different. He was a man who had made countless impossibilities and wild imaginings come true.
President Emmanuel suddenly recalled the last words of his father, who had used the chaos of the Great Cataclysm to amass an astronomical fortune almost overnight.
“Everything that happens in this world is an investment and a deal. If someone wants something, give it to them freely. But always get back more than you gave.”
People had despised his father, calling him the “Merchant of Death.” But even if he had gone to hell, he probably had no great regrets.
He must have watched his son make a better deal than anyone.
Young lawyer Emmanuel had given one man a loyalty bordering on obedience, and in return had become President Emmanuel.
Soon, he would possess power beyond the presidency—power so absolute that Emmanuel the First would hardly be too grand a name for him.
“Emmanuel the First...”
President Emmanuel murmured dreamily. Then the grandfather clock against the office wall chimed.
*Dong. Dooong.*
A bird and a dwarf popped out of the clock and spun around. Emmanuel checked where the hour hand pointed and blinked.
“Noon? Already?”
He must have lost track of time while reminiscing. He slowly tapped his desk.
*It’s taking longer than I expected.*
With the time difference between France and Korea, it was now eight in the evening in Seoul, where the World Hunter Federation’s inaugural ceremony would be underway.
He checked his smartphone just in case, but no word had come from the person he was waiting for.
*Well, it would be strange if it ended early.*
This wasn’t just any gathering. It was the World Hunter Federation’s first inaugural ceremony.
Given its importance to the future of global security, a meeting as long as a full marathon was hardly surprising.
Still, even with his unwavering faith in Michael Silbert, he couldn’t help feeling a little anxious.
*Knock, knock.*
President Emmanuel frowned at the sudden knock.
“What is it?”
An attendant’s voice came through the crack in the closed door.
“It’s time for your meal, Mr. President.”
“I don’t need it. And don’t let anyone near my office until I call for them myself. Understood?”
“Yes, I’ll pass that along.”
How could he have an appetite with the most important moment of his life just ahead?
President Emmanuel cursed inwardly at his dim-witted attendant, then stared down at the smartphone in his hand.
After hesitating, he tapped one person’s number.
*Brr. Brr. Brr.*
The call rang on and on.
Emmanuel ran his hand over the cigar box, trying to suppress his anxiety. At last, there was a click, and someone answered.
“The ceremony—how did the inaugural ceremony go?”
The other person was silent for a moment before replying.
“It ended successfully.”
The words he’d waited so long to hear.
Joy surged through Emmanuel, and he burst out laughing. He punched the air without realizing he’d clenched his fist and thanked the man who had given him the answer he wanted so badly.
“Thank you! Thank you so much! Huginn, you’ve worked so hard, too—!”
“Thank me? I’m the one who should be thanking you.”
“What?”
At that moment, Emmanuel realized something.
The voice on the other end was deeper and rougher than usual.
And its owner wasn’t in Seoul.
He was standing outside the door.
The price of realizing it too late was about to be paid.
*Crash!*
With a thunderous boom, the centuries-old office door burst into dust.
A massive man with graying hair strode through the opening and gave the frozen president a friendly smile.
“Long time no see, Emmanuel. You little rat—I could tear you apart and kill you, and it still wouldn’t be enough.”
“You—you’re...”

“Funny, isn’t it? A moment ago, I thought I could fall asleep in three seconds. But looking at your face has driven the tiredness right out of me. Johnson, who should be in Switzerland right now, probably feels the same way. Don’t you think?”
Chuck Hagel laughed heartily.
He shoved Huginn’s smartphone into his back pocket, then spoke to Emmanuel, who stood frozen like a statue. His voice was different now, deep and dark as an abyss.
“Michael Silbert is dead. By the hand of the new Alliance Leader we chose ourselves, in the name of the World Hunter Federation.”
“Now it’s your choice. Get dragged out with your arms and legs broken, or walk out on those cotton-swab legs of yours.”
It was over. All of it was over.
Everything he’d built, along with every future he could have had, had collapsed.
Faced with a reality he couldn’t believe, he trembled, forgetting even to breathe. After turning it over in his mind again and again, he finally managed a word.
“C-cigar.”
“What?”
“Could I smoke one cigar before I go?”
Chuck Hagel blinked, then let out a booming laugh.
“A cigar? Now that sounds good.”
Then he drove a fist like a lump of iron straight into Emmanuel’s face.
*Wham! Crash!*
Teeth and blood sprayed through the air. Emmanuel flew back like a cannonball, shattered the window, and disappeared from sight.
“Asshole. What kind of question was that?”
Chuck muttered and looked down through the broken window.
Dozens of Ares Guild members waiting below were pouring potions over the president who had fallen from the sky.
“Is he alive?”
“Ah, yes. He’ll live.”
“Good. Just keep him breathing.”
“Understood. But, Mr. Hagel, where are we headed next?”
“Don’t worry about that. Our mission is over.”
“So we’re heading straight back?”
“No. Wait a little. There’s still something to do.”
Chuck opened the cigar box sitting neatly on the table and smiled with satisfaction.
“Something very important. Mm.”
A little while later, people drawn by the unexpected commotion saw their president being carried away, his body crushed, and pale smoke drifting out through the Élysée Palace’s broken window.
But that was not the last shock awaiting them.
When they picked up their smartphones to report this unprecedented crime, an enormous bomb no one could have foreseen rocked the world.

**Breaking News:** World Hunter Federation’s first official announcement: “Two hours ago, we summarily executed Michael Silbert and his followers, who betrayed humanity. The operation is still ongoing.” **Unprecedented bloodshed.** Choi, descendant of the Savior and interim spokesperson for the World Hunter Federation: “We will reveal the truth, along with all the evidence.” **[Live] World Hunter Federation Official Press Conference**
The press conference began amid confusion and shock on a scale that “unprecedented” could hardly capture.

And even as Choi Minwoo calmly continued speaking before everyone, captured by hundreds of camera lenses, the key figures of the New World Hunter Federation spread across the globe like dandelion seeds on the wind, uprooting the weeds Michael Silbert had left behind.
One day. Two days. Three...
They were still at it on the day a young man finally woke from his deep sleep.

At those words from Michael Silbert, Emmanuel—now a senator who embodied Paris and the leader of the largest party in parliament—had a sudden certainty.
The election was over before it had even begun.
He would be the next master of the Élysée Palace.
And at last, on the day that prediction came true, President Emmanuel mustered the courage to ask the benefactor who had come to see him:
“Why did you choose me, of all people?”
The answer was brief.
“You listened well.”
“Pardon?”
“I want only one thing.
Give me your absolute loyalty, just as you have until now.
If I tell you to bark, bark.
If I tell you to bite, bite.
Don’t repeat your predecessor’s mistake, and I’ll put not only enormous wealth and honor in your hands, but this entire country.”
“Will you be loyal to me?”
“No.
I’ll obey you.”
Michael Silbert laughed aloud at that perfect answer and handed his new watchdog a box of cigars decorated with gold leaf.
“These are...”
“A gift.
When my goal is realized, you’ll be as good as a king.
Save these cigars for that moment.”
The memory of that day was still vivid.
As President Emmanuel gazed at the box and sank into thought, he felt his heart pound.
*A king.
A king.*
A king in the twenty-first century—in this country obsessed with revolution, no less.
It was madness.
But when Michael Silbert said it, that was different.
He was a man who had made countless impossibilities and wild imaginings come true.
President Emmanuel suddenly recalled the last words of his father, who had used the chaos of the Great Cataclysm to amass an astronomical fortune almost overnight.
“Everything that happens in this world is an investment and a deal.
If someone wants something, give it to them freely.
But always get back more than you gave.”
People had despised his father, calling him the “Merchant of Death.” But even if he had gone to hell, he probably had no great regrets.
He must have watched his son make a better deal than anyone.
Young lawyer Emmanuel had given one man a loyalty bordering on obedience, and in return had become President Emmanuel.
Soon, he would possess power beyond the presidency—power so absolute that Emmanuel the First would hardly be too grand a name for him.
“Emmanuel the First...”
President Emmanuel murmured dreamily.
Then the grandfather clock against the office wall chimed.
*Dong.
Dooong.*
A bird and a dwarf popped out of the clock and spun around.
Emmanuel checked where the hour hand pointed and blinked.
“Noon?
Already?”
He must have lost track of time while reminiscing.
He slowly tapped his desk.
*It’s taking longer than I expected.*
With the time difference between France and Korea, it was now eight in the evening in Seoul, where the World Hunter Federation’s inaugural ceremony would be underway.
He checked his smartphone just in case, but no word had come from the person he was waiting for.
*Well, it would be strange if it ended early.*
This wasn’t just any gathering.
It was the World Hunter Federation’s first inaugural ceremony.
Given its importance to the future of global security, a meeting as long as a full marathon was hardly surprising.
Still, even with his unwavering faith in Michael Silbert, he couldn’t help feeling a little anxious.
*Knock, knock.*
President Emmanuel frowned at the sudden knock.
“What is it?”
An attendant’s voice came through the crack in the closed door.
“It’s time for your meal, Mr.
President.”
“I don’t need it.
And don’t let anyone near my office until I call for them myself.
Understood?”
“Yes, I’ll pass that along.”
How could he have an appetite with the most important moment of his life just ahead?
President Emmanuel cursed inwardly at his dim-witted attendant, then stared down at the smartphone in his hand.
After hesitating, he tapped one person’s number.
*Brr.
Brr.
Brr.*
The call rang on and on.
Emmanuel ran his hand over the cigar box, trying to suppress his anxiety.
At last, there was a click, and someone answered.
“The ceremony—how did the inaugural ceremony go?”
The other person was silent for a moment before replying.
“It ended successfully.”
The words he’d waited so long to hear.
Joy surged through Emmanuel, and he burst out laughing.
He punched the air without realizing he’d clenched his fist and thanked the man who had given him the answer he wanted so badly.
“Thank you!
Thank you so much!
Huginn, you’ve worked so hard, too—!”
“Thank me?
I’m the one who should be thanking you.”
“What?”
At that moment, Emmanuel realized something.
The voice on the other end was deeper and rougher than usual.
And its owner wasn’t in Seoul.
He was standing outside the door.
The price of realizing it too late was about to be paid.
*Crash!*
With a thunderous boom, the centuries-old office door burst into dust.
A massive man with graying hair strode through the opening and gave the frozen president a friendly smile.
“Long time no see, Emmanuel.
You little rat—I could tear you apart and kill you, and it still wouldn’t be enough.”
“You—you’re...”
“Funny, isn’t it?
A moment ago, I thought I could fall asleep in three seconds.
But looking at your face has driven the tiredness right out of me.
Johnson, who should be in Switzerland right now, probably feels the same way.
Don’t you think?”
Chuck Hagel laughed heartily.
He shoved Huginn’s smartphone into his back pocket, then spoke to Emmanuel, who stood frozen like a statue.
His voice was different now, deep and dark as an abyss.
“Michael Silbert is dead.
By the hand of the new Alliance Leader we chose ourselves, in the name of the World Hunter Federation.”
“Now it’s your choice.
Get dragged out with your arms and legs broken, or walk out on those cotton-swab legs of yours.”
It was over.
All of it was over.
Everything he’d built, along with every future he could have had, had collapsed.
Faced with a reality he couldn’t believe, he trembled, forgetting even to breathe.
After turning it over in his mind again and again, he finally managed a word.
“C-cigar.”
“What?”
“Could I smoke one cigar before I go?”
Chuck Hagel blinked, then let out a booming laugh.
“A cigar?
Now that sounds good.”
Then he drove a fist like a lump of iron straight into Emmanuel’s face.
*Wham!
Crash!*
Teeth and blood sprayed through the air.
Emmanuel flew back like a cannonball, shattered the window, and disappeared from sight.
“Asshole.
What kind of question was that?”
Chuck muttered and looked down through the broken window.
Dozens of Ares Guild members waiting below were pouring potions over the president who had fallen from the sky.
“Is he alive?”
“Ah, yes.
He’ll live.”
“Good.
Just keep him breathing.”
“Understood.
But, Mr.
Hagel, where are we headed next?”
“Don’t worry about that.
Our mission is over.”
“So we’re heading straight back?”
“No.
Wait a little.
There’s still something to do.”
Chuck opened the cigar box sitting neatly on the table and smiled with satisfaction.
“Something very important.
Mm.”
A little while later, people drawn by the unexpected commotion saw their president being carried away, his body crushed, and pale smoke drifting out through the Élysée Palace’s broken window.
But that was not the last shock awaiting them.
When they picked up their smartphones to report this unprecedented crime, an enormous bomb no one could have foreseen rocked the world.
**Breaking News:** World Hunter Federation’s first official announcement: “Two hours ago, we summarily executed Michael Silbert and his followers, who betrayed humanity.

The operation is still ongoing.” **Unprecedented bloodshed.** Choi, descendant of the Savior and interim spokesperson for the World Hunter Federation: “We will reveal the truth, along with all the evidence.” **[Live] World Hunter Federation Official Press Conference**
The press conference began amid confusion and shock on a scale that “unprecedented” could hardly capture.

And even as Choi Minwoo calmly continued speaking before everyone, captured by hundreds of camera lenses, the key figures of the New World Hunter Federation spread across the globe like dandelion seeds on the wind, uprooting the weeds Michael Silbert had left behind.
One day.
Two days.
Three...
They were still at it on the day a young man finally woke from his deep sleep.

chapters.title: Chapter 789
paragraphs: It must have started a few years ago.
Before that, I could close my eyes anywhere, anytime, and fall asleep as if I’d passed out. Then the nightmares began.
In a way, it was only natural.
Even someone as thick-skinned as me would start to fall apart after crossing the line between life and death several times a week and watching people close to me die or get hurt.
This nightmare was no different.
But it was far calmer, sadder, and, in a way, even more welcome than the ones I usually had. Because I met people I missed inside it.
“Son. While Dad’s at work, play nicely with Hayeon, okay?”
I heard my father’s voice.
“Just call me hyung. Hyung.”
“Whoa, we hit the jackpot with these Magic Gems today. Since we’re on a roll, let’s keep going till the end of the day, yeah?”
I saw the smiling faces of Cheonsu and the other team members who’d died in the Mutated Gate.
“It wasn’t your fault. You did everything you could.”
I got to stand beside Butler Kim once more as he struggled for breath and tried to comfort me.
Of course, if it had ended there, I wouldn’t have called it a nightmare.
Even in my dream, I fought without stopping.
I cut down people who all looked the same and drove my spearhead into monsters’ chests.
Then, amid blood that reached my thighs and corpses piled like mountains, I heard the screams of those I hadn’t managed to save.
“Help me! There are people here! Please, at least save my child...”
I looked around. A hellscape stretched out on every side.
No—maybe it was hell itself.
A familiar face came into view, one more at home here than anyone else.
“This is a pleasant place, wouldn’t you say?”
“Go fuck yourself.”
I swung my spear as I answered.
*Slash.*
Michael Silbert’s head flew into the air as he approached at a leisurely pace.
But the smile on his lips and the black gleam in his eyes didn’t disappear.
“Take a good look at this scene we made together.”
His headless body moved of its own accord.
*Clap. Clap. Clap.* The slow applause rang out, and I clenched my teeth. Flames erupted from my spear as I slashed diagonally downward, swallowing him whole.
*Whoosh!*
Michael Silbert’s body, moving as though controlled by invisible strings, turned to ash and crumbled away.
But the flames weren’t satisfied. They raced over the blood pooled everywhere.
Farther. On and on.
*Fwoosh.*
A great inferno rose, feeding on the blood and countless corpses like firewood, completing the hellscape.
The screams of those still alive rose higher than ever—then died away without a trace.
Everything was dead. Everything was burning.
The terrible sight before me was something beyond a dream.
I let my spear droop and stared blankly as the whole world went up in flames.
Then I heard a monster who had stubbornly survived even this calamity begin to speak.
“Please, survive until the end. Struggle with everything you have, every moment, until the very end of this world. That way, you can watch it all with your own eyes—”
*Pop! Thud-thud.*
I stomped down with all my strength, and his head burst like a watermelon.
But the silence I’d finally won wasn’t an ending. It was the beginning of something new.
*Crack. Crack.*
The world shook with a deafening roar.
The sky split apart, and space warped in every direction.
At the same time, a single word flashed through my mind like a bolt of lightning.
*Rift.*
*Rrrumble!*
That was when it happened.
As my senses slowly faded, someone’s distant shout caught hold of me and pulled me up from the depths of the nightmare.
*Ppa?*
“Oppa!”
At that moment, radiant light filled my vision. I woke from the nightmare and finally saw Hayeon’s face, drenched in tears for some reason.
After a brief but difficult deliberation, I greeted her with all sincerity.
“Don’t cry. You’re ugly enough as it is. If your makeup runs, it’ll only get worse...”
*Smack!*
Ow.
I hurt, therefore I am.
I couldn’t tell how the rest of that day passed.
Right after I woke up, Hayeon—having been hit with the hard truth—smacked my arm with a hand that stung just like Mom’s.
Then she hugged me for the first time since kindergarten and burst into tears.
Mom had stepped away for a moment. When she came hurrying back... Well, there’s no point going on. It’ll only make my mouth tired.
She sobbed so bitterly that I thought I’d woken up in a morgue instead of a hospital room.
If the medical staff who’d been waiting nearby hadn’t insisted she stop, I might have drowned in their tears. I’m only exaggerating a little.
“Um, could the family calm down for a moment? We need to run some tests first...”
Mom wouldn’t have budged even if Demon King Asmodeus had come knocking—but a few words from a renowned doctor and healer were enough to make her step back without a fuss.
Of course, she made sure to clasp their hands and ask them again and again to look after me.

“Please take good care of my son. Check if anything’s wrong with him. And there won’t be any lasting effects, will there? My younger one said Taekyung started talking nonsense as soon as he woke up...”
“Nonsense?”
“Yes. I’m not sure exactly what he said. I’d stepped out for a moment.”
“Understood. Patient, do you remember what you said?”
I answered.
“I told her not to cry because she’d look even uglier if her makeup ran.”
“And it wasn’t nonsense. I almost closed my eyes again as soon as I opened them.”
“You may not know this, but once she takes off that makeup, it’s a disaster. You don’t have to go looking far for a Monster Wave.”
Hayeon glared at me as if she wanted to kill me. The medical staff listened with their mouths hanging open, then gathered in a corner of the room and started whispering.
“Is he all right?”
“Does he look all right to you?”
“Hard to say. His younger sister looks pretty, at least. Her makeup’s waterproof, so I don’t think it ran...”
“I can’t believe this. Is that what you’re worried about right now? Are you in your right mind? Who recommended you for this job?”
“I did. Sorry.”
“I’m sorry, Professor. What should we do?”
“Hmm. There doesn’t seem to be anything obviously wrong with his body, but the aftereffects could have affected his brain. Let’s run a full set of tests.”
“Yes. We’ll include a psychiatric evaluation.”
I’d told the truth, and they were treating me like a lunatic.
It was unfair, but there was nothing I could do. The fastest way to stop Mom from crying was to show her I was healthy.
*Like I’d be sick.*
But I swallowed that thought and cooperated with the healers and doctors.
Even after they’d put me through every test known to this world, I was forced to rest until the following day.
Two days.
It wasn’t a bad stretch.
Honestly, it was peaceful for once.
I was stuck in bed for two whole days without a smartphone or TV, all in the name of rest. But the people I cared about most were right there with me.
I ate, slept, laughed, and talked with my family. It felt like a dream.
If not for the nightmare I’d had just before waking up, those days would have been so happy I wouldn’t have felt a hint of anxiety.
But I already knew I couldn’t make them last any longer.
If I wanted to quiet the unease growing inside me, it was time to step back out into the world.
Mom and Hayeon. The medical staff. And all the friends who didn’t come to visit because they wanted me to rest.
They might have kept quiet about what was happening outside for my sake, but the System hadn’t.
*Alliance Leader, huh?*

The System notifications I hadn’t had a chance to check told me what had happened. Right after I’d finished Michael Silbert off for good, the World Hunter Federation had appointed me its new Alliance Leader while I was unconscious.
*Never thought I’d end up as Alliance Leader, of all things.*
I was surprised at first, but after thinking it over, I decided to accept.
It was their decision, but it was mine too.
I’d seen more than once what someone’s ambition—what a hunger for power—could lead to.

Team Leader Choi or Magic Johnson would make a leader several times better than me. But if I was the one they’d chosen, I was willing to live up to their expectations, even if I still had a lot to learn.
*I’ll do the best I can.*
Before that, though, there was one thing I had to take care of.
“Hayeon.”
“Yeah?”
“You know Team Leader Choi’s number, right?”
“No. Rest.”
Her answer was immediate and firm.
Hayeon continued, her face set.
“Mom would be thrilled to hear that. Right?”
“Call him for me.”
“There’s something I need to take care of. Please.”
At my earnest request, Hayeon bit her lip.
“Ugh, this is driving me crazy.”
“Thanks.”
“Are you crazy? Who said I’d call him for you?”
“You always bite your lip before agreeing to do me a favor.”
Hayeon stared at me without a word, then let out a deep sigh.
That meant yes.
“The wind’s cold.”
That was the first thing Team Leader Choi said when I saw him after several days.
I was sitting alone on a bench. Glad to see him, I broke into a grin.
“How long has it been?”
“Today makes exactly one week since that day.”
“Must’ve been a busy week. In more ways than one.”
Team Leader Choi smiled back and joked, “Yes. While you were lying comfortably in bed, we were running around like mad.”
“You make me feel bad. Should I apologize?”
“No need. It’s one of the boss’s privileges. Though the press is desperate to find out how you’re doing.”
“Fair enough. They made a fuss last time, too. Now I’ve even got the title of Alliance Leader.”
Team Leader Choi paused at my calm response.
“You knew?”
“Yes.”
“That’s not quite the reaction I expected. Did your family tell you?”
“No. They wouldn’t even let me lift a finger.”
“Hmm. I wonder where the news leaked from. I told everyone to keep quiet so you could rest.”
“Who knows? I’ve got sources you don’t know about, too.”
Team Leader Choi studied me for a moment, then nodded without saying anything.
The gesture said he wouldn’t ask any more.
He already suspected I had secrets other people didn’t know about. To him, why I’d contacted him only two days after waking was probably the more important question.
“Things outside are going smoothly, despite what you may think. You could rest a little longer.”
“Is that so?”
“Yes. A week ago, we arrested a number of key figures with close ties to Michael Silbert. Among them...”
He rattled off names: French President Emmanuel, Swiss Interior Minister Werner, who was almost certain to become the next president, and the head of a massive corporation.
Every one of them was a heavyweight who held sway over politics and business around the world.
There were few Hunters among them. The ones who could have been called their leaders had either died alongside Michael Silbert that day or been captured.
“It was a bold and excellent decision. If you’d spared them, a much larger civil war would have broken out.”
Yes. That was exactly why we couldn’t let the bastards live.
The battle at the National Assembly had been a bloody bargain: their lives in exchange for tens, perhaps hundreds, of thousands of others.
But Team Leader Choi still hadn’t mentioned the one being I wanted to know about.
What had happened to the one person I was worried about. The source of this unease.
“Team Leader Choi.”
I looked up at the night sky, thick with stars. No—I looked at the information for the Main Quest, *Cataclysm*, still hanging there, and continued.
“Where is The Prophet?”

“Who knows?
I’ve got sources you don’t know about, too.”
Team Leader Choi studied me for a moment, then nodded without saying anything.
The gesture said he wouldn’t ask any more.
He already suspected I had secrets other people didn’t know about.
To him, why I’d contacted him only two days after waking was probably the more important question.
“Things outside are going smoothly, despite what you may think.
You could rest a little longer.”
“Is that so?”
“Yes.
A week ago, we arrested a number of key figures with close ties to Michael Silbert.
Among them...”
He rattled off names: French President Emmanuel, Swiss Interior Minister Werner, who was almost certain to become the next president, and the head of a massive corporation.
Every one of them was a heavyweight who held sway over politics and business around the world.
There were few Hunters among them.
The ones who could have been called their leaders had either died alongside Michael Silbert that day or been captured.
“It was a bold and excellent decision.
If you’d spared them, a much larger civil war would have broken out.”
Yes.
That was exactly why we couldn’t let the bastards live.
The battle at the National Assembly had been a bloody bargain: their lives in exchange for tens, perhaps hundreds, of thousands of others.
But Team Leader Choi still hadn’t mentioned the one being I wanted to know about.
What had happened to the one person I was worried about.
The source of this unease.
“Team Leader Choi.”
I looked up at the night sky, thick with stars.
No—I looked at the information for the Main Quest, *Cataclysm*, still hanging there, and continued.
“Where is The Prophet?”

paragraphs: “Where is The Prophet?”
At that single question, the smile on Team Leader Choi’s lips faded.
Not *What happened to him?* but *Where is he?*
A man with a keen mind, he immediately grasped the simple but clear distinction. And I already knew what the brief silence meant.
“You still haven’t found him.”
Team Leader Choi watched me with a grave expression, then nodded.
“That’s right.”
“You don’t even know where he is?”
Team Leader Choi didn’t answer. Silence was as good as a yes.
*Damn it.*
I swallowed the curse and looked up at the night sky.
Just because you’re in the same place doesn’t mean you’re all looking in the same direction.
Just like Team Leader Choi and I were looking at different scenery at that very moment.

**System Quest Cataclysm** A new era has drawn near, and the final word of this long and fierce story has yet to be written. Hope. Or despair. And at this very moment, you are the only one holding the pen. May good fortune in battle be with you. **Grade:** Main Quest **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung **Mission:** ??? **Reward:** ??? **Failure:** ???
I stared at the holographic window covered in question marks and muttered to myself.
*The Quest still isn’t complete...*
That could only mean one thing.
The being those question marks stood for had never been Michael Silbert.
*Why? Why the hell?*
I hadn’t seen this coming. I’d been certain that eliminating Michael Silbert was the only way to complete the Quest and stop the coming Cataclysm.
But I’d been wrong. Completely wrong.
*The Prophet.*
That deranged fanatic who called himself God’s messenger and a prophet—the terrorist I’d taken for a lackey following Michael Silbert’s orders—was the real key to this Main Quest.
Or...
He was where the coming Cataclysm would begin.
*Ding.*

**System** Information for the Main Quest, **Cataclysm**, has been updated. The mission has changed in accordance with your realization. **Mission:** Eliminate **The Prophet** within the time limit (Incomplete).
New holographic windows filled my vision. At the same moment, I understood.
The clock on the bomb called Cataclysm, the one that would soon shake the world, was ticking even now.
These days, even “global village” sounded outdated.
More happened across the world in a single day than anyone could keep track of. People had grown used to seeing one shocking story after another on TV and the internet, then promptly forgetting them.
But what had happened a week ago had shaken even them.

Across the world, Hunters had launched armed crackdowns and arrests, sudden as land mines going off. Those caught up in them included high-ranking politicians—even presidents—some of the world’s wealthiest people, and Hunters.
Every one of them was a heavyweight with influence over global politics, business, and security—not merely a particular region or country.
People waiting for the new World Hunter Federation’s inaugural ceremony were thrown into confusion. Soon, confusion gave way to shock.
“The whole truth is in here.”
Choi Minwoo stood before the cameras as interim spokesperson, holding a microchip smaller than a fingernail.
Of all the many cameras installed throughout the National Assembly to capture a moment in history, it was the only one to survive the aftermath of the tremendous battle.
It was also a Pandora’s box, containing a truth no one could bear to face.
The footage ran for just over three hours. But once it was uploaded to a streaming site where the whole world could watch, it plunged the world into a pit of silence.
Choi Minwoo had told the truth. Everything was there.
No edits. No lies.
Only facts, plain and undeniable.
Billions of people were confronted with an unbelievable truth—and, within the Pandora’s box that had suddenly opened, they discovered something still left inside.
Hope.

The Prophet will die soon, just like bin Laden, and then we’ll finally have real peace. └ Jin. Please wake up soon. We’re waiting for our hero.

A week was nowhere near enough time for the world to recover from the shock. Even so, humanity was quickly finding its footing again, sustained by faith in the World Hunter Federation and hope that things would get better.
But somewhere beyond their sight, something new was already stirring.
Or perhaps a fire was starting—one that would swallow the world.
“Concentrate every force we can mobilize in the Middle East. Right now.”
Choi Minwoo relayed Jin Taekyung’s words straight to the World Hunter Federation’s leadership. No one questioned them.
This wasn’t a request. It was an order.
The first order from the Alliance Leader they had chosen.
And there had never been any doubt about their answer.
“Yes, boss.”
The World Hunter Federation began to move.
“They’re coming.”
A trembling voice echoed through the cave.
The Prophet silently looked down at the man prostrate at their feet, then spoke.
“What is their estimated strength?”
“Th-that...”
“Answer.”
The man hesitated, then pressed his head to the ground.
“We estimate at least a hundred thousand.”
A hundred thousand.
The staggering number, far beyond what they had expected, froze the already chilly air in the cave.
Everyone gathered there knew those hundred thousand weren’t ordinary infantry.
*The World Hunter Federation.*
Hunters were rare, whatever their rank. Only one person in a thousand had the chance to awaken, and even then, they had to undergo specific training before they could be recognized as a Hunter.
But their enemy was the World Hunter Federation.

True to its name, every Hunter in the world belonged to that vast organization. From humanity’s billions, millions had beaten the 0.1 percent odds and been chosen by God. Now they were bearing down on the desert.
No—the whole world was coming.
“The entire desert is under surveillance.”
“We’ve lost contact with our informants planted in the Pentagon.”
“The residents of nearby villages and small towns are being evacuated.”
“We have reports that the United States has moved an aircraft carrier...”
Their growing fear spilled into their voices. For a long while, they poured out everything they had learned. The situation was already hurtling toward the worst possible outcome.
A week ago, Michael Silbert’s unexpected death had marked the beginning of their downfall.

The newly formed World Hunter Federation had moved boldly, without hesitation. It had begun by bathing its inaugural ceremony in blood, then set about gathering up the seeds Michael Silbert had sown. By revealing the whole truth without hiding or embellishing a thing, it had won support across the world.
Pure goodwill.

Nothing could stop the hammer the World Hunter Federation had brought down. A nation’s president, the head of a corporation powerful enough to sway the world’s stock markets—they had all fallen, bleeding.

Half a century ago, after Osama bin Laden’s terrorist attack, Pakistan and other Middle Eastern countries had refused to let the United States cross their airspace. Even they would not dare oppose this operation.
They could hardly do something as insane as make enemies of the World Hunter Federation and the entire world. If they did, they would be met with artillery fire and a great many Hunters.
But unlike those who could choose to compromise, the people gathered in this cave had no choice at all.
“Prophet!”
“Please, please show us the way we must go!”
Desperate cries rang out from all sides.
Armed with fanaticism, they all knelt and prostrated themselves before one person alone.

They feared the enemy closing in. But they also held fast to their faith in the path they had walked: offering their lives to God, following the prophet He had sent, and witnessing the astounding miracles the Prophet had shown them.
“Teach these lost servants!”
“Defeat these infidels and proclaim God’s will to the whole world!”
*Fwoosh. Fwoosh.*
The torches lighting the cave flickered in the wind. From beneath the Prophet’s deeply drawn hood came a voice whose age and gender no one could place.
“As you wish, I shall carry out God’s will and punish them. Inshallah.”
“God is great!”
“Inshallah. Inshallah!”
The anxiety that had threatened to burst gave way to cheers. As they cried out about God’s greatness and bowed again and again, the Prophet watched them and thought:
The long wait would soon bear fruit.

chapters.title: Chapter 791
paragraphs: As far as I knew, the Middle East mattered more to the world than most people realized.
Depending on how you defined it, it stretched from Western Asia to the countries of North Africa.
And since the Great Cataclysm, active resettlement policies had pushed its population past a staggering three hundred million.
That wasn’t all.
The oil fields that had sustained the region were still doing their part, while Gates scattered throughout the area yielded Magic Gems—a resource that had rapidly overtaken oil in importance.
*Of course, half the Magic Gems obtained that way probably disappear through back channels.*
That was just how things worked around there.
There were no powerful civic groups or government agencies to investigate corruption, so even when resources came in, plenty leaked out the back.
In the Middle East, royal families held virtually unlimited wealth and power. Terrorist groups operated openly, and hypocrites who’d started as revolutionary leaders had evolved into dictators.
To them, the law was gum they could spit out whenever the flavor was gone.
*Michael Silbert knew exactly how to exploit that.*
Smuggling Magic Gems and leaving them unrefined were grave crimes under international law, but there were plenty of loopholes.
Especially in the Middle East and Africa, where terrorist groups and rebels were everywhere.
But a man who was already dead was no longer the problem.
*It’s the one who’s still alive.*
*Tap.*
I set down the tablet and rubbed my eyes. Staring at text for hours had worn me out.
Or maybe it was those three syllables I couldn’t get out of my head.
*The Prophet.*
Thinking of someone whose face I didn’t even know, I gazed out the window.
As the plane’s wing cut across the cloud-choked sky and rain poured down, the voice I’d heard on TV seemed to rumble like thunder.
“Following God’s will, we will not stop. Starting today, we will judge and punish you.”
Who was that bastard?
Even though the voice hadn’t been altered, I couldn’t make out their gender or age. Their face was hidden, too, beneath a hood pulled down low.
*Did they cover up so carefully because people would recognize their face?*
Probably, but even that wasn’t certain. The Prophet was as hard to make out as the storm clouds outside the window.
“The weather’s bad.”
A voice spoke beside me. Still looking out the window, I answered.
“It sure is. Doesn’t look like good flying weather at all.”
“It’s worse than that. This is about as bad as it gets.”
“Think The Prophet planted a mole at the weather service?”
“What makes you think that?”
“What do you mean? It’s the perfect setup for an assassination.”
Team Leader Choi dropped into the seat beside me.
“I can tell you two things. First, the airport forecast was accurate. This is just a change in the weather caused by magical power. Second, if I were The Prophet, I wouldn’t waste my time.”
“Why not?”
“Even if this plane crashed, you would survive, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Wouldn’t you?”
“Who knows? I’ve never been in a plane crash.”
Even that was a ridiculous answer. A crash from this height, in weather like this, should obviously be fatal.
Team Leader Choi seemed to think so too. He shook his head, then glanced at the tablet on the table.
“Have you read it all?”
“Yes. Enough times to be sick of it.”
Some material had been added, but about half of it was already painfully familiar.
Before the World Hunter Federation was founded, I’d spent several nights reading those same documents over and over.
They concerned Michael Silbert, so naturally they covered The Prophet and the Middle East too.
“What do you make of them?”
“Hard to say. I can tell you at least three things.”
I glared at the tablet, crammed with text.
“The Middle East is damn huge, so finding The Prophet quickly will be tough. And that bastard is damn good at hiding.”
“And the third?”
“That fucking bastard has an enormous amount of unrefined Magic Gems.”
Right. That was the problem.
The Prophet had launched indiscriminate terrorist attacks around the world, then gone quiet after Michael Silbert’s death. The public figured they’d gotten scared and was starting to relax.
But that only made me more uneasy.
This mood. This calm before the storm.
*They’re planning something bigger. I’m sure of it.*
I’d been given a Main Quest unlike any before, one important enough for the System to name it *Cataclysm*.
That was why I’d mobilized the World Hunter Federation immediately.
Even after setting aside the personnel needed to prevent further terrorist attacks and monster waves, we’d sent a full hundred thousand troops to the Middle East.
Every one of them was a Hunter. That made for an enormous force.
Even Korea, recognized worldwide as a Hunter powerhouse, couldn’t mobilize that many Hunters, regardless of their individual levels.
Some people had murmured that we were deploying far too many troops right from the start, but that nonsense died as quickly as it started.
That was how much authority and power the World Hunter Federation held now.
The UN General Assembly, representing nearly every country on Earth, had given its approval. All of humanity supported us.
If the United States had *called itself* the world’s police, the World Hunter Federation was recognized as such by everyone—and untouchable.
Even Russia, which had clashed constantly with the Western powers led by the United States, had promised to cooperate fully with the Federation and warned the Middle Eastern countries that objected.
—If you don’t want to die, clear a path.
The diplomatic cable was long, but that was the gist.

Vladimir Furin, Russia’s president for life, was deeply upset that a terrorist attack had destroyed Red Square. He’d also been itching to settle the score with several Middle Eastern countries that had sided with Michael Silbert at the recent UN General Assembly.
So what choice did they have?
The Middle Eastern leaders hadn’t been thrilled at the prospect of a hundred thousand Hunters showing up, but within a few hours they’d thrown open their airspace and territorial waters.
International condemnation was one thing. They might also find themselves drinking radioactive tea one sunny morning.
But the whole world’s cooperation wouldn’t make The Prophet fall into our hands on its own.
“How far has the search gotten?”
Team Leader Choi answered at once.
“Everyone is doing their best, but so far, no one has found anything unusual. The area is vast, and it’s only been a day since the search began.”
I knew. That was one of the main reasons I was heading to the Middle East myself.
Even so, I couldn’t help asking again, even if it was premature.
“How long do you expect it to take?”
“In the worst case, more than sixty days. That estimate assumes we mobilize every Federation Hunter and all the allied forces that joined afterward.”
“...Sixty days.”
“Again, that’s only the worst case. If we put everything we have into it, we may well finish sooner.”
Would we, though?
I said nothing, but unease stirred inside me.
*They’re not going to be easy to deal with.*
The Prophet had evaded surveillance around the world even before the Federation was founded.
The worst terrorist in history, far beyond the South American drug lords or even his much older predecessor, Osama bin Laden.
Some people might have thought it was amazing we could catch someone like that within two months...
I wasn’t.
*Two months is too late.*
If my guess was right, The Prophet had an enormous quantity of Magic Gems. Unrefined, and therefore all the more dangerous—a ticking time bomb.
No one knew when it would go off.
In a month. In two weeks. Or...
*It could be tomorrow.*
And when that bomb went off, the Cataclysm named in my Main Quest would begin. It wasn’t hard to imagine.
If that happened, a disaster on par with—no, possibly even worse than—the terrorist attacks The Prophet had carried out so far would sweep across the world.
“It’s your turn now. Let’s see you struggle with everything you’ve got. I’ll be watching from up there.”
A voice suddenly echoed in my ears.
Now I understood what Michael Silbert’s last words had really meant.
But just as I’d sent that bastard, who’d seemed impossible to stop, plunging into the depths of hell, I was ready to fight again.
And I had a suspicion that was close to certainty.
*The Prophet isn’t ready yet, either.*
A hungry person wouldn’t hold back with a delicious meal right in front of them.
The Prophet probably hadn’t finished preparing to set off the bomb. They were lying low, holding their breath so they wouldn’t be found before the cooking was done.
*I have to find them before that happens. No matter what.*
I looked at Team Leader Choi.
“What about the cargo? Is it behaving?”
“The cargo? Oh.”

sentences.text: As far as I knew, the Middle East mattered more to the world than most people realized.
Depending on how you defined it, it stretched from Western Asia to the countries of North Africa.
And since the Great Cataclysm, active resettlement policies had pushed its population past a staggering three hundred million.
That wasn’t all.
The oil fields that had sustained the region were still doing their part, while Gates scattered throughout the area yielded Magic Gems—a resource that had rapidly overtaken oil in importance.
*Of course, half the Magic Gems obtained that way probably disappear through back channels.*
That was just how things worked around there.
There were no powerful civic groups or government agencies to investigate corruption, so even when resources came in, plenty leaked out the back.
In the Middle East, royal families held virtually unlimited wealth and power.
Terrorist groups operated openly, and hypocrites who’d started as revolutionary leaders had evolved into dictators.
To them, the law was gum they could spit out whenever the flavor was gone.
*Michael Silbert knew exactly how to exploit that.*
Smuggling Magic Gems and leaving them unrefined were grave crimes under international law, but there were plenty of loopholes.
Especially in the Middle East and Africa, where terrorist groups and rebels were everywhere.
But a man who was already dead was no longer the problem.
*It’s the one who’s still alive.*
*Tap.*
I set down the tablet and rubbed my eyes.
Staring at text for hours had worn me out.
Or maybe it was those three syllables I couldn’t get out of my head.
*The Prophet.*
Thinking of someone whose face I didn’t even know, I gazed out the window.
As the plane’s wing cut across the cloud-choked sky and rain poured down, the voice I’d heard on TV seemed to rumble like thunder.
“Following God’s will, we will not stop.
Starting today, we will judge and punish you.”
Who was that bastard?
Even though the voice hadn’t been altered, I couldn’t make out their gender or age.
Their face was hidden, too, beneath a hood pulled down low.
*Did they cover up so carefully because people would recognize their face?*
Probably, but even that wasn’t certain.
The Prophet was as hard to make out as the storm clouds outside the window.
“The weather’s bad.”
A voice spoke beside me.
Still looking out the window, I answered.
“It sure is.
Doesn’t look like good flying weather at all.”
“It’s worse than that.
This is about as bad as it gets.”
“Think The Prophet planted a mole at the weather service?”
“What makes you think that?”
“What do you mean?
It’s the perfect setup for an assassination.”
Team Leader Choi dropped into the seat beside me.
“I can tell you two things.
First, the airport forecast was accurate.
This is just a change in the weather caused by magical power.
Second, if I were The Prophet, I wouldn’t waste my time.”
“Why not?”
“Even if this plane crashed, you would survive, Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
“Wouldn’t you?”
“Who knows?
I’ve never been in a plane crash.”
Even that was a ridiculous answer.
A crash from this height, in weather like this, should obviously be fatal.
Team Leader Choi seemed to think so too.
He shook his head, then glanced at the tablet on the table.
“Have you read it all?”
“Yes.
Enough times to be sick of it.”
Some material had been added, but about half of it was already painfully familiar.
Before the World Hunter Federation was founded, I’d spent several nights reading those same documents over and over.
They concerned Michael Silbert, so naturally they covered The Prophet and the Middle East too.
“What do you make of them?”
“Hard to say.
I can tell you at least three things.”
I glared at the tablet, crammed with text.
“The Middle East is damn huge, so finding The Prophet quickly will be tough.
And that bastard is damn good at hiding.”
“And the third?”
“That fucking bastard has an enormous amount of unrefined Magic Gems.”
Right.
That was the problem.
The Prophet had launched indiscriminate terrorist attacks around the world, then gone quiet after Michael Silbert’s death.
The public figured they’d gotten scared and was starting to relax.
But that only made me more uneasy.
This mood.
This calm before the storm.
*They’re planning something bigger.
I’m sure of it.*
I’d been given a Main Quest unlike any before, one important enough for the System to name it *Cataclysm*.
That was why I’d mobilized the World Hunter Federation immediately.
Even after setting aside the personnel needed to prevent further terrorist attacks and monster waves, we’d sent a full hundred thousand troops to the Middle East.
Every one of them was a Hunter.
That made for an enormous force.
Even Korea, recognized worldwide as a Hunter powerhouse, couldn’t mobilize that many Hunters, regardless of their individual levels.
Some people had murmured that we were deploying far too many troops right from the start, but that nonsense died as quickly as it started.
That was how much authority and power the World Hunter Federation held now.
The UN General Assembly, representing nearly every country on Earth, had given its approval.
All of humanity supported us.
If the United States had *called itself* the world’s police, the World Hunter Federation was recognized as such by everyone—and untouchable.
Even Russia, which had clashed constantly with the Western powers led by the United States, had promised to cooperate fully with the Federation and warned the Middle Eastern countries that objected.
—If you don’t want to die, clear a path.
The diplomatic cable was long, but that was the gist.
Vladimir Furin, Russia’s president for life, was deeply upset that a terrorist attack had destroyed Red Square.
He’d also been itching to settle the score with several Middle Eastern countries that had sided with Michael Silbert at the recent UN General Assembly.
So what choice did they have?
The Middle Eastern leaders hadn’t been thrilled at the prospect of a hundred thousand Hunters showing up, but within a few hours they’d thrown open their airspace and territorial waters.
International condemnation was one thing.
They might also find themselves drinking radioactive tea one sunny morning.
But the whole world’s cooperation wouldn’t make The Prophet fall into our hands on its own.
“How far has the search gotten?”
Team Leader Choi answered at once.
“Everyone is doing their best, but so far, no one has found anything unusual.
The area is vast, and it’s only been a day since the search began.”
I knew.
That was one of the main reasons I was heading to the Middle East myself.
Even so, I couldn’t help asking again, even if it was premature.
“How long do you expect it to take?”
“In the worst case, more than sixty days.
That estimate assumes we mobilize every Federation Hunter and all the allied forces that joined afterward.”
“...Sixty days.”
“Again, that’s only the worst case.
If we put everything we have into it, we may well finish sooner.”
Would we, though?
I said nothing, but unease stirred inside me.
*They’re not going to be easy to deal with.*
The Prophet had evaded surveillance around the world even before the Federation was founded.
The worst terrorist in history, far beyond the South American drug lords or even his much older predecessor, Osama bin Laden.
Some people might have thought it was amazing we could catch someone like that within two months...
I wasn’t.
*Two months is too late.*
If my guess was right, The Prophet had an enormous quantity of Magic Gems.
Unrefined, and therefore all the more dangerous—a ticking time bomb.

In two weeks.

I’ll be watching from up there.”

chapters.title: Chapter 792
paragraphs: “...What’s that?”
Xiao Shen turned at the words but saw nothing unusual. The Skeleton King did.
Even though Magic Johnson’s illusion magic had given him a human appearance, he was fundamentally a monster.
And not just any monster—one of the highest-ranking undead.
The sensation gripping the Skeleton King at that moment was something connected to the very source of his power.
*Damn it. This is...*
There was no doubt.
The feeling was faint, but unmistakable.
Beneath a dark sky that swallowed even the moonlight, he sensed the energy of death scattering across the endless desert.
There wasn’t a single drop of blood or a corpse in sight, but the Skeleton King recognized the energy stirring his instincts from beyond the darkness: death qi.
He knew, too, what had happened to the search squad that had suddenly gone silent about an hour ago.
“Young human brat.”
“Yes?”
“Contact the main force. Tell them we found the search squad.”
The desert was still, without a trace of anyone. But the Skeleton King’s words were the opposite of reassuring.
Xiao Shen finally understood what was happening. His face stiffened as he nodded, and the Skeleton King started walking, following his instincts.
*Crunch. Crunch.*
His feet left prints in the sand, grains crumbling beneath each step.
After about ten paces, he stopped and muttered, “Whoever did this buried them deep.”
The next moment—
*Fwoosh!*
A section of the desert, stretching out like an endless sea, surged into the air.
With a single gesture, the Skeleton King sent out a vast surge of magical power that held the sand aloft. Beneath it lay twenty bodies. At the sight of them, he froze.
A recent memory flashed through his mind, bringing an ominous premonition with it.
*Wait. Then could it be...*
His thoughts went no further. They couldn’t.
*Whoosh.*
A chill wind blew in from somewhere, sweeping sand through the air.
Something else was carried in it.
The Skeleton King stared into a distant stretch of pitch-black desert, then turned to Xiao Shen, who had noticed nothing yet.
“Have you contacted the main force?”
“Yes. They said they’re sending the support team stationed nearby right away...”
“How long?”
“Thirty minutes at most.”
“Thirty minutes. That’s awkward.”
He clicked his tongue.
“I’m not sure I can protect anyone.”
“Hmm.”
He looked Xiao Shen up and down. Then, with a sigh, he said, “Listen, young human brat. I’m giving you two missions.”
“Ah, yes! I’ll do anything you ask, Teacher King.”
“Good attitude. First, take out that damned special radio of yours and contact the main force again.”
“What should I tell them?”
“Send the most capable humans they have, as fast as they can. Not some weak support team riding in on turtles. Got it?”

Xiao Shen didn’t know why recovering the bodies called for such speed or so many capable people, but he nodded without hesitation. The person he respected most in the world was Jin Taekyung, and the Skeleton King was Jin Taekyung’s friend.
“Understood. What’s the second mission?”
Even Xiao Shen had to ask again when he heard the answer.
“Pick up a weapon.”
“What?”
“And protect yourself. If you don’t think you can, you can run.”
“W-wait a second.”
What was that supposed to mean?
Xiao Shen blinked at the baffling order. He understood soon enough.
*Rrrumble. Rrrumble.*
An unfamiliar tremor traveled through the ground. It grew stronger, sending countless grains of sand bouncing into the air all around them.
Then the Skeleton King spoke, turning Xiao Shen’s suspicion into certainty.
“Quite a crowd.”
Xiao Shen didn’t answer. He stood with his mouth open, staring at the distant horizon. In his eyes, the darkness writhed like a living thing.
No. Those were monsters, too many to count.
*Monster Wave...!*
At the moment the words that had become humanity’s nightmare struck Xiao Shen’s mind—
*Crunch.*
The Skeleton King walked toward the rapidly approaching tide of monsters.
There was no fear or hesitation in his steps. Mighty magical power surged from him, reaching farther and farther across the desert.
“In the name of the King, I command you.”
His low voice echoed across the desert. It pierced the thick darkness and roused the spirits crushed beneath the weight of ages and countless grains of sand.
“Answer the call.”
*Rrrumble!*
A tremor like an earthquake swept through the desert.
At their king’s call, steeped in the energy of death, spirits that had lain in deep slumber burst through the sand and rose to the surface.
*Crackle!*
Pale sand scattered. White bones gleamed in the darkness.
*Grrr.*
An Arabian leopard, its beautiful hide lost in death, stretched. Above wolves and hyenas whose eyes shone green, dozens of eagles spread wings stripped down to bone and soared into the air.
*Eeeee!*
Their sharp cries split the night. With wings spanning several meters, the eagles glided high overhead.
They flew past the monster army charging across the ground in a storm of sand, then scattered over the vast desert and woods. They had only one mission:
Find a certain being who wasn’t here, by the King’s command.
“Somewhere in this desert, there’s something with the scent of humans on it. Find it. Without fail.”
The eagles beat their wings vigorously.
They had magical power to carry them on the wind instead of feathers, and though they’d lost the life within them, their vitality would never run dry.
*Whoosh!*
Far below, the King watched the flock disappear into the distance. He thought of the human bodies he had uncovered moments ago, then walked toward the monster army bearing down on him.
*What kind of trace was it?*
*Whoosh—BOOM!*
A vast surge of magical power burst from his outstretched fist and swallowed the monsters at the front. A hundred or so beasts rushed into the gap it left, tearing into the enemy.
*Yowww!*
*Smack!*
A swipe of the leopard’s forepaw sent an Orc’s upper body flying. A pack of hyenas nimbly dodged a club falling toward their heads, then sank their teeth into a Troll’s body.
*Crunch!*
The living monsters outnumbered them beyond comparison.

But as soon as the battle began, the Skeleton King understood. Absorbing part of Michael Silbert’s magical power had strengthened his powers enough to let even these spirits, once mere wild animals, crush ordinary monsters in an instant.
*Splatter! Crunch!*
*Graaaah!*
Blood and flesh flew. The living screamed.
The enemy formation began to crumble in moments.
With a single strike, the Skeleton King knocked the heads off three ogres. Then he looked toward a dark stretch of desert.
He couldn’t see anything, but he knew. Whatever had killed the search squad had already left and vanished somewhere out there.
*What the hell are you?*
The question he asked himself went unanswered. The Skeleton King stared into the darkness with sunken eyes, then raised an ogre lying like a rotten log from the dead.
No—not just the ogre. Everything around him.
“Answer the call.”
*Fwoosh.*
A dazzling golden radiance spread in every direction, so bright it was hard to believe it was magical power.
The undying army, now twice its former size, fell upon the living.
*BOOM!*
*Grrrrr!*
The desert was gradually buried beneath countless screams and death.
Xiao Shen stared blankly at the scene before remembering the mission he’d forgotten.
“Base. Base, respond.”
*Chhh.*

Static hissed from the radio enchanted with communication magic as it sent out a mana-laced signal. The signal pushed through the unstable magical power permeating the air, traveling farther and farther.
And when Xiao Shen’s urgent transmission finally reached the main force—
“Company, halt!”
An aircraft carrying someone landed smoothly on the runway, between ranks of soldiers and Hunters standing in flawless formation.
This operation involved a hundred thousand Hunters and a coalition of nations from across the world. It was massive—less an operation than a war.
Plenty of Hunters remained at the main base, and there were so many soldiers you could hardly take a step without running into one. An army of different nations and races.
The World Hunter Federation had to choose its commander at the base carefully, in case the chain of command broke down. Team Leader Choi, an excellent adviser, recommended someone.
A man with extraordinary strength and a distinguished record as a Hunter, along with the strategy and knowledge to command a large army.
A Hunter and a soldier. The only man to have reached the top of both professions.
Chuck Hagel—an S-rank Hunter active since the Great Cataclysm and the former Secretary of Defense of the good ol’ U.S. of A.
“Oh. Sleeping Beauty finally showed up. Or were you hibernating?”
Chuck Hagel’s idea of a greeting drew quiet laughter from the people lined up on either side of me.
It vanished without a trace the next moment.
“You’re laughing? Does this fucked-up wartime situation look like a joke to you?”

“You lunatics. From now on, anyone who laughs in front of me is getting their ass kicked, rank be damned. I don’t care if you’re some pasty Yankee dumbass who thinks white skin is your greatest achievement in life, a darkie spouting bullshit about political correctness, or a yellow monkey who can’t stop staring at his smartphone. I’ll beat every last one of you half to death. Understood?”
“Yes, sir!”
“Goddamn it. I can’t hear you!”
“Yes!! Sir!!”
Only after everyone shouted at the top of their lungs did Chuck Hagel nod and take a drag from his cigar.
“Okay, ladies.”
Holy shit. The man had presence.
He really was a living legend. Even Senior Kim Soodan would have to concede he had a thing or two to learn from Hagel about taking over a stage.
Of course, those thick arms like a bear’s and the violence he was born with had a lot to do with creating this brisk atmosphere.
*He’s definitely the right man for the job.*
Just as I thought that, a military jeep came tearing across the runway and screeched to a stop in front of us. A soldier in dress uniform hurriedly called out.
“Monster Wave! We’ve received an emergency request for support. It’s a Monster Wave!”
If I’d been an ordinary traveler, I would’ve taken a day to recover from jet lag.
But my life had parted ways with the word *ordinary* a long time ago, and there was no chance of them ever getting back together.
“Where is it?”
